title: Busy-waiting deep in MQTT Client close_connection() when executing IoTHub Client destroy
body:
Hi,

When I try IotHub Client MQTT sample (with mbedTLS and socketio_berkley from azure-c-shared-utility /adapters), everything works good but when I try to destroy IoTHub Client, then program hangs. I traced where the problem is.

Used: 
- Windows 10, MSYS32 with ESP-IDF (ESP32 toolkit - uses Freertos, Berkley sockets, mbedTLS)
- IoTHub Client (with customized build process for ESP-IDF), with dependencies:
    - azure-c-shared-utility (with adapters from /adapters)
    - MQTT (without AMQP, Websockets)

Source code:
[iothub_client_sample_mqtt](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/tree/master/iothub_client/samples/iothub_client_sample_mqtt)

Trace:
-> iothub_client_sample_mqtt_run(...) ([/iothub_client_sample_mqtt/iothub_client_sample_mqtt.c#L199](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/samples/iothub_client_sample_mqtt/iothub_client_sample_mqtt.c#L199))
IoTHubClient_LL_Destroy(...) ([iothub_client_ll.c#L707](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/src/iothub_client_ll.c#L707))
-> IoTHubTransport_Destroy(...) ([iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c#L2120](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/src/iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c#L2120))
-> DisconnectFromClient(...) ([iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c#L1742](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/src/iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c#L1742))
-> mqtt_client_disconnect(...) ([mqtt_client.c#L1091](https://github.com/Azure/azure-umqtt-c/blob/master/src/mqtt_client.c#L1091))
-> sendPacketItem(...) ([mqtt_client.c#L320](https://github.com/Azure/azure-umqtt-c/blob/master/src/mqtt_client.c#L320))
-> tlsio_mbedtls_send(...) ([tlsio_mbedtls.c#L571](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/tlsio_mbedtls.c#L571))
-> on_io_send(...) ([tlsio_mbedtls.c#L296](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/tlsio_mbedtls.c#L296))
-> socketio_send(...) ([socketio_berkeley.c#L526](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/socketio_berkeley.c#L526))
-> sendComplete(...) ([mqtt_client.c#L177](https://github.com/Azure/azure-umqtt-c/blob/master/src/mqtt_client.c#L177))
-> close_connection(...) ([mqtt_client.c#L72](https://github.com/Azure/azure-umqtt-c/blob/master/src/mqtt_client.c#L72)) <- There is maybe source of the problem
-> tlsio_mbedtls_dowork(...) ([tlsio_mbedtls.c#L595](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/tlsio_mbedtls.c#L595))
-> decode_ssl_received_bytes(...) ([tlsio_mbedtls.c#L116](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/tlsio_mbedtls.c#L116))
-> on_io_recv(...) ([tlsio_mbedtls.c#L249](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/243a825cfc7a16034c68401b6327a697728c9224/adapters/tlsio_mbedtls.c#L249)) <- There is spinning because receive nothing

I think... In the MQTT Client ([mqtt_client.c#L75](https://github.com/Azure/azure-umqtt-c/blob/master/src/mqtt_client.c#L75)) `close_complete` is equal to 1 (determined by sample executing) before entering the do-while loop. So the do-while loop will be terminated anyway, but the program calls `xio_dowork` and hangs in loop that receiving nothing.

I tried to rewrite do-while loop into only while. The while condition evaluates, the while loop is skipped and IoTHub Client is successfully destroyed but this workaround is probably not a real solution.

title: Mqtt twin timeout cleanup
body:
Fixes #1210 which has additional details.

If a reported property ended up timing out, we got into states where we weren't cleaning it up in a timely manner. It would be destroyed on closing the client handle, but this could be well off into the future.

After this fix make it so in our timer queue, remove message after too much time has elapsed.

This corrects the initial fix - #1217 - which was subsequently reverted.  Initial fix for #1217 had a bug where it was not always setting message creation times in the messages.  This change takes initial #1217 but also renames some variables so message time creation is more obvious, consolidates how we create these messages into more common code paths, and sets the Unit Test clock so that it starts at 30 minutes (instead of 0) to flush out timer-not-initiated type issues.

title: Heap corruption in gateway.dll during module loading
body:
Found a bug and luckily this one is 100% repro: During module loading, the gateway.dll suffers from a heap corruption when built in release. It doesn’t happen in debug. Modules loading are the dotnet OPC UA client module and the IoT Hub module.

You should also build PDBs for Release builds to make debugging stuff like this easier.
comments:
[2017-01-31T18:47:19Z | avranju | comment]
The issue here was that when you switched the build configuration to *Release* in Visual Studio for the gateway, it continued to link with the *Debug* build of the dependencies that it automatically built for you when you ran cmake. This is bad because on Windows, one gets different implementations of the C runtime (CRT) with different build configurations which means that anytime we have memory allocations and frees mixed between different CRTs, chaos ensues. A comprehensive fix for this issue will require us to change how we deal with gateway dependencies. We will essentially need to switch to depending on packages from external repositories such as *nuget* and *Aptitude*. This will take somewhat longer to accomplish and is on our backlog.

In the meantime we have checked in a change (https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/commit/655cd7cb72d1c084f20c10732c21f9b1bddab587) that enables the following:

  - Propagate build configuration while automatically building dependencies when you run cmake, i.e., now when you run cmake you can pass the build configuration via the `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` cmake variable and it's value will be used as the configuration to use when building dependencies.
  - Support *rebuilding* of dependencies when running the build script (`build.cmd` or `build.sh`). This is necessary when you are *switching* configurations. For example,  you may have been working with the *Debug* configuration and would now like to build *Release* bits. In order to accomplish this you can now run the build script like so -
    ```
    build.cmd --rebuild-deps --config Release
    ```
  - Enable generation of debug symbols for all release configurations on Windows

This should hopefully unblock you.

title: Cross-build not finding libraries
body:
The handling of cross development appears to be fundamentally broken.

In my cmake toolchain file, I specify where the libraries are.  When
building c-utility, it finds libssl, but not libcurl (which is in the
_same_ directory).

Here's the content of deps/c-utility/build/error.txt:


    /home/nextgen/toolchain/bin/../lib/gcc/arm-unknown-linux-uclibcgnueabi/4.6.3/../../../../arm-unknown-linux-uclibcgnueabi/bin/ld: cannot find -lcurl
    collect2: ld returned 1 exit status
    gmake[2]: *** [CMakeFiles/aziotsharedutil.dir/build.make:1138: libaziotsharedutil.so] Error 1
    gmake[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:68: CMakeFiles/aziotsharedutil.dir/all] Error 2
    gmake: *** [Makefile:139: all] Error 2

And here's deps/c-utility/build/CMakeFiles/aziotsharedutil.dir/link.txt:


    /home/nextgen/toolchain/bin/arm-linux-gcc -fPIC
    -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200112L -fPIC -Werror -g -shared
    -Wl,-soname,libaziotsharedutil.so -o libaziotsharedutil.so
    CMakeFiles/aziotsharedutil.dir/src/base64.c.o
    [...]
    CMakeFiles/aziotsharedutil.dir/src/x509_openssl.c.o -lcurl
    /home/nextgen/buildroot-new/output/host/usr/arm-buildroot-linux-uclibcgnueabi/sysroot/usr/lib64/libssl.so
    /home/nextgen/buildroot-new/output/host/usr/arm-buildroot-linux-uclibcgnueabi/sysroot/usr/lib64/libcrypto.so
    -lpthread -lm -luuid
    -Wl,-rpath,/home/nextgen/buildroot-new/output/host/usr/arm-buildroot-linux-uclibcgnueabi/sysroot/usr/lib64:

As you can see cmake found the ssl library files and specifed the full
path.  But for the curl library (which is in the same location as ssl
library files), it just uses "-lcurl".  That's broken.

I've tried setting CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS, CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS,
CMAKE_C_FLAGS with "-L" options to specify the library directory, but
those settings are apparently ignored and never show up in
aziotsharedutil.dir/link.txt

How are you supposed to configure the location of library files when
doing cross development?

[2017-02-07T06:18:23Z | damonbarry | comment]
I agree this should be fixed. In our azure-c-shared-utility dependency, the root [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/Azure/azure-c-shared-utility/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L513) file simply references curl, without doing a proper CMake `find_package()` first.

trick to it:

    SET(CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS "-L<whatever>" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)

title: build.sh --clean doesn't work
body:
The build.sh --clean option appears to be ignored.  There doesn't seem to be any way to rebuild
sources.
comments:
[2017-02-07T06:28:24Z | damonbarry | comment]
Yeah, `--clean` was part of the original build script, but didn't see much use and eventually went stale. The right thing to do is to remove it, since the build script deletes the cmake `build/` folder every time (i.e., every build is a clean build).

If you've already built and you want to rebuild the gateway bits without calling the build script, the way to do it in Linux is (from the repo root folder):
```
cd build/
make clean
make
```

If you're talking about rebuilding everything including dependencies, there's a flag in the latest build script for that: `--rebuild-deps`.

Fix is in the [2017-03-06](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/tree/2017-03-06) release.

var m = new Message(message.content ? message.content.buffer : []);

Replacing this with the following solves the problem:
```js
var m = new Message(JSON.stringify(message.content));

title: [.NET Binding][Improvement] Use preferred types for interop
body:
(separated from #20)
Use `IntPtr` instead of `long` for pointer or handle types in the surface between managed code and native code. This solves a potential marshaling problem when the gw sdk runs in x86 or arm32 in the future.
comments:
[2016-11-30T19:00:41Z | damonbarry | comment]
Thanks for reporting this! Sorry for the delay, we plan to fix this soon.

[2016-12-09T02:43:40Z | damonbarry | comment]
@yfakariya: in our C code we're converting module/broker pointers to `long long` (always 64 bits). We're sending the 64-bit values to the C# Broker constructor, which takes C# `long` arguments (always 64 bits).

So on 64-bit platforms everything should work nicely. And on 32-bit platforms, the 32-bit pointer values will be promoted to 64-bits, and then everything should work nicely. All the pointer values originate in native code, and all pointer access happens in native code; they're simply used as opaque identifiers in the managed code.

So I may be overlooking something important...is there really a problem with using a 64-bit integer instead of IntPtr here?

[2016-12-09T14:22:58Z | yfakariya | comment]
Sorry I missed casting to `long long` in C code. I agree it is no problem. Thanks!

title: IoT Hub C module does not receive C2D messages if no D2C messages are sent
body: The C IoT Hub module as it is written will receive C2D messages only if at least one D2C message is sent first. This doesn't seem right. It's conceivable that there may be gateways where IoT Hub is only being used for commanding purposes and not for telemetry. In this case the C2D messages will not get delivered at all.

title: segmentation fault in Java binding's Module_Start
body:
Hi team,
thank you for great work and quick response!

I saw segmentation fault (or access violation in Windows) from `Gateway_CreateFromJson`. The debugger said that the exception had been thrown from jvm.dll which had been called https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#

### Environment

* Windows 10 x64 with CU
* Using NuGet package (https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Azure.Devices.Gateway.Native.Windows.x64/)
   * I manually extracted the dll and pdb from the package's `runtime` folder to investigate.
* Oracle JDK 8u 131

### Additional information:

* My code calls `Broker#publish()` and wait for "response message" for request-response style messaging for initialization in `GatewayModule#start()`.
* When I commented out `Broker#publish()` call from `GatewayModule#start()`, the segfault looked disappear.
* As of our logging code in Java, `GatewayModule#start()` finished successfully.
* Another module sent messages to the Java module continuously.
* The debugger said that the invalid address is almost '0x270' and '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` once.
    * I failed to check call stack when I saw '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`. 

### Hypothesis

As far as I look, I found similar error in [Xamarin Android](https://bugzilla.xamarin.com/show_bug.cgi?id=13521#c17), it is race condition of `JNIEnv*`.
So, my hypothesis of this issue is race condition of `env` field of `MODULE_JAVA_DATA` as following:

1. The java host module initializes `JAVA_MODULE_HANDLE_DATA` as module data in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L116).
2. The `module_worker` created from the broker, passing `module_info` in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/core/src/broker.c#L373).
3. The `JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L473). I will call this thread as "main-thread".
4. The `module_worker` calles `JavaModuleHost_Receive` simultaneously, and it also calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and then stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L407). This step overwrites `JNIEnv*` for "main-thread". I will call this thread as "worker-thread"
5. The `GatewayModule#start()` is finished, then ``JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `ExceptionOccurred` with overwritten. It causes segmentation fault.
    * If the "worker-thread" already called `DetachCurrentThread`, it is reasonable the `env` field was invalidated with jvm as `-1L`.

So I think that `JNIEnv*` should be stored in the local variable instead of "effectively global" variable in the struct, ant it may solve this problem. In fact, it just works in our testing environment.

Any idea?

Thank you for always.

@abhatikar I reproduced the issue you're seeing (you're on Pi, I'm on a Docker Ubuntu 16.04 container, but same error). Here's how I encountered it:

```bash
apt-get install -y nodejs npm nodejs-legacy # installs v4.2.6
git clone https://github.com/azure/iot-edge.git
cd iot-edge
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # produces the original error for this GitHub issue
curl -sL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_8.x | bash -
apt-get install -y nodejs # installs v8.0.0
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # produces your error, in the nanomsg binding
```
I fixed the problem by cleaning the repo before building again:
```
git clean -xdf .
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # build succeeds
```
I think your error was just some weird interaction between the old and new versions of Node.js. Specifically, the `nanomsg` module uses node-gyp to build its underlying C library, and I'm pretty sure C interop is not compatible between major versions of Node.js. So using nanomsg built from an older version of Node.js isn't guaranteed to work. Deleting the `proxy/gateway/nodejs/node_modules/` folder forces everything to rebuild, and then it works.

Can you trying cleaning/rebuilding the iot-edge code, as I did above?

[2017-06-08T22:26:20Z | damonbarry | comment]
@camauser The following command in the build script:
```
CORES2=$(expr ${MEMAR[0]} / 500000)
```
Evaluates to this in your environment:
```
expr 498380 / 500000
```
...which returns the value `0`. That's all fine, except that the _exit status_ of the `expr` command in this case is non-zero, so the `set -e` command at the top of the script causes the script to exit.

Since we care about the expression result and not the exit status of `expr`, I've made a pull request that causes the script to disregard the exit status of this particular command.

title: Build with .NET binding fails: missing metahost.h
body:
I followed the directions in Getting Started document. But when I ran"build.cmd --enable-dotnet-binding", I'm getting errors. The reason is it cannot find metahost.h. This affects dotnet, dotnet_hl, dotnet_hl_static, and dotnet_static projects.

[2016-10-03T17:38:18Z | aribeironovaes | comment]
Hi @leeprtc , 

Thanks for using our SDK. Yes, we are aware of this problem and we are working to find a fix and also document the root cause. 

Apparently this happens because when you have 8.1 and 10 SDK CMAKE defaults to Windows 10 SDK, which doesn't build for the current .NET Binding. So, in order to mitigate that while we work on a fix you can:
1-Open the Visual Studio Project and, on the project it's failing (dotnet_hl.dll and all the dotnet host project), change from the Windows 10 SDK to Windows 8.1 SDK). Build again on visual studio. 

Keep in mind that this will surface again if you run again the build.cmd. 

Let us know if this doesn't fix your problem. 

Thanks a lot, 

Angelo Ribeiro.

[2016-10-03T19:06:48Z | leeprtc | comment]
Changing to Windows 8.1 SDK fixed the errors. 

Thanks!

[2016-12-08T23:25:11Z | damonbarry | comment]
Fixed with commit 00ab31f.

Metahost.h is available in several locations (and they're all the same for our purposes), e.g. on my dev box:

     C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\8.1\Include\um\metahost.h
     C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\NETFXSDK\4.6\Include\um\metahost.h
     C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\NETFXSDK\4.6.1\Include\um\metahost.h

Metahost.h is NOT available in the Windows 10 SDK for whatever reason. If you're targeting this SDK, I think it is expected that you'll pull it from the NETFX SDK instead. What's weird is that the NETFX SDK include path *IS* part of the INCLUDE env var, and INCLUDE *should* be searched by VC build, but apparently that's not happening here.

So the fix is to add %NETFXSDKDir%Include\um to the include directories in the dotnet and dotnet_static projects. The NETFXSDKDir environment variable is set in the VS Developer Command Prompt (and the MSBuild Command Prompt).

title: [v2 request] Can modules be allowed to start when there is no network
body:
As per iot-edge-runtime doc([1](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/iot-edge-runtime)), during the public preview, the runtime must be connected every time it tries to authenticate a device. This is perfectly fine. But, currently, if the gateway is started without internet connectivity, only the edgeAgent module is started. All other modules including the edgeHub are not even started. We are trying to migrate a v1 application to v2. The failure to start the modules will result in failure to even collect data and hence we will lose data.

Can v2 modules be allowed to start even if there is no internet connectivity? Please see that request is only to allow modules to start. There is no necessity the modules be allowed to connect to edgeHub. This module to edgeHub connectivity could be delayed till there is internet connectivity (until then SendEventAsync/IoTHubClient_LL_SendEventToOutputAsync will fail).

We are ok write code to persist data locally within modules when there is no connectivity. We are ok to live with a local copy of module twin when there is no connectivity.

Will take this up as a bug and get it resolved. Thanks for filing this.

[2018-07-10T18:08:00Z | darobs | comment]
Hello @chriswaters78 , @neumanndaniel,

We need to document this better, but if you set the Environment variable "OptimizeForPerformance" to "false" for the EdgeHub, all of our known OOM issues are resolved:

In the portal, this is set in a deployment by selecting "Configure advanced Edge Runtime settings, and adding an environment variable to Edge Hub.

In the deployment JSON, this would look like this:

```json
                    "edgeHub": {
                        "type": "docker",
                        "settings": {
                            "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0",
                            "createOptions": "{\n  \"HostConfig\": {\n    \"PortBindings\": {\n      \"8883/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"8883\"\n        }\n      ],\n      \"443/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"443\"\n        }\n      ],\n      \"5671/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"5671\"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
                        },
                        "env": {
                            "OptimizeForPerformance": {
                                "value": "false"
                            }
                        },
                        "status": "running",
                        "restartPolicy": "always"
                    }
```

My edgeHub container has been running for 13 days today. If this doesn't solve your issues, we'll have to start a new investigation.

Updated:  
[We do have this documented in our Troubleshooting section.](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/troubleshoot#stability-issues-on-resource-constrained-devices)

@darobs Thanks! That solved the issue and even better that this is now in our docs!

I'm going to close this issue as this has been addressed in the GA release.  Thank you all for your patience while we worked it all out.

title: [V2] std::bad_alloc error
body:
This error just happens on ARM (Raspberry Pi).

If I use `SetDesiredPropertyUpdateCallbackAsync` in a custom module which is just pumping data into the EdgeHub and I call once a module twin update through the Azure CLI like in the sample below

```
az iot hub module-twin replace -n codin -d rpi-temp-demo -m tempSensor -j module-twin.json
``` 

the custom module is stopping sending data after several calls to `SendEventAsync`. When looking in the logs of the EdgeHub I see then the following line

```
2018-01-22 11:48:33.461 +00:00 [INF] - Binding message channel for device Id rpi-temp-demo/tempSensor
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what():  std::bad_alloc
Aborted
```

The same code is running fine in Linux-x64.
comments:
[2018-01-22T23:58:40Z | damonbarry | comment]
This is the 2nd report I've seen of `std::bad_alloc` exceptions on RPi. @dariuszparys can you attach the code for the custom module (inline or gist)? Also, are there any other modules running or devices connected? What do the routes look like on Edge Hub? If we can repro locally we should be able to figure out what's going on...

[2018-01-23T06:10:47Z | dariuszparys | comment]
This is currently a work in progress module, so here is the link to the code I used here https://github.com/Azure/azureiotedge-simulated-temperature-sensor/pull/2. The image itself can be pulled from `dariuszparys/azureiotedge-simulated-temperature-sensor:twin-linux-arm`. No other modules involved and the route is just the default one created by the portal, so no changes there. I'm just pushing into `temperatureOutput` @damonbarry I added you to the repo as it is currently private

[2018-01-24T01:23:25Z | damonbarry | comment]
It looks like the Edge Hub is dying in this particular scenario. `std::bad_alloc` is an exception thrown by the C++ standard library, and the only native component I can think of in Edge Hub is RocksDb (used as a durable queue for messages, twin updates, etc.). So I suspect RocksDb is involved but I'm not sure how.

I'm marking this as a bug, and we'll do more investigation.

[2018-08-30T23:51:39Z | aribeironovaes | comment]
Closing this issue since we have a set of fixes on this area. If you see that again, please open a new github issue here: https://github.com/Azure/iotedge

Windows does not support `host` networking, as documented by Docker at https://docs.docker.com/network/host/ So it's expected that it won't work, and is not related to IoT Edge.

Now, as documented at https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/container-networking/network-drivers-topologies , you could create a new Docker network yourself using the `transparent` driver. If you then set that network name to be the value of `moby_runtime.network` in `config.yaml`, all your modules would be started on this network instead of the default `nat` network.

However, Moby on Windows has another bug where any non-built-in networks become unusable after a reboot. This is because they get a new ID but all containers remain associated with the old ID, so they don't start. The only mitigation is to delete all containers and let them be recreated, so that they attach to the new ID. This bug is also why IoT Edge itself does not default to using the `azure-iot-edge` network on Windows like on Linux, and instead uses the built-in `nat` network. I suspect that any network you create manually would have the same problem.

If the network you create *does* have that problem, then you will need to follow up with https://github.com/moby/moby/issues

Device Id had quote sign at start and shared key had it at the end, as 606simps noted. I fixed that in my local code, but did not work anyway. Because it was adding back slash ( \ )before forward slash ( / ) in the shared key. Something to do with encoding or reading of config file.

Hi @barnstee, 

Thanks for raising this. So, here is what we came: 
So, I tested and you are right, for a .NET module develop the latest change we make can cause a regression. 

Although we think that the current implementation is better than the previous one for the following reason:
Before the configuration just accepted pure String Configuration (like the one you are using on OPC US MODULE “devicekey;somethingelse”. Now the user can actually put JSON value (include pure strings). 

So, just to summarize: 

Before we used to have: 
            "args": {
                "dotnet_module_args": "module configuration"
            }

And the DotNEt Module received: module configuration as it’s content.

Now we are proposing having things like this: 
            "args": "module configuration"
Or 
            "args": {
                    "arg1": "value1",
                    "arg2": "value2"
                    }

And you would receive on your DotNEt Module: 
\”module configuration\”
Or
{\"arg1\":\"value1\",\"arg2\":\"value2\"}


And we now can claim that we support all types of JSON (Which we couldn’t do before). 
Example this: 
[
                {
                    "firstName": "John",
                    "lastName": "Doe"
                },
                {
                    "firstName": "Anna",
                    "lastName": "Smith"
                },
                {

                }
            ]
Would turn into this on our .NET Module
[{\"firstName\":\"John\",\"lastName\":\"Doe\"},{\"firstName\":\"Anna\",\"lastName\":\"Smith\"},{\"firstName\":\"Peter\",\"lastName\":\"Jones\"}]

This one the only thing you should do on your module would be to parse whatever you receive as JSON. 


So, with that, I will go ahead and close the issue. 

Thanks a lot Erich!

Angelo Ribeiro.

title: Broken access to homedir/sockets causes service failure after installing Azure IoT Edge runtime on Raspbian
body:
Hi,

I hope you'll be able to help, perhaps I'm missing something obvious, but I figured I'll share the issue and the results of my troubleshooting.

Issue:
After following the default how-to guide ([here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/how-to-install-iot-edge-linux-arm)) the `iotedge.service` fails to start.

Situation:
* Architecture/OS: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ freshly flashed with Raspbian Stretch (image dated on 2018-06-27); After flashing there was only: `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`, SSH server enabled, public SSH key copied
* The version of the runtime - I suppose the one the how-to points to is V1 (later in my troubleshooting I noticed `mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-agent:1.0` and `mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0` being used)
* Docker version:
```
Client:
 Version:      18.03.1-ce
 API version:  1.37
 Go version:   go1.9.5
 Git commit:   9ee9f40
 Built:        Thu Apr 26 07:17:20 2018
 OS/Arch:      linux/amd64
 Experimental: false
 Orchestrator: swarm
Server:
 Engine:
  Version:      18.03.1-ce
  API version:  1.37 (minimum version 1.12)
  Go version:   go1.9.5
  Git commit:   9ee9f40
  Built:        Thu Apr 26 07:15:30 2018
  OS/Arch:      linux/amd64
  Experimental: false
```

Description:
While troubleshooting (`journalctl -u iotedge --no-pager --no-full`) I noticed that by default the home directory for the IoT Edge Agent container is set to a non-existing `/tmp/iotedge` - running manually `sudo -u iotedge /usr/bin/iotedged -c /etc/iotedge/config.yaml` confirmed a _file not found_ error on `/tmp/iotedge`. I fixed that by setting `homedir` in `/etc/iotedge/config.yml` to a pre-existing directory.

At this point the service could make some more progress but it was still failing - this time with an `access denied` error. Checking the output of the manually ran service command showed that the issue was related to the socket files in `/var/run/iotedge/`.

I explored and experimented with the user IDs and permissions and noticed that by default:
* The IoT Edge Agent container (`mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-agent:1.0`) is launched by a systemd process running as `iotedge` user & group
* The IoT Edge Hub container (`mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0`) runs as an `edgehubuser` host user and internally has an `edgehubuser` with the UID set to 1000 and the GID set to 1000
* To further complicate the matters Raspbian's `pi` user has already UID 1000 & GID 1000
* It is possible to override the internal user of the IoT Edge Hub container by setting the value of _EdgeHubUser_ but that does not change the user with which the container itself is executed
* On the other hand attempting to override that with a setting in _Create Options_ (see contents below) on the Azure Portal is not effective either:
```
{
  "HostConfig": {
    "PortBindings": {
      ... [ default content of this key removed for readability] ...
      ]
    }
  },
  "Config": {
    "User": "root"
  }
}
  ```

Poking around further I used the following workarounds to make the service start:
* I created user & group "aliases" for both `iotedge` & `edgehubuser` (with UIDs & GIDs set to 1000) prior to installation (having multiple users with the same UID can lead to potential issues though)
* I relaxed the file/directory modes in `/lib/systemd/system/iotedge.mgmt.socket` & `/lib/systemd/system/iotedge.socket` (but this opens up a potential security hole)

I automated the whole installation process including workarounds with Ansible - see the repo [here](https://github.com/altermarkive/install-azure-iot-edge-on-raspbian-with-ansible)

I also noticed that others are also struggling with similar issues:
* [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50244863/iot-edge-hub-exception-unable-to-start-kestrel](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50244863/iot-edge-hub-exception-unable-to-start-kestrel)
* [https://mistywest.com/docker-more-than-a-cute-whale/](https://mistywest.com/docker-more-than-a-cute-whale/)

I don't know enough to suggest a solution (perhaps using `iotedge` user instead of `edgehubuser` could help) but maybe you will have an idea what is wrong. Of course, I'll be glad to provide any particular diagnostics/logs/outputs to help resolve the issue.

And thanks for reading the long post!

Eureka! That makes sense.

The config.yaml in the package is slightly different than the "default", 
and those difference affect how the iotedged works.

1) Try this:

```
sudo apt-get remove iotedge
sudo rm /etc/iotedge/config.yaml
sudo apt-get install <iotedged package>
```

When you edit /etc/iotedge/config.yaml, only replace the `<ADD DEVICE CONNECTION STRING HERE>` with your connection string. 
`sudo systemctl restart iotedge`

That should get you going without any trouble.

2) You aren't the only person having this problem, so I'm going to suggest a revision to our documentation to make this more clear.

Thank you!

title: Edison build fails during config due to host linker being invoked instead of cross linker
body:
Using the Intel Edison toolchain and build corresponding script in "tools" subdirectory fails with 
**cannot find crt1.o: No such file or directory**
On analysis, during the CMake config steps where it tries to validate the C compiler, it correctly uses the Edison cross-compiler, but then the link step uses the host's linker (/usr/bin/ld)

That is obviously not correct behavior, and leads to the above error early in the build.

Adding this "hack" to the inteledision_c.sh script works around the problem:
**-DCMAKE_LINKER=/opt/poky-edison/1.7.2/sysroots/core2-32-poky-linux/usr/bin/i586-poky-linux-ld**

But CMake should behave when CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER are properly set to point to the compilers, which they are.  

I have verified this behavior on a clean clone, and made sure all the cmake cache files were deleted, etc.

Anyone know the "right" way to fix this?

title: cmake drops build settings when descending into submodules - compiler checks fail
body:
I have prototyped a build script modeled after Intel Edison build script and it's corresponding environment setup script from Intel Edison toolchain.  When my build script starts, it sets up the environment, and calls cmake on build_root, the top level CMakeLists.txt performs the compiler checks and they pass.

`-- Check for working C compiler: /home/chris/mgc-cedar-minnowmax/embedded/codebench/bin/i686-pc-linux-gnu-gcc -- works`

But as soon as the build system descends into any submodule, these checks fail: (some debug messages() have been added)

`-- CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR:         /scratch/sandbox/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/deps/ctest`
`-- Check for working C compiler: /home/chris/mgc-cedar-minnowmax/embedded/codebench/bin/i686-pc-linux-gnu-gcc -- broken`

Upon further inspection, the variables that were set in the toolchain_file passed to cmake (using cmake's SET() directive) are blank, ie they have not been propagated into the submodule. Therefore, all my CFLAGS and LDFLAGS are effectively null, and the compiler check naturally fails.

What I know about cmake could fill a paragraph, and not more (well, actually I'm learning way more than I ever wanted to about cmake LOL!)

Where am I going wrong?
Note that I faced a similar failed compiler check running the Intel Edison example using the stock Edison toolchain and corresponding build script.  I documented that in https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/issues/71

title: Add better error handling for non-Ascii/UTF-8 encoded JSON config files
body: Currently the `parson` lib seems to only supports `utf-8` and `ascii` encoded files for calls to `json_parse_file`, and the gateway just errors out with a generic "can't open file" message.  Given that many text editors and shells (e.g. PowerShell) will default to creating/saving files as "Unicode" (e.g. PowerShell's Out-File function, *which should be codepage 1252?*), it would be helpful to have the Gateway error out with a more useful message on file open issues that suggest encoding problems as a starting point for troubleshooting.  There should also likely be documentation that notes potential file encoding problems.
comments:
[2017-01-04T20:59:45Z | damonbarry | comment]
Parson opens the file for us, and it doesn't print any error messages to the console or return any error codes (it just returns NULL if something goes wrong). For us to provide better error handling here, we'd need to replicate some parson functionality in our own code, which at this point we're not willing to do.

You mention that "many text editors" default-save to UTF-16, but I can't think of any. And PowerShell's `Out-File` command has an `-Encoding` argument that can be set to `ascii` or `utf8`.

I think the best thing we can do at this point is to clearly document that the JSON config file passed to Gateway_CreateFromJson must be ASCII or UTF-8.

title: Node.js module initialization issue when starting module is .NET
body:
Hey guys,

first of all I want to thank everybody who is contributing to this repo. I really think you're doing an amazing job here providing us with this open foundation for creating custom hybrid solutions in a fast and consistent way. Also looking forward to be a contributor very soon.

Right now I'm messing around with various gateway configurations and ran into an issue when setting up a Node.js module as sink and a starting .NET module as source.

When I start up the gateway it outputs the following message: **Info: Module has not been initialized yet: State: 1, Module: ../../../../samples/nodejs_simple_sample/nodejs_modules/filewriter.js**

Then the gateway prints: **Gateway is running.** and the .NET source module starts sending messages to the broker correctly.

The first message is not being processed by the Node module. 
Oddly enough, after ignoring the first message, the Node.js module starts processing incoming messages just fine.

I'm guessing the very first message kind of initializes the Node module and after that the module works as expected.

My question:
Is there anything that I'm missing in the configuration to instruct the gateway to initialize **all** modules on start? Am I doing something else wrong here or this an actual issue?

As a workaround I'm thinking about sending an initial wake-up / warm-up message, so that Node modules are initializing.

Thanks for reading all of that and y'all have a good one.

Thanks for filing the issue @teamdevmatch. From what I can tell it sounds like a race condition of sorts. The .NET module appears to get initialized and starts producing messages before the Node.js module has had a chance to load and initialize. Are you commencing sending of messages from your .NET module from the `IGatewayModule.Create` method or are you using the `IGatewayModuleStart.Start` method as a signal for triggering the start of message production?

[2017-01-13T00:14:13Z | teamdevmatch | comment]
Hey @avranju, the .NET module is the SDK's sensor sample (DotNetSensorModule) and the thread for publishing messages is created in the  `IGatewayModuleStart.Start` method. This should be the right place, I reckon.
Going to fiddle around a bit on replacing the `Thread` with a `Timer` or `Task` but I not sure if that'll make any difference.
Thanks so far looking into this topic.

[2017-01-13T00:55:32Z | avranju | comment]
I see. I am going to say that this is an issue with the Node.js binding implementation. In this case I would expect the binding code that bridges the Node.js runtime with the rest of the gateway to delay delivery of the message to the JS code till it has been initialized. I'll file a task for this and get this addressed. Thanks for reporting this!

title: See ${} when creating solution
comments:
[2018-08-03T06:25:29Z | LazarusX | comment]
This is by design. We will have `"${container_registry_server}/filtermodule"` as repository value in module.json after scaffolding, and the build process will replace the placeholder with active container registry server value in .env. The benefit is that if the user want to update the container registry server, he only needs to update the .env file.

[2018-08-03T06:33:17Z | LazarusX | comment]
However, I am reconsidering the adding new module experience as we are going to support multi container registries.

Currently, the solution on top of my mind is:
* Require the user to provide image registry when adding a new module
* Fill module.json with the actual value of image registry
* Update .env to include credential entries for the new image registry
* Update the `registryCredentials` section in deployment.template.json to include references to the registry credential env.

I have a issue tracking this: https://github.com/Azure/iotedgedev/issues/215

title: fix - dust sensor which doesn't work all the time
body:
There's already a PR meant for the dust sensor, but it doesn't address all problems: https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/365

There's also a post on the forum that addresses the issues with the dust sensor:
https://forum.dexterindustries.com/t/dust-sensor-in-python/1767/19

Finally, there is an improvement that was asked on this topic on the forum:
https://forum.dexterindustries.com/t/improving-dust-sensor-resolution-from-30-seconds-to-10-seconds/4912/11
comments:
[2018-07-05T14:03:59Z | RobertLucian | comment]
I have noticed that the timing in the `grovepi.py` script isn't handled in all places. 

I realized that when I tried to poll the dust sensor faster at higher rates without adding any delay between the I2C calls. When I would do that, the dust sensor function would no longer notify me of new values through the `databack[0]` parameter:
```
def dustSensorRead():
	"""
	By default, the sample rate is set to 1 at every 30 seconds and this
	function was written only for that interval.

	If you wish to use a different
	interval, then use dustSensorReadMore function. To set a
	different interval, use setDustSensrInterval function.
	"""
	write_i2c_block(address, dus_sensor_read_cmd + [unused, unused, unused])
	time.sleep(.2)
	#read_i2c_byte(address)
	#number = read_i2c_block(address)
	#return (number[1] * 256 + number[2])
	data_back= bus.read_i2c_block_data(address, 1)[0:6]
	#print data_back[:4]
	if data_back[0]!=255:
		lowpulseoccupancy=(data_back[3] * 65536 + data_back[2] * 256 + data_back[1])
		#print [data_back[0],lowpulseoccupancy]
		return [data_back[0], lowpulseoccupancy]
	else:
		return [-1,-1]
```

Looking at this code of  the `grovepi.py`, I noticed that there's no `time.sleep` after the second I2C call. After adding one in there the dust sensor started working really well. So the problem is that the for loop in the firmware needs some time to run it and when 2 consecutive I2C calls are made with no delay between them, things will get messed. 

What's interesting is that a bunch of functions don't have the 2nd delay added for the 2nd call, which might mean this is the cause for #412 .

[2018-07-17T15:26:50Z | RobertLucian | comment]
Seems like with the new changes that allow a much faster polling rate, the dust sensor no longer reports the correct values when the polling rate is slightly higher than what it used to be. Since this issue ought not to be fixed by adding delays, I resorted to finding the bug and seeing where it actually gets stuck.

After digging some time into this issue, I came to the conclusion that the problem comes from the variable that holds the low pulse occupancy value, whose value gets changed w/o having to when it's being used in the main loop and in the ISR. The problem doesn't come from not being a volatile variable or anything humanly imaginable, but it comes from the fact it was using `unsigned long` as a data type. It seems like when `unsigned longs`  (volatile) are used in both ISRs and the main loop, the variable change's its value without any sense. 

Changing the data type to a 16 bit one seems to mitigate the issue so most likely this is a compiler issue.

title: fix - I2C protocol issues (OSError/IOError) possibly caused by no support of repeated-starts on I2C
body:
Someone also has reported issues when communicating with the dust sensor device when using the GrovePi. An I2C error is thrown, but it could very well be just a firmware issue - possibly there’s a mismatch between the GrovePi does and what the Pi expects. Also other IOError/OSError exceptions have been encountered along the way.

Personally, I haven't encountered this issue just yet.

title: fix - getting max values (1023) (or invalid) when using analogRead/DHT/US/etc sensor
body:
It seems like when using the `analogRead` function or when using the DHT sensor, sometimes outlier values are returned (i.e. value 1023). This can be a hardware issue or even possibly a firmware issue.

https://forum.dexterindustries.com/t/piezo-sensor-i2c-error/4396
https://forum.dexterindustries.com/t/solved-dht-sensor-occasionally-returning-spurious-values/2939
comments:
[2018-07-24T19:38:07Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The bug seems to be caused by the HW bug with the I2C interface on the Raspberry Pi, where the clock stretching functionality doesn't seem to work well. Apparently, the Pi recognizes a clock stretch if the signal line is kept low and when it rises again it doesn't take into consideration the clock stretch that happened and thus the positive pulse gets to be too narrow (say less than the regular 7.6 uS).

Here's how it looks like when the stretching is done badly:

![analyser](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26958764/43161475-e8a1bb6e-8f90-11e8-8e95-60d0f08d1f64.PNG)

More can be read here: https://github.com/raspberrypi/linux/issues/254

Anyway, lowering or speeding up the I2C rate is rather cumbersome (and prone to changes with each new release) on the Pi and that's something that we shouldn't do.
Using software serial on the Pi could be a good idea but again, we would need a library that's solid and well tested by the community. 
Using delays in the firmware would have been a good idea, but the default implementation hides away the actual process when the data is sent back to the master. Currently the data is loaded in an ISR-triggerred function by using `Wire.write` s which actually don't send anything until the function ends - this basically takes away the ability to add delays when doing the actual transmission.

My best bet was to identify each transmission by an ID and thus not accept any transfer that comes in. So far it works, but it's not the perfect solution because it doesn't fully solve it - bad values still get through but at a lower rate, which I'd say it's a success.

The best thing we could do is use SPI instead, but unfortunately we are bound by our hardware.

title: fix - values of sensors get overwritten on others and vice-versa
body:
The readings of a sensor are overwritten to another one and vice versa. This happens when sensors like the DHT, the ultrasonic sensor, the dust sensor and analog sensors are used. There had been countless of occurrences on this issue.

comments:
[2018-07-10T20:24:57Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The values which were getting overwritten on other readings was caused by bad timing on the GrovePi and a lack of organizing the requests one after the another in an orderly manner. 

A mechanism to check if there's available data on the GrovePi has been added which basically reduces the need to use `sleep`s on the Pi. Now, we can just poll the GrovePi until it gets a response for the requested data. 

Huge improvements to the sample rate on basic functions (reading/writing on digital/analog ports, ultrasonic sensor, etc) have been brought. Before these improvements, in order to have a reliable connection to the GrovePi and still be able to poll the GrovePi for values (or for writing to ports) a sample rate of 10-15 was doable - now we can see sample rates of up to 380 while the system is running without any hiccups.

The DHT sensor at the moment takes roughly 550 ms for a reading. I think that number can be brought down to a half. It still needs to be investigated.

[2018-07-11T12:03:24Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The firmware would resort to reading twice for both the temperature and humidity sensor (with the DHT11) and that was quite inefficient. I have come up with another function in the firmware that does both of them in one run, thus taking the reading time down to ~280ms (up to 3.54 samples / sec from ~1.7 samples / sec).

[2018-07-11T18:12:28Z | RobertLucian | comment]
Support for the IR receiver has been added. What's super confusing is that there was a IR-related function in `grovepi.py` but it didn't do anything. The same thing for the firmware. 

So, long story short, we now also have support for the IR receiver on the GrovePi. I'm getting 150-170 samples / sec for the IR receiver, which to me I'd say it's a success.

Thanks for the report. This looks like it's the exact same problem as in #411. I'm already debugging it and I'm trying to see where this comes from.

[2018-07-27T12:54:23Z | RobertLucian | comment]
@yeeking in the first case, were NaNs the only thing you were seeing? If not, have you considered reading the DHT sensor until you'd get valid data and then repeat the process? 

What I have noticed is that the DHT sensor cannot be read too fast. When that happens, you get NaNs as a response - it's in the library of the sensor actually. So that's why it would be a probably good idea to run a loop with a sleep in it until you get valid data.

The error you are getting on wxgtk2.8 is normal on the Buster image. This package is required for the GUI interface which I think you don't need, which means you can bypass the installation of it by running:
```
curl -kL dexterindustries.com/update_grovepi | bash -s -- --bypass-gui-installation

Truth to be told, we don't support any of our robots (or devices) on Buster/Pi4 because this distribution is still very buggy and because we're still working on making everything work smoothly. It's in the pipeline, but it's gonna take a bit more time until it's ready.

- Mitigated abnormality caused by the Raspberry Pi not supporting clock stretching on the I2C [#411](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/411)
- Debugged and sped up the rate of acquisition of the DHT sensor [#418](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/418)
- Add IR receiver functionality for any remote control and fix inherent issues with the library [#416](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/416)
- Add option to set the flow meter and the dust sensor on different ports other than D2 [#421](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/421)

Hello there. Not sure if this is the correct place for this. I am testing the v1.3.0 firmware using our Go package Gobot's recently added support for GrovePi+. 

With a single analog device plugged into A1 is reading values as expected. however if I plug in a second device into either A0 or A2, than the reading from both analog devices is the same as the new device.

This is the code that communicates with the GrovePi here https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot/blob/master/drivers/i2c/grovepi_driver.go#L194

To summarize: a single analog device seems to read fine, but 2 at the same time are both returning the same value.

[2018-09-06T20:32:50Z | RobertLucian | comment]
@deadprogram: When I had done my round of testing for the GrovePi with this firmware `v1.3.0`, I was able to poll the analog input ports simultaneously just fine, which means there has got to be something incompatible in your implementation.

I'm making 2 assumptions:
1. You implemented the API according to this version of the firmware and not the old one which had lots of bugs and which is not compatible with this one.
1. You're polling the ports in a single thread/process. The communication between the Pi and the GrovePi still isn't thread-safe and it won't be in the foreseeable future.

If both of my assumptions are correct, then I'm not sure what could be wrong with your implementation. Still, I could test the GrovePi again and see if polling multiple analog sensors continuously works - just to be 100% sure.

[2018-09-06T21:22:00Z | deadprogram | comment]
Hi @RobertLucian thank you for the quick response. 

Both of your assumptions are mostly correct. Firstly, yes, this is the 1.3.0 API. Second, even though there are 2 goroutines, access to the i2c bus on the *host* is synced. However, after looking closer at the driver, it was not really synchronous enough when talking to the GrovePi as a device. You mentioning the threading was the clue. I added an additional mutex to control "transactionality" of the communication with the GrovePi, and now it is responding as expected.

Thanks again!

title: feature - add interrupts on all pins (release 1.4.0)
body:
This PR comes with 2 significant improvements to the GrovePi for version 1.4.0:

- Add support for setting up interrupt events on each digital port of the GrovePi, thus breaking the limit of just two available hardware interrupts [#446](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/pull/447)
- Enable the Grove Dust Sensor, the Grove Encoder and the Grove Flow Meter to work on any digital port of the GrovePi and support 7 or 3 or respectively 7 devices at the same time [#447](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/pull/446)

Along with these 2 improvements, the following changes were also made:

- Update documentation to reflect the newest changes.
- Curate root README to a slimmer version of it and add badges for the docs and license as an attempt to make the documentation popup easier.
- Update example programs for the aforementioned devices.
- Fix broken images in the documentation.

body:
I'm not sure if this is setup via the SDK or if it is a general Fault in the Brain Code, but its a bit disturbing:
When adding Buttons to the NEEO Brain via the SDK some there is no consisted order. As example i first expose all NEEO Remote Hardkeys via the Buttongroup (VOLUME, Controlpad, Menu and Back, Channel Zapper and POWER) then i do all predefined Softkeys also via Groups (Numpad, Color Buttons, Transport, Transport Search, Transport Scan, Transport Skip, Record) and a single Button INFO.
These are then displayed as alphabetic order on the Apps Shorcut page but gets disturbed by single Buttons that are added seperatly (you can have a look into my Enigma2 driver [index.js](https://github.com/carp3-noctem/neeo-driver-enigma2/blob/master/devices/enigma2/index.js) for all the signle buttons.
BUT the Buttons i add seperatly uses the order i add them and are not sorted alphabetic and also intermixed with the Button Group. Bit hard to describe what exactly i mean. If you like to have further Infos, just ask for it, i don't can describe it better currently.

title: Title and Fishy error
body:
While working on the Kaleidescape driver, I named a text label 'title' (by accident actually - should have been 'movieTitle') like...
`moviePlayer.addTextLabel({ name: 'title', label: 'Title'}, (deviceId) => controller.getMovieTitle(deviceId));`

After I added it into the brain, when I clicked on the device - it would startup but when it went to draw the UI - I'd get:

When I changed the name from 'title' to 'movieTitle' - it suddenly started working again.

Not sure if this is a bug or there are certain 'reserved' words that should not be used (then the SDK should be rejecting them at the start - so probably still a bug).

title: Bug in routing
body:
From express/server.js - you set the routes like
'/db' - routeDatabase
'/device' - routeDevice
'/' - routeDeviceRegistration

'/db/search' for device search
'/db/{0}' where device definition

'/device/xxx' - device discovery/set/get values

'/xxx' - adapter subscription

The problem really occurs with the last one - where 'xxx' is defined as '/:adapterName/yyy'

What if I was very bad and decided to name my adapter "db" or "device"?!?  Routing would get really screwed up since I was able to match a different route.  Same goes if you change the device ID to a string - then I could have a device id of "search" and screw that part up.

The routes should be more explicit - something like
'/db/search'
'/db/get'
'/device/discovery/xxx'
'/device/get/xxx'
'/device/set/xxx'
'/device/subscribe/xxx'
'/device/unsubscribe/xxx'

That way they 'dynamic' part of the route can't screw up your routing.

```
function findFirstNeeoBrain() {
    return new BluePromise((resolve, reject) => {
        const nets = os.networkInterfaces();
        for (const netName in nets) {
            const max = nets[netName].length;
            for (var idx = 0; idx < max; idx++) {
                const netInfo = nets[netName][idx];
                if (netInfo.internal === false && netInfo.family == "IPv4") {
                    mdns.findFirstNeeoBrain(netInfo.address)
                        .then(buildNEEOBrainModel)
                        .then(serverInfo => resolve(serverInfo));
                }
            }
        }
    });
}
```

That will loop through all the non-loopback IP4 interfaces and attempt to find the brain using that interface calling...

The **mdns.js** patch for the interface:

```
function findFirstNeeoBrain(netIf) {
  debug('findFirstNeeoBrain');
  return new BluePromise((resolve, reject) => {

    function serviceUpListener(service) {
      if (!service || !service.txt) {
        debug('invalid entry ignored');
        reject(new Error('INVALID_SERVICE_FOUND'));
      }
      debug('found a NEEO Brain: [%s]', service.name);
      resolve(service);
    }
    var bonjour = require('bonjour')({ interface: netIf });
    const mdnsBrowser = bonjour.findOne({ type: MDNS_NAME }, serviceUpListener);
    mdnsBrowser.start();
  });
}
```

Pretty self explanatory - basically create bonjour with the specified interface.

I don't have two brains (yet) so I can't really test to see if this works when each brain is on a different interface - but it looks like it should.

title: startServer fails due to unresolvable host
body:
I am using discovery feature to find the brain on my network. This was working well until recently. Lately the connection to the brain has been timing out if I use discovery. 

If I print out the brain information I see the following:
`{ name: 'NEEO Theater',
  host: 'NEEO-b23d007d.local',
  port: 3000,
  version: '0.49.10-20180116-9347090-0420-125452',
  region: 'US',
  iparray: [ '192.168.1.169' ] }`

The problem is that the hostname discovered is not resolvable on my network. If I override the host value with the value from the first entry in the iparray everything starts up & registers properly. For example, in order to work around this I manually set `brain.host = brain.iparray[0];` before calling `neeoapi.startServer(...)` in my driver code.

See the current examples, they use `neeoapi.discoverOneBrain()` which exactly returns one brain. Do you use this function?

The corresponding log from when I overwrote the host with the IP address shows that it connects properly: 
https://gist.github.com/barnabycourt/29d45872c0ecc5535e4a19701f776c05

It appears to be something going sideways in the brain register where the discovered hostname being returned by the brain via ssdp is not actually resolvable on the network even though the IP address works fine for connecting.

Thanks @barnabycourt for the logs. The relevant line is `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND neeo-b23d007d.local neeo-b23d007d.local:3000` -> which means the host cannot resolve mdns names (.local suffix). Thats why the second example works where you use an IP address.

ah and another hint, there are some access points that split the multicast subnet for the 2.4 and 5ghz network. maybe theres an `enable upnp` option on your ap

that means mdns resolution does not work (might be the router or an issue with mdns on windows), as a work around you can use the first ip address (see hint above).

title: "sudo" is not available for root user in docker container
body:
**Hi!**

and thank you for publishing your code!
I tried the application to get started with docker an get following exception:
```
Exception in thread Thread-10:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/threading.py", line 917, in _bootstrap_inner
    self.run()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/threading.py", line 865, in run
    self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/listener.py", line 84, in execute
    result = self.execute_instance.execute(root_allowed)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/execute.py", line 167, in execute
    output = execute_cmd(cmd, self.data.get('cwd'))
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/execute.py", line 58, in execute_cmd
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/subprocess.py", line 756, in __init__
    restore_signals, start_new_session)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/subprocess.py", line 1499, in _execute_child
    raise child_exception_type(errno_num, err_msg, err_filename)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'sudo': 'sudo'
```
I think the last message ``No such file or directory: 'sudo': 'sudo'``is the key. Everytime you log in or running a docker image, you are the user _root_ inside of the running container. An _root_ doesn't know the command ``sudo``:

https://github.com/Nekmo/amazon-dash/blob/96e5493f1ea61a4bb014bd52f367985cf987f031/amazon_dash/execute.py#L48

Is root really needed in this case?

**My configuration file**
```
settings:
  delay: 2
devices:
  7a:48:dd:53:99:a1:
    name: Kitchen button 1
    cmd: 'echo "1" >> /usr/src/app/amazon-dash.yml'
```
kind regards,
André

The docker default user is root - so no need to use sudo. 
The next issue you will run into is the usage of bash as the shell - this is also not installed in the provided DOCKERFILE.
On my local machine I patched the execute.py by removing the sudo in the command and used 'sh' instead of 'bash'.
But this is just a hack - for really fixing this you would first want to check the user running the script and second check whether you are missing something from sh which only bash can provide.

body:

The sensors I'm using are Linear/Nortek/GoControl WADWAZ-1 door/window sensors with an external switch feature. Note that in Home Assistant there is a different sensor than the reed switch which home assistant detects as:
sensor.linear_unknown_type_2001_id_0102_alarm_level
It changes in value from 0 to 255 depending on the status on the external switch.

title: [bug] Device is re-added to HA after changing name/location
body:
**Version**

Build/Run method
- Docker
- ~PKG~
- ~Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build )~

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.0.6
Openzwave Version: ? (don't know which is used in Docker image)

**Describe the bug**
When using Home Assistant discovery both the `identifier` of the device as the `unique_id` of the entity are based on the location and name of the device. This means that if you rename (or "move"/change location) a device that the device will be rediscovered in Home Assistant as the `identifier`/`unique_id` changed. So persistent ids must be used, this most likely could be the node id which will be unique in the network.  Preferably prefixed with something else (either some unique identifier of the Z-Wave network, or something like the MQTT prefix). This so the id will also be unique when you're running multiple instances of Zwave2Mqtt / having multiple ZWave networks. So the `identifier` of the device will then be some prefix with the node id, and the `unique_id` of the entity will then be the same (prefix + node id) but having the ValueID (I believe it's called) appended to it, which already is the case.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
I'm not sure if these are the proper steps, but I believe they are
1. Make sure you have Home Assistant discovery enabled
2. Check that the device is also shown in Home Assistant (so auto discovery works)
3. In Zwave2Mqtt change either the location, or name, of one of the devices/nodes
4. Restart Zwave2Mqtt / change settings and apply them (this will re-send the Home Assistant discovery messages)

**Expected behavior**
When checking Home Assistant again there still is only one device shown. But instead two devices are shown, one for the node were all entity ids etc have the old name/location, and one where the entity ids etc have the new name/location.

**Additional context**
Changing this behavior would be a backwards incompatible change as after an upgrade all devices a user has will be rediscovered by Home Assistant (because of the new `identifier` for the device and `unique_id` of the entity). But this at last makes sure that the same device will never be rediscovered (/show up twice, and one being "dead"). But I believe that's acceptable, and Home Assistant already has done changes like such many more times, where the automatically generated entity ids are changed after an upgrade to have more consistent and reliable ids from then on so they never have to change again. Furthermore the automatically generated entity id can still be changed in Home Assistant so the user doesn't have to use those awkward names anyway (when changing them manually) and other integrations, like zigbee2mqtt also use those kind of "random numbers" as unique id and thus generated entity ids (zigbee2mqtt does use the serial of the device)

[2019-12-21T09:12:47Z | petergebruers | comment]
I think it worth pointing out that OZW 1.6, in general, "auto clears" these values:
Scene Activation
Central Scene
Alarm aka Notification

When one of those events are reported by the device, OZW will change the value to indicate it got triggered. Then, after some time OZW will clear that value.

So In the log you first see the button press or alarm, then after some time:

""Automatically Clearing Scene" if it is Central Scene
""Automatically Clearing SceneID/Duration in" if it is Scene Activation
""Automatically Clearing Alarm in %dms"" if is an Alarm (Notificaton)

In case of the Alarm, the situation is more complex than the Scene classes and here is a separate discussion about that:

https://github.com/OpenZWave/open-zwave/issues/1889 "COMMAND_CLASS_ALARM "magic" clear issue"

I dont have access to my logs right now, but I was experiencing the same thing with both the LZW30-SN and LZW31-SN (I dont think config files for the LZW31-SN are not on github yet). Here is what I discovered:

- When OpenZwave 1.6 loads the config file the very first time, everything works except for scenes.
- If you restart z2m or use refresh note info, ozw appears to check for an updated config file online
- Ozw claims to find an updated config, so it renames the original config file to something like lzw31-sn.xml.1 and attempts to download the updated config
- The updated config file either does not download or does not save.  Since the new config does not exist, none of the settings appear, **but scenes now work**

I think there is a problem with ozw downloading updated config files (or maybe a permission issue?).  The problem with scenes appears to be caused by a combination of data in the config file and the way 1.6 detects scenes now.

My temporary solution was to disable the automatic download of new config files, and to edit the existing config files, removing the Central Scene Command Class from the Inovelli xml files.  This allows me to have working settings and working scenes.

title: [bug] Fibaro Double Switch II autodiscovery
body:
**Version**

Build/Run method
- [*] Docker
- [ ] PKG
- [ ] Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build ) 

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.1.1
Openzwave Version: 1.6

**Describe the bug**
First of all, im really sorry for logging another bug. I think Z2M is a great piece of software and appreciate the time and effort you are putting in this project. Please dont treat my tickets as demanding attitude, it's more like football fan supporting his club - I think that Z2M has many advantages over HA native Zwave support and I just want it to succeed. 

Ive got a problem with Fibaro Double Switch II (FGS223) HA autodiscovery.
Among 16 other devices attached to this node, Z2M detects both dimmer (incorrectly, as the device doesnt have dimming capability) and a switch (correctly) for each relay. I know that this probably can be sorted out by devices.js, but that's not the major problem here. 
The switches, while they have HASS autodiscovery JSON field showing up in Z2M panel, are not being discovered in HA. Other "devices", including dimmers detected by Z2M as part of Fibaro FGS223 are being seen in HA.

That has no sense. The payload is parsed into into json and json supports Boolean types.

If you are using `Just Value` as payload it is not a JSON so it cannot be parsed as boolean. 

You should set payload on/off to strings:

 "payload_off": 'false',
  "payload_on": 'true', 
```

` "value_template": "{{ value | bool }}"`

title: [bug] command classes which were hidden in HA/OZW1.4 are visible in Z2M
body:
**Version**
2.1.1

Build/Run method
- [*] Docker
- [ ] PKG
- [ ] Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build ) 

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.1.1
Openzwave Version: 1.6

**Describe the bug**
Some devices have CommandClasses which dont work or should be hidden. Such entities were not visible in HA/OZW1.4, but Z2M generates values for them.
Examples of such devices:
- Fibaro FGS-213
- Fibaro FGS-223
Which are both binary switches but theoretically support _COMMAND_CLASS_SWITCH_MULTILEVEL_ but as per OZW device config file it isn't functional though:
```
  <!-- COMMAND_CLASS_SWITCH_MULTILEVEL. This class is in the list reported by the device, but it does not respond to requests -->
  <CommandClass id="38">
    <Compatibility>
      <GetSupported>false</GetSupported>
    </Compatibility>
  </CommandClass>
```
and HA/OZW1.4 was not creating device entities for this class.
Looking at OZW config files, there's plenty of other devices which have Command Classes which dont work.

**Expected behavior**
Such command classes should be hidden, values coming from them should not be visible in Z2M web interface or passed to HA.

**Describe the bug**
Home Assistant autodiscovered lock stopped working after zwave2mqtt update from 2.2.0 to 3.0.0

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install / Update zwave2mqtt 3.0.0
2. Go to Home Assistant and try to Unlock/Lock. Lock will remain in "unlocked" state. Lock does not respond to commands

**Expected behavior**
Locking and Unlocking should operate the lock. Status should be reflected in Home Assistant

**Additional context**
This seems to be related to the attempt to fix lock discovery changes in Home Assistant 0.104+ - https://github.com/OpenZWave/Zwave2Mqtt/issues/203

**Workaround**
Tweaking the discovery json payload in Z2M > [Lock Configuration] > Home Assistant - devices fixes the issue and restores the lock functionality.

1. Quote true/false value around lock state booleans
Replace
```
    "state_locked": true,
    "state_unlocked": false,
```
With
```
    "state_locked": "true",
    "state_unlocked": "false",
 ```
2. Add payload_(lock|unlock) booleans as Home Assistant sends "LOCK" "UNLOCK" json payloads by default which seems to be ignored by Z2M. 

```
    "payload_lock": "true",
    "payload_unlock": "false",
```

After changes, discovery payload should look like this:
```
discovery_payload": {
    "command_topic": "[prefix_topic]/2/98/1/0/set",
    "state_locked": "true",
    "state_unlocked": "false",
    "payload_lock": "true",
    "payload_unlock": "false",
    "value_template": "{% if value_json.value == false %} false {% elif value_json.value == true %} true {% else %} unknown {% endif %}",
...
```

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.0.1

**Describe the bug**
GE fans show up as lights in hass rather than fans (see image below):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11232787/61327783-b1931080-a7e7-11e9-9599-2db960f541ed.png)


The zwave protocol is using command class 38, which is supposed to be reserved for lights, so this likely needs to be fixed using a manual hard-coded approach. Maintaining a list of anomalies might be a good idea.

So far, I've seen this issue with the following device ids:
99-12340-18756
99-12593-18756

The configuration for the fans can be found here:
https://github.com/OpenZWave/open-zwave/blob/master/config/ge/12724-dimmer.xml

**Describe the bug**
I have a switch ( you know the one) that does weird things on changing it.
This was fixed a while ago by allow "Verify Changes" to be set for the vlaue, this worked fine on openzwave 1.4 but it is now broken again.

Split this of from #23 as I think this is fixed, with a caviat.

Zwave2Mqtt version: master @ 20190805
Openzwave Version: 1.6.848

**Describe the bug**
Once of the devices I have is missing configuration in OpenZwave, while in the progess of writing a config file for it. I noticed values of type`short` are not handled properly.

**To Reproduce**
Per the manual, parameter 10 should be `short`:
https://manuals.fibaro.com/content/manuals/en/FGWOEF-011/FGWOEF-011-T-EN-v1.0.pdf

![param10](https://imgur.com/PXCOp6e.png)

```xml
    <Value type="short" index="10" genre="config" label="LED frame - power limit" value="36800" min="500" max="36800" size="4">
      <Help>This parameter determines maximum active power. Exceeding it results in the LED frame flashing violet. Function is active only when parameter 11 is set to 8 or 9.
500-36800 (50.0-3680.0W, step 0.1W) - power threshold</Help>
    </Value>
```

With `short` (above) it shows up as a negative value, when I switch to `int` (below) it shows up correctly with the default value of '36800'

```xml
    <Value type="int" index="10" genre="config" label="LED frame - power limit" value="36800" min="500" max="36800" size="4">
      <Help>This parameter determines maximum active power. Exceeding it results in the LED frame flashing violet. Function is active only when parameter 11 is set to 8 or 9.
500-36800 (50.0-3680.0W, step 0.1W) - power threshold</Help>
    </Value>
```

I think it might be a signed vs unsigned issues here, not sure if is in zwave2mqtt or in node-shared-openzwave. But accoriding to https://github.com/OpenZWave/open-zwave/wiki/Adding-Devices a `short` is the correct type to use as it more closely matches the range. 

```
o int - A integer can represent a number from 0 to 4294967295
o short - A Short can represent a number from 0 to 65535
```

**Expected behavior**
Values of type short to be disaplyed correctly.

This checks if the message length has received and uses that info for the remaining bytes rather than the expected size.  Prevents you from timing out if you use a wrong data type.

Since I am probably not the only fool in the world, maybe returned data can be auto-interpreted from the number of received bytes and then be cast to double ? Or do you have another list of data points ?

body:
We're facing provisioning issues of SparkFun Blynk Board from iOS devices. From the logs it is seen as the board just can't connect:
```
SSID: freud

Auth: 04b3b38ab7bb4ffab779d3275e620d6c
Host: qa.blynk.cc
Port: 8442
Connecting to qa.blynk.cc
Connecting to: freud
..............
Timed out connecting to WiFi.
```
I've noticed, that in such case, the iPhone is still connected to board's WiFI AP (e.g. "BlynkMe-BBYR"). This seems to be an issue.

This is not the case with Android, because Android drops connection to board after sending `config` http request. Unfortunately, there is no way to do the same on iOS.

As experiment, we've tried to provision board from Android without explicitly dropping connection to it after `config` http request. The result was the same as on iOS: board couldn't connect to instructed WiFi network.

title: Maximum Payload Size Exceeded Error after updating to Lora-app-server version 0.13.1
body:
Hello, currently I'm having some problem on sending more than 65 bytes of data from app-server to end-device. According to LoRaWAN specification v.1.0.2 Regional Parameters KR Band, the maximum payload size with SF7 should be 242 bytes. This configuration works with previous version of LoRa-App-Server. However, I got error after lora-app-server version is updated to 0.13.1. I didn't change any configuration that's working before.
### Is this a bug or a feature request?
Node configuration stay the same as the previously working one. Setup:
Class C; Receive window RX2; RX2 data-rate = 5 (SF7); Freq Band Config: KR920_923;
### What did you expect?
maximum payload size = 242 btyes
### What happened?
{"error": "push data-down error: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = maximum payload size exceeded",
  "code": 2}
when the payload is bigger than 65 bytes.
### What version are your using?
Lora-app-server version 0.13.1
loraserver version 0.21.0
### How can your issue be reproduced?
tested through Lora App Server REST API sending more than 65 byte of packet through Downlink queue

is this a bug or is there any steps that I'm missing?

Thank you.
Eddy.

After digging a little bit deeper into the sources, I concludes that I might've put the question in the wrong area (should be in loraserver issue). I don't have any problem on receiving 242 bytes of data from the end-device, with the CTXDataRate is shown correctly at 5, same with the RX2Datarate. Does the loraserver has some limitation on sending data, with maximum payload only 65 bytes?

Thank you.
Eddy.

title: Request queuing multiple downlink packets close together causes duplicate fCnt numbers
body:
### Is this a bug or a feature request?
Bug

### What did you expect?
When using the /api/devices/{devEUI}/queue POST API with requests very close together, the downlink packets that are queued up should each get different fCnt numbers. The 'getting' of the next fCnt number and saving the record needs to be wrapped in a transaction so that no two queued packets get the same fCnt number.

### What happened?
When calling /api/devices/{devEUI}/queue POST from another app to queue up multiple downlink packets at the same time / very close together, some packets are being given the same fCnt.

This causes ERROR webhooks to be sent for the second packet when all the packets get transmitted next time the end device checks in (class A)

backend_1     |   error: 'invalid frame-counter',
backend_1     |   fCnt: 43 }
