title: MQTT adapter stops working as soon as AMQP credits run out
body:
Hey,

I think there's an issue with the current protocol adapter imeplementations.

I ran some load tests against the mqtt adapter and have some findings. I wonder if there are any configuration gotchas or something I might have missed.

Let's start with the test scenario:

6 AWS EC2 instances fire against the hono mqtt adapter using jmeter. Device authentication is enabled (pwd, sha-512). The hono cluster is rather small, 3 t2.medium nodes running kubernetes with 3 masters. 
One message has a 512 byte payload.

Everything works fine with a total throttled throughput of 200 messages/sec. (10 devices on 1 tenant)
As soon as I ramp up the load everything breaks (2000 messages/sec total from 10 devices and 2000 messages/sec from 200 devices). 

The problem as far as I can tell is: 

The mqtt adapter runs out of credits and closes the connection, see this log message:

VertxBasedMqttProtocolAdapter - cannot process message for device [tenantId: DEFAULT_TENANT, deviceId: loadTestClient-4, topic: telemetry/DEFAULT_TENANT/loadTestClient-4, QoS: AT_MOST_ONCE, cause: no credit available for sending message

Closing the conncetion also deletes the registration assertion which in turn makes it necessary to gather the registration data from the device registry service on the next message. The device registry gets overwhelmed by those requests (100k in a 10min test run in my case).
The messaging service does not receive any more messages the mqtt adapter failes to recover by itself. I would expect the system to behave differently: Drop new messages from the affected tenant, instead it tries to accept them and 'kills' backend services. 

Are there any problems with my setup as far as you can tell? Imo the behavior is not acceptable, as there is a hard limit on throughput that brings down a deployment and requires manual intervention.

I'm happy to provide more information, just give me some pointers if necessary

Cheers
comments:
[2017-10-10T11:49:34Z | sophokles73 | comment]
None of the observed behavior is acceptable FMPOV. From what you describe, I see multiple issues we should probably address:

1. As you already mentioned, closing the connection also entails discarding of the registration assertion. Given the cost at which it needs to be created, one could ask whether it makes sense to close the connection at all once the adapter runs out of credits. On the other hand, closing the connection may trigger the client to (re-)connect to another adapter instance which hopefully has credits available.
1. The adapters currently assume that the registry is always available for issuing an assertion. However, IIRC the device registry just hands out 20 credits to an adapter for issuing requests. I think this will prove to be a bottleneck in the scenario described by you when hundreds of devices re-connect and send their first message. We should probably take precautions in the adapters to refuse messages if there are no credits available for requesting assertions from the Device Registration service.

In any case, your expectation regarding the system remaining in a stable state and degrading gracefully is more than appropriate.

[2017-10-11T11:21:25Z | sophokles73 | comment]
@pellmann @sysexcontrol @ppatierno @dejanb 

Guys, I think that we should make the behavior described in 1) configurable, i.e. if the MQTT adapter should close the connection if it runs out of credits for any of the following: forwarding the data to Hono Messaging or getting a registration status assertion from Device Registration.

WDYT?

[2017-10-11T11:53:29Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
Actually I think **running out of credits** should not be considered as an error case , but rather as a situation that at least every once in a while happens as normal behaviour.

Thus to close the connection to the client in such a case sounds to me like a "brutal" reaction - especially if the client did not misbehave at all, but only too many devices of the same tenant just sent data via the affected protocol adapter instance.

So, +1 for not closing the connection when running out of credits.

But I am not sure about why this should be configurable: I guess the configuration would then behave like it is now and disconnects the device? So if overload is the source of running out of credits, a large number of devices would constantly reconnect and jump through all adapter instances?
I would think this behaviour is hardly ever desired - rather more sophisticated strategies (like no single device can completely prevent other devices at the same adapter coming through with their payload) could be a midterm-solution.
WDYT?

[2017-10-11T12:52:13Z | pellmann | comment]
I am with @sysexcontrol and think running out of credits is a normal case and should not end in disconnection. The case that this might be true for a longer time, is something we need to figure out and how to handle it. So I think we should start with not closing the connection and collect experiences with this. If we make this configurable we do not have a real solution but a bigger amount of possible system states, which makes understanding of the system as a whole harder.

[2017-10-12T08:21:32Z | ppatierno | comment]
Unluckily, MQTT 3.1.1 doesn't have a way for providing errors to the client (it will be addressed with MQTT v5) and the only way is to close connection if errors occur.
In this specific case I agree on not closing the connection but just because we are supporting only "AT MOST ONCE" delivery so the client can expect that a packet is lost and is not delivered to the service.
If we'll move to support telemetry with "AT LEAST ONCE" then we can't just drop the message when the adapter runs out of credits.
For now, +1 for not closing the connection.

[2017-10-12T08:25:56Z | dejanb | comment]
I agree as well. For me it seems natural to just drop telemetry messages if there's no credit. For event (and other QoS1) messages, we should drop the message and not send puback back. IIRC that should indicate to the client that message is not received and it can try to redeliver it after a timeout.

[2017-10-12T08:28:53Z | sophokles73 | comment]
> For event (and other QoS1) messages, we should drop the message and not send puback back. IIRC that should indicate the client that message is not received and it can try to redeliver after a timeout.

I agree with @dejanb, even for QoS 1 we do not need to close the connection, we just do not send the PUBACK. This is already implemented.

I will then change the code accordingly, i.e. do not close the connection if we run out of credits (regardless of whether it is credits for Registration or Hono Messaging).

Thanks for your opinion, guys :+1:

[2017-10-12T08:29:14Z | ppatierno | comment]
Yes I agree with @dejanb regarding QoS 1, I made a mistake saying that "we can't just drop the message" ... the good idea is dropping message and not sending the PUBACK hoping that the adapter will receive more credit in the future.

[2017-10-16T12:40:01Z | sophokles73 | comment]
should be fixed in 41067c1d5ff1455d09c3cd2f73616bdfc50ec632

@alexmabsi can you give it a try and see if the MQTT Adapter remains in a stable state with these changes?

[2017-10-17T16:13:09Z | sophokles73 | comment]

The `HonoClientImpl` is dependent on the information of `isConnected()`, which it implements by using `isDisconnected()` from `ProtonConnection`. Which implements this in `ProtonConnectionImpl` as:

title: Protocol handlers may wait indefinitely on delivery updates
body:
When a protocol adapter sends a message downstream and Hono Messaging looses its link to the downstream AMQP Messaging Network, then the adapter may wait indefinitely for a delivery update because the senders created by `HonoClientImpl` do not set a time limit for waiting for a delivery update from the peer.
The adapters may thus leak memory when it accumulates stale delivery update handlers for such messages over time.

title: Grafana & influxDB are not getting deployed to Kubernetes/Openshift
comments:
[2018-02-14T09:20:18Z | sophokles73 | comment]
The reason for this seems to be missing quotation marks around the *version* label in the Kubernetes resource descriptors we use for deploying Grafana/influxDB. When the value is something like `0.5-M11` then Kubernetes is smart enough to determine that the value is a string. However, when the value is just `0.5` it tries to parse it as an integer and fails to do so.

[2018-02-16T07:49:55Z | sophokles73 | comment]
This problem can be circumvented quite easily.

If you are deploying using the binary archive downloaded from the [Download page](https://www.eclipse.org/hono/download/), do the following:
```shell
eclipse-hono-example-0.5$: sed -i.orig -e 's/version: *0.5/version: "0.5"/' deploy/kubernetes/*.yml
```
Then deploy using
```
eclipse-hono-example-0.5$: deploy/kubernetes/kubernetes_deploy.sh
```

If you are deploying from the source tree, do the following *before* you run the build:
```shell
HONO_HOME$: cd example
HONO_HOME/example$: sed -i.orig -e 's/version: *${project.version}/version: "${project.version}"/' src/main/deploy/kubernetes/*.yml
```

Then do the build and deploy to Kubernetes as described in the deployment guide.

title: HonoClient does only re-connect one time if no disconnect handler was provided in connect()
body:
Hi,

when I use hono client connect() without disconnect handler, re-connection just works fine for the very first time. But when client looses connection again there are no more re-connects. As JWT token expires every 10 minutes, hono clients configured like this do never re-connect after 20 minutes. This is also already mentioned #239 

Problem seems to be that when no disconnect handler is set, a handler gets set for reconnect that just invokes onRemoteDisconnect(): https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/6777c3e048a46d95c7985d441c7ac485eeb23858/client/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/client/impl/HonoClientImpl.java#L251-L269

Then during next re-connect, disconnect handler is not longer null and gets invoked, i.e. onRemoteDisconnect gets invoked. However, before invocation, connection gets set to null. But now failed connection and current connection (which is null now) are not the same and re-connect stops with a warn log statement: 

https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/6777c3e048a46d95c7985d441c7ac485eeb23858/client/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/client/impl/HonoClientImpl.java#L241-L249

Was there a reason why reconnect gets called with a disconnect handler, even when the user did not set one? Why not just invoke reconnect with null disconnect handler?

Thanks 
Daniel
comments:
[2018-02-14T17:27:18Z | sophokles73 | comment]
Hmmm, I tend to agree with your analysis and consider this a bug. It indeed doesn't seem to make much sense to invoke the *reconnect* method with a disconnect handler when the client originally did not provide one.

[2018-02-14T17:30:57Z | sophokles73 | comment]
Just to make sure:  you are not experiencing this problem when the client does indeed provide a disconnect handler, right? The protocol adapters provide one that simply invokes *connect* again. At least I haven't seen them having any problems re-connecting after the token has expired for the second time.

[2018-02-15T07:57:50Z | DanielMaier-BSI | comment]
Exactly, we use setting disconnect handler that reconnects also as a workaround at the moment and problem does not occur in this setup.

title: Support end-to-end AT LEAST ONCE delivery in Telemetry API
body: Currently Hono immediately accepts and settles telemetry messages. In order to allow clients to verify that telemetry messages have been received by downstream consumer, Hono messaging needs to be adapted to properly forward messages and AMQP dispositions frames between clients and downstream consumers.
comments:
[2018-02-23T15:44:25Z | sophokles73 | comment]
In fact, the `org.eclipse.hono.telemetry.impl.ForwardingTelemetryDownstreamAdapter` currently immediately accepts and settles all telemetry messages it receives from an upstream protocol adapter before forwarding the message to the downstream AMQP Messaging Network. So, the current implementation is not compliant with the sequence diagram illustrating the [message flow of the Upload Telemetry Data](https://www.eclipse.org/hono/api/telemetry-api/#upload-telemetry-data) operation.

title: UsernamePasswordCredentials does not handle illegal Base64 strings
body:
When a client registers a *hashed-password* credential, the device registry does not validate the given password hash to comply with Base64 encoding. Thus, when the client registers an improper password hash, authentication fails when data is published from a device using the corresponding credentials.

In this case, `UsernamePasswordCredentials` fails with an uncaught IllegalArgumentException as shown below (in this case the password hash started with a single quote character):
```
07:19:41.952 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-0] ERROR i.v.e.w.impl.RoutingContextImplBase - Unexpected exception in route
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Illegal base64 character 27
	at java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode0(Base64.java:714)
	at java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode(Base64.java:526)
	at java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode(Base64.java:549)
	at org.eclipse.hono.service.auth.device.UsernamePasswordCredentials.matchesCredentials(UsernamePasswordCredentials.java:151)
	at org.eclipse.hono.service.auth.device.AbstractDeviceCredentials.lambda$validate$1(AbstractDeviceCredentials.java:55)
	at java.util.stream.MatchOps$1MatchSink.accept(MatchOps.java:90)
	at java.util.stream.ReferencePipeline$2$1.accept(ReferencePipeline.java:175)
```

Currently an explicit `flow()` call is issued, which throws an exception if initial credits were not set to `0` in the setup.

This prevents calls to the http adapter with `hono-ttd` request param set and effectively leads to an unresponsed HTTP request.

Instead, the initial credits must be set to `1` and the direct call to `flow(1)` needs to be eliminated.

title: Caching of CommandConsumer make receiver links unusable
body:
After very few opened ProtonReceiver links the cache introduced in ebf7193cd708710c459c0345537bc264274d0df2
breaks `Command and Control` in the HTTP adapter.
The effect is that no receiver link will be opened anymore, since the cached version of the ProtonReceiver cannot be resurrected.

In any case, the caching of multiple ProtonReceivers (one per device) in memory would probably run into a large memory footprint and thus seems to be not desirable.
comments:
[2018-07-06T14:10:59Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
Http adapter fixed by 7ddbe1bb77feab65416e219d0cdf868d5e4b6c82.

[2018-07-06T14:12:16Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
@pellmann : would you please take over to eventually remove the caching of receiver links again?
We can discuss the reasons for that proposal by using this issue e.g.

[2018-07-09T13:20:18Z | pellmann | comment]
As discussed, the idea of the getOrCreate..() method and the map is not to cache the command consumer after closed state, but to be able to get the already established and open receiver link, when a device sends command ready events. 

This is especially important for connection based adapters like MQTT but also with e.g. HTTP it could happen, that the device sends an other event with ttd while the receiver link is already opened by an other one and should not be created a second time but reused.

[2018-07-09T13:23:03Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
That makes sense and thus the cache of `opened` command consumers should stay in the code.
It turns out that it was just a bug that it was not removed from the cache after closing, which was fixed by the commit.

So :+1: for having the cache in the code.

[2018-07-09T17:09:52Z | sophokles73 | comment]
@pellmann @sysexcontrol 

> This is especially important for connection based adapters like MQTT but also with e.g. HTTP it could happen, that the device sends an other event with ttd while the receiver link is already opened by an other one and should not be created a second time but reused.

For MQTT I see the benefit of caching the already established link and re-using the command consumer because the consumed commands (from the application) will always be published using the same `MqttEndpoint` instance representing the device. However, in the HTTP adapter, a cached link + consumer will always need to be associated with a new `RoutingContext` (representing the device's current request). We need to make sure that the consumer, which has been originally associated with the link at creation time, is not *overwritten* by a new consumer (for a new request from the same device) before the original consumer has finished its work, i.e. sending back a command to the device. I have not thought this through yet, but I guess it is worth spending one or two thoughts on whether this can actually happen or not.

[2018-07-10T07:47:50Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
@sophokles73 @pellmann 
If we have e.g. two parallel HTTP requests from the same device with a `ttd` set, we would have following scenario IMHO:
- first request comes in and a receiver link is opened
- second request comes in at
  - the same instance: the receiver link is reused, which is associated with the first `RoutingContext`
  - another instance: an additional receiver link is opened, which is associated with a different `RoutingContext` (even in a different JVM)

Next the application receives the downstream message with `ttd` and sends a command upstream:
- if the two requests were opened in the same instance: the command is written to the `RoutingContext` of the first HTTP request
- if the two requests were opened in different instances: the AMQP network decides which of the two links gets the command, and this determines which of the two HTTP requests will receive the command in the response. This assumes we have the routing setup in `balanced` mode.

Additionally we have the scenario that the `ttd` of one of the two requests expires:
- if the two requests were opened in the same instance: the link will be effectively closed, which disables the application to successfully send the command to the second request (since no link is open anymore). This is detectable by the application and can always happen if there would be network problems in delivering the command to the device anyway, so it can be considered as not being an error - the application has to repeat the command later.
- if the two requests were opened in different instances: then the other request will receive the command and puts it to the response.

The described scenario should behave the same with more than two parallel requests, so it should be sufficient to show it for two requests instead of `n` requests.

I hope I did not miss anything - and I will verify the behaviour of the described scenarios (was not done yet).

In general it is a good question IMHO if the scenario of multiple HTTP requests with `ttd` parameters is a realistic scenario - nevertheless it must never malfunction, of course. But the impact that the application may have to repeat a command in special cases (see above) should be acceptable since it might be an unusual use case. Any thoughts on that?

[2018-07-11T16:50:16Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
@sophokles73 @pellmann 

Result of verifying the behaviour of parallel HTTP requests to one adapter instance from the same device with a ttd set:
- as outlined, the first pending request receives the command, even if the second request triggered the sending of the command in the app.

Several fixes resp. improvements were necessary, but the basic behaviour matched with the description above.

Tests for multiple instances follow (should be much simpler).

@sophokles73 @pellmann

title: Deadlock in HTTP Adapter of Hono 0.6-Final
body:
Hi Hono Devs,

we're running Hono 0.6 (Release) in a kubernetes cluster.
Sometimes we are encountering problems with an unresponsive Hono HTTP Adapter. 

The last time we took a thread dump of the pod, which shows a java deadlock:

```
Found one Java-level deadlock:
=============================
"vert.x-eventloop-thread-4":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fc1c000d0a8 (object 0x00000000f07a7c40, a io.vertx.ext.web.impl.RouteImpl),
  which is held by "vert.x-eventloop-thread-0"
"vert.x-eventloop-thread-0":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fc1c408c318 (object 0x00000000f07a8fc0, a io.vertx.ext.web.impl.RouteImpl),
  which is held by "vert.x-eventloop-thread-4"
```
I'm attaching the log file and thread dump:
[logs-from-hono-adapter-http-vertx-in-hono-adapter-http-vertx.txt](https://github.com/eclipse/hono/files/2170657/logs-from-hono-adapter-http-vertx-in-hono-adapter-http-vertx.txt)
[threadDump.log](https://github.com/eclipse/hono/files/2170659/threadDump.log)
 
Sadly I don't have concrete steps to reproduce the issue yet. But maybe someone else experienced  something similar or got a hunch what could be the problem.
comments:
[2018-07-09T17:01:19Z | sophokles73 | comment]
I have started to look into this. I am quite sure what the problem is (thanks to the thread dump) but I am not (yet) sure how to properly address the problem.

[2018-07-10T11:47:02Z | sophokles73 | comment]
The problem seems to be that we *switch* the vert.x `Context` while processing requests. When a request comes in it is handled on the event loop context that has been created when the HTTP adapter verticle gets deployed. This Context is associated with one of the event loop threads, say *event-loop-thread-0*.

When Spring instantiates the HonoClient instances for connecting to the registry and AMQP network, these instances all create a new vert.x Context to run on in their constructor. So, let's say the client for accessing the Tenant service runs on a Context that is associated with *event-loop-thread-1*.

Now, when an HTTP request is being processed, we first try to authenticate the device which includes a lookup of the tenant that the device belongs to. Thus, the request handler invokes the Tenant HonoClient which will add a task to the *event-loop-thread-1*'s event loop. When the result of the lookup operation is received from the Tenant service (still on *event-loop-thread-1*) the HonoClient completes the result future and the processing of the HTTP request can continue. This involves invocation of `Router.next()` in order to determine the next handler to invoke for processing the HTTP request. However, the Router instance (which has been created on *event-loop-thread-0* when the HTTP server has been started), will now be concurrently accessed from two threads: *event-loop-thread-1* (with the result of the tenant lookup) as well as from *event-loop-thread-0* (for handling the next request coming in from a device).

We now have a situation where two threads try to lock on the same objects (the `Route`s registered in the Router) which seems to be prone to ending in the observed deadlock situation.

I think that we will need to make sure that the result of the operations invoked on the HonoClient instances gets processed on the calling code's Context (and underlying thread). I am currently thinking about ways how to achieve this.

[2018-07-12T08:07:06Z | sophokles73 | comment]
As a corollary to the strategy of fixing this issue, we also need to get the validation of client certificates off of the event loop because the `TenantApiBasedX509TrustManager` uses the `HonoClient` for the Tenant service to look up the tenant that the device belongs to. However, since the `X509TrustManager.checkClientTrusted` method is blocking the current thread, we cannot run both on the same event loop (we would never get the result of the tenant lookup because the result handler is scheduled to the same event loop which is still blocked by the trust manager check).

Assuming that we still want to do validation of client certs based on the dynamic lookup of the trust anchor, we will need to move the validation of the certificate chain up to the application level, i.e. into the `X509AuthHandler`. This actually is less frightening as it at first seems because we need to lookup the tenant there anyway in order to be able to do the credentials lookup (which is always scoped to the tenant).

[2018-07-19T09:54:10Z | sophokles73 | comment]
fixed in https://github.com/eclipse/hono/commit/4e7dc3aeba95d03804518aed3655ab2c71f82a2c

title: Services can be flooded with requests
body:
Pushing "too many" requests towards the Hono HTTP protocol adapter make it behave rather poorly. My expectation would be that Hono would still be able to handle the amount it can handle, but it looks to me as if the HTTP adapter mostly breaks down.

I tried to dig a little bit into this and I think I know one reason why this could be. Pushing HTTP requests  make the HTTP protocol adapter issues requests towards the device registry. If such a request cannot be handled in a specific amount of time (default 200ms) then it will be aborted and the HTTP request failed.

My understanding of the message flow is the following:

![request handling](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/202474/43648168-f907dc12-9739-11e8-9054-6c62f032e8d9.png)


<details>
title Request handling

Client->+Endpoint: Send request
note right of Endpoint: Validate Request
Endpoint->EventBus: Publish request
Endpoint-->-Client: Accept request

note over  Client: New credits are available

note right of EventBus: Process request
EventBus->Endpoint: Publish response

Endpoint->+Client: Send response
Client-->-Endpoint: Accept response
</details>

This would mean that the client (the protocol adapter) can push at a higher rate than the EventBus/RequestProcessor/Verticle can handle. Building up requests and slowing down the process.

That would also mean that, if requests stay longer than 200ms in some kind of queue on the EventBus side, then they would time out on the Protocol adapter side. So once your are in state that the EventBus queue is at a size that requests have to wait more than 200ms, then all requests will timeout. Which in fact means that no HTTP requests will be accepted any more.

A possible solution for that problem would be to delay the accept of the request until the response was send. The reject or release could still be sent directly after the validation of the request.

Another possible solution would be to get rid of the EventBus completely. As some initial profiler run showed that most of the time is spent processing EventBus messages.

This may as well relate to issue #735.
comments:
[2018-08-03T15:28:43Z | sophokles73 | comment]
> A possible solution for that problem would be to delay the accept of the request until the response was send. The reject or release could still be sent directly after the validation of the request.

I do not quite understand how this would help. If  the request messages take longer than 200 ms to process in the device registry, then the requests towards the registry will still time out in the adapter, because the response does not arrive in time (within 200 ms). The result should be the same: the adapter will reject HTTP requests with a 503, or am I mistaken?

Once the adapter runs out of credits from the registry, it should actually immediately return a 503 to clients without trying to invoke the registry.

Did you experience this same behavior using the "load test mode" of the registry, where it simply returns a response without looking up the data?

[2018-08-03T15:37:46Z | ctron | comment]
> I do not quite understand how this would help. If the request messages take longer than 200 ms to process in the device registry, then the requests towards the registry will still time out in the adapter, because the response does not arrive in time (within 200 ms). The result should be the same: the adapter will reject HTTP requests with a 503, or am I mistaken?

And that is what happens. Yet, on the device registry side, that request is still present and will be processed, delaying requests coming in after that. So all requests which arrive in the future will also time out.

> Once the adapter runs out of credits from the registry, it should actually immediately return a 503 to clients without trying to invoke the registry.

It does, but that is not the problem.

> Did you experience this same behavior using the "load test mode" of the registry, where it simply returns a response without looking up the data?

Yes.

Assuming you have a device registry which allows for 100 credits, but only can process 1 request a second and the timeout it one second. And the request rate is 10 requests per second:

On the first second, you have 10 accepted requests and 1 response. 9 timeouts. And 9 requests in the queue. As canceling requests doesn't remove them on the device registry side.

On the second you have 10 accepted requests, 1 response (already timed out), 10 timeouts and 18 requests on the queue …

[2018-08-03T15:54:45Z | sophokles73 | comment]
So, then the issue actually seems to be the fact that the registry flows a credit to the adapter with each request message it accepts (due to the prefetch we set in `RequestResponseEndpoint.onLInkAttach`). 
We would need to change this to manual flow control and flow the credit back to the adapter only *after* we have sent back the response ... This way, we should be able to build up back pressure appropriately. WDYT?

[2018-08-06T07:39:32Z | ctron | comment]
You are right. That was a misunderstanding from my side about how it works. My understanding was that the disposition also handles the credit. Which it does not.

So the solution would be as you suggested, send the credit manually. I will create a PR and assign you as a reviewer.

[2018-08-06T09:58:05Z | ctron | comment]
Summarizing the discussion from IRC:

Currently there is the problem that, on the request/response service side, there is no correlation between the receiver of the request and the sender of the response. So it isn't possible to do proper credit tracking.

My proposal would be to re-structure the request/response functionality in a way that is uses the EventBus reply feature and use that as a way to send the response to the requestor. This also seems to appropriate way to use the EventBus from a vertx point of view.

For this to work, it is required though to know to which link to send the response to. For this, an in-memory map will be added, which records which senders are registered for each reply-to address.

This change would also eliminate the need the an explicit call to `consume` on the event bus, and thus resolves the memory leak described in #753.

> For this to work, it is required though to know to which link to send the response to. For this, an in-memory map will be added, which records which senders are registered for each reply-to address.
This change would also eliminate the need the an explicit call to consume on the event bus, and thus resolves the memory leak described in #753.

I agree that this will prevent EventBusConsumers to leak in the situation described in #753. However, it will introduce another potential leak: when a client breaks away, we still need to make sure that the sender gets removed from the map. So, in any case we need to deal with clients breaking away unexpectedly.

I would therefore rather stick with the current implementation in order to not turn everything upside down (again), add the *sender/reply-to* map and make sure that we both close the corresponding EventBusConsumer and remove the sender from the map when a client disconnects (unexpectedly). The map can then be used to flow credit to the sender when a response message has been received from the event bus.

Using the "reply" functionality would definitely make the code more understandable IMHO. As there is clear connection between the request and the response. But yes, technically that will work as well, if you want to stick to the current pattern. Let me know and I will make a PR.

title: New Bcrypt credentials enables DoS attack on the protocol adapters.
body:
As per Credentials API, Hono is using Spring security for Bcrypt password encoding.

Spring security supports bcrypt password encoding with log rotations from 4 to 31, 10 being default (i.e:- 2^10 hash iterations). Once hashed, the log rotation used is part of the password like 

`$2a$21$LQdzaDSINBpHmYRiGEVtkOVt2GScZ6bPvEyoAIpiVIE6F4rviemdm`

where $21 represents the log rotation used. There is currently no max limit defined in Hono. If a user, say stores the password with higher rotation, then it could enable a DOS attack on the adapters.

I tested the time taken for `BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches` with higher log rotation on my laptop (Intel Core i7 - 2.7GHz 8 core, 32 GB RAM) it took

- 10 - 105 milliseconds
- 12 - 360 milliseconds
- 18 - 21 seconds
- 21 - 178 seconds
- 31 - more than 1 hour and I had to abort it.

Setting 31 as log rotation will definitely block the protocol adapters.

As a best practise, I would restrict the log rotation to 12 or 14, document them as part of credentials API and have this checked in 

org.eclipse.hono.util.CredentialsObject.hasValidSecrets()
comments:
[2018-09-20T12:49:46Z | sysexcontrol | comment]
@balsmn Thanks a lot for this detailed report!
IMHO very reasonable, I will schedule a fix for the next milestone 0.8-M2.

[2018-10-01T12:10:00Z | sophokles73 | comment]
Nice catch @balsmn :+1: 
There seem to be two issues to consider in this context:
1. Make sure that we do not allow a DOS attack by registering a bcrypted password with more iteratins than seem reasonable.
2. Make sure that we do not block the event loop of protocol adapters that validate a password against a bcrypt hash.

The first item should probably be addressed by introducing a (configurable) upper limit to the Credentials endpoint implementation included in Hono. However, other Credentials API implementations that do not make use of the base classes provided by Hono will need to enforce such a limit themselves.

The second item needs to be addressed in Hono's `AbstractDeviceCredentials` class by scheduling the hash validation on a worker thread instead of running it on the event loop.

WDYT?

However, other Credentials API implementations that do not make use of the base classes provided by Hono will need to enforce such a limit themselves.

title: MQTT/AMQP adapter: Deleted/disabled devices should not be able to connect
body: A device has been registered and credentials for that device has also been added.  Then the device is deleted but not the corresponding credentials. In this case, the deleted device is still able to subscribe to control endpoint, receive commands and send command responses.
comments:
[2018-11-05T09:05:25Z | sophokles73 | comment]
If a device is deleted (I assume you are referring to the process of removing its registration information from the Device Registration service) then the device should no longer be able to connect to the MQTT adapter at all, and thus not be able to subscribe to the command topic.

I suspect that the behavior you experience is merely because the registration information (the assertion, to be precise) is cached in the protocol adapter for a configurable amount of time. We (currently) do not invalidate the cache if the underlying information is removed from the registry. Can you validate this by e.g. restarting the MQTT adapter after deleting the registration information and see if the device can still connect? You should also be able to simply wait for the cache to expire (5 minutes?) instead of restarting the adapter.

> If a device is deleted (I assume you are referring to the process of removing its registration information from the Device Registration service) then the device should no longer be able to connect to the MQTT adapter at all, and thus not be able to subscribe to the command topic.
> 
> I suspect that the behavior you experience is merely because the registration information (the assertion, to be precise) is cached in the protocol adapter for a configurable amount of time. In Mqtt adapter, currently device registration assertion `getRegistrationAssertion()` is not being done during subscription and uploading command response. FMPOV this needs to be done.

No, it should be done as part of establishing the connection. If a device is disabled or doesn't even exist, then it should not be able to connect to the MQTT adapter. If we make sure that this is the case then I do not see why we should need to do the check on every interaction ...

[2018-11-05T09:34:54Z | kaniyan | comment]
Currently for telemetry and event messages, this check is being done while receiving those messages. I agree that it should be done as part of establishing the connection.

As per this solution, we check the device registration at the time of the connection establishment.  Assume a device, which is connected to the Mqtt adapter, is deleted. In this case, the deleted device, 
 that remains connected, can still perform telemetry, event and command operations until the Mqtt adapter is restarted or the device reconnects.  I think that this scenario (Handling deletion of connected devices) is also applicable to other adapters.

Makes things a little more complicated, but for security reasons we do not have a choice, do we?

title: DefaultFailureHandler expects response message to be set correctly
body:
The `DefaultFailureHandler` uses the status message of the request if the context has a status code set: https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/c947ae6be19e27e24938335c8b508a1f3fc331e2/service-base/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/service/http/DefaultFailureHandler.java#L73
but in some cases the status message was not yet set and the default message ("OK") is used: 
https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/6aafd1733bb82ef71a69675c4414c1a0210d7fcf/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/http/impl/HttpServerResponseImpl.java#L89
For example this is the case when using the Vertx AuthHandler which will fail the context but doesn't set a status message: 
https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-web/blob/af922fb2b6b46ccbb18568ca5ac4123be8a33491/vertx-web/src/main/java/io/vertx/ext/web/handler/impl/AuthHandlerImpl.java#L193-L200

In this case when the authorization fails, the status will be `401` but with a body of `OK`.

Maybe the DefaultFailureHandler should defer the status message from the status code?
comments:
[2018-11-30T16:04:46Z | sophokles73 | comment]
Once we have upgraded to vert.x 3.6.0, the AuthHandlers that Hono uses will override the *processException* method of `AuthHandlerImpl` to not only fail the context with the status code but always with either an `HttpStatusException` or a `ServiceInvocationException`. The response body will then be set to the message contained in the exception. However, what you propose still makes sense to me, i.e. deriving the body from the status code if the context has been failed with a status code only (and no exception).

[2018-11-30T16:05:52Z | sophokles73 | comment]
@mbaeuerle  would you like to create a PR for `DefaultFailureHandler`?

	at io.vertx.mqtt.impl.MqttServerConnection.handlePublish(MqttServerConnection.java:323)
````
`metrics.incrementUndeliverableMessages(context.endpoint(), context.tenant())` fails with an NPE because `context.tenant()` is null.

My guess here would be that the actual tenant in this case comes from the authenticated device (see `VertxBasedMqttProtocolAdapter.checkAddress` - "use authenticated device's tenant to fill in missing information") and `context.tenant()` is still the original value.

title: [#1013] Fix wrong exception being thrown on SASL handshake failure.
body: This fixes #1013.
comments:
[2019-01-29T16:23:27Z | calohmn | comment]
As a further differentiation, the `SaslSystemException.permanent` flag could be checked, maybe throwing a `ServerErrorException` with `HTTP_UNAVAILABLE` ("failed to connect") if `permanent` is false. But I'm not sure about that.

[2019-01-29T17:13:07Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
it is true that the behavior in vertx-proton has changed. However, `ProtonSaslClientAuthenticatorImpl` uses different exceptions to indicate different types of failures:
```
  private void handleSaslFail() throws SaslException {
    switch(sasl.getOutcome()) {
    case PN_SASL_AUTH:
      throw new AuthenticationException("Failed to authenticate");
    case PN_SASL_SYS:
    case PN_SASL_TEMP:
      throw new SaslSystemException(false, "SASL handshake failed due to a transient error");
    case PN_SASL_PERM:
      throw new SaslSystemException(true, "SASL handshake failed due to an unrecoverable error");
    default:
      throw new SaslException("SASL handshake failed");
    }
  }
```
In particular, the most probable cause for failure (wrong credentials) is indicated by a `javax.security.sasl.AuthenticationException` (a subclass of `javax.security.sasl.SaslException`).

So, I think that we should catch `javax.security.sasl.SaslException` here instead of `SecurityException` and add another catch clause for `SaslSystemException` which is used to indicate cases where the server is not ready to process the handshake and fail with a `ServerErrorException` in that case.

right, I now see I was concentrating on only one case, the one thrown in `handleSaslInit` if no SASL mechanism is found: 
````
throw new SaslSystemException(
            true, "Could not find a suitable SASL mechanism for the remote peer using the available credentials.");
````

A further note about this:
That case can also occur if the PLAIN mechanism is used and no username/password was given (so, not an exotic case). 
In general, I would prefer to throw a `ClientErrorException` in that case - also keeping the behaviour from before the vert.x update. WDYT?

(Unfortunately, to distinguish that case from the `SASL handshake failed due to an unrecoverable error` case, a match on the exception text is required. We could add a small integration test to be safe concerning future vert.x changes here.)

[2019-01-30T09:03:49Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
Giving it some more thought, I think that the `reconnect()` method in general should
* fail the attempt with a `ClientErrorException` (e.g. 401) in case of an `AuthenticationException`
* retry to connect in case of a `SaslSystemException` with *permanent* being `false`
* fail the attempt with a `ServerErrorException` (e.g. 503) in case of a `SaslSystemException` with *permanent* being `true`
* retry to connect in case of another `SaslException`

Regarding the case where no SASL mechanism is found, I agree that this should cause a the attempt being failed with a `ClientErrorException` and that we would need to match on the exception's description (for the time being). I think that proton-vertx should throw an `AuthenticationException` in this case instead of a `SaslSystemException`. I will create a PR for that. Thanks for spotting this :+1:

[2019-01-30T09:51:13Z | calohmn | review_comment]
I agree that it's better to throw `AuthenticationException` in `handleSaslInit`.

Regarding your list of cases above:
By "fail the attempt", do you mean fail the overall connection attempt, ignoring the `reconnectAttempts`, and doing no further connection attempts?

In the "retry to connect" cases, do you mean reconnect without taking the `reconnectAttempts` into account, potentially doing reconnect attempts indefinitely?
I think that wouldn't be a good idea - if the user has explicitly overridden the default of `reconnectAttempts=-1` (infinite), no further attempts should be done.

[2019-01-30T12:33:09Z | calohmn | review_comment]
I've updated the commit - now failing directly on `AuthenticationException` and permanent `SaslSystemException`.

[2019-01-30T13:59:10Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
can we add a comment here indicating the temporary nature of this check?

[2019-01-30T14:55:07Z | calohmn | review_comment]
ok, I've added a comment and additional checks in the unit tests for the exception message.

[2019-01-30T17:21:29Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
IMHO we should move this test to `org.eclipse.hono.tests.amqp.AmqpConnectionIT` because
* we already perform similar tests there as well and
* the AMQP adapter is a component under our own control which we can make sure behaves in the way we expect it to

[2019-01-30T17:21:57Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
`testConnectFailsWithClientErrorForTransientSaslSystemException`

[2019-01-30T20:51:42Z | calohmn | review_comment]
I've changed that.

[2019-01-30T20:54:54Z | calohmn | review_comment]
At first glance, I also thought so - seeing the already existing `testConnectFailsForWrongCredentials` method there.
But, this method is using the `ProtonClient` directly instead of the `HonoClient`. Of course this could be changed, but that would mean either having this one case (plus the new test method) where the `AmqpAdapterTestBase.connectToAdapter` method is not used in favour of a HonoClient-using method. Or it would mean adapting all invocations of `AmqpAdapterTestBase.connectToAdapter` - these are quite many.

So, I think this test doesn't fit that well there after all, since the focus in the `amqp` package is on the AMQP adapter.

Having a separate `HonoClientImplIT` in a separate package makes it clearer that this test is about `HonoClient` functionality. And it also offers the possibility of adding various other test methods for testing the `HonoClientImpl` there later on.
If the test class is already there, the hurdle of actually adding an integration test later on is lower.

[2019-01-31T10:57:36Z | calohmn | comment]
A note about the change here of not doing a `reconnect` any more in all cases:
I think we have to take care to not cause issues with this in cases where code relies on infinite `reconnect` attempts and where there is the "Authentication failed" SASL outcome being returned although that is wrong in that particular case (e.g. in a timeout scenario).
One possible issue concerning `HonoSaslAuthenticator` is described here: https://github.com/eclipse/hono/issues/1015#issuecomment-459111757.

[2019-02-01T14:50:03Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
I still don't like it. In particular, we are not verifying any specific behavior of Hono here, so I do not see why we should have an *integration test* for `HonoClientImpl`. FMPOV all of the client's expected behavior can easily be tested using unit tests (which you already do).
Anyway, I will merge it for the time being. Let's see how it evolves ...

[2019-02-01T14:52:13Z | sophokles73 | review:CHANGES_REQUESTED]
Please document the client's changed reconnect behavior in the release notes under API changes.

[2019-02-01T16:38:33Z | calohmn | comment]
I've added a note in the release notes.

[2019-02-04T18:16:36Z | calohmn | review_comment]
> FMPOV all of the client's expected behavior can easily be tested using unit tests

The thing here is that the client's behavior is also defined by the underlying vert.x-proton.
The plain unit test relies on mocks to mimic the behavior of vert.x proton and qpid. If that behavior changes with an update (e.g. throwing an `AuthenticationException` in `handleSaslInit`) the unit test possibly is still green. The integration test won't be in that case.

title: [#1289] Disable auto-accept for command receiver links
body:
This fixes #1289.

Adds a new `createReceiver` method in `HonoConnection` with an `autoAccept` param.
CommandConsumer classes use this to disable `autoAccept`.

(An alternative solution would have been to just set `receiver.setAutoAccept(false)` on the returned receiver, but letting the flag be set inside the `createReceiver` method *before* `receiver.open()` is called is the cleaner solution IMHO.)

title: Update and docker-wrap JMeter tests.
body:
Hi,

as I tried to execute the JMeter tests against my sample Hono installation on an AKS cluster they did not work as expected.

I mainly edited the RESTful calls to the device registry (JMeter scripts used outdated API) and upgraded the JMeter scripts that they are runnable with Apache JMeter 5.1.1 and MQTT XMeter 1.0.1. In addition to that I wrapped everything in a container that the current three load test bash scripts can be run from directly without having to worry about installation of JMeter and the plugins (XMeter and Hono). 

I used a dockerfile instead of the build style of fabric8io in pom, but included a link to this dockerfile so that fabric8io plugin will generate the load test image within a full Hono build as well.

Waiting for your questions, remarks and update requests!
Thanks,
Florian

body: not_available_in_source
comments:
[2019-01-21T08:10:18Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
For the *released* outcome this is the right choice. However, if the transfer results in the *modified* outcome, the 400 code is quite accurate FMPOV. Can you add another `else if` branch for the *modified* outcome?

[2019-01-21T09:51:14Z | calohmn | review_comment]
Looking at the [spec](http://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-modified) and for example this [qpid ticket](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/DISPATCH-366), I think we should look at the values of the _modified_ fields here:
````
delivery-failed	        count the transfer as an unsuccessful delivery attempt
undeliverable-here	prevent redelivery
````
So, if `undeliverable-here` is `true`, I think we should probably send back 400 `HTTP_BAD_REQUEST` (same as in `rejected` case). 
If `delivery-failed` is `true`, it looks to me as if we probably should return a status so that the client tries again - which would point to 503 `HTTP_UNAVAILABLE`. WDYT`?

[2019-01-21T12:41:07Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
I agree with using 503 for *delivery-failed* = `true`.
For *undeliverable-here* = `true` I can also imagine returning 404 to distinguish it from the case where the message itself is unprocessable (*rejected* case) and we return a 400 already.

title: Groups should not be assignable for non groupable permissions
body:
When granting permissions to a user or a role, it is always allowed to assign a group while, for some domain it doesn't make sense. For example the domain "broker" is not groupable hence the group field should not be assignable. Here is a first list of (currently) non groupable domains:
* Domain
* Account
* User
* Group
* Tag
* Role
* Access Info
* Access Token
* Credential
* Broker
* Device connection
* Device events
* Device lifecycle
* Device managements
* Job

The package names and versions shown in the packages view are the name inside the `.dp` package.

body: When entering expiration date for Credentials and Permissions in Users, years should be added as four digit number (YYYY) but Kapua accepts all dates from 0 - 199999. Testflow: 1. Login as kapua-sys 2. Go to Users, add or edit existing user (e.g. kapua-user1) 3. Select kapua-user1, go to Credentials and/or Permissions and set Expiration date with the year parameter > 9999. **If Expiration date is in range 0 - 199999, Kapua accepts it, although format is _YYYY_.** Screenshot (Entering Expriation date in wrong format): Browsers used: - Google Chrome (Version 63.0.3202.84 (Official Build) (64-bit)) - Safari (Version 11.0.2 (13604.3.5)) - Mozilla Firefox (57.0.1 (64-bit)) - Opera (Version 49.0.2725.64)

Although it's a border line case (of course no one would want to input a date with a year > 9999, but that could be true for years > 2100, actually), it's technically conforming to the format. title: Kapua GUI Moves Upwards if User Hits Bottom With Pop-up Windows
body:
Best way to describe this issue is through an example. Lets say user goes to Roles and tries to add (create) a new role (e.g. role1). title: Device management operations hide errors
body:
During a device management operation if the communication does not incur in TimeoutException or other communication-related errors but the device returns an error code while processing the message, no error code or error alert is returned to the caller of the device management operation.

So if you perform any operation in which the device does not respond 200 as responseCode the only way to see the device management operation result is to look at the DeviceEvent created.

It would be more appropriate that, if an error occurs, an appropriate exception si thrown to notify the caller.

body:
`sys_housekeeper` if your deployment is on mySQL with charset set to `utf8_unicode_ci`.

The field has a length of `255` and the charset `utf8_unicode_ci` uses 4 bytes per chars.

title: Lockout policy conflicts with Swagger UI
body:
Hi,

It is a very annoying and rare problem I have experienced, but I could not repeat until now. When I am using the Swagger UI and the Kapua WebConsole simultaneously, after switching from one to another I lose my authentication credentials, so I have to log in again. The problem is, that if I change the System Admin (kapua-sys) password, he could get locked out. It does not depend on whether the Lockout Service is enabled or not, or if it is how it is configured. The system admin gets locked out with the preset Lockout Service settings.

Note: The lockout happens instantly, you don't even have to type a wrong password...

Here is the test sequence:

1. Install Kapua and log in with _kapua-sys_
2. Create a child account ("c_account")
3. Enable infinite child users
4. **Disable Lockout service**
5. Create a new user of c_account (c_user, pass: new_password)
6. Grant him ALL permissions
7. **Change system admin password** (clicking change password in the top right corner)
[new pass: new_password]
8. Go to Swagger UI
9. Request authentication/user and log in with c_user/new_password (not with sys-admin)
10. Go back to web console (you will be dropped out after a few seconds)
11. Try to log in with kapua-sys/new_password
12. It will say that the account is locked contact System Administrator...

NOTE: I also observed some things which can be helpful
- As in my example the child account's user password and the system admin changed password was the same. (but I don't think that matters)
- The system admin has been locked out, however I still could use the child account's user
- The system admin was useless both in the web console and the Swagger UI
- The system admin lockout was resolved after a day passed from last login attempt (but I think that was just the default 10800 seconds of the Lockout Service)
- It **only** occured **when I changed the** system admin **password**
- Because of the long resolution time I couldn't run more experiment on this matter
- I cannot change the Kapua settings until I create a child account (the settings are grey)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26169252/37404990-ba40bf5a-2793-11e8-91cd-e92f455527eb.png)
- After I have a child account I switch to that account, go to settings, change back to kapua-sys, refresh, and THEN I can change the settings.

It was extremely frustrating the first time and now that I can recreate it and have fears using the web console and the Swagger UI simultaneously because of that. Thank you for your help.

Hi @Sealdolphin,

Thanks for the report. I'm going to investigate on this.

However, about the last two points: it's actually by design that a user cannot change its own Settings, but rather a user from the parent account should be the one entitled to change them via the Child Accounts --> Settings view. This means that you cannot change settings for the root account, but since it's meant to be only a "container" for children accounts you shouldn't need to change them anyway. All the settings should stay disabled since that page is meant as a review only, so it's actually an issue if you manage to somehow "unlock" them. I'll investigate on this as well.

title: service events - error during locator initialization
body:
#### Description 
The error occurs during the startup phase of the REST API. The log reports the following:

> Caused by: com.google.inject.ProvisionException: Unable to provision, see the following errors:
>  
> 1) Error injecting constructor, java.lang.NullPointerException
>   at org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceImpl.<init>(UserServiceImpl.java:72)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceImpl
>   at org.eclipse.kapua.locator.guice.KapuaModule.configure(KapuaModule.java:121)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.UserService
>     for field at org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceModule.userService(UserServiceModule.java:27)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceModule
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.commons.core.ServiceModule annotated with @com.

The error is due  to the fact that the list of service modules are retrieved (and instantiated) before completing the initialization of the locator (for the Guice implementation). The retrieve of the service modules triggers the initialization of some service implementations which in turn try to access the locator.

#### Expected behavior
Objects managed by the Kapua locator do not have to be created before the locator itself is completely initialized (for the Guice implementation). The solution is to defer the instantiation of any object until the locator is fully initialized.

title: Device Management - Missing `ConnectionStatus` check
body:

we are currently missing a check on the `DeviceConnection.getStatus()` attribute.
When performing a device management operation we should check that the `Device` has a `DeviceConnection` and that this `DeviceConnection` has a `status` which is `CONNECTED`. 

Without this check any operation performed by `Job`s or REST API device management will end up in a operation executed which will always timeout.

Regards,

body:

in some device management services we lost the managing of the `KuraResponseCode` when parsing the response from the device. 

If the response is `200` everything is fine, while on error not parsing this response code causes `NullPointerException` in the subsequent code.

Affected device management are:

DeviceAssetManagementService
DeviceBundleManagementService
DeviceConfigManagementService
DevicePackageManagementService
DeviceSnapshotManagementService

Regards, 

_Alberto_

Actually, after trying to find a solution I discovered that the issue was caused from the `throw`ing of the `Exception` of the response code was not `200`. title: Filtering Through Kapa Not "Unified"
body:
For now, filtering is not "unified". For example, some of the fields require that searched string is exaclty the same as "target" string (e.g. Custom Attributes fields in Device filter), others require that a character entered is anywhere in the "target" string (e.g. Job name). Is this OK, or not? What is the proper filter operation? 

**_Connections:_**
**- Connection CLiend ID:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Cliend ID
**- Conncetion Client IP:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Connection Client IP

**_Devices:_** 
**- Device Client ID:** Finds a match if string of characters matches beginning of the target string (if a device's ID is "device123", Kapua will not find it, if users enters "evi" or "123", but will find if entered "d", "dev" or "devic")
**- Device Display Name:** Finds a match if string of characters matches beginning of the target string (if a device's Display Name is "device123", Kapua will not find it, if users enters "evi" or "123", but will find if entered "d", "dev" or "devic")
**- Serial Number:** / non-testable
**- IoT Framework Version:** String has to be complete match (e.g. KURA_3.1.1, not even "K" or "KURA" will suffice, user has to enter "KURA_3.1.1" into search field)
**- Applications:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Applications field
**- Custom Attribute No. 1:** String has to be a complete match (e.g. if attribute is "device123", user has to enter "device123", "dev", "123", device12" will not work)
**- Custon Attribute No. 2:** String has to be a complete match (e.g. if attribute is "device123", user has to enter "device123", "dev", "123", device12" will not work)

**_Jobs:_**
**- Job Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any job name

**_Tags:_**
**- Tag Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any tag name

**_Users:_**
**- Username field:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any username

**_Roles:_**
**- Role Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any role name

**_Access Groups:_**
**- Access Group Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any group name

**_Child Accounts:_**
**- Account Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any account name
**- Account Organization Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any organization name
**- Account Email:** Finds match if character or string entered appears any email name

title: Console - Data view metric filtering not working properly
body:
Looking at the code of the GwtDataServiceImpl it seems that the filtering by headers is not properly working.

It shows the only selected metric, but It does not add the datastore predicate (it should use the `metricPredicate`)  to the query.

[GwtDataServiceImpl:450](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/server/GwtDataServiceImpl.java#L450): header are passed and never added to the query

[GwtDataServiceImpl:469](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/server/GwtDataServiceImpl.java#L469):  header are passed and never added to the query again.

[KapuaGwtDataModelConverter:73](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/shared/util/KapuaGwtDataModelConverter.java#L73): header are used to extract specific metric from the message payload, but it could be that one of the extracted messages hasn't the requested metric.

The result is that you'll end up with empty cell in the result table, while the correct behaviour should be that the messages should be skipped from the results.

title: Kapua Reporting Locked User Because Of Password Expired Date
body: If we create a user with expired password, Kapua reports (when we are trying to login as this use) that "User has been locked. Contact your account administrator..." although PASSWORD credential is not really locked and therefore user is not actually locked. I propose three solutions: 1) If user sets Expiration Date for a Credential in the past, _Status_ (the "key" icon) or the _Lock Status_ should turn red. After the user would unlock the credential, Expiration Date would be deleted (set to null, N/A). 2) Second option is to change the error message from "User has been locked..." to "User's PASSWORD hass expired. Contact your account administrator." This introduces some security "risks" as potential attacker then knows that password has expired and user has not been actually locekd. 3) Changing the Kapua message to "User has been locked or password has expired. Contact you account administrator." or something similar. Maybe other ideas/suggestions? **Testflow:** 1) Login as kapua-sys 2) Go to Users, create a user (e.g. kapua-user0) 3) Set Expiration date for kapua-user0 password for a time and date in past 4) Logout as kapua-sys and try to login as kapua-user0 **Observe the error message from Kapua.** **Expected behavior** If user sets an Expiration Date for Password (or API_KEY) in the past, the lock symbol should turn red or error message should be changed when trying to login with user whos password has expired. **Screenshot No. 1 (Setting an expired password for a user):** ![screen shot 2018-07-03 at 09 23 26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15121999/42206295-008242da-7ea7-11e8-8a5a-6edfee297728.png) **Screenshot No. 2 ("User locked" error message, although only user's password is expired):** **Version of Kapua** 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT **Type of deployment** [ ] Local Vagrant deployment [x] Docker [ ] Openshift (in its variants) [ ] Others **Main component affected** [x] Console [ ] REST API [ ] Message Broker [ ] - Others Browsers used: - Google Chrome (Version 67.0.3396.99 (Official Build) (64-bit)) - Safari (Version 11.1 (13604.3.5)) - Mozilla Firefox (61.0 (64-bit)) - Opera (Version 54.0.2952.41)

title: Unable to unmarshal KapuaListResult objects
body:
**Describe the bug**
Using `XmlUtil.unmarshalJson()` to unmarshal a JSON string representing a `KapuaListResult` throws an exception:

```
javax.xml.bind.UnmarshalException: Line -1, Col: -1.
    Error message: 
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].
Internal Exception: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
    Linked exception message:
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].
Internal Exception: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
- with linked exception:
[Exception [EclipseLink-6065] (Eclipse Persistence Services - 2.6.3.v20160428-59c81c5): org.eclipse.persistence.exceptions.QueryException
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].
Internal Exception: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException]
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Using REST API, get a JSON representing a `KapuaListResult` object (e.g. GET /users)
2. Try to unmarshal such JSON via `XmlUtil.unmarshalJson()`

**Expected behavior**
The JSON is correctly unmarshalled to the desired object

**Version of Kapua**
1.0.0-M7

**Type of deployment**
[x] Local Vagrant deployment
[x] Docker
[x] Openshift (in its variants) 
[x] Others

_Note: since this is strictly a code issue, it always appears regardless of the deployment_

**Main component affected**
Test
REST API

**Additional context**
The exception is thrown because the `getItems()` method of KapuaListResult returns an unmodifiable collection; however this unmodifiable list makes little sense, since you can add and remove items from them using various methods on KapuaListResult.

title: Kapua Reports Locking User After n+1 Attempt
body:
If user sets lockoutPolicy.maxFailures to e.g. 4, Kapua will report that user is locked after the fifth attempt and not after fourth (see screenshots).

**Testflow:**

4. Try to login 4 times with wrong password
**After the fourth attempt try to login again with wrong password and observe how Kapua just now reports that user has been locked.**

**Expected behavior**
Kapua should report that user has been locked after fourth attempt ant not after fifth.

[2019-02-07T09:22:05Z | Coduz | comment]
Hi Leo,

just take a closer look to this. 

I think that the current behaviour is more correct. 

If I have 4 attempts available and I fail 4 times, the 4th time the actual error is that the credentials are wrong. While the 5th time the user's credential are actually locked.

Why you think it should be returned on the 4th attempt? 

Regards, 

_Alberto_

[2019-02-11T06:20:59Z | LeoNerdoG | comment]
Hi Alberto,
If we look at the setting in Child Accounts -> Account Settings -> CredentialService there is setting called "lockoutPolicy.maxFailures" and the description of this setting is: "Number of consecutive login failures before the user gets locked. Valid if lockout policy is enabled."

This description is the reason I opened this issue. There is a certain similarity with entering PIN number when you go to ATM. You get 3 shots at entering the right PIN. If you miss three times, you do not get another shot, because you have already used all the tries and ATM would give you error message after the forth try, even if it is the right combination. 

It is similar here - after third try user does not get the message that he is locked out, but rather that enterd password is not correct. He then gets another try and if he enters right password this time, it is no use - Kapua would throw "locked out" error message in any case. 

So I see two different solutions now - either we throw "user locked" error message after 3rd try (if "lockoutPolicy.maxFailures" is set to 3 - as it is logical to inform user that he is locked after the las valid attempt) or we change the description of the setting to be more informational. 

Leonardo

I have verified that this issue ahs been resolved.

title: Database schema: act_account table / parent_account_path length issue
body:
There is a possible inconsistency in the **act_account** table, specifically the **parent_account_path** field.
The current create script (**act_account_create.sql**) defines this field as a **VARCHAR(64)**. Given that there is no limit to the depth of sub-account creation this seems to be too short.
Specifically, this length is exceeded even with an account tree 3 levels deep. An example is as follows.
When creating 3 account levels, the resulting parent path is
'\1/-4796103609285693743/-4305601355848753009/-1017280879925618445'
Please note that this string is 65 characters long and as such it causes an JdbcSQLException.
As it looks it seems that this inconsistency was introduced when the old (and shorter) IDs were replaced with the new BigInteger (far longer) IDs.

title: Service events - uncorrect ServiceEvent stack handling on nested calls
body:
The ServiceEvent bean stack is not correctly managed by the ServiceEventScope. The end method cleans the stack regardless if there is more than one object in the stack.
So if a main event raises a child event, the end call of the child event will clean the ServiceEvent stack leading the end call of the main event to throw a KapuaRuntimeException.

To fix it the end call should check for the stack size before cleaning it from the ThreadContext.

title: Database schema: General issue with IDs
body:
There is a general issue regarding the ID fields in the database.
The table creation scripts define all IDs as BIGINT(21) UNSIGNED (i.e. **scope_id    BIGINT(21)  UNSIGNED NOT NULL**).
Nevertheless it is possible to create an ID from a negative integer (i.e. **new KapuaEid(BigInteger.valueOf(-1))**) and the database will not complain. Searching the database with such ID is also successful.
This is somewhat counter-intuitive, as the field definition seems to imply that IDs with negative values should be rejected by the database.

After some investigation I think I found the root cause. It's not about downloading Jetty, but the startup of Jetty itself is failing:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Cannot read file: modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_191.mod
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.registerModule(Modules.java:202)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:355)

Usage: java -jar $JETTY_HOME/start.jar [options] [properties] [configs]
       java -jar $JETTY_HOME/start.jar --help  # for more information
```

```
ln -s /opt/jetty/modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_181.mod /opt/jetty/modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_191.mod
```
since `alpn-1.8.0_181.mod` is the latest ALPN module in Jetty.

title: Service event loader overrides the service event address with the module configured address
body:
**Describe the bug**
The current service event implementation allows to set a different address to each service ([ServiceEventClientConfiguration](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/develop/commons/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/commons/event/ServiceEventClientConfiguration.java)), but the service event loader ([ServiceEventModule](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/develop/commons/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/commons/event/ServiceEventModule.java)) uses the module address ([ServiceEventModuleConfiguration](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/develop/commons/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/commons/event/ServiceEventModuleConfiguration.java#L18)) to bind the listening/raising service to the correct address.
This bug doesn't allow to specify a different listening/raising address for the services contained in the same module.

Hi all, 

this is caused by the fact that CRON does not directly aware of the timezone. To avoid any problem with the server timezone (which is often depending on the underlying OS) I've set all CRON expression created to be based on UTC. 

The solution proposed by Aleksandra remove this forcing to UTC, but if (if I'm correct) make thing work only when the timezone of the browser is matching the timezone of the server, and would definitely not work with users from different timezones. 

i.e.:
User A creates a CRON with his timezone (+2:00 for example) like:
Starts: 10:00
End: 12:00
CRON: `0 0 12 * * ?`

User B views/edits the trigger from another timezone (+5:00 for example) and sees
Starts: 13:00
End: 15:00
CRON: `0 0 12 * * ?` <-- same problem, since CRON does not have any link to the timezone from which is created.

Moreover, if the trigger is created/retrieved/managed from the REST API we will not have any info about the User's timezone from the browser.

Let me know what you think.

As an alternative solution I would try to make clear that CRON is in UTC.

Regards,

_Alberto_

title: Wrong Error Messages When user Does Not Have Proper Permissions
body:
This was originally planned to be part of solution for issue #1796 and PR that will fix it, but for fixing and testing reasons has been split to a new issue.
For now, Kapua's error messages when permissions are not sufficient is for example: "Device edit failed: User does not have permissions to perfrom this action. Missing permissions: device:write:xxxx:xxxxx".
The issue here is the first part, "Device edit failed", which is unnecessary, as user can persume that edit has failed, due to the error shown. 
Bellow there is list of scenarios where this happens. 

1. If user has no more Device:Delete permissions and tries to delete a device (Screenshot No. 1)
2. If user no longer has Device:Write permissions and tries to edit a device (Screenshot No. 2)
3. if user no longer has Device_management:Execute permission and tries to execute a command or start/stop a bundle (Screenshot No. 3)
4. If user no longer has Device_management:Write permission and tries to upload a Snapshot (Screenshot No. 4)
5. If user no longer has Device_Management:Write permission and tries to change device's configuration; For now, Kapua reacts as new changes are saved/discarded (flash, loading screen, refresh), but changes are not actually saved. It should be done as in Assets: if user does not have permissions any more and clicks anything, everything disables. (Screenshot No. 5)
6. If user no longer has Job:Delete permission and tries to delete a job Step (Screenshot No. 6)
7. If user no longer has Job:Delete permission and tries to delete a job (Screenshot No. 7)
8. If user no longer has Job:Execute permission and tries to start or restart a job (Screenshot No. 8)
9. If user no longer has Job:Delete permissions and tries to delete a Target (Screenshot No. 9)
10. If user no longer has Schedule:Delete permission and tries to delete a Schedule (Screenshot No. 10)
11. if user no longer has Tag:Delete permission and wants to delete a tag. Also here are two identical errors - this should be fixed also (Screenshot No. 11)
12. If user no longer has Credential:Delete permission and wants to delete a credential (Screenshot No. 12)
13. If user no longer has Credential:Write permission and wants to edit a credential (Screenshot No. 13)
14. If user no longer has Credential:Write permission and wants to unlock a credential (Screenshot No. 4)
15. If user no longer has Access_info:delete permission and wants to delete a role in users (Screenshot No. 15)
16. If user no longer has Access_info:write permission and wants to add a role to users (Screenshot No. 16)
17. If user no longer has Access_info:delete permission and wants to delete a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 17)
18. If user no longer has Access_info:write permission and wants to add a permission - here Kapua  returns wrong error ("Role assigning failed"), although we are assigning a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 18)
19. If user no longer has Domain:read permission and wants to add a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 19)

title: Telemetry message published through Streams Api has a wrong clientId stored
body:
**Describe the bug**
Telemetry message published through Streams Api has a wrong clientId stored.
The clientId stored is coming from the internal Mqtt connection pool.  

**To Reproduce**
Publish message using Streams Api

**Expected behavior**
curl http://127.0.0.1:9200/index/message/_search?pretty should return:
~~~~
...
"sent_on" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z",
"body" : null,
"captured_on" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z",
"client_id" : "client-id-set",
"timestamp" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z"
...

instead of

"sent_on" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z",

title: Add permission forward-ability
body:
Hi all,

we need to implement the feature of "forward-ability" of the permissions. 
This means that an account A with a child account B must be able to manage resources of the account B.

The logic would be that a user A of the account A that has per permission A has the same permission on the account B, as if user A has both A and B permission. 

To allow restriction of this behaviour a new flag on the permission will tell if the permission is forward-able or not. 

The current situation is that `kapua-sys` account can manage child account because it has `*:*:*:*` permission. But if a child account A of `kapua-sys` has another child account B, the A account will only be able to delete the account and not to create users/roles/etc on the account B.

Regards, 

_Alberto_

We have a bug that is also a security problem. 
When we add a new permission we do not check the `targetScopeId` set.

If not, any user with `role:manage` or `access-info:manage` can add permission in other accounts.

title: Liquibase script refactoring
body:
Hi all, 

while working on #583 I discovered something odd on Liquibase.
By default it uses absolute path name as a key to know if a file has been executed already or not. 
This means that If the same script is executed from a different directory Liquibase wouldn't be able to recognize that is has already been executed and try to execute it again.

There is a property to override this called `logicalFilePath`, which value is used as a key instead of the absolute path. This property must be added to all file with changeset to execute. 
I was not able to add it to the plan SQL file and I suspect that we have to convert them to XML|YAML|JSON format to be able to specify that property. 

BTW the current layout works fine for tests and demo deployment. It could be a problem in case of more complex usage.

Regards,

_Alberto_


EDIT: 
Documentation page of this property: http://www.liquibase.org/documentation/databasechangelog.html
