title: Random QA tests failures
body:
Hi all,

after merging #583 some random test failures started to appear more frequently. We had already some random failures on qa tests but they were occasional.

After digging a bit I discovered that is a problem related to how Liquibase script are loaded and the fact that the Kapua Liquibase Client  is run from many different places concurrently. 

The KapuaLiquibaseClient was implemented to copy resources from the jar to a tmp directory and then execute it immediately. With the improvement contained on #583  all scripts gets copied and then executed. 

For the fact that KapuaLiquibaseClient is run from different places it can happen that the copied resources gets overwritten by another KapuaLiquibaseClient is executing them, with even more chance that now that apply of Liquibase scripts takes a bit longer.

I'll fix this making execution of Liquibase script `synchronized` as a simple patch.

Regards,

_Alberto_

[2017-06-26T14:25:52Z | riccardomodanese | comment]
The log line you noticed is not an issue at all. Based on our data schema, version conflicts may occur when the same entity is published at high frequency until ES does its indexing refresh.
Or if similar messages, not already indexed, are published to different broker instances more or less at the same time. So we have a refresh_time window in which similar log lines can be noticed for every message that contains new informations (channel, client or metrics) not alredy indexed.
Since is not an issue and there is no way to avoid this condition whithout impacting in the performance, I wasn't considering that as an issue, but the missed storing for the subsequent messages.
In our test we did messages count and that count confirmed that no message lost were occurred.
So may be that we had that issue in the past and now it is fixed as result of other datastore fixes.

[2017-06-26T14:56:37Z | ctron | comment]

[2017-06-27T12:39:23Z | ctron | comment]
4 msg/s ... 250ms delay ... Which should be handles easily. However my setup did have more than 2 GB or RAM. It was more like 16GB of RAM which IMHO should be more than enough for handling thousands of messages per second.

[2017-06-27T13:42:22Z | riccardomodanese | comment]
@ctron my intention wasn't to open a discussion about which could be an agressive rate or not without having defined a stress target platform and a stress test load. And honestly, I'm assuming this issue is not related to the load in the system.

I was just trying to reproduce the issue so going close to your target environment and your publishing rate.

[2017-06-27T14:43:15Z | riccardomodanese | comment]
mmm it's coming another idea in my mind... I'm wondering if could be related to the bind/unbind of the KapuaSecurityContext in the ThreadLocal made by Camel workers.

title: Custom Date Range Problem
body:
When trying to set custom date range for presenting data I found some errors: 

**1)** It is possible to enter negative year.
**2)** Dates till 31.12.1936 are automatically added 100 years (e.g. 1.1.1900 = 1.1.2000, 12.10.1936 = 12.10.2036...).
**3)** Dates from 10.10.2037 are mapped 100 years earlier (e.g. 1.10.2037 = 1.10.1937, 12.11.2042 = 12.11.1942...).
**4)** All dates from 0 - 18xx are mapped to 19xx (e.g. 1810 = 1910, 1712 = 1912...).
comments:
[2018-01-25T11:36:07Z | lorthirk | comment]
This is due to the time format used in the custom date range dialog. Since it's in a M/d/yy (single-digit month/single digit day/two digit year, e.g. 01/25/18 for January 25th, 2018) it gets wrongly parsed to a Date object by `SimpleDateFormat`. According to the SimpleDateFormat JavaDoc:

> For parsing with the abbreviated year pattern ("y" or "yy"), SimpleDateFormat must interpret the abbreviated year relative to some century. It does this by adjusting dates to be within 80 years before and 20 years after the time the SimpleDateFormat instance is created. For example, using a pattern of "MM/dd/yy" and a SimpleDateFormat instance created on Jan 1, 1997, the string "01/11/12" would be interpreted as Jan 11, 2012 while the string "05/04/64" would be interpreted as May 4, 1964. During parsing, only strings consisting of exactly two digits, as defined by Character.isDigit(char), will be parsed into the default century. Any other numeric string, such as a one digit string, a three or more digit string, or a two digit string that isn't all digits (for example, "-1"), is interpreted literally. So "01/02/3" or "01/02/003" are parsed, using the same pattern, as Jan 2, 3 AD. Likewise, "01/02/-3" is parsed as Jan 2, 4 BC.

I propose to use a more explicit format for the year, using yyyy, and more in general to use the following format for the date and time, already used in Kapua in other sections: `dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm`

@stefanomorson what do you think?

[2018-01-25T13:08:51Z | lorthirk | comment]
Should be fixed in [fix-data_date_interval_format](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/tree/fix-data_date_interval_format)

[2018-01-26T08:32:05Z | LeoNerdoG | comment]

title: Stop Endpoint Info fallback if there are Endpoints specified in scope
body:
This PR changes the way `EndpointInfoServiceImpl` uses the fallback mechanism, reflecting on parent accounts only if the current one has no entries.

**Related Issue**
N/A

**Description of the solution adopted**
Before this one, when an Endpoint wasn't found in an account, the query was repeated for parent account, scaling up the hierarchy up to the root. This meant that a query could return no entries for a specific filter, even if there were endpoints available that didn't match the filter, and scale up the hierarchy.

Now, before activating the fallback mechanism, an additional query is performed to be sure that the current account contains no endpoints at all.

title: Fixed OptimisticLockExeption handling in DeviceEventServiceImpl
body:
This PR fixes the handling of concurrent modification error while updating the `Device.lastEvent` field. 

**Related Issue**
This PR integrates changes made on PR #2729 and completely fixes #2714 

**Description of the solution adopted**
Fixed the Exception caught while updating this field.

JPA `OptimisticLockException` is always wrapped from `KapuaOptimisticLockException` when thrown by a Service, so `KapuaOptimisticLockException` is the correct `Exception` to catch and handle.

_None_

Added some informations about the retry processing.

title: Job Targets CSV Export and Jobs Registry readonly REST API
body:
This PR introduces two features:

- A console user can now export Targets for a given Job to a CSV file
- Readonly REST APIs are now available to query all Jobs related informations. The following endpoints are now available:
  - Jobs:
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/_query`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/_count`
  - Targets:
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/targets`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/targets/{targetId}`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/targets/{targetId}/executions`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/targets/_query`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/targets/_count`
  - Executions:
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions/{executionId}`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions/{executionId}/targets`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions/_query`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/executions/_count`
  - Triggers:
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/triggers`
    - `GET {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/triggers/{triggerId}`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/triggers/_query`
    - `POST {scopeId}/jobs/{jobId}/triggers/_count`

**Related Issue**
No related issues

title: Fix KapuaNamedEntity name validation
body:
This PR fixes the validation on `KapuaNamedEntity`es.

The validation of the `name` field for some entities had thw wrong check on the UI and the wrong/none validation on the backend.

**Related Issue**
This PR also fixes #2709 , #2710 

**Description of the solution adopted**
Created a new utility method in `ArgumentValidator` class that validates the value provided supposing it is a `KapuaNamedEntity` name.

Checks for:

- not null
- min length and max langth (provided)
- That contains only alphanumerics, dash, underscore and whitespaces

**Screenshots**
_None_

**Any side note on the changes made**
Removed some unused code.
Refactored `ArgumentValidator. lengthRange(...)` with was requiring `Long` type for max and min length that made no sense.

title: Move CORS filter to Shiro
body:
This PR moves the `CORSResponseFilter` from the Jersey logic to the Shiro logic. This is because when a request fails with `401 Unauthorized` error code, Shiro stops the request processing before reaching Jersey and the CORS filter and returns a response without the needed headers. The browser will then complain because it receives a response without such headers.

**Related Issue**
No related issue

**Description of the solution adopted**
`CORSResponseFilter` inherits now from Shiro `OncePerRequestFilter` and is added in the chain before `KapuaTokenAuthenticationFilter`

title: Liquibase Client improvements
body:
This PR improves the LiquibaseClient to allow fix to TIMESTAMP columns on MariaDB and MySQL.
See  https://liquibase.jira.com/browse/CORE-1958

**Related Issue**
_None_

**Description of the solution adopted**
Added scripts to modify columns to add the subsecond part.
This script are run based on the version of Liquibase module. If after `3.3.3` the script will be executed. If executed prior to that version, the script will modify the columns without the subsecond part again. This fix can be also forced with an additional parameter.

**Screenshots**
_None_

**Any side note on the changes made**
Silenced the Liquibase Client log.
Added a utility class `SemanticVersion` to simplify handling of the component versions.

title: Memory leak and concurrency issue in 'EventHandlerServlet'
body:
IMHO there is a huge memory leak and beside that a concurrency issue in the newly added `EventHandlerServlet`.

There is only a single queue for buffering events. This queue is unbounded and if no web session reads those events, then the queue will fill up until all memory is used up.

Beside that events which have been sent to one user won't be sent to others.
comments:
[2017-01-12T11:44:42Z | amitjoy | comment]
Yes, it has been kept unbounded intentionally. The events fired by WireEmitter instances are maintained here. There also exists consumer threads which consumes the data from this queue. So, we can make sure that for every data produced by the queue, there will be enough number of consumers to consume this data at the same time. There cannot be data producers without consumers or vice versa. And that's why the queue is unbounded.

[2017-01-12T13:48:44Z | ctron | comment]
The only consumer of this queue is the `doGet` method of the servlet.

So when Wire applications are running (in the background) they are producing events. Filling up the queue. So as long as no one keeps a Web UI open, Kura will OOM at some point. Is that the intention?

Beside that only one Web UI session will receive events. So the Web UI may only be used by a single user. Is that also intentionally.

[2017-01-12T14:07:31Z | amitjoy | comment]
The size of the `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` is unbounded and if producers are producing values faster than the consumers, it can indeed end up with OOM. It is definitely better to switch to bounded blocking queues to prevent OOM. Good catch 👍.

[2017-01-12T14:07:58Z | amitjoy | comment]
I will make the necessary changes.

Found in Kura 2.0.2. Not verified in Kura 2.1.0.

Typically passwords have ``Password`` type and they are base64 encoded in the dowloaded snapshot.
For example (password is "admin"):

```
<esf:configuration pid="org.eclipse.kura.web.Console">
    <esf:properties>
        <esf:property type="Password" name="console.password.value" encrypted="true" array="false">
            <esf:value>YWRtaW4=</esf:value>
        </esf:property>
    </esf:properties>
</esf:configuration>
```

The PPP password is different. It's a ``String`` (not a Password) and not base64 encoded.

```
<esf:property type="String" name="net.interface.ppp0.config.password" encrypted="false" array="false">
    <esf:value>password</esf:value>
</esf:property>
```

Not a big deal since the password is likely stored in clean in the ppp pap/chap scripts...

Let's say you have a configuration snapshot from a golden sample that you want to use it, as snapshot_0.xml,  to seed the initial configuration of like gateways.

## Cellular modem

- /opt/eurotech/esf/data/kuranet.conf
- /etc/ppp/peers/LE910_2-1
- /etc/ppp/scripts/chat_LE910_2-1
- /etc/ppp/scripts/disconnect_LE910_2-1
- /etc/ppp/chap-secrets
- /etc/ppp/pap-secrets

and create the ppp0 softlink:

```
ln -s /etc/ppp/peers/LE910_2-1.5 ppp0
```

## Other interfaces
- /etc/dhcpd-eth0.conf
- /etc/dhcpd-wlan0.conf
- /etc/hostapd-wlan0.conf
- /etc/wpa_supplicant-wlan0.conf
- /etc/network/interfaces

## DNS
- /etc/bind/named.conf

## Firewall
- /etc/sysconfig/iptables
- /etc/init.d/firewall_cust  (where needed)

This seems like a deadlock situation to me which is in the end "resolved" by running into a timeout. Maybe not properly cleaning up by that.

The `CamelCloudClient` is unsubscribing from topics and for this executing a call on the `CamelContext` inside a thread the executor of the `cloudClientExecutor` executor service. Which belongs to the `CamelContext`.

The other thread is the service itself, calling into the `CamelContext`, closing it, which is then closing all services, the executor service being one of those services, since it is shut down by using `shutdown`, waiting for all tasks (including the unsubscribe from above) to complete.

I think it should be sufficient to not use an executor service from Camel, but to simply maintain a plain `ExecutorService` from `newSingleThreadExecutor()`, disposing it during the `release` call.

title: [Wires] Wires DataType lacks the KuraPayload float type
body:
Wires DataType only supports double precision floating point numbers (why?).
The single precision floating point type of a KuraPayload cannot be removed for backward compatibility reasons.

* Add the float type to DataType or
* Document that metrics of type float received by a WirePublisher will be converted to a float DataType when converting the KuraPayload to a WireRecord
comments:
[2017-04-04T17:56:07Z | MMaiero | comment]
The official HSQLDB documentation states (http://hsqldb.org/doc/1.8/guide/ch09.html):

> The recommended Java mapping for the JDBC datatype FLOAT is as a Java type "double". Because of the potential confusion it is recommended that DOUBLE is used instead of FLOAT.

[2017-04-04T21:24:52Z | amitjoy | comment]
Single precision floating point doesn't provide large degree of precision and to retain accuracy in performing precise calculations, wires didn't include `floats`.

The idea was to include primitive types (except `floats`) to be used as the datatypes in wires. And keeping this in mind, the existent datatypes were included. Previously while designing, I was not aware of the backward compatibility issues of `floats` in `KuraPayload`. You are right, it should be introduced.

title: [Kura 3.0.0 QA] Configuration service: mixing configurable services with factory components
body:
I will describe 2 scenarios that may occur when I want to use ExamplePublisher with Kura 3.0.0. Both show some issue.

Scenario 1:
New Kura installation.
Install example publisher bundle from OSGi console (install file:///.../ org.eclipse.kura.example.publisher-1.0.100.jar). Don't start the bundle, yet. Try to add a new service (+). It's not listed. Start the bundle (e.g. start 95). Try to add it again and now it's listed as a factory component. Don't add it, anyway. Stop and/or uninstall the bundle. Make sure it's not listed in OSGi anymore (`ss` doesn't list it). Try to add the service now – it's still listed as a factory component. It can be added and configured. Configuration service doesn't handle bundle (and factory component, in this case) unregistration.

Scenario 2:
New Kura installation.
Add the old publisher from Amazon and also uninstall it after it publishes a few messages.
Then add example publisher bundle from the jar, available with the build. It's the one that should be started after you create an instance using a factory. But a configuration for the component already exists in the latest snapshot. It will start publishing when you click '+' to add a new service. But you don't have to complete the form – clicking '+' is enough. The trouble is that this one is not configured properly – has no cloud service reference and no app.id.
If you add the new instance, you will now have 2.

Kura 3.0.0 b31 on RPi3

title: [Wires] Deleting a Timer instance might stop all other Timers
body:
In the current implementation the `finalize()` method of the Timer component stops the Quartz scheduler instance shared across all Timers. If a Timer is garbage collected while other instances of this component are running they will stop ticking.
A possible solution could be keeping a static counter of the active timer instances and shutdown the scheduler when the last Timer instance is deactivated.
comments:
[2017-06-26T17:32:33Z | cdealti | comment]
@nicolatimeus or wrap Quartz in an lazy OSGi service that would be activated on the first Timer using it and deactivated when there are no more Timers.

[2017-06-26T17:40:23Z | amitjoy | comment]
A timer will not be garbage collected since the shared scheduler instance will be active in all the other timer references. If the Quartz instance could have been declared with soft or weak reference, it could have been collected by the GC but currently it is a strong reference. 

I like the idea of wrapping quartz as an OSGi service that could be really helpful in managing dependencies amongst other service components.

[2017-06-27T10:16:50Z | nicolatimeus | comment]
I've tried the approach of crating a lazy OSGi service that wraps the scheduler. It works but the scheduler service will never be deactivated by the framework even if there are no references to it, causing a resource leak.

This is caused by the fact that the Equinox DS implementation never deactivates lazy components by default (see [here](https://wiki.eclipse.org/Equinox/RuntimeOptions#System_properties_of_bundle_org.eclipse.equinox.ds)).

I've also tried to specify the `-Dequinox.scr.dontDisposeInstances=false` runtime option to change this policy, but this caused the Timer to stop working. (the scheduler service is unexpectedly unbound by the framework with the timer component being still active, I didn't investigate the cause of this).

title: connect.retry-interval=0 causes DataService activation failure
body:
Setting the `connect.retry-interval` to 0 seems to work until reboot.
After a reboot, the DataService component starts continuously to try to activate, determining the impossibility to use the default cloud service and all the related stack.
I believe the root cause is related to the `IllegalArgumentException` thrown by the [scheduleAtFixedRate](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/ScheduledExecutorService.html#scheduleAtFixedRate(java.lang.Runnable,%20long,%20long,%20java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit)) .

This determines that the `startConnectionMonitorTask` method throws that runtime exception till going up in the stack-trace at the `activate` level. This causes the component to continuously be restarted by the framework.

I've tested the same behaviour in Kura 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT and Kura 3.0.0. I've not done tests for previous versions of Kura.

title: [Artemis] MQTT clients fail to reconnect after the broker is restarted
body:
Stopping and restarting embedded Artemis broker instances might cause a previously connected client to fail to reconnect.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Enable the **Simple Artemis MQTT Broker** or the **ActiveMQ Artemis Broker**.
2. Connect a Kura Cloud Service instance to the broker.
3. Stop and restart the broker.
4. Try to reconnect the client.

After repeating steps 3 and 4 a couple of times the cloud service might fail to reconnect.
The Kura log reports this exception:
```
org.eclipse.kura.KuraConnectException: "Connection failed. Cannot connect"
	at org.eclipse.kura.core.data.transport.mqtt.MqttDataTransport.connect(MqttDataTransport.java:333)
	at org.eclipse.kura.core.data.DataServiceImpl$2.run(DataServiceImpl.java:609)
	at java.util.concurrent.Executors$RunnableAdapter.call(Executors.java:511)
	at java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.runAndReset(FutureTask.java:308)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.access$301(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:180)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.run(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:294)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1142)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:617)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
Caused by: Invalid client ID (2)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.ExceptionHelper.createMqttException(ExceptionHelper.java:31)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.ClientState.notifyReceivedAck(ClientState.java:990)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.CommsReceiver.run(CommsReceiver.java:118)
	... 1 more
```
The client Id of the CloudService is valid since it has been previously accepted by the broker.
This seems to be caused by the fact that in the [MQTTConnectionManager](https://github.com/apache/activemq-artemis/blob/c8982d775b55849836ae20739a9e82f7eaf1d650/artemis-protocols/artemis-mqtt-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/mqtt/MQTTConnectionManager.java#L43) class there is a static set that contains a list of the connected client ids, a new connection is not accepted by the broker if the client ID is already present in this set.
It seems like this set is not properly cleared, during my tests it always contains the client id of the CloudService that fails to connect even after that the broker is disabled.

The fact that the broker does not accept a connection if there is a client already connected with the same clientId violates the MQTT spec, according to [MQTT-3.1.4-2](http://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v3.1.1/csprd02/mqtt-v3.1.1-csprd02.html#_Toc385349768) the broker should disconnect the existing client and accept the new connection.

The existence of this static set also introduces some coupling between the **Simple Artemis MQTT Broker** and **ActiveMQ Artemis Broker** services: it is not possible to connect to one of the two instances if there is a client already connected to the other with the same clientId.

title: Bluetooth notifications do not work
body:
Due to misprint in the `org.eclipse.kura.linux.bluetooth.le.BluetoothGattImpl` class notifications do not work.
Misprint in line 416 `String x = "Notification hanlde = ";` needs to be corrected.

Also, starting from some bluez version `gatttool` uses escape sequences in output. So, the line 417 in same file (see below) works incorrectly:
`String sub = line.substring(x.length()).trim();`
It seems it should be replaced with something like this:
`String sub = line.substring(x.length() + line.indexOf(x)).trim();`
Otherwise handle id cannot be extracted correctly.

Hello everyone,
I'll try to formalise here our idea on how to solve this issue. The constraints we see are the following:
- we would like to preserve the existing tag. That is the effective tag used to perform the 3.1.0 release and that should be kept as is.
- we would like to not modify the release branch. Indeed, since the changes are already merged into develop, the branch could be easily removed without loosing commits and preserving the linearity of the contributions.
- we would like to have the exists plugin always enabled and give the capability to disable it by selecting a specific profile. In our opinion, having it enabled only during the release process will highlight possible issues too late in the process.

To meet all those requirements, we started a maintenance branch called `maintenance-3.1` that has, as a first commit, a fix for the exists plugin by providing a profile to allow the user the capability to disable it when building.
We will create a new tag named `KURA_3.1.0_RELEASE_AMENDED`.

The SensorTag Driver sometimes fails to connect to the SensorTag causing the device to be lock by the connection attempts. The kura.log file is filled by Timeout exception during connection. 
This issue is partially fixed by #1852, but it needs more investigation.

To reproduce the issue, create a Wire graph with a Timer, an Asset binded to the SensorTagDriver and a Logger. Start it and check the logs.
comments:
[2018-03-07T10:20:13Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
The issue seems to be caused by an error during disconnection. If the device is not properly disconnected, bluez/tinyb keep it connected. So, further attempts to connection fail. A simple workaround is to manually disconnect it:

`bluetoothctl`
`disconnect <address>`
`exit`

[2018-04-04T13:17:59Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
Both the SensorTag example and Driver had been updated here [1]. The modifications increase the reliability of the code, but there are still some connection problems.

Using the ```org.eclipse.kura.example.ble.sensortag.tinyb```, there is a recurring error on kura.log:

```
2018-04-03 14:23:10,154 [pool-27-thread-1] INFO  o.e.k.e.b.t.t.BluetoothLe - Connecting to TiSensorTag B0:B4:48:BD:0D:03...
2018-04-03 14:23:16,496 [pool-27-thread-1] ERROR o.e.k.e.b.t.t.TiSensorTag - Failed to get GATT service
org.eclipse.kura.KuraBluetoothResourceNotFoundException: BLE resource not found.
	at org.eclipse.kura.internal.ble.BluetoothLeDeviceImpl.findService(BluetoothLeDeviceImpl.java:46)
	at org.eclipse.kura.example.ble.tisensortag.tinyb.TiSensorTag.getGattResources(TiSensorTag.java:1442)
	at org.eclipse.kura.example.ble.tisensortag.tinyb.TiSensorTag.init(TiSensorTag.java:94)
	at org.eclipse.kura.example.ble.tisensortag.tinyb.BluetoothLe.readSensorTags(BluetoothLe.java:261)
	at org.eclipse.kura.example.ble.tisensortag.tinyb.BluetoothLe.performScan(BluetoothLe.java:196)
	at java.util.concurrent.Executors$RunnableAdapter.call(Executors.java:511)
	at java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.runAndReset(FutureTask.java:308)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.access$301(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:180)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.run(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:294)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1142)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:617)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
2018-04-03 14:23:19,129 [pool-27-thread-1] ERROR o.e.k.e.b.t.t.BluetoothLe - Cannot connect/disconnect to TI SensorTag B0:B4:48:BD:0D:03.
```

It seems that the device successfully connect with SensorTag, but it fails to retrieve the exposed GATT Services and it is forced to disconnect. However, after several attempts the example can get the services and the errors disappear also after reboots.
This is due to the fact that Bluez keep a cache containing info about connected devices. When the example re-connects, Bluez fetches the information from the cache. To reproduce the issue, it is sufficient to delete the ```<device_address>``` folder under ```/var/lib/bluetooth/<adapter_address>``` and reboot.

[1] https://github.com/eclipse/kura/commit/56b081d548fd5bc7e473047265d805227ddf76b7#diff-69ff6e137d85850038cdbe97888402db

[2018-04-04T13:24:57Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
A possible solution is to increase the timeout for retrieving GATT resources from a BLE device or make it configurable (but a change on the API is needed). In the current implementation of ```BluetoothLeAdapterImpl```, ```BluetoothLeDeviceImpl```, ```BluetoothLeGattCharacteristicImpl``` and ```BluetoothLeGattServiceImpl```, a fixed timeout of 5 seconds is set. Increase it to 30 seconds will improve the reliability:

```
private static final Duration TIMEOUT = Duration.ofSeconds(30);
```

A better solution is to make the timeout configurable, i.e.:

```
public BluetoothLeGattService findService(UUID uuid, Duration duration) throws KuraBluetoothResourceNotFoundException {
```

[2018-04-06T13:18:54Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
The #2030 introduces the modifications suggested in these comments. However, there are still some problems related to connection that can cause in some situation a JVM crash or a disconnection error.
It should be investigated if they are caused by the type of device (SensorTag) or by the underlying library (TinyB) or something else.

[2018-04-12T10:14:21Z | MMaiero | comment]
@pierantoniomerlino Maybe we can close this, since it seems mitigated now and open another issue for the JVM crash?

[2018-04-12T10:35:27Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
Ok. The JVM crash issue should be investigated anyway...

[2018-02-20T10:14:13Z | nicolatimeus | comment]
This issue is likely caused by the localisation, in particular it is caused by the fact that all localisation resources bundles are currently fragments of the `org.eclipse.kura.localization` bundle. 

According to the OSGi spec a bundle/fragment is updated OSGi performs a refresh (stop and restart) of the bundles in its _dependency closure_. The dependency closure contains the list of bundles that directly or indirectly "depend" on the bundles being updated, and is obtainable using the `FrameworkWiring.getDependencyClosure()` method. The dependency closures of the bundles included in the `org.eclipse.kura.script.filter` dp are the following:

```

The rules for computing the dependency closure are explained in the OSGi spec. Roughly speaking in this case the following should happen:
* Since the `org.eclipse.kura.wire.script.filter.localization` fragment is going to be updated, its host, 
`org.eclipse.kura.localization` belongs to the dependency closure.
* If a bundle A imports a package from bundle B that belongs to the dependency closure, then A belongs to the dependency closure as well.

`org.eclipse.kura.core.configuration` is in the closure because it imports the  `org.eclipse.kura.core.util` package from the `org.eclipse.kura.util` bundle, which in turn imports the `org.eclipse.kura.localization`package.

This should also explain why the Web Ui is restarted in scenario shown in issue #1689.

title: [DbDataStore] Stale messages not purged with timezone other than UTC
body:
Kura uses a HouseKeeper thread to purge messages from the internal data store once they have been published. The query to find these messages (QoS == 0) is of the form:

`DELETE FROM <table_name> WHERE qos = 0 AND publishedOn <= DATEADD('ss', 5, NOW()) AND publishedOn IS NOT NULL;"`

The NOW() function returns the current time from the underlying OS. However, when updating the "publishedOn" column once a message is published, the Java code uses Date().getTime(), which always returns UTC. Because of this, systems with a timezone set to anything west of UTC will never clear messages from the datastore.

Kura should be able to handle systems with a timezone set to something other than UTC.

    - Name:
    - Version:
     
- Textual description of the issue:

Currently Kura generates the `/etc/bind/named.conf` configuration file using two different templates, depending (at least) on the value of the configuration parameter **Pass DNS Servers through DHCP** in the **DHCP and NAT** section of the web UI.

Both of these configuration file variants specify a custom logging configuration for `named`:

1. If the parameter is set to `false`, `named` is configured for logging on `data/named.run`.
2. If the parameter is set to `true`, `named` is configured for logging on `/var/log/named.log`.

In the scenarios above I've found the following issues:

1. In the first scenario, if the daemon is invoked using `/etc/init.d/bind9 start`, it will fail to start printing the following messages on `/var/log/syslog`:

```
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: automatic empty zone: EMPTY.AS112.ARPA
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: command channel listening on 127.0.0.1#953
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: couldn't add command channel ::1#953: address not available
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: isc_stdio_open 'data/named.run' failed: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring logging: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: loading configuration: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: exiting (due to fatal error)
```

The daemon start correctly if the following log-related section of `/etc/bind/named.conf` is removed:

```
logging {
	channel default_debug {
		file "data/named.run";
		severity dynamic;
	};
};
```

If the section above is removed bind will use the default logging configuration and forward log messages to the `syslog` daemon.

2. In the second scenario, `bind` is configured to log on `/var/log/named.log`, and to keep 3 backup versions of the file. When the daemon starts it will try to rename `/var/log/named.log` into 
`/var/log/named.log.0`, but it will fail because it does not have the permissions for modifying the `/var/log/ `directory, as it runs as the `bind` user

```
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: generating session key for dynamic DNS
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: sizing zone task pool based on 6 zones
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: set up managed keys zone for view _default, file 'managed-keys.bind'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: command channel listening on 127.0.0.1#953
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: couldn't add command channel ::1#953: address not available
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: unable to rename log file '/var/log/named.log' to '/var/log/named.log.0': permission denied
```

This can be fixed as well by removing the logging related section of `/etc/bind/named.conf`. The `/var/log/named.log` is created by Kura installer script, which also changes the ownership of the file to the `bind` user. If the file is removed, `bind` will not be able to recreate it and it will fail to start.

Disabling the watchdog causes the following exception in the Kura log:

~~~
2018-04-03 15:37:46,002 [Component Resolve Thread (Bundle 7)] INFO  o.e.k.l.w.WatchdogServiceImpl - WatchdogServiceImpl task cancelled? = true

Caused by: java.lang.InterruptedException
        at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
        at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:502)
        at java.lang.UNIXProcess.waitFor(UNIXProcess.java:395)
        at org.eclipse.kura.linux.watchdog.WatchdogServiceImpl.runCommand(WatchdogServiceImpl.java:220)

comments:
[2018-04-03T15:58:38Z | MMaiero | comment]
Never seen that in other systems. Is that causing issues?

[2018-04-04T07:41:35Z | cdealti | comment]
For sure the KuraException is not properly built.

The format message is intended to produce something like `Command 'sync' failed with code -1` but here the wait for the command `sync` to complete is interrupted so there's no exit code.
An example is [here](https://github.com/eclipse/kura/blob/release-3.2.0/kura/org.eclipse.kura.linux.net/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kura/linux/net/util/IpAddrShow.java#L67).

@ctron It would be useful to have a little more context (log lines before the exception) and an explanation on how you managed to disable the watchdog at the precise time the watchdog service was executing the sync+reboot action.

@MMaiero 
> Never seen that in other systems. Is that causing issues?

I don't think it's causing issues. The sync+reboot action is simply aborted as expected if the service is disabled. However let's wait for a confirm by @ctron.

[2018-04-04T07:47:25Z | ctron | comment]
As there are other issues with the watchdog, I am not sure this didn't have any impact. So short answer: I don't know.

The full set of logs is here: [kura-logs-20180404-090416.tar.gz](https://github.com/eclipse/kura/files/1874733/kura-logs-20180404-090416.tar.gz)

[2018-04-04T08:11:09Z | ctron | comment]
So looking at the code shows that this probably wasn't happening when disabling the watchdog, but when the watchdog wanted to reboot:

~~~java
    private synchronized void performWatchdogActions() throws KuraException {
        // watchdogToStop is used to avoid multiple action executions and kill Kura after a while
        if (!this.watchdogToStop) {
            this.watchdogToStop = true;
            runCommand("sync");
            runCommand("reboot");
        } else {
            refreshWatchdog();
        }
    }
~~~

Now if the call to `sync` fails, then the reboot command it not being executed. However the watchdog is disabled at the same time.

I am not sure why the call to `sync` returns a non-zero result, but in any case the reboot should be executed IMHO.

[2018-04-04T08:11:43Z | ctron | comment]
Which I think also explains the follow up issues like #2011.

[2018-04-04T08:34:42Z | ctron | comment]
Ok, looking more closely the issue gets more complex. 

The exception is not coming from the call to `sync`, but to the combination of modifying the watchdog and a reboot being in progress. The call to sync took a while (as it might happen) and at the same time (not intentionally) I did disable the watchdog (which causes an update). Which then causes a call to `cancel` on the poll task, which was busy waiting for `sync` at the same time. So it is not the `sync` command which failed, but the Java task of waiting for the return. However `IOException` is treated the same as `InterruptedException`.

So I think there are a few things to fix here:

1. A failed call to `sync` should not prevent a reboot
1. The shutdown of the watchdog should not cancel the task with `mayInterruptIfRunning` set to `true`. If the reboot is in progress then it should continue.
1. I think the poll task could be left alone if the ping interval didn't change
1. Also the logic of the `performWatchdogActions` seems a little bit odd to me. Maybe this is again designed that way and I simply don't understand it. But if the watchdog should be stopped (`watchdogToStop = true`) and the call gets executed again (like in this scenario), then the watchdog is refreshed. I do understand that the HW watchdog should be kept alive as long as the "sync" is running. But in the cause either "sync" or "reboot" fail, the watchdog should not be refreshed any longer. So in case of any exception to one of those two calls, refreshing the watchdog should stop IMHO.

[2018-04-04T14:52:30Z | cdealti | comment]
> The exception is not coming from the call to sync, but to the combination of modifying the watchdog and a reboot being in progress. The call to sync took a while (as it might happen) and at the same time (not intentionally) I did disable the watchdog (which causes an update).

This is what I was asking in my first comment.

The outcome of this race condition, disabling the `WatchdogService` while it was running the shutdown actions, effectively canceled the shutdown. It does not look a bug.

I agree that the current code may be improved with your suggestions and we will consider them for the next development cycle.

[2018-04-06T16:17:40Z | cdealti | comment]
@ctron OK, I should give up with software ;).

If the WatchdogService is re-enabled later on, the damned flag `watchdogToStop` remains set to true (I hate flags), preventing further watchdog actions.

It must be fixed for 3.2.0.

title: [NetAdmin] Fix AT escape sequence timings in TelitModem
body:
The GPS disable logic for Telit Modems currently does not perform a 1 second pause after sending the `+++` escape sequence for switching serial port from GPS to AT mode.
This can cause the ModemMonitorService code to miss the `NO_CARRIER` modem response at the `+++` command and can cause the GPS disable process to fail.

title: [NetAdmin] Race condition between NetAdmin and PositionService after modem reset
body:
During the reset of a USB modem with GPS enabled that uses the same port for AT and GPS data, a race condition can occur between 2 threads that contend access to modem serial port.

The process is initiated by the ModemMonitor thread, that resets the modem and immediately enables GPS and posts ModemGpsReadyEvent.
The following threads are involved in the race condition:

1 - the PositionSerivce that handles ModemGpsReadyEvent and opens GPS serial port
2 - the ModemMonitorService.trackModem() method, that runs on an “anonymous” executor, that tries to identify the modem using at commands on the same port.

Thread 2 is the one responsible for tracking modems, it is triggered due the USB events that occur during modem reset.
The race condition can cause PortInUseExceptions in any of the two threads, and further modem resets.

title: [NetAdmin] Some state of the logic that manages modems persists across resets
body:
A part of the logic that manages modems is provided by the `CellularModem` subclasses, that are instantiated by a `CellularModemFactory` and are cached.
Currently a `CellularModemFactory` always returns the same `CellularModem` instance for a given modem, even if the managed modem has been reset.
This behaviour can cause problems because some of the `CellularModem` implementations keep internal state.

For example, the `TelitModem` class defines a boolean flag that specifies if the GPS is enabled or not, if the modem is reset with GPS enabled and the `NetAdmin` fails to disable GPS, the value of this flag will be retained. This can cause the NetAdmin to incorrectly assume that the GPS is still enabled after the reset even if it is not.

The state of the `CellularModem` instances should be cleared after a modem reset.

title: emitAllReadChannels method doesn't handle Runtime exceptions
body:
The `emitAllReadChannels` method in `WireAsset` class doesn't handle the unchecked exceptions, but only `KuraException`. So, if an unchecked exception as `RuntimeException` is thrown, it is simply passed to the upper layer and this can stop the current thread.

For example, if a Driver doesn't support readings, the `emitChannelRecords` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` that is not caught by the `emitAllReadChannels` method. The results is that the current thread on Wires is closed.

For the WireAsset I agree that we can catch and log any unchecked exceptions emitted by the Driver.

title: BLE Beacon data assembly overflow
body:
**Describe the bug**
Beacons have a few fields of limited length reserved for their internal data or user data. Among them are major and minor code, and transmit power. All are Integers in the API. That means that they can reach up to 4B while length limit of those fields is 2B. Since API update is expensive, amend length check in [to2BytesHex()](https://github.com/eclipse/kura/blob/3a4cab4972432194316eb479c5dcb39caa80282e/kura/org.eclipse.kura.linux.bluetooth/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kura/linux/bluetooth/le/beacon/BluetoothAdvertisingData.java#L71) and cut the excess hex characters.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install BeaconAdvertiserExample
2. Enable and set Major to > 65535
3. Apply

**Expected behavior**
Advertised minor and tx power should be as set, but are instead overwritten by major's bytes.

title: [Modbus] Implement the MBAP header for TCP/IP communication

Without the header the slave device rejects the transmission when checking the header content.

title: iwScanTool fails to parse scan results
body:
There's a network in my area which causes iwScanTool to fail when parsing the results of `iw dev wlan0 scan`.

The following error is produced:

```
2016-08-02T09:07:46.384Z [qtp27081630-40] WARN org.eclipse.kura.web.server.util.KuraExceptionHandler - RPC service non-application error
  org.eclipse.kura.KuraException: An internal error occurred. scan operation has failed
...
...
  Caused by: org.eclipse.kura.KuraException: An internal error occurred. error parsing scan results
    at org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.util.iwScanTool.scan(iwScanTool.java:162)
    at org.eclipse.kura.net.admin.NetworkAdminServiceImpl.getWifiHotspots(NetworkAdminServiceImpl.java:1161)
    ... 38 more
  Caused by: java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: "IBSS"
    at sun.misc.FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString(Unknown Source)
    at sun.misc.FloatingDecimal.parseFloat(Unknown Source)
    at java.lang.Float.parseFloat(Unknown Source)
    at org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.util.iwScanTool.parse(iwScanTool.java:372)
    at org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.util.iwScanTool.scan(iwScanTool.java:160)
    ... 39 more
```

The failure is caused by the following item in the list:

```
BSS 00:11:22:33:44:55(on wlan0)
    TSF: 10275279415182 usec (118d, 22:14:39)
    freq: 2412
    beacon interval: 100 TUs
    capability: IBSS Privacy (0x0012)
    signal: -84.00 dBm
    last seen: 8070 ms ago
    Information elements from Probe Response frame:
    SSID: TheSSID
    Supported rates: 1.0* 2.0 5.5 11.0 6.0 9.0 12.0 18.0 
    DS Parameter set: channel 1
    IBSS ATIM window: 0 TUs Extended supported rates: 24.0 36.0 48.0 54.0 
    WMM: information: 01 00
```

Specifically, the line:
`IBSS ATIM window: 0 TUs    Extended supported rates: 24.0 36.0 48.0 54.0`

This seems like a bug in iw (version 3.11), and it is really supposed to be two separate lines.
Even so, we can handle this situation better in Kura: https://github.com/eclipse/kura/blob/KURA_1.4.0_RELEASE/kura/org.eclipse.kura.linux.net/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kura/linux/net/util/iwScanTool.java#L371

For systems that may not have package managers installed. To keep the build uniform, we create install scripts for all platforms (RPi, BBB, Intel Edison, etc.). title: [Net] PppFactory is not a factory and its design is wrong
body:
`PppFactory` is used by `ModemMonitorServiceImpl` to both create new instances and return already created instances. There are several defects:
1. It's not a factory. It's more similar to the [Multiton Pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiton_pattern).
2. `obtainPppService(String iface, String port)` is misleading and error prone. Internally only the interface name, for example `ppp0` is used as the key.

The above can lead to the following scenario:
- Initially `obtainPppService(ppp0, /dev/ttyACM0)` creates a new `IModemLinkService` instance for the interface `ppp0` running on the modem serial port `/dev/ttyACM0`. This instance is tracked internally by PppFactory by the interface name `ppp0`. The monitor will spawn `pppd` on `/dev/ttyACM0`
- The modem gets reset/unplugged (for any reason). On Linux is entirely possible that the serial port device name changes for example to `/dev/ttyACM1`.
- In the next loop iteration the monitor will call `obtainPppService(ppp0, /dev/ttyACM1)` again but this will return the previous instance since the serial port name does not matter. The monitor will spawn `pppd` on `/dev/ttyACM0` which is clearly wrong.

title: Replace all calls to ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String)
body:
All calls to `org.osgi.service.cm.ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String)` should be replaced to calls of `org.osgi.service.cm.ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String, String)` providing `null` as the location parameter.

Most calls in Kura already are already migrated to that call, but not all. Using Apache Felix ConfigAdmin actually enforces the default binding which is generated otherwise and will not configure some components. Also see OSGi spec for `getConfiguration(String)`:

> Bind its location to the calling bundle's location.

That effectively binds the configuration to the Kura configuration bundle which is wrong. It should instead be bound to the bundle containing the service. Leaving the argument `null` would do that automatically once the service is registered.

title: [Modem] NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.modem.SupportedUsbModems
body:
This issue is caused by commit 9f5870537e36afa6641dc6d3d237686e82407f02 
Everything works right if the device has no internal modem, while, if the modem is available, the execution will stop at boot due to a `NoClassDefFoundError` on class `org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.modem.SupportedUsbModems`.

The issue is triggered by `SupportedUsbModemsInfo.isSupported` that tries to call `SupportedUsbModems.isSupported`. Before executing the `isSupported` method, the `SupportedUsbModems` static block will invoke `getLsusbInfo` that will call `LinuxProcessUtil.startWithStats`. 
The static block in `LinuxProcessUtil` modified by 9f5870537e36afa6641dc6d3d237686e82407f02 tries to get a service reference of the `SystemService`, but the result of this invocation is a null value. This is due to the fact that the `SystemService` component definition has a dependency on the `NetworkService`, but the network service needs the `SystemService` to execute: an indirect dependency loop is generated in this way, preventing the code to execute properly.

@ctron Could you take a look at this?

title: [DbDataStore] defrag and checkpoint are not per-table operations
body:
DbDataStore exposes two methods ``defrag`` and ``checkpoint`` that act on the entire DB and not on the DB table associated with the DbDataStore.
When multiple ``DbDataStore`` instances exists (since the introduction of the multiple cloud connections feature), each ``HouseKeeperTask`` instance will periodically call ``defrag``, potentially concurrently.

title: [DbDataStore] repair is very slow on big tables
body:
The ``repair`` operation contains a DB query to detect duplicates of the primary key (which should not occur).
The operation was added due to this [bug](https://sourceforge.net/p/hsqldb/discussion/73674/thread/a08046eb/).

The query has shown to take a very long time (in the order of minutes) on relatively large **file** databases (for example enabling the "almost persistent" configuration in kura.properties).

The bug is only known to happen on certain gateways using a raw flash storage configuration.

Since these gateways are no longer supported, the ``repair`` could be executed only once on startup maybe subjected to a configuration parameter.
comments:
[2017-05-26T07:14:42Z | cdealti | comment]
This will be addressed as part of the switch to the H2 Database.

[2017-06-15T14:19:48Z | nicolatimeus | comment]
The db repair addresses an HSQL-specific issue so hopefully it is no longer needed after the switch to H2.
The code that performs the repair is still present in the H2 implementation but is disabled by default. It can be re-enabled setting `db.store.repair.enabled=true` in kura.properties.

title: Kura's WEB bundles detection
body:
When Kura starts, the /var/log/kura.log contains the following:
```o.e.k.c.s.SystemServiceImpl - Kura has web interface? true```
even if web interface wasn't even built
comments:
[2016-12-06T13:50:12Z | cdealti | comment]
Minor thing:
 
 https://github.com/eclipse/kura/blob/release-2.1.0/kura/org.eclipse.kura.core/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kura/core/system/SystemServiceImpl.java#L316

Posponed

[2017-03-03T14:04:12Z | MMaiero | comment]
The message is maybe misleading. Probably it would be better to say "Is Kura web interface enabled?". That value is based in a property set in kura.properties file and that allows to disable the web interface if not needed. It has no relation to the fact that the web ui was built or was available.
We will change the logged message accordingly.
Thanks for finding that out.

[2017-03-03T14:26:01Z | markoer | comment]
Even this question implies presence of web UI. But it is still better than the existing one.

[2017-03-03T14:30:14Z | MMaiero | comment]
Just to complete the answer: the fact that the web bundle exists or not is not catched by Kura. What is managed by this property is that if the web bundle exists in the filesystem, the user can choose if he wants to have that bundle started or not.

title: Kura NN should not depend on ethtool, bind9, isc-dhcp-server, hostapd
body:
This bug was originally filed at https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=476616.

Original Message:

Unless I'm missing something, I believe the "no network" .deb package should not be depending on any networking tool, right?

Agree. 
However, just one exception, it seems that ethtool is still needed for LinuxNetworkUtil bundle to get ethernet MAC address for kura MQTT default client-id.

I am going to use this bug to track bug fixes for the _NN_ installation packages. At present, not only are the networking system dependencies required, but the networking bundles are also being installed and started. This is not the correct behavior and should be corrected.

Thanks,
--Dave

title: [Kura 2.1.0 QA] eth0 netmask configuration
body:
2 similar cases are covered:

1. 16-bit netmask

Disable eth0 interface in Kura web UI.
Apply the configuration. Interface is not actually disabled (#876).
Now configure it as:
  * Enabled for WAN
  * Manually
  * add IP Address and Gateway IP
  * add netmask 255.255.0.0

Apply configuration.
As a result the actual applied netmask will be 255.255.255.0 and Kura's config will show 255.255.0.0.

2. 32-bit netmask

Disable and later configure eth0 as before.
This time set netmask to 255.255.255.255.
Apply configuration.
As a result the actual netmask will be 255.255.255.0 and Kura's config will show an empty field.

Note:
Netmask is properly applied only after IP Address is also updated. In case of 255.255.255.255 is is still not shown in web UI.

Kura 2.1.0 build 12, Raspberry Pi 3, fully updated `Linux raspberrypi 4.1.18-v7+ #846 SMP Thu Feb 25 14:22:53 GMT 2016 armv7l `
comments:
[2016-12-01T09:13:44Z | cdealti | comment]
1) It may take some time to apply the changes. Can you wait longer before you check the netmask with ``ip``

2) This is a corner case. I don't know of any such usage with Ethernet.

[2016-12-01T09:44:32Z | markoer | comment]
1. I find that `ifconfig` returns a bit nicer output. Anyway, the changes are normally updated rather fast - as soon as the UI closes the modal waiting indicator. And it seems also a second netmask update actually updates it. So - netmask is updated in case IP changes or netmask is updated the second time. If IP remains the same as before, netmask is not properly set the first time.

2. That's what test(er)s are for :)

[2016-12-06T15:52:44Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
1. 16-bit netmask

As reported in #867, the `dhcpcd` service is normally running on the RPi3. So, the netmask is updated by the dhcp server even if the user configured a static IP from Kura webUI. Removing (`apt-get purge dhcpcd5`) and killing the service fixes the issue.

2. 32-bit netmask

I agree that this is a corner case, however if the user sets a 255.255.255.255 netmask, the interface is accordingly configured and `ifconfig` reports the correct configuration. The problem is that the webUI doesn't show the netmask because this code on the TabTcpIpUi.java file:

```
if (config != null && config.getSubnetMask() != null && config.getSubnetMask().equals("255.255.255.255")) {
    config.setSubnetMask("");
}
```

[2016-12-09T09:45:48Z | cdealti | comment]
@markoer can we close this? As for #867 we will document to disable ``dhcpcd``.

About the /32 netmask not shown in the web UI I would create a separate issue with label ``kura-web``.

[2016-12-09T09:55:43Z | markoer | comment]

title: [Configuration] Empty Values In Service Properties
body:
If I set the value of a service property to an empty string in the web UI and hit Apply the empty string is accepted and the corresponding service gets the empty string. When KURA gets restarted the value reverts to the default value from the metatype file. If I change the value to a non empty string the value is preserved across a KURA restart.
I'm changing command.working.directory but see the same behaviour on other properties.
comments:
[2016-01-18T17:43:11Z | cdealti | comment]
> If I set the value of a service property to an empty string in the web UI and hit Apply the empty string is accepted and the corresponding service gets the empty string. 

If the configuration with an "empty" value is validated by the Web UI, it means that the `required` attribute of the property in the service metatype is set to false.
If the property has a default value in the metatype, the Kura `ConfigurationService` should pass this default to the service (a `ConfigurableComponent`). This is the behavior when Kura starts reading the configuration from the latest snapshot file but there is no configuration for the service. We say that we merge the configuration snapshot with the metatype defaults. 

> When KURA gets restarted the value reverts to the default value from the metatype file

We will make sure a configuration update through the Web UI will be merged with metatype defaults if needed.

About your use case, since you are working on a Windows port of Kura, I'm quite sure you don't want a metatype default for the **command.working.directory**. This is because Kura assumes there is only one metatype XML file matching the service pid.
In other words you can only have a single default value and in your case it won't work well both for Linux and Windows.

By removing the default from the metatype, the service will not receive the **command.working.directory** and can fallback using a default working directory which is suitable for every OS, for example the temporary directory through the Java property **java.io.tmpdir**.

If you are happy with this, please also update the property description in the metatype to describe what is the default working directory if it is not explicitly set.

title: org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider provides API and service implementation
body:
The bundle `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` provides base classes and a service implementation at the same time. That way it is impossible to exchange the service implementation with a different implementation.

As we are using OSGi we should follow the idea of splitting up API/base classes and internal service implementation.

Currently the "web" bundle requires a reference to `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` in order to use `BaseChannelDescriptor` and thus Kura an only be used with the single implementation of `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider`.
comments:
[2016-12-19T10:15:31Z | amitjoy | comment]
This is a design decision that we have to consider thinking of its pros and cons in OSGi dynamic environment. You are absolutely right. It is not possible to change the implementation at runtime. It has a history behind it.

`Asset` is a concept that is introduced with `Wires`. `Asset` is a logical representation of device in `Kura` (not restricted to `Wires`). To perform read/write operations on a physical device, users can use `Asset-Driver component model `in `Kura`. We provide the base implementation of `Asset` in `BaseAsset`.

`Asset` is also used as a logical node or `Wire Component` in `Kura Wires` dataflow graph. As `BaseAsset` provides all the necessary implementations to associate `Driver` for reading and writing data from physical devices, `WireAsset` (An implementation of `Asset` and `WireComponent`) leverages the basic implementation of `Asset` (`BaseAsset`).

Now, why did we extend `BaseAsset`?

To leverage the implemented functionalities of `Asset`. So, when an user uses `Wires` with a `WireAsset` configured the the dataflow graph (`Wire Graph`), only one service component is registered - `WireAsset`. And when an user uses `Asset-Driver component model` without `Wires`, only `Asset` service component is registered. 

Why `BaseAsset` is not associated with `WireAsset`?

The lifecycles of `BaseAsset` and `WireAsset` are managed by OSGi configuration service and hence, we didn't choose to create `BaseAsset` manually and inject to `WireAsset`. This could have prevented us to manage the lifecycle of `BaseAsset` in runtime. That's why `WireAsset` does not associate `BaseAsset` but extends.

[2016-12-19T11:51:18Z | ctron | comment]
Since this is new in Kura 3.0 I would say we can ignore "backward compatibility".

So technically, what speaks against separating those two into different bundles?

[2016-12-19T12:46:42Z | amitjoy | comment]
The two bundles are kept separated, depending on the implementations it provides. `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` provides `BaseAsset` implementation whereas `org.eclipse.kura.wire.component.provider` provides all the implementations of `Wire Components` including `WireAsset`.

[2016-12-19T13:22:47Z | ctron | comment]
I meant the bundle "org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider".

[2016-12-19T13:25:45Z | amitjoy | comment]
If I have understood the question correctly, `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` provides the implementation for `Asset-Driver Component Model` that can be used in isolation (without `Wires`). And that's why it is kept separated.

[2016-12-19T13:28:10Z | ctron | comment]
I do want to split up the bundle "org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider". Not merge it with something else.

[2016-12-19T15:27:28Z | amitjoy | comment]
As I have mentioned earlier, we need OSGi to manage the lifecycles of `BaseAsset` service component and `WireAsset` service component. If we split up `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` bundle to have a fragment to contain `WireAsset`, it is not possible to export it as fragment does not allow exporting services.

[2016-12-19T16:35:12Z | ctron | comment]
Sure, but the instance can be exported from any bundle. Not necessarily just this one. And not necessarily from a fragment.

[2016-12-19T16:44:39Z | amitjoy | comment]
So you mean, the instance of the service component can be exported from any bundle. But what would be the advantage of exporting the instance from other bundle?

[2016-12-19T16:48:13Z | ctron | comment]
You are not exporting BaseAsset instances from this bundle. I will dig into this next year and try make an example for you.

[2016-12-19T16:59:36Z | amitjoy | comment]
Actually `BaseAsset` instances are exported from `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider` bundle when it is required. That is, when user only uses `Asset-Driver component model` to perform read/write operations, `BaseAsset` instances are exported from `org.eclipse.kura.asset.provider`  bundle. But while using Kura Wires, no `BaseAsset` instance is created rather `WireAsset` instances are exported from `org.eclipse.kura.wire.component.provider` bundle.

title: Improved type conversions in OPCUA driver
body:
This PR adds an additional property in OPCUA driver channel configuration, named `opcua.type`.
This property is considered only in case of a write and is ignored otherwise, it allows to specify the type of the OPCUA variable to be written.
The driver will attempt to convert the Java value to be written to the specified type. The allowed values for this property are the following:

* DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE
* BOOLEAN
* SBYTE
* INT16
* INT32
* INT64
* BYTE
* UINT16
* UINT32
* UINT64
* FLOAT
* DOUBLE
* STRING
* BYTE_STRING
* BYTE_ARRAY
* SBYTE_ARRAY

This PR should extend the set of types that can be written using the driver to the list above, types not included in the list are still unsupported.

The default value for this parameter is DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE, if this value is selected, the driver will perform the conversion automatically as in the current implementation, as follows:

Java -> OPCUA
BOOLEAN -> Boolean
DOUBLE -> Double
FLOAT -> Float
INTEGER -> Int32
LONG -> Int64
STRING -> String
BYTE_ARRAY -> SByte[]

Backwards compatibility is preserved by the fact that DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE is the default.

This PR also changes the way in which BYTE_ARRAY Java type is handled, now the driver should support reading and writing the following OPCUA types using the BYTE_ARRAY Java type:

ByteString,
Byte[] (array of unsigned bytes)
SByte[] (array of signed bytes)

This PR also includes some tests for type conversions.

Closes #1840

body:
This PR fixes a potential issue on USB modem detection. The USB modems expose a set of serial ports that can be used for ppp connection, AT commands or get NMEA strings from the GPS module. 
Kura identifies the right serial port based on the tty device name. However, the modem serial ports can be mapped to tty devices in an unpredictable order and change after a modem reset.

So, this PR changes the way the tty devices are identified based on the bInterfaceNumber of the USB tty interface. Moreover, the issue reported in #520 is fixed (the PppFactory should be refactored, however...).

title: Fix concurrency issue in command service
body:
The command service was implemented in a way that it did execute all
command written out to a single shell script. This can cause the issue
that two requests issued at the same time would fail.

This change does write out seperate script files using the
Files.createTempFile method. It also does not fork "chmod" and
"dos2unix" since those operations can be performed inside Java which
saves two additional process forks.

Also is the "cd" statement not necessary when the ProcessBuilder
is instructed to change the directory first. For this the process
started can now accept an optional working directory.

This change also includes a unit test for the command service.

backend does locate the components the communication stack is made up.

the factory id from the service, locates the factory instance and
fills the result in one step.

the requirement on a CloudService that is has to be configurable, the
requirement on the factory to be implemented using OSGi DS.

title: Fix concurrency issue in command service
body:
The command service was implemented in a way that it did execute all
command written out to a single shell script. This can cause the issue
that two requests issued at the same time would fail.

This change does write out separate script files using the
Files.createTempFile method. It also does not fork "chmod" and
`dos2unix` since those operations can be performed inside Java which
saves two additional process forks.

Also is the `cd` statement not necessary when the ProcessBuilder
is instructed to change the directory first.

This change also includes a unit test for the command service.

Signed-off-by: Jens Reimann <jreimann@redhat.com>

title: Wrong approach for handling the bundles providing automation resources - host and fragments
body:
We use "bundle.getEntry" to check if a bundle is a provider of automation resources. This method searches only the contents of this bundle for the entry. Then we check if this bundle is a fragment, and if it is, we do not process it. So, if the host does not contain automation resources then it will not be processed; the fragment will not be processed either - as a result these resources will never be loaded.

title: POST request for thing addition gives 500 if same UID exists already
body:
If a thing is already added and if we try to add the same thing again by sending the POST request to `/things`, it gives a 500 error. If we try again then the response is 200 and the thing is added.

What is happening here is, if we try to add the same thing again the old thing is removed first (according to the method `addThingSafely` in `ThingSetupManager` class) but before it adds the new thing, it is sending back 500 error somehow.

When we retry the request, it creates the thing because the old thing has been removed in the previous step.

I am trying to figure out what is wrong there. Anyone has a clue?
comments:
[2016-04-13T13:12:09Z | sjsf | comment]
Just tried to reproduce it, but I get a "409: Conflict" on the second try when the thing already exists. Do you happen to have some logs which you could share here?

[2016-04-13T13:25:49Z | sjsf | comment]
Oh, I just noticed: You are adding the thing via the PaperUI, I assume... It's using the deprecated ThingSetupManagerResource (i.e. POST /rest/setup/things), and not the "proper" rest API (i.e. POST /rest/things). That one indeed doesn't do a duplicate check and therefore raises an IllegalArgumentException, leading to the described behavior. 
However, as it's in the process of getting dropped and replaced (see #1013), I don't think it's worth spending any efforts in fixing it.

[2016-04-13T13:33:53Z | shry15harsh | comment]
Oh, I was indeed using the deprecated API. Though adding through /rest/things (after adding the thing) giving me 500 error and not 409.

Logs are here http://pastebin.com/GLXPFqxZ

[2016-04-13T14:33:35Z | sjsf | comment]
According to the line numbers in your stacktrace, you are working on a state about 4-5 months old. There indeed was no check if the thing already existed...
Update your codebase an you will be fine.

[2016-04-14T07:26:47Z | shry15harsh | comment]
You're right. Actually I was using older Openhab2 build. Now they have changed it to Openhab2-addons and distro (which runs on Java 8 and has lot of change), so did not update the runtime.

Though, as according to the latest code, addThingSafely method ensures that thing is removed first and then added. I wonder how come you get 409 error, you should get successful response with the thing added, right? Or was it because the second request was made immediately after the first? If we wait then it would give 200?

[2016-04-14T09:08:58Z | sjsf | comment]
> I wonder how come you get 409 error

That's how:

``` java
        if (thingUID != null) {
            // check if a thing with this UID already exists
            Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(thingUID);
            if (thing != null) {
                // report a conflict
                return getThingResponse(Status.CONFLICT, thing, locale,
                        "Thing " + thingUID.toString() + " already exists!");
            }
        }
```

(see https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/io/org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.core/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/rest/core/thing/ThingResource.java#L127)

the paperui sends a request with payload

{controller_exclude: -232323}

the ThingResource.updateConfguration() receives in configurationParameters

{controller_exclude=-232323.0} //Double

[2016-05-11T12:13:02Z | maggu2810 | comment]
- In "Perform Setup Tasks…" disable the "Launch Generate All Models"
- Proceed as normal
- Use the "Package Explorer" to open the bundle "org.eclipse.smarthome.model.codegen" of the Working Set "Bundles"

You should see different launch configurations here:
- 1 Generate Items Model.launch
- 2 Generate Sitemap Model.launch
- 3 Generate Script Model.launch
- 4 Generate Rule Model.launch
- 5 Generate Persistence Model.launch
- 6 Generate Thing Model.launch
- Generate All Models.launch

The "Generate All Models" (used by the setup tasks) should execute 1-6, but is currently broken.

So if you execute 1-6 manually (which should succeed) you get the same result.

title: ChannelItemProvider depends on bundle start order
body:
#1288  introduced the ChannelItemProvider

If I understand the mechanism correctly, the "virtual" items are now created (createItemForLink) if a Thing or a ItemChannelLink has been added.

It seems to me that (at least) on startup it is possible that "createItemForLink" is called before all the bundle XMLs are completely parsed (see: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1519#issuecomment-221020452).

I can reproduce the error here in a Karaf container where the most ESH bundles are using the same start-level (I am using the our karaf and karaf-tp features).
I can workaround that startup behavior if I increase the start-level of the core.thing bundle.

I'm not familiar with Java yet, but overloading the update method for an item type is another way to go too? Presumably that's already in use for setting a channel from the various supported item types.

---

It hasn't been stated where this might be caused? I was assuming it was on openHABs end, but is it due to the way the UIs were implemented? Classic UI works as you'd expect, Paper UI seemed fine too. I was only able to reproduce the problem with Basic UI. I take it the other UIs account for this issue and deal with it on the client side. 

If you are going to change this, my suggestion would be a JSON update(instead of raw text?) with an identifier property for the item being updated followed by Element type(Colorpicker, Slider, Switch etc). Elements in the UI should be able to easily update by matching element type and item id. This is even better for UIs built around Redux, the update arrives, reducer combines the new object to the items state object(which could contain more properties than the update object provides, easy to merge state with spread operator), then with React(and Angular2 I think?) UI components update to reflect the new state.

title: Sonos Things are shown ONLINE although not on the network
body:
It seems that the Sonos thing handler sets the status to ONLINE on initialization, even if the device is not reachable (or not even on the network).
I would expect it to be OFFLINE instead.
comments:
[2016-06-14T14:45:08Z | R-Edelhoff | comment]
Yes i can reproduce the issue with following steps:
- Sonos player will be paired while reachable in network -> State of created thing is ONLINE
- Restart the runtime and disconnect the Sonos device afterwards
- When the runtime is back again the state of the thing is still ONLINE 

The rootcause for this issue is that the polling runnable (where the thing state is periodically updated)
will not be scheduled when the ThingHandler gets initialized. This happens because the UpnpIOParticipant (which is the ZonePlayerHandler in this case) is not registered to the UpnpIOService at this time and the "isRegistered()" check prevents the handler to schedule the runnable during initialization.

However the "isRegistered()" is not required at this point because the UpnpIOParticipant will anyway be registered (if not already done) when using the UpnpIOService in the following calls of "addSubscription()" and "*.invokeAction()". Hence we can remove this check which is fixing the issue and does not create any regression as i have tested as well.

I will not going to set the thing status to OFFLINE after initialization because the Thing state will appear as OFFLINE for 60s after pairing the device which is confusing. We rather need to make sure that the polling runnable will always be scheduled to enforce a thing status update within max. 60s.

title: Automation: multiple triggers
body:
I don't know if my understanding of the rule engine is correct.

If I add two trigger to a rule, I assume it is executed 
- if the first trigger matches
- if the second trigger matches

Is this correct?

I add two item state changed event trigger to a rule, one for ITEM_SWITCH_0 and one for ITEM_SWITCH_1.
The rule is only triggered for one of both.

@danchom, @marinmitev: Is this a bug or is my understanding wrong?
comments:
[2016-06-09T08:34:41Z | maggu2810 | comment]
The rule looks like:

``` text
{
  "enabled": true,
  "status": {
    "status": "IDLE",
    "statusDetail": "NONE"
  },
  "triggers": [
    {
      "id": "trigger_1",
      "label": "Item State Change Trigger",
      "description": "This triggers a rule if an items state changed",
      "configuration": {
        "itemName": "SWITCH_IN_0"
      },
      "type": "ItemStateChangeTrigger"
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger_2",
      "label": "Item State Change Trigger",
      "description": "This triggers a rule if an items state changed",
      "configuration": {
        "itemName": "SWITCH_IN_1"
      },
      "type": "ItemStateChangeTrigger"
    }
  ],
  "conditions": [],
  "actions": [],
  "configuration": {},
  "configDescriptions": [],
  "uid": "rule_3",
  "name": "T",
  "tags": []
}
```

The function "internalCreate" of "GenericEventTriggerHandler" looks if there is already a handler for "ruleUID + module.getId()". A new one is only created if there is no one.
The module.getId() returns the ID of the module itself, but not the ID that is used in the rule  (not trigger_1 or trigger_2 but itemStateChangeTriggerID).
So there will not be two handlers created but only one.
I assume this is not correct.

[2016-06-09T08:38:44Z | maggu2810 | comment]
The ID of the children of CompositeTriggerType (of all composite types) needs to be unique.

[2016-06-09T10:10:22Z | danchom | comment]
Hi Markus,
1) Your understanding is not correct. Each one of the triggers can trigger the rule. There is OR relation between triggers. Your use case is close to CEP (complex event processing) which is not supported by the Automation module. May be you can implement it with conditions, where the state of one switch will be get from the system (through the ScriptCondition) when the other triggers the rule. The conditions are related with AND between them.
2) One handler can be reused by many modules. I'm not sure if this is a good practice, but it is up to module type and handler creator. IMHO it will be more clear to have relation 1:1, otherwise the handler implementation is more complex. May be it is useful when all modules of same type have to share common resources
3) module.getId() returns id of the module, not module type id. May be you are using module.getTypeUID() which returns the module type of the module.
4) yes child modules in composite module type must have unique ids in scope of composite module. But I don't see a reason to put one and the same module multiple times in composite module type.

[2016-06-09T11:04:32Z | maggu2810 | comment]
1) This is what I mean :wink: Perhaps my spelling was wrong.

I think my example is rather simple and easy to reproduce.
- Create two switch items
- Create a rule with two composite triggers of the same type, e.g. the ESH "ItemStateChangeTrigger" (https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/90e1804/bundles/automation/org.eclipse.smarthome.automation.module.core/ESH-INF/automation/moduletypes/EventTriggersTypeDefinition.json#L45)
- the first ItemStateChangeTrigger is using the first switch item
- the second ItemStateChangeTrigger is using the second switch item

The rule is triggered only by one item.

Both composite trigger has a unique ID.
The child of the first composite trigger, the ItemStateChangeTrigger has the same ID as the child of the second composite trigger. So the same handler is used and because of that the last configuration wins.

title: Integer config parameter is stored as decimal
body:
If a service is configured through the Paper UI (and therefore through the REST API), numbers are sent in JSON always as double, i.e. an integer 1 becomes 1.0.
The REST API then stores this value as a BigDecimal with 1 decimal digit, so that it is not regarded as an integer anymore.

A concrete problem with this behavior is described here: https://community.openhab.org/t/change-homekit-setting-in-paperui/11407
