For me it has been the combination of the (unused but active) Z-Wave binding in the runtime and the circumstance that the Paper UI loads all thing types "/rest/thing-types".
The response content length is 1,579,263 Bytes

[2016-08-04T14:43:57Z | markusjw | comment]
I just wanted to raise the same issue.
The effect is reproducible when you have a Number item (usually defined via a thing channel) with a high maximum value, combined with a small step value.
The problem is multiplied with the number of affected Number items. If there are several of these items, the page script can take minutes to load. It seems to load eventually, so it might be rather a very long than an infinite loop.

An example would be an energy counter item which can reach high numbers. Such item definitions actually exist, so this effect is not just theoretical.

I suppose that the slider control is not designed to create a high number of discrete value stops.

[2016-08-26T10:27:47Z | markusjw | comment]
@aounhaider1 Does this information help to find out more about the problem?
I hope there is a solution because right now the Control UI is just not usable for things with wide range Number items.

[2017-03-27T09:14:35Z | markusjw | comment]
Besides the fact that the web UI should not block, there is a general question:
Should a slider be shown for values with large number ranges? In these cases, the slider is no longer usable for precise inputs.
@kaikreuzer What do you think?

[2017-03-27T10:08:38Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Does the slider cause any issue? It is still the fastest way to get close to some desired value - and with large ranges, you usually do not want to have a precise number. For the cases where you need it, the number value itself can be selected and the desired value can simply be typed in.

[2017-03-28T07:43:52Z | markusjw | comment]
Yes, it seems to me that it is the slider that causes the issue. As said above, the problem rises especially when using large range number items with small steps.

There are use cases for "large range, but high precision". For example, if you can configure a light duration. For some applications youtwant to set it precisely for a few seconds (that is why the step should be in seconds), but in other applications you want to duration to be 8 hours (which would already be 28800 seconds)

You are right, the number value input is usable. But maybe the slider should be deactivated for larger ranges, especially if it cannot be made to work properly so that is blocks the complete control page.

knx.items:

knx.rules:

```
// Connects KNX boardroom dim % to dim gCloud
rule "KNXLightDimmer"
when
        Item knx_boardroom_dimmer received command
then
        var PercentType percent
        if(knx_boardroom_dimmer.state instanceof PercentType)  {
            percent = knx_boardroom_dimmer.state as PercentType
            sendCommand(gHue, percent)
        }
end
```

It seems specific to something Classic UI is doing?

[2016-07-04T08:18:13Z | afuechsel | comment]
This could be related to the initialization of the isOsramPar16 in the HueLightHandler, which could be missed, as we recently have seen in some unstable tests and due to #1479. A workaround could be to remove this property completely and check the light type each time a command is processed, whether it is an OSRAM bulb and needs special handling. Unfortunately I have no OSRAM bulb to reproduce the bug and to retest a potential fix. 

However, as it does not happen with newer firmwares, is there a chance that we could remove the special OSRAM handling completely (it is currently anyway only implemented for PAR16 50 TW) and we require the users to use the latest firmware for their bulbs?

[2016-07-04T11:56:30Z | afuechsel | comment]
Any comments about removing the OSRAM hack completely? 

After analyzing this a bit, it turns out, that both this bug (where the isOsramPar16 is initialized too late) and also the spurious test failures, where the expected property value has not yet been set (https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1652#issuecomment-230226871) have the same reason: 

Previously, as properties could be stored, it happened that they threw a lot of exceptions and the initialize method was called several time until all properties have been set (see my analysis here: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/588#issuecomment-226458476). Therefore we removed in #1682 this feature, so properties will never be persisted. Unfortunately, due to #1479, now the initialize method initializing both the properties and the isOsramPar16 will sometimes be called too early. It is however ensured, that the properties will be set, after the bridge comes online.

[2016-07-04T12:26:47Z | afuechsel | comment]
Created #1799 which should fix this issue. I am lacking of OSRAM bulbs, so @joergkling could you please retest with this branch? The PR should also fix the sporadic test failures.

196 | Active   |  80 | 0.9.0.201607221840    | Eclipse SmartHome hue Binding

[2016-07-25T11:49:57Z | afuechsel | comment]
I would assume so. As I already commented on #1880, the removal of the initialization loop in HueBridgeHandler#onConnectionResumed could sometimes lead to the situation, that the properties would be initialized right before the polling loop resumed the connection so the lightId is still null and model or type values could not be retrieved. And so also the OSRAM hack would not work as the binding just does not know, that it's an OSRAM bulb. 

The whole problem with the hue binding is the asynchronous polling loop. If we could avoid the polling things would be easier. But as it stands, there is probably no other way then to poll for the changes. 

Any arguments against just adding the removed code lines again from #1880? Maybe @lolodomo could also jump in here and check.

title: RawType base64-encoded value is written to log file every time state changes
body:
Hi,

whenever an item changes, the ItemStateChangedEvent is logged (on info level), containing the old and the new state of an item:
`itemName + " changed from " + oldItemState.toString() + " to " + itemState.toString();`

If a RawType item has changed, the toString method of the RawType outputs its Base64-encoded value:
`PortableBase64.getEncoder().encode(bytes);`

This is not really nice as I don't need the binary file in my log file and this can increase the size of the log file quite fast.
comments:
[2016-07-04T06:42:53Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I agree, this should be avoided.
It would be nicest to implement RawType.toString() so that it comes up with something short like "binary content", but as the toString method is also used to have a full string representation from which types can be reconstructed again, this won't work.
So the better fix is probably to change the toString method of the item events in a way that they behave differently for RawTypes.

[2016-07-24T19:59:23Z | thhart | comment]
> but as the toString method is also used to have a full string representation from which types can be reconstructed again, this won't work

Can you explain this further please. Sorry for being this direct but IMHO it is not very good design to have a full Base64 encoding nor a full data return in a toString() method.

[2016-07-25T08:05:37Z | maggu2810 | comment]
IIRC:
Currenty every type should have a static method valueOf(String) that returns an instance of that type.
The instance should be equal to the one the toString method is called to receive the string.
So `Type.valueOf(type.toString()).equals(type)` should be true all the time.

[2016-09-28T15:17:24Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I think there are two options:
We could create a static function that returns a simplified string of the state for debugging purpose etc.
It can then skip the value encoding for RawType

``` java
    protected String getSimpleStateString(final State state) {
        if (state instanceof RawType) {
            return "<skip-raw-type-encoding>";
        } else {
            return state.toString();
        }
    }
```

This method could be used in [Group]ItemStateChangedEvent or whenever a message is logged.

Okay, but that does not look good as a static method does need to decide how a state should be logged and not the state class itself.

> Currenty every type should have a static method valueOf(String) that returns an instance of that type.
> The instance should be equal to the one the toString method is called to receive the string.
> So Type.valueOf(type.toString()).equals(type) should be true all the time.

For the first step we could (for the transition phase)
- change the Type interface to define two methods `toStringFull()` and `toStringSimple()`
- `toStringSimple()` should return a simplified string that does not need to contain the whole state (e.g. for RawType the first bytes + "...")
- `toStringFull()` behaves similar as the current `toString()` method (full string representation of the internal type)
- `toString()` logs a message + stack trace that one of the other methods should be used (e.g. info or debug level) AND returns the value of `toStringFull()`
- [Group]ItemStateChangedEvent could be changed to use `toStringSimple()`

If this has been done and all usages of `toString()` has been changed to full or simple (no code is broken in this time as toString() works as before just log some info to change the usage), we could use the refactor mechanism of the IDE to change toStringSimple to toString again (if this is what we want).

WDYT?

[2016-09-29T01:58:26Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I agree that option 1 is not really clean as we have some special handling in the event class for a certain type. Nonetheless, I wonder if we could say that RawType qualifies to be treated exceptionally - then we can consider this option to be the simplest way to solve the issue.

For option 2, I am not sure if we manage to reach everyone that relies on the current toString() behavior; planning to change it some time in the future means a backward compatibility breaking change, which I would like to avoid. Woudn't it be also an option to reduce it to introducing a new method Type.toSimpleString() and use this in the event class, while keeping toString() untouched?

[2016-09-29T06:03:21Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> Woudn't it be also an option to reduce it to introducing a new method Type.toSimpleString() and use this in the event class, while keeping toString() untouched?

Sure. It is only about that toString is the convenient method for logging (e.g. slf4j calls toString() implicitly etc.).

> For option 2, I am not sure if we manage to reach everyone that relies on the current toString() behavior; planning to change it some time in the future means a backward compatibility breaking change, which I would like to avoid.

We can use a very long transition phase and state that toString should not be used serialization if the whole internal information should be kept.
How is it different from all the other methods that are marked deprecated to remove them in e.g. after a new major release?

[2016-09-29T06:50:10Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> How is it different from all the other methods that are marked deprecated to remove them in e.g. after a new major release?

Well, most of the others were introduced as part of new APIs that were still under development and thus changed. The behavior of toString() is the same since the first commit in 2010 and thus has been a stable since the very beginning. Hence I feel that the risk is much higher to do changes to this, in comparison to changing newly introduced classes that not many people are anyhow familiar with yet.

[2016-09-29T08:23:07Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I have done some changes on my working copy, but know I don't know how to proceed.
Let's assume there is a full and a simple string generation method (we don't neet to care is toString() is the same as full or not, I just want to use clear names here).

At which places we do need a full string and where is a simple sufficient?
Does an Event require, that the one that receives the event is able to create a type that is equal to the data in the event?

Here some usages:
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemEventFactory.createStateChangedEvent
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemStateChangedEvent.toString
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemStateEvent.toString
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.jvmmodel.RulesJvmModelInferrer$1$2.accept
- at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.script.interpreter.ScriptInterpreter.getStateOrCommand

The question is where can we use the simple version?

[2016-09-29T09:04:58Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Does an Event require, that the one that receives the event is able to create a type that is equal to the data in the event?

Up to now, yes. E.g. the UIs get the event stream and dynamically update their views without the need to do any further requests to the server. The PaperUI also supports this for the image item type already.

We hence must make sure that the "payload" of the events is complete. So the following occurences need the full information:
- org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemEventFactory.createStateChangedEvent
- org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent

while 
- org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemStateChangedEvent.toString
- org.eclipse.smarthome.core.items.events.ItemStateEvent.toString
  could be simple.

The ones in rules/scripts probably are not applicable to raw types at all (you won't script an image...), but in general these should be the full version as well.

Why do we need to use that for rules?

PaperUI is not setting the properties field. It is returned in the response when a rule is requested. I think something is broken on the server side. [2016-07-05T09:39:25Z | maggu2810 | comment]
We are using often DTO objects for JSON (de)serialization.
This is not be done for the REST Rule API.

Here a map is used for the configuration and we translate between the map and the Configuration class object:
https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/dto/ThingDTO.java#L29

For the Rule REST API the Rule class is used directly and so the Configuration class, too.
https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/automation/org.eclipse.smarthome.automation.rest/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/automation/rest/internal/RuleResource.java#L162

As the key value pair of the Configuration class are set in the member properties of the Configuration class I assume that causes the need of the properties field.

It seems to me that the migration of the Rule API to use the Configuration class is not finished and we are now in a state where the REST API is broken.

What to do?

title: Discovery result toast links to wrong url
body: When a discovery result is created in the background, the toast links to "inbox/setup" and hence ends up on the page that lists the bindings, while it should instead link to "inbox/search" in order to show the current inbox entries.

title: Binding initialization stalls during startup (intermittently)
body:
There have been numerous reports of bindings "stalling" (for lack of a better word) at startup.  I have experienced the problem with the zwave and systeminfo bindings.  Others have reported similar behavior with knx, rfxcom, meteostick, and max.

I first noticed this behavior with the 6/19 build, and it continues through the most current build (#399). At the time I was installing builds on almost a daily basis, and I do not recall seeing this behavior in the 6/17 and prior builds (I think I skipped installing the 6/18 build, so I don't know about that one).  I started this forum thread, which has now become quite long.
https://community.openhab.org/t/binding-not-starting-consistently-since-6-19-build/11741

There are other forum threads describing similar behavior.  
Here.
https://community.openhab.org/t/z-wave-binding-things-initializing-after-restart/12173
And here.
https://community.openhab.org/t/testing-z-wave-binding-on-openhab-2/7522/1372

This originally was thought to be related to the circular reference issue.  However, the problem continues even after the circular reference fix.

There may be some relationship to the XML file loading issue, but perhaps not.
https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/1796

body:

    at java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock$Sync.tryRelease(ReentrantLock.java:151)[:1.8.0_101]

    at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing.internal.ThingManager$8$1.call(ThingManager.java:1)[102:org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing:0.9.0.201607221840]
    at org.eclipse.smarthome.core.common.SafeMethodCaller$CallableWrapper.call(SafeMethodCaller.java:177)[96:org.eclipse.smarthome.core:0.9.0.201607221840]
    at java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.run(FutureTask.java:266)[:1.8.0_101]
    at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1142)[:1.8.0_101]
    at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:617)[:1.8.0_101]
    at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)[:1.8.0_101]
```

The `LifxNetworkThrottler.unlock()` method always tries to release all locks. Even those of other threads. The exception seems to occur when a bulb is added that was not yet available before the `LifxLightHandler.broadcastPacket(..)` method called `LifxNetworkThrottler.lock()` .

As a result of this, the whole LIFX binding becomes unusable. The thread in which the exception occurs does not unlock all its locked ReentrantLocks .

Due to my setup this concurrency issue is often reproducible:
- 34 LIFX bulbs
- fast development PC (Skylake i7-6700K)

@cdjackson Yes, options are permitted in case they are true. Note that I kept all your alarm "Switch" channels in place with options (saying "Ok" and "Alarm"). My question is really if PaperUI shouldn't provide a toggle control even when options are provided. Ie the logic in PaperUI could have been that any control with type switch, use the toggle even if options are provided.  This would have allowed options to be specified, such that if someone used a text widget sitemap, it could be presented using the options.

[2016-09-12T06:04:27Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I think there is no general right answer, since we do not have the flexibility here as when using sitemaps where the user can specify whether he wants toggles or selection options instead.
As Paper UI is mainly for setup&testing the devices, I think it makes sense to show the option texts, if they are available - rendering a toggle would suppress this information, so you would not have a chance to see whether the options are correctly working.

>  I think it makes sense to show the option texts, if they are available - rendering a toggle would suppress this information, so you would not have a chance to see whether the options are correctly working.

Maybe, but you're telling me that in order to make the widget work in PaperUI, I'm not allowed to have state descriptions, so they aren't rendered anyway.

Let's leave it as it is untill after the next beta, but I think this logic is wrong. State descriptions should provide additional information that can be used in the UI, but the UI should be able to able to decide to render what it thinks is best with the various bits of information it has available.

[2016-09-12T06:43:36Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The Paper UI treats the state options like the Classic UI behaves when it finds "mappings" defined; if there is no special information (On/Off simply does not provide any additional info), this should be omitted.

As I said, this is only the case for the Paper UI, which is meant for administrative purposes and NOT for operation. On any other UI, the user can (e.g. through sitemaps) decide how it should be rendered.

[2016-09-12T07:55:07Z | cdjackson | comment]
> On/Off simply does not provide any additional info

But it does since by adding these states into the system, it can be internationalised. It can also be On/Off rather than the actual ON/OFF enum states.

> As I said, this is only the case for the Paper UI, which is meant for administrative purposes and NOT for operation

Sure - fully appreciate that, and again, the system should allow state descriptions to be added. Just because PaperUI doesn't support them is not a good reason to remove them (IMHO anyway).

title: ThingManager should adapt state updates to linked item type
body:
I have a hue light defined like this in hue.things:

```
Bridge hue:bridge:xxx "Philips Hue Bridge" [ ipAddress="192.168.1.3", userName="xxx" ] {
    0210 1 "Hue White and Color - Living Room Ceiling" @ "Living Room" [ lightId="1" ]
```

I want to have an on/off switch on my sitemap, so I defined an item for it as

```
Switch living_light_ceiling_switch "Living Room Ceiling Switch" <light> (gLights) { channel="hue:0210:xxx:1:color" }
```

I read in the documentation that I need to use the :color channel instead of :switch to make it work. So now I have a sitemap definition as

```
Switch living_light_ceiling_switch "Living Room Ceiling Switch" <light> (gLights) { channel="hue:0210:xxx:1:color" }
```

It works nicely as far as turning the light on and off from the UI but if I try to turn the light on/off from the real Hue app the state doesn't get updated in the classic UI or HABdroid. I see in the basic UI that it gets updated with its HSB value (68,88,0) instead of an ON/OFF state.

This is problematic because in openHAB 1.x I had quite a few rules depending on the ON/OFF state of the item, for example if conditions like (living_light_command is another switch item):

```
if (living_light_ceiling_switch.state != living_light_command.state) { ... }
```

 and now those are not working at all. Can this be fixed in the binding? Either create/enable the :switch channel for the thing, or make the :color channel converted to ON/OFF states when the items is a simple switch.

Issue #866 might be related, but I thought I better open a new issue for this, as that one is not really about this switch state problem. I understand that rewriting my rules to somehow check for the brightness value might work, but it's far from ideal and probably I'm not the only one who will be hit by this during transition to openHAB2.

Oh, and I'm using beta4.
comments:
[2016-10-05T07:47:47Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Thanks, @adarazs, this is indeed an unexpected behavior (let's call it bug :-)). It is actually NOT a problem within the hue binding itself, but needs to be fixed in the core ESH framework instead. I therefore adapted the issue title to make this clear.

[2016-10-05T17:09:11Z | adarazs | comment]
Thank you for acknowledging the bug, I mean behavior. :)

I think it's clear for you at this point but just stating that this also affects dimmer types too, not just switches.

For others fighting with the same problem, my workaround is:
- remove the hue link from the switch item
- add a rule that updates the switch items periodically directly from the "color" type items like this:

``` java
// for color lights
postUpdate(living_light_ceiling_switch, if(living_light_ceiling_color.state.toString.split(",").get(2) == "0") OFF else ON)
// for dimmer only lights
postUpdate(dress_light_switch, if(dress_light_dimmer.state.toString == "0") OFF else ON)
```

Now the switch items are actually updated properly to their ON/OFF state and can be used in rules, but cannot be used to control the lights (use the color or dimmer items instead). It would be also possible to add rules that change the dimmer/color items when the switches receive a command, but I didn't do that.

title: Duplicate channels on Thing
body:
A thing's channels are stored as a List<Channel> , see 

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/e0985e90d389350580e59bfbcd7e0adaaccf7519/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/ThingImpl.java#L49

Because this is a list, its possible for a Thing to have duplicate channels with the same ID. This also means that calling "getChannel(String id)" will only return the first instance of the duplicate channel. My assumption would be that a thing can only have a single instance of a channel.
comments:
[2016-10-05T14:24:33Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
See also https://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/t/1081737/

[2016-10-06T12:54:32Z | sjsf | comment]
@kaikreuzer in the forum discussion you mentioned to use a SortedSet. However, from a user's perspective it makes sense to keep the order in the same way as the channels were defined. Therefore a LinkedHashSet would make more sense IMHO.

However, changing the List to a Set would break pretty much everything. You sure this is a good idea? I'd suggest to ensure uniqueness internally only and keep the API stable.

[2016-10-06T13:03:44Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
You are right, a LinkedHashSet would be the implementation that retains the given order, a SortedSet might actually mess it up by sorting it itself.

> However, changing the List to a Set would break pretty much everything. You sure this is a good idea?

I didn't suggest this, I only said that this should have better be done from the start.

>  I'd suggest to ensure uniqueness internally only and keep the API stable.

Yes, we should simply add some checks, that should be good enough. Probably mainly the ThingBuilder needs to be fixed.

title: Basic UI does not update icons of read only switches
body:
I've done some more testing with the functionality provided by #2030 and it seems that icons of read only switches in the Basic UI are not properly updated. I typically use these for representing the state of motion/smoke/CO sensors.

You can easily reproduce this in the demo by replacing the `Group demo` in `demo.sitemap` with

```
        Text label="Group Demo" icon="firstfloor" {
            Switch item=Lights mappings=[OFF="All Off"]
            Group item=Heating
            Group item=Windows
            Text item=Temperature
            Switch item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling
            Text item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling
        }
```

and replacing the definition of `Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` in `demo.items` with:

```
Switch Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling     "Ceiling [%s]" <switch> (gC, Lights)
```

When you then switch `Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` or `Lights mappings`, the icon of `Switch item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` is properly updated. 

However the icon of `Text item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` is not.

Only after reloading the page it will again represent the right state.

Another way to reproduce it is to open `Group Demo > Open windows`. And issue the following commands in the console:

```
smarthome:update Window_GF_Frontdoor OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Kitchen OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Living OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Toilet OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bath OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bed OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Window OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Door OPEN
smarthome:update Garage_Door OPEN
```

Now all window icons should be open. But they only are after reloading the page. The same way windows should be closed after issuing:

```
smarthome:update Window_GF_Frontdoor CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Kitchen CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Living CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Toilet CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bath CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bed CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Window CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Door CLOSED
smarthome:update Garage_Door CLOSED
```

title: VoiceManager fails to find suitable voice
body:
There is some problem with the selection of the right voice to use in VoiceManager.

If e.g. MaryTTS is installed, you have:

```
openhab> voice voices
marytts:bits1hsmm bits1-hsmm (de)
marytts:cmuslthsmm cmu-slt-hsmm (en_US)
marytts:bits3hsmm bits3-hsmm (de)
```

Calling

```
openhab> voice say test
```

results in 

```
21:39:47.778 [ERROR] [se.smarthome.core.voice.VoiceManager] - Error saying 'test ': Unable to find a voice for language de
```

When the locale (in Configuration->System) is set to "de" instead of "de_DE", TTS works as expected.

title: NTP Tests bug, when time is changed
body:
In the NTP Binding Tests the "Europe/Helsinki" time zone is used. But recently there has been a time change in this time zone and that broke two of the tests:

1) 'if no time zone is set in the configuration, the string channel is updated with the default one'

The message is:
The string channel was not updated with the right timezone
Expected: is "EEST"
     but: was "EET"

Aparently the abbreviation EEST(Eastern European Summer Time) is used only in summer and now that the time is changed the abbreviation, that is returned is EET(Eastern European Time) - https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/eest

2) 'if no time zone is set in the configuration, the dateTime channel is updated with the default one'

The message is:
The dateTime channel was not updated with the right timezone
Expected: is "+0300"
     but: was "+0200"

Now that the time is changed, the current offset is +0200, not +0300

I have made a PR with a fix for this: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/2377

[2016-11-17T18:06:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Further investigation showed that I had a binding, which declared a certain Thing type to be a bridge, but instantiated a ThingHandler and not a BridgeHandler for it - as a result, [this code](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/BridgeImpl.java#L69) returned null, although a handler was set in the Thing.

2. Enforce ThingHandlerFactories to return BridgeHandlers for Bridges.

title: BaseThingHandler:channelLinked() called frequently / too much
body:
In a simple setup with a single Item -> Channel definition in the DSL, the above method is called three times (for the given channel) at startup of the runtime, twice triggered by ThingManager.added() and once by ItemRegistry.allItemsChanged(). 

Expected behaviour would be that the method is called once for each time an Item definition is parsed, taking into account the fact that "temporary" items are created. 

In my use case the channelLinked() triggers a read request on a bus (e.g. KNX), which is not designed to be flooded in this way, especially when reading out the same value multiple times.

title: ClassCastException in HandlerFactories
body:

Before the Thing refactoring, this code was working, so it seems that this must be some bug in the framework, not in the bindings. See a log here:

title: ThingHandlers stay UNINITIALIZED of registration runs into timeout
body:
The method `ThingManager.registerChildHandlers()` has the following code:

```
                        registerHandler(child);
                        initializeHandler(child);
```
Within `registerHandler` the handler registration is done in a "Safe" call, i.e. it might return after 5 seconds without having successfully registered the handler by that time.
As a result, `initializeHandler` will simply do nothing, since it checks whether the handler is correctly registered already.

The outcome is that the Thing stays in UNINITIALIZED state indefinitely.

[This seems to be like a report](https://community.openhab.org/t/binding-handler-registration-issues/17422) of exactly that situation.

[2016-11-30T08:02:20Z | sjsf | comment]
btw, we have this pattern 4 times within the ThingManager, i.e. everywhere where registerHandler(...) ist called. Therefore I think it would make sense to remove the SafeMethodCaller from the doRegisterHandler block and protect the above to lines instead together, so it is ensured the second line will always be executed after the handler was registered, even if it took too long.

body:
I have set the language and locale to "German" resp. "de_DE". The PaperUi shows the translated names of the things but the "...description" entries in the properties file are ignored. 

This is an example from the Yahoo Weather binding:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/616792/20861883/7f82ce60-b99b-11e6-98d6-d1da5d67c33f.png)

[2016-12-04T09:47:42Z | MHerbst | comment]
I set everything in the Paper UI (under Preferences I selected German and under System/Locale I set the locale to de_DE).
I tried it again this morning and have some additional information that may help. For the Homematic things the display texts are correct under Things/Configuration:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/616792/20865302/88ca711c-ba0e-11e6-9a3c-af413f6cd271.png)

BTW: as you can see in the screenshot also the name of Yahoo binding and its description is not shown in the correct language.

The Homematic binding does not use the i18n properties files. So it seems that the problem happens only with i18n properties files.

[2016-12-12T21:04:32Z | MHerbst | comment]
I have some additional information from some tests with the REST API. IF I execute this request with "Accept-Language" set to "de"
```
curl -X GET --header "Accept: application/json" --header "Accept-Language: de" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/rest/bindings"
```
I get the correct german description for the binding. If I set "Accept-Language" to "de_DE" or if I leave it empty the english text is returned.

[2016-12-14T10:31:13Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Thanks for the analysis. So it is clearly not an issue of the Paper UI, but rather a bug on the server side / REST API.

[2016-12-14T18:13:18Z | MHerbst | comment]
It seems so, but I not absolutely sure yet. Maybe it is combination of Paper/Basic UI and server side. In my test I create an own REST request. 
I have planned to perform more tests and log the REST request that were executed by Basic and Paper UI with different combinations of language and locale.

[2016-12-16T21:37:21Z | MHerbst | comment]
@kaikreuzer I have executed some more tests and to me it looks like there is a either problem with the language string passed to methods implementing the REST API or the method that tries to parse the language is implemented too simple. In my test environment I used a fresh openHAB installation (Build 644), no explicit locale was set and language in preferences was set to "German" (same as the browser language). 

I have debugged method `org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.core.binding.BindingResource#getAll` and these are the results:

**Test 1:** REST request with explicit "Accept-Language: de" ()
```
curl -X GET --header "Accept: application/json" --header "Accept-Language: de" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/rest/bindings"
```
The parameter `language` contains the value "de" and a correct locale is constructed from the language and so the results are OK.

**Test 2:** REST request without "Accept-Language"
```
curl -X GET --header "Accept: application/json" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/rest/bindings"
```
Now parameter `language` contains this value `de,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.6` and the method created a locale from this language:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/616792/21278594/7327b4be-c3dc-11e6-9ab3-7eae027670e5.png)

To me this does not look like a valid locale.

**Test 3**: I opened URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/ui/index.html#/configuration/bindings
Parameter `language` again has this value: "de,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.6"

**Test 4**: Set locale to de_DE and performed "Test 3" again
Same result as Test 3.

**Test 5:** Similar to Test 2 but with a browser that uses english as language
Now parameter `language` contains value "en-US,en;q=0.5". This will work correct because "en" is separated from the string and then used as locale:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/616792/21279002/622ac8e8-c3de-11e6-9de1-8b75dff441db.png)
This is a correct definition.

**Test 6**: English browser with preference language set to "German" and then I openend URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/ui/index.html#/configuration/bindings
Language has the value "en-US,en;q=0.5".

This explains why locales other then english do not work correct. Either the content of the language string passed to server is wrong or method `LocaleUtil#getLocale` (that simply splits the language string at the first "-" to get the language) does not fit to the content of the language string.

Another result of my test is that the language setting under "Preferences" seems not to work because always the browser language is used. 
BTW: why these different ways to set a language? We have the browser language, the language that can be set under _Preferences_ and also the locale definition under _System_. The locale definition is important because it defines more then just language. But is the language under _Preferences_ really necessary? 

Before performing further tests and fixing the other issues related to locales I think this problem needs to be solved.

[2016-12-23T14:19:18Z | MHerbst | comment]
I have created a PR (#2699) that solves this problem that is caused by the wrong interpretation of the Accept-Language HTTP header. But the language handling in Paper UI in general seems not to work correct (e.g. the preferences settings seems to be ignored). I will do some further testing and create a new issue for that.

title: Config parameters normalisation not working for thing parameters
body:
I'm seeing some parameters being stored in the jsondb as a STRING when they are defined as INTEGER.

My guess is that this is happening in the normalisation code. The parameters in question are in the thing config descriptions - not the thing-type.

This is more obvious when using HABmin since HABmin only sends updates to parameters that have changed - if I don't change these parameters, then nothing is sent in the REST interface, but these parameters are being changed to STRING. PaperUI is sending the parameter as a number, and it's getting stored as 12.0 in json which is still wrong, but it does at least work in this instance.

I assume that whatever code does the normalisation is using the config descriptor for the thing-type, and not the thing itself. Possibly [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/48e405fb3f1e60b56333e26bd42021bd5cfc1bc8/bundles/io/org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.core/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/rest/core/thing/ThingResource.java#L671).

Having updated the zwave binding to allow [textual thing definitions](https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/issues/153), the binding no longer functions if parameters are updated with the UI.

[2017-01-03T11:42:45Z | sjsf | comment]
On a first glance it looks like the GenericThingProvider still "knows" about the old Thing being there, so it informs its listeners about an  `update`.  On the other hand, the ThingManager (being of of these listeners) does NOT seem know the old version (anymore?). 

I'm wondering why the ThingManager maintains its own cache at all and does not use the ThingRegistry. 

I'm now trying to figure out why the data model became inconsistent... Maybe the root-case could be the `dispose()`-`initialize()` taking too long, but I'm not sure yet.

[2017-01-03T12:16:00Z | sjsf | comment]
Okay, wrong guess as it turns out...

It seems that the [GenericThingProvider](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.thing/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/thing/internal/GenericThingProvider.xtend#L409) does not catch Things nested within the Bridge, assumes they are removed and informs its listeners accordingly. As a result, the "update" later on fails. 

Now I'm only wondering if and why this ever worked an will provide a fix.

PS: As a work-around if you don't want to restart your OH every time, you could temporarily define your things like this:

```
Bridge rfxcom:bridge:1 [ serialPort="/dev/ttyUSB1" ] {}

Thing rfxcom:lighting2:remote1_1 (rfxcom:bridge:1) [deviceId="12260194.1", subType="AC"]
Thing rfxcom:lighting2:remote1_2 (rfxcom:bridge:1) [deviceId="12260194.2", subType="AC"]
Thing rfxcom:lighting2:remote1_3 (rfxcom:bridge:1) [deviceId="12260194.3", subType="AC"]
Thing rfxcom:lighting2:remote1_0 (rfxcom:bridge:1) [deviceId="12260194.0", subType="AC"]
```

Just keep in mind that you will end up with different UIDs in that case.

[2017-01-03T20:39:14Z | metbril | comment]
I actually copied this syntax from the example for the Hue binding, that has been there ages ago.

```
Bridge hue:bridge:1 [ ipAddress="192.168.0.64" ] {
	0210 bulb1 [ lightId="1" ]
	0220 bulb2 [ lightId="2" ]
}
```

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.hue/README.md

[2017-01-04T09:09:04Z | sjsf | comment]
Yes, and this syntax is correct and your are fully right to use it - and until 3 weeks ago it actually was working. I only wanted to tell you about a workaround until the fix reaches your OH2 installation.

title: PaperUI, text entry and annoying shifting
body:
In the PaperUI->Control - if you have a channel that is a simple string and start typing letters, eventually you'll enter the 8th character and the whole field shifts down a line.

The problem with the shift down is that the field loses focus.  Especially annoying is if you click it again and backspace once (so we have 7 characters) - it shifts back up and loses focus again. This behavior makes it very difficult to enter something in.

I'd rather it either get's focus (and the carot position is after the last character) or the field simply scrolls

title: Hue Binding: No status update for things with Id 0000/0010
body:
Have an issue here when items are being switched on/off via external app or switch (eg. Hue App):
- items with thing Id 210 are being updated in openhab
- items with thing Id 0000 or 0010 (Switches) are not being updated in openhab (no log entries)

There is no log entry either for items where status is not being updated. With my configuration I can control all items via openhab2. When controlled with openhab2, status changes accordingly. Issue is effective with external controls only.

title: [REST Api] Inconsistent response of REST-Api for items with mapped values
body:
I'm currently using openHAB 2 build #692 with the following items / map Definition (as also described here: [https://community.openhab.org/t/mapping-of-item-values-not-correctly-shown-in-habpanel/19518](url))
```
Contact Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed  "Wohnzimmerfenster 1 [MAP(de.map):%s]" (Wohnzimmer, Wohnung_Fenster) { channel="max:shuttercontact:NEQ0897054:LEQ0791036:contact_state" }

Contact Wohnzimmer_Fenster2_OpenClosed  "Wohnzimmerfenster 2 [MAP(de.map):%s]" (Wohnzimmer, Wohnung_Fenster) { channel="max:shuttercontact:NEQ0897054:LEQ0790888:contact_state" }
```
de.map:
```
CLOSED=zu
OPEN=offen
```
When I make a REST-Api call 
`http://homenuc:8080/rest/items/Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed/state`

it returns **always** CLOSED respectively OPEN

When you call the item with
`http://homenuc:8080/rest/items/Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed`
 
returns the mapped value "zu" and "offen" beside the key "state":
```
{
  "link": "http://homenuc:8080/rest/items/Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed",
  "state": "zu",
  "stateDescription": {
    "pattern": "",
    "readOnly": false,
    "options": []
  },
  "type": "Contact",
  "name": "Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed",
  "label": "Wohnzimmerfenster 1",
  "tags": [],
  "groupNames": [
    "Wohnzimmer",
    "Wohnung_Fenster"
  ]
}
```

The same also when calling it via a "sitemaps" call like:

`http://homenuc:8080/rest/sitemaps/zuHause?jsoncallback=callback` 

```
"widgets": [
                      {
                        "widgetId": "Wohnzimmer_0",
                        "type": "Text",
                        "label": "Wohnzimmerfenster 1 [zu]",
                        "icon": "contact",
                        "mappings": [],
                        "item": {
                          "link": "http://homenuc:8080/rest/items/Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed",
                          "state": "zu",
                          "stateDescription": {
                            "pattern": "",
                            "readOnly": false,
                            "options": []
                          },
                          "type": "Contact",
                          "name": "Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed",
                          "label": "Wohnzimmerfenster 1",
                          "tags": [],
                          "groupNames": [
                            "Wohnzimmer",
                            "Wohnung_Fenster"
                          ]
                        },
                        "widgets": []

```

On  the "Event channel" it is also always "unmapped". This leads for example in HABpanel to the problem that the values are "jumping" between their mapped and unmapped representation dependent of the way the last call was made.

I would have had expected, that the values are always send in der mapped representations via the REST Api.

Kind regards,

André

[2017-01-10T12:14:05Z | sjsf | comment]
This inconsistency indeed is weird... Thanks for reporting this!

Before I break bazillions of SmartHome solutions: Does anybody (@kaikreuzer, @cdjackson?) know any good reason for the states NOT being transformed at those two places (i.e. rest/items/.../state and in the Events)?

[2017-01-10T13:19:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Before I break bazillions of SmartHome solutions

You are standing a good chance to do so ;-)

> any good reason for the states NOT being transformed at those two places (i.e. rest/items/.../state and in the Events)?

They simply provide the REAL item state, i.e. the full truth. Note that item states are for "headless" use, i.e. not UI related at all.

When defining an item like

```
Contact Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed  "Wohnzimmerfenster 1 [MAP(de.map):%s]" 
```

you have to note that the part in quotes specifies a "default label" to use, if no other label is specified in a UI. So while there is one single state of the item, it might have many different visual representations depending on its usage. That's why the sitemap endpoint provides the mapped state (but note that you could have specified the mapping in the sitemap as well and this could be a different one than the default given in the item file).

So the remaining question is (which also came up in the android client related discussion): Do we need an additional field in the EnrichedItemDTO containing the mapped value?

From my (maybe to simple) understanding I would assume "yes". The mapping is often used as a translation of the language or a translation to have a better understanding of the meaning of the value. If the REST-Api omits that, every UI which uses the REST services directly would have to implement such a translated view. Wouldn't it then be better to define a translation at one place and provide that as an alternative view to all UIs via the REST Api?

title: Fix events and event order fired by the automation module
body:
When a rule is added the first NOT_INITIALIZED event is redundant.
For example:
osgi> 14:28:16.652 INFO  s.event.RuleStatusInfoEvent[:43] - rule_3 updated: NOT_INITIALIZED
14:28:16.657 INFO  s.event.RuleStatusInfoEvent[:43] - rule_3 updated: IDLE
14:28:16.658 DEBUG o.e.s.c.c.r.AbstractManagedProvider[:62] - Added new element rule_3 to ManagedRuleProvider.
14:28:16.658 INFO  smarthome.event.RuleAddedEvent[:43] - Rule 'rule_3' has been added.

or when the rule can't be resolved, the following events are fired:
osgi> 14:28:16.652 INFO  s.event.RuleStatusInfoEvent[:43] - rule_3 updated: NOT_INITIALIZED
14:28:16.657 INFO  s.event.RuleStatusInfoEvent[:43] - rule_3 updated: NOT_INITIALIZED
14:28:16.658 DEBUG o.e.s.c.c.r.AbstractManagedProvider[:62] - Added new element rule_3 to ManagedRuleProvider.
14:28:16.658 INFO  smarthome.event.RuleAddedEvent[:43] - Rule 'rule_3' has been added.

1) The first one NOT_INITIALIZED must be skiped
2) Order of events should be:
- Rule 'rule_3' has been added.
- rule_3 updated: NOT_INITIALIZED
- rule_3 updated: IDLE
comments:
[2017-01-13T13:31:29Z | danchom | comment]
May be the NOT_INITIALIZED  should not be fired in case of resolved rule:
At the moment the events are:
1) added/updated -> NOT_INITIALIZED  -> IDLE <->RUNNING
2) added/updated -> NOT_INITIALIZED
3) DISABLED -> NOT_INITIALIZED  -> IDLE <->RUNNING
4) DISABLED -> NOT_INITIALIZED
5) IDLE / RUNNING -> NOT_INITIALIZED ->DISABLED
6) NOT_INITIALIZED ->DISABLED

but they should be:

1) added/updated -> IDLE <->RUNNING
2) added/updated -> NOT_INITIALIZED
3) DISABLED -> IDLE <->RUNNING
4) DISABLED -> NOT_INITIALIZED
5) IDLE / RUNNING / NOT_INITIALIZED ->DISABLED

What do you thing?

[2017-01-13T17:30:11Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The current situation is similar to [what we have on the Things](https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/concepts/things.html#status-transitions). The important information here is that the state actually describes the handler status and the thing status at the same time - UNINITIALIZED describes the handler and it is a natural status on the transition to getting a Thing to ONLINE.

But I am open to discuss to follow a different logic for the rules - i.e. only describing the status of a rule itself (and NOT_INITIALIZED simply means that there is some issue with a handler, be it that they are not there or that something is misconfigured). So your suggestion sounds fine to me.

@maggu2810 & @sjka, do you have any comments?

[2017-01-15T11:28:00Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I don't see a real cons if we change the status for rules at the moment, so okay for me.

[2017-01-16T07:35:50Z | sjsf | comment]
I'm okay with changing them now. However, one thought about the name of the state: For Things we use UNINITIALIZED instead of NOT_INITIALIZED. IMHO we should strive for consistency throughout the project. Especially as the meaning is more or less the same.

[2017-01-16T09:24:27Z | danchom | comment]
There is one cons, when a rule is added it will be without status until it goes into IDLE or NOT_INITILIAZED (uninitialized - I'm ok to change the name). If someone call getStatus(theRule) it will receive null. This can be long time in case of deadlock of handler initialization. May be it is better to have INITIALIZING status for this period of time.
For example:
added -> initializing -> idle
added -> initializing -> not_initialized
because at the moment we have:
added -> not_initialized(without statusDetails) -> idle
added -> not_initialized(without statusDetails) -> not_initialized(with statusDetails) , which I think is not sufficient. 
What do you think?

[2017-01-16T10:11:35Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Introducing INITIALIZING, we would then be very close to the Things statuses, which isn't bad.
But note that the state diagram of the Things say that UNINITIALIZED is the starting point.
So we would actually have:
added -> UNINITIALIZED -> INITIALIZING -> IDLE
added -> UNINITIALIZED -> INITIALIZING -> UNINITIALIZED (with details)

I think we should use the same definition in this case. Imho there is no need to send an event for the first "UNINITIALIZED" status after a rule has been added (this could simply be set internally and returned, if anybody calls getStatus() at that time). Looking at what we get as events, we would hence end up with what you suggest.

[2017-01-16T10:46:54Z | danchom | comment]
>added -> UNINITIALIZED -> INITIALIZING -> IDLE
added -> UNINITIALIZED -> INITIALIZING -> UNINITIALIZED (with details)

this is ok for me. I think also there is no need of event for the first UNINITIALIZED(without details) state.

title: Module outputs are not available in scripts
body:
The values of outputs of other modules are made available to script, which is also directly supported by the rule editor:

![screen shot 2017-01-18 at 10 15 23](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3244965/22057952/507b7474-dd67-11e6-88b9-7b4b69045d65.png)

When trying to access those outputs, an exception is thrown.

The problem is that in the rule context, they are made available as e.g. "1.newState", which is provided as a map 1->newState in within the rule execution context. It is probably rather a bad idea to define "1" as a variable name...
comments:
[2017-01-18T16:36:08Z | danchom | comment]
The keys of outputs in rule context are in form "moduleId.outputId". Here  "1.newState" the 1 is the moduleId. If you have modules of the same module type (they will have same output uids), what "newState" will you get?

[2017-01-18T16:37:46Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
See https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/2850#issue-201521946.

[2017-01-18T16:41:51Z | danchom | comment]
ok but if you have 2 item modules
print(context.get('1.newState')) - will return the state of the first one
print(context.get('2.newState')) -  will return the state of the second one
print(newState) - what will return this? State of the first or the second item?

[2017-01-18T16:45:08Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> what will return this?

Undefined, it might be the one or the other. That's why you should use the other option in case you have the same output id twice.

[2017-01-18T19:24:39Z | danchom | comment]
For me, the right way here, is to use inputs in script module and the script must be write using them. In that way the scripts can be reused and will not depend on state of the system (The inputs always will be available, the outputs of other modules can missed in rule context). Btw the inputs are also in available in rule context under their names.

[2017-01-18T20:32:21Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
@danchom We discussed that already a long time ago: You are mixing up users with developers here.
Only developers have a chance to define a module TYPE (on which they could declare inputs that their script needs). But the usecase at hand here is for the (expert) end user: He uses the existing "ScriptAction" and can get hold of the rule context to do fancy stuff. Note that this "user" feature has been introduced a long time ago already and the Paper UI supports offering the outputs since a few months. And imho, this is a very neat feature for the end user.

What you are talking about are rather "scripted action types" - this is something that will be addressed with https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1783. And yes, there you would clearly define inputs for your scripted type, so that you can easily match it etc. But this means that the script is part of the module type and not of the module itself.

[2017-01-19T07:23:05Z | danchom | comment]
May be I was not clear, I'm not talking about #1783. My proposal was to add some numbers of inputs (5 or 10) to the current ScriptCondition and ScriptAction module types. In that way the users will have ability  connect them to outputs of other modules (module connections are not part of the module type, they are part of rule creation and can be done by the users) and the advance users will have opportunity to write scripts using these connected inputs (the rule engine set their values and make available in the rule context).
The current approach has followin cons:
- Only the outputs of the module which was triggered are available in the rule context. For example : 
1 - is  ItemTrigger module for the first item
2 -  is  ItemTrigger module for the second item
and the first Item change its state
print(context.get('1.newState')) - will print the new state 
print(context.get('2.newState')) - won't be available in rule context. (because at the moment all the outputs are stateless)
print(context.get('newState')) - won't know state of which item is printed.
BTW I want to open discussion about stateless / stateful outputs. I know that we have discuss this but I think we can do some improvements. I'll add an issue about that, 

- this script "print(context.get('1.newState'))" can't be reused or can stop working because it relays on the module name. When the user change the name of the module, the rule will be compromised.

[2017-01-19T08:14:50Z | sjsf | comment]
> My proposal was to add some numbers of inputs (5 or 10) to the current ScriptCondition and ScriptAction module types.

Why do you think it's convenient to have a fixed number of inputs and force the user to wire them in an additional step? In the end, the user will have to "remember" what exactly "input3" was. I can really recommend trying this out yourself!

> Only the outputs of the module which was triggered are available in the rule context.

Of course, this is what I would expect. What kind of useful input should come module wich did _not_ trigger the rule?

> When the user change the name of the module, the rule will be compromised.

As will it be when the user changes item names... Of course, this is expected!

[2017-01-19T08:21:12Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
@danchom My PR #2850 is meant to provide a solution for the "simple rule editor" as discussed in https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/2763#issuecomment-272826754 and I think this addresses it nicely.

Your ideas regarding script actions with defined inputs is something that would only be relevant for a (not yet existing) expert rule editor. Ok for me to discuss what makes sense there , but I think it should be an independent discussion and not block #2850.

[2017-01-19T09:21:55Z | danchom | comment]
@Kai, I'm not blocking #2850, I just share our experience and how we implemented these module types. I'm ok the current PR to be merged.
@sjka 
>Why do you think it's convenient to have a fixed number of inputs

It's not convenient to have a fixed number and I'll open discussion to invent a way to define them dynamically (in time of rule creation)  
>and force the user to wire them in an additional step

This is normal way to exchange dynamic data between modules. Through the connections the user define (shows) source input data. At the moment you don't have opportunity to see your scriptCondition which item it checks.  
Also with the inputs you have opportunity to write scripts which other users can use in their rules. For example: The script: input1 + input2 + input3 + input4 + input5 will sum data of connected inputs and this script can be used independent of the state of the system and can be used in different usecase.
>Of course, this is what I would expect. What kind of useful input should come module wich did not trigger the rule?

There are different type of outputs. For example ItemTriggers.newState is example of stateful output, The timestamp of the TimerTrigger is stateless output. Why we need a stateful outputs?  For example if you want to create a rule which has to be executed when two items are ON, and do this with two comparator conditions (yes can do this ItemStateCondition but this is just an example and it only compare item states, it can't do some other complicated logic base on the state o fitems). Unfortunately this can't work because only one (the changed one) of comparators can be evaluated, the other won't receive input and logic and may be failed.
>As will it be when the user changes item names...

As Kai said the "advanced user" will write the script (script programmer), the user of home system, can decide to change a name of trigger of rule in his home and will brake the logic of script programmer. I think this is a real use case.

title: Switch Groups changing to UNDEF
body:
With OH2 GA (might also occur with other versions) I do face an issue with Group:Switch:OR going to "UNDEF" instead of ON or OFF.

I do own some motion sensors (Homematic HM-Sen-MDIR-O-2) and "itemized" them as follows:

```
Group:Switch:OR(ON,OFF) gMotion "Motion detected"
Switch M1 "Motion Sensor #1" <motion> (gMotion) { channel="homematic:..." }
Switch M2 "Motion Sensor #2 " <motion> (gMotion)  { channel="homematic:..." }
```
However, the group's state only is ON or OFF if both sensors have the same state. If their state's differ, the group reports itself as UNDEF.

On motion, the event.log prints

```
[GroupItemStateChangedEvent] - gMotion changed from OFF to UNDEF through M1
[ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - M1 changed from OFF to ON
```
later:

```
[ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - M1 changed from ON to OFF
[GroupItemStateChangedEvent] - gMotion changed from UNDEF to OFF through M1
Source of Issue (issue reported by m0wlheldChristoph Dahlen):
https://community.openhab.org/t/issue-with-group-switch-or-going-to-undef/21403
```

My findings:
If all switches are OFF, the group is OFF
If only one or several are ON, then the group is UNDEF
If all are ON, the group is ON

###################
I checked another group of 30 switches. All have changed from NULL to OFF after starting OH. The group then switches from NULL to OFF too, when the last item of the group switches to OFF.
`gStickyUnreach changed from NULL to OFF through Win_Kind1_StickyUnreach`

So far so good.

But when I change one switch to ON, the group goes UNDEF for some reason.
```
2017-02-18 11:34:46.020 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - Heiz_WohnZ_StickyUnreach changed from OFF to ON
2017-02-18 11:34:46.023 [GroupItemStateChangedEvent] - gStickyUnreach changed from OFF to UNDEF through Heiz_WohnZ_StickyUnreach
```

title: Installing Rules Engine Crashes Event Source
body:
It seems that when I install the Rules engine (either through PaperUI or by hitting the endpoint `http://{ip_addr}/rest/extensions/misc-ruleengine/install`) the event stream crashes, hence why the loading spinner never completes in PaperUI.

Steps to reproduce:
- `curl http://{ip_addr}/rest/events` to listen to the event stream.
- Install the rules engine in PaperUI > Add-ons > Misc > Install Rules Engine (Experimental)
- *curl process gets terminated and loading spinner never completes*

Our app depends on the Rules engine, so it needs to be able to listen for the install completed event. I've tried installing other extensions and I can see them being logged when they're installed/uninstalled. This seems to only happen when installing the Rules engine.
comments:
[2017-03-13T21:26:22Z | RyanRamchandar | comment]
Yes, I'm seeing the same thing and I am able to reproduce this with your steps.

[2017-03-13T21:42:33Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Could you investigate, why the Paper UI actually succeeds to receive the event? For me the spinner stops and I can see the "Rule Engine installed" notification.
It only fails to do so, if at the same time I also do the curl command. Maybe there is some issue with providing SSE events to different receivers at the same time?

[2017-03-14T00:20:37Z | jvivanco28 | comment]
If I don't `curl` the event stream, the callback still never happens and the loading spinner animates indefinitely. I'm running my own instance of openhab where nothing is listening to the event stream.

I just tried installing/uninstalling some of the other extensions in Add-ons > Misc and this happens to a few others as well. **Google Calendar Scheduler** never receives the finished callback when installing, but it does receive the finished callback when uninstalling. **HomeKit Integration** doesn't receive the finished callback for either installing or uninstalling. **Hue Emulation** receives the finished callback when installing, but doesn't when uninstalling. This is very odd.

I'm experience similar behaviour on both openhab 2.0.0 and 2.1.0-snapshot. I'm not entirely sure how to debug this.

[2017-05-02T07:19:40Z | htreu | comment]
Here are my findings regarding the loss of SSE connection during/after extension install:

The problem occurs only on extensions which extend the REST API of ESH. During install/uninstall of these extensions the OSGi JAX RS bridge ([found here](https://github.com/hstaudacher/osgi-jax-rs-connector/blob/master/bundles/com.eclipsesource.jaxrs.publisher/src/com/eclipsesource/jaxrs/publisher/internal/ServletContainerBridge.java)) recognises a change in REST resource configuration and   calls `reload` on the underlying ServletContainer (find sources [here](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/glassfish/jersey/containers/jersey-container-servlet-core/2.22.1/)). ServletContainer#reload will then shutdown the ApplicationHandler (which handles all requests and also serves as a ContainerLifecycleListener for all resources, sources [here](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/glassfish/jersey/core/jersey-server/2.22.1/)) and create a new ApplicationHandler with the changed resource config.

I assume the effect we are seeing here is a race condition between the SSE thread and the OSGI JAX RS bridge. Sometimes the SSE comes first and is able to provide feedback to the UI. Nevertheless will the SSE connection be broken after the ServletContainer reloads all resources.

[2017-11-08T13:03:39Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
There does not seem to be any good way to address this issue with the current REST API implementation (that is based on Jersey). So I think we should close this as a won't fix.

It has been easy to find the (first) root cause of the problem. It is caused by some singletons that are created and kept over the bundle lifecycle. So, we break the whole OSGi concept here.
There are different places such "getInstance()" logic is used.

Does it make sense to invest time to solve this one and refactor some classes?

If #1783 is finished, are that bundle obsolete some time?

[2017-03-19T08:43:23Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Unfortunately, #1783 won't make those bundles obsolete as we will still support Xbase as a scripting language to be backward compatible.

Note that the singletons were introduced because of many issues with Guice, which is internally used by Xtext. I am not saying that it cannot be solved, but a while ago I already spent significant time on getting this stuff to work at all. It won't be easy to solve the refresh issue, but I agree it should be done.

title: Group Item Does Not Have Valid Defaults For Group:Dimmer and Group:Switch
body:
The Item syntax in `Items.xtext` clearly indicates that the `ModelGroupFunction` is optional, even if the `ModelItemType` is specified. However, at least with `Group:Dimmer` and `Group:Switch` (without a `ModelGroupFunction`), declarations like
```
Group:Dimmer   bedroom_dimmers
Group:Switch   bedroom_switches
```
result in an error 
```
[ERROR] [arthome.core.items.dto.ItemDTOMapper] - Group function 'AND' requires two arguments. Using Equality instead.
```
This is in conflict with the openHAB documentation at http://docs.openhab.org/configuration/items.html#groups

> By default, if no function is provided to the group, the Group uses OR.

Pretty clearly, that's wrong, between the error message, and it not working.

Expected Behavior:

An appropriate default would be implemented for the impacted `ModelItemTypes`

---

The reason to support a group qualified by `ModelItemType` is at least three-fold:
* Clarify what can and what shouldn't be added to the group
* Provide at least Designer, if not run-time protection of adding the "wrong" kind of items to the group
* Narrow choices within Designer's pickers

I'm not terribly concerned as to _what_ the default is. I can always specify it if I'm using the group for more than just collecting it's elements for ease of management or for iterating over them.

See further https://community.openhab.org/t/items-bug-group-function-and-requires-two-arguments-using-equality-instead/25268

title: JSON Field Type Mismatch in `/rules` Endpoint.
body:
Hi,

It seems like there might be a JSON field type mismatch when hitting the `/rules` endpoint. 

When fetching the rules from `GET /rules`, sometimes the JSON response for a rule contains the field `"required": "false"` which I believe is meant to actually be a `boolean` (inside `Rule->Actions->Inputs`).

Steps:
- I created a new rule (containing just one trigger) with `POST /rules`. 
- Next, I updated that rule so that it would have a second trigger by calling the `PUT /rules/{ruleUID}` endpoint.
- After refreshing the list of rules by calling `GET /rules`, the newly updated rule JSON now contains the field `"required": "false"`. That field wasn't there prior to adding a second trigger.

Here's what the final JSON response looked like (scrapping out all of the unnecessary stuff).
`
{
...
	"actions": [{
		"inputs": {
			"required": "false"
		},
		"id": "2",
		"configuration": {},
		"type": "script.ScriptAction"
	}],
...
}
`

Is this intended, or a bug? The `/module-types` endpoint also uses the `Inputs` JSON schema, but that one actually sets the `"required"` field to a `boolean` instead of a `String`.

title: Change to DayLigth saving Time causes stop in timerelated persistence strategies
body:
As reported in the OH community ( [Link](https://community.openhab.org/t/openhab-not-saving-mesaurements-after-daylight-saving-time-change/25647)) the change to DayLigth Saving Time caused persistence schedules that are only using a time based strategy (everyMinute etc.) to stop at the time-switch.

Checks done on my side:
Actual values continued to be displayed.
The check of the database (rrd4j with a "everyMinute" strategy) showed the last value to be stored at the time-switch.
Several users confirmed that after restart of the OH-instance the time-scheduled persistence was working again. 
There is also an report on a cron based rule that stopped working, can't say if it is really related to the above.

title: BasicUI: Images and Charts not updating according to Configuration
body:
There's been a discussion in the community about images and charts not updating as expected:
https://community.openhab.org/t/basic-ui-image-refresh-rate-in-seconds-instead-miliseconds/27152

Some tests suggest that the refresh parameter is interpreted differently:
* ClassicUI: milli sec
* BasicUI: sec

**Fix**: Use same time base for all UIs

Also, in my own setup the update works only on images not on charts.
The chart initially loads in BasicUI but then instead of updating it shows a broken image symbol.
comments:
[2017-04-25T14:54:51Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
It should be a value in milli secs, see [here](http://docs.openhab.org/configuration/sitemaps.html#element-type-chart).

So I would say that it is a bug in the Basic UI. @resetnow, Would you agree?

[2017-04-25T15:17:19Z | vlad-ivanov-name | comment]
Yes, it's a bug, value is multiplied by 1000 in BasicUI. Obvious fix but I think we need to set a lower limit (50 ms?) to avoid accidental request spam.

[2017-04-25T15:33:19Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Yes, a lower limit makes sense. 50ms sounds sensible to me, maybe even 100ms.

title: thingUpdated() gets called during initialize()
body: As observed in https://github.com/openhab/openhab2-addons/pull/2019#issuecomment-298440882 and https://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/t/1085852/ it seems that `ThingHandler.thingUpdated()` gets called while the handler is still in `ThingHandler.initialize()`. This puts the unnecessary burden of handling synchronization on bindings and is not intended.
comments:
[2017-05-24T19:21:57Z | martinvw | comment]
Pitty, was no one yet able to make progress on this, it's blocking openhab/openhab2-addons#2019

Was it confirmed to happen, do we have any call traces where the calls actually come from, because the code  I see in openhab/openhab2-addons#2019 does do an async initialization.

And the documentation (which can of course be incorrect or outdated) states that `ThingHandler.thingUpdated` is:
>  This method is only called, if the thing has been initialized (status ONLINE/OFFLINE).

So that actually means that it should not even be called before the async initialization was finished.

[2017-05-24T19:26:14Z | martinvw | comment]
> And the documentation (which can of course be incorrect or outdated) states that  @@

There it starts, it was changed in #3088 ;-)

I think it might actually be really closely related to that change. @sjka can you look along with me?

[2017-05-26T08:03:53Z | sjsf | comment]
Yes, I think I know what the problem is here:

1. There indeed was a conscious decision to also inform the handler about an update as soon as the `initialize()` method returned. The assumption is the even if the Thing is not yet in ONLINE/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN status, the ThingHandler still started doing something, hence also needs to be informed if something changed.  You are right, the documentation needs to be updated. We missed that. 

2. There was another change in the ThingManager which made the `initialize()` be called asynchronously. As it seems, this broke the "protection" described above, so that `thingUpdated()` currently also can get called while the `initialize()` is still running. This is a bug and needs to be fixed somehow. 

It's all a bit tricky, therefore I can't promise to fix it immediately, but I will have a look into this in the next couple of days.

title: LIFX color temperature channel not working as expected
comments:
[2017-05-08T19:31:53Z | wborn | comment]
It would indeed be better if the temperature channel behaved like how it behaves in the App. The value currently only changes the K value of the HSBK quadruple.

The only issue with such a change is that it no longer allows you to programmatically set all elements of a HSBK value. The Kelvin values are always used to tint HSB values, see for instance this answer/discussion in the LIFX community: https://community.lifx.com/t/interpolating-colors-whites/573/6

So I currently use this in some presets where the tint of the K value makes or breaks how nice (warm) the light is. 

The behavior could perhaps also be a configuration option on the temperature channel? It would then default to how it works in the App.

Something I also don't like in the current binding implementation is that 2 channels need to be updated for a full HSBK value update. From what I've read people would also like to use custom fade times from within rules. Any ideas on how that could be accomplished? Except for some String channel that takes hsbk,fadetime values. ;-)

[2017-05-09T10:18:21Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> It would indeed be better if the temperature channel behaved like how it behaves in the App.

As I said, it already did so in the past, so we have a regression here.

> it no longer allows you to programmatically set all elements of a HSBK value

Imho it is fully ok with dropping that "feature" as I fully agree with the comment from LIFX:
_"We went with kelvin also setting saturation to 0 as we felt it covers the most common use case where people would want the light to be set to white when they set kelvin."_

Actually, I doubt that setting a Kelvin value for any color (but white) makes any kind of sense...
So the color temperature channel should always set the saturation to 0.

> So I currently use this in some presets where the tint of the K value makes or breaks how nice (warm) the light is.

You just have to choose another hue/saturation combination to reach exactly the same goal. There isn't such a thing as HSBK, this is an (unduly) invention by LIFX.

> would also like to use custom fade times from within rules. Any ideas on how that could be accomplished?

I do not want to go into this - ESH does not support parameterized commands, this would lead us to RPC-style communication with a lot additional complexity. So my recommendation would be to have people define different items that are all linked to the same channel and where the fadetime is [configured on the link](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/583).

[2017-05-09T17:37:01Z | wborn | comment]
> You just have to choose another hue/saturation combination to reach exactly the same goal. There isn't such a thing as HSBK, this is an (unduly) invention by LIFX.

The need for having control over K values comes from the fact that when you use the App for picking colors, it does not use a default K value. Instead it uses the last selected K value from the whites picker. So it becomes difficult to exactly reproduce the colors selected in the App with the binding.

So what also could work is fixing the regression so the binding works exactly like the App. Then it should be possible with rules to first change the light temperature, followed immediately by a color update. That should also keep things simple without unnecessary configuration options.

title: LIFX Infrared channel not working as expected
body:
I just tried a LIFX+ bulb with IR support. From the app, it seems that the IR light can only be switched on and off, but it isn't able to dim it.

The LIFX binding offers IR as a dimmer, though. I tried that and checked the light intensity with an IP cam, but it seems that it indeed does not dim - I see some changed in intensity when using the slider, but this is not continuous and also not significant. So I assume that we probably should change it to a switch channel. @wborn wdyt?
comments:
[2017-05-08T21:45:34Z | wborn | comment]
Thanks for the feedback! It looks like the endianness of the FIELD_STATE in `StateLightInfraredResponse` and `SetLightPowerRequest` needs to be changed to `.little()`:
```
    public static final Field<Integer> FIELD_STATE = new UInt16Field().little();
```

It got copied from `SetLightPowerRequest` where the endianness does not matter. :-)

Now when I hook up a power meter it also shows correct readings when changing the slider. Changing the IR slider causes the power consumption to range between 0W and 5W. With this fix through my Nest cam in IR mode it also seems to work like a dimmer but the cam always auto adjusts the IR brightness.

In the Android App it is not even possible to enable/disable IR control. There is only an "eye" symbol that indicates if IR is on and when you tap it you can see the IR brightness percentage (but you can not change it). Most likely the app will some day get updated with IR schedules and brightness configuration.

In the future other IR (flood) lights may get introduced that waste even more energy on full IR brightness and get mapped to the `colorirlight` Thing type. So I do think the dimmer has a use. We could also implement `OnOffType` commands on that channel (maybe even reusing the powerOnBrightness channel configuration option).

[2017-05-09T08:30:58Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Ok, sure, if the IR light actually is dimmable, then let's stay with the dimmer channel here.
So please simply create a PR that fixes the behavior of it!

[2017-05-15T19:43:50Z | sjsf | comment]
@m-memova Could you please heeeelp? 😢
