Really? Again? What are you doing with those tests, man ? :-D I will take a look.

[2017-05-16T13:21:06Z | sjsf | comment]
I don't know. Just executing them, I guess? 😉 

The problem with these tests for sure is that they actually are integration tests, not only testing the binding, but indirectly also the complete ESH framework. That's why the are hit by asynchronous behavior, automated magic like autoupdate if item states, auto linking and all that. If some of these things change in a slight aspect (e.g. timing, implemented in a different way), then these tests also suffer.

I think if you want to really get rid of this stuff, then it would make sense to reduce the test scope to the binding itself, just making sure it uses the ESH APIs correctly. I.e. if you want to test if a certain action leads to an item update, just take the standalone ThingHandler, feed it with a mocked ThingHandlerCallback and ensure it's calling `stateUpdated(...)`. Don't care what happens afterwards. 

The new [testing documentation](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/docs/documentation/development/testing.md#mockito) gives a pretty good example of how this can be done using plain Java 8 (hooray) with Mockito. For the majority of binding tests, this suffices and there is hardly any need for OSGiTests.

body:
If you don't use an extension service but open the rule category in the PaperUI (http://127.0.0.1:8080/paperui/index.html#/rules) it complains about a non available service using a notification:
ERROR 503 - Service not available

The service that is not available is the extension one.
I don't think we need to warn every time the rules category is opened that the extension service is not available but accept the missing service silently.

When this notification chain returns to the first place, it _again_ removes the item from the map. So it lost track of it, but the registry still has it.

It actually needs three things to cause this issue: 

* The GenericItemChannelLinkProvider has some amnesia. It clears its context map, so it doesn't properly remember what it created/provided before. It needs an even number of updates, before a model removal can cause this issue (so it's not a heisenbug, it's just a 50% chance). Because of this amnesia, the ItemChannelLinks remain in the registry, therefore the ChannelItemProvider kicks in an creates the excess items. 
* As said before, the ChannelItemProvider has a built-in amnesia due to the internal-remove/inform-and-thereby-recreate/internal-remove sequence which makes it impossible for it to remove its own item later on when the model gets loaded again (I have described this above). It just didn't surface so far because items from other providers seldomly come and go all the time.
* The question is why the ChannelItemProvider is part of this game at all... As the links for model items actually also come from the model, it actually should not need to. It would me much more clever of the GenericItemProvider if it would _first_ create the items and _then_ create the links (and vice versa for deletion) so that the ChannelLinkProvider will not need to become active at all. This I think is the root-cause for the long outstanding, somehow mysterious #2491, which is very annoying for all bindings which do something "expensive" stuff whenever a channel gets linked.

title: PaperUI advanced configuration group
body:
This may or may not be a bug - seems to work differently then channel advanced settings.  For a transport that I've been working on - I have a configuration descriptor (below).  When you go to Configuration->Services->Press the Configure button on my transport - I expected the advanced group to be hidden behind a 'Advanced' or 'Show More' type of button - but it was simply displayed as is (see the screen shot below).

Here is my config:
`

        <parameter-group name="advancedSettings">
            <label>Advanced Settings</label>
           <description>Advanced Settings</description>
           <context>String</context>
          <advanced>true</advanced>
        </parameter-group>    

        <parameter name="ipAddresses" type="text" required="true">
            <label>HostNames/IP Addresses</label>
            <description>"Auto" to auto-detect or a comma delimited list of Hostnames and/or IP Addresses</description>
            <default>Auto</default>
        </parameter>
        
        <parameter name="exposeAll" type="boolean" required="true">
            <label>Expose All</label>
            <description>Expose all things</description>
            <default>false</default>   
        </parameter>
        
        <parameter name="localIpAddress" type="text" required="false" groupName="advancedSettings">
            <label>Local IP Address</label>
            <description>Local IP Address (leave blank to auto discover)</description>
            <default></default>   
        </parameter>
`
I expected PaperUI to provide an "Show More" type of button similar to advanced channels in the thing configuration - but it simply displayed the 'advanced' group in the configuration dialog.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20641634/26949088-a02de3e4-4c66-11e7-83b9-8f01bdea02c1.png)
comments:
[2017-06-09T06:49:06Z | htreu | comment]
I noticed this too a few days ago. Will have a look at it later.

[2017-06-09T12:41:06Z | aounhaider1 | comment]
The problem here is that PaperUI checks the advanced property of parameters only and not of the group. In the above case it is false for all parameters, so the questions is should the advance property on group supersede the advance property of encapsulating parameters? @maggu2810 wdyt?

[2017-06-09T12:43:49Z | tmrobert8 | comment]
According to [Eclipse SmartHome XML reference](https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/development/bindings/xml-reference.html) - there is no advanced property on the parameter itself (that's why I went with a group instead).  Is this an oversight on the document?

[2017-06-09T12:56:02Z | aounhaider1 | comment]
The doc should be updated in that case, the advance property is part of the Parameter description https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/config/org.eclipse.smarthome.config.core/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/config/core/dto/ConfigDescriptionParameterDTO.java#L41.

[2017-06-09T13:07:38Z | tmrobert8 | comment]
Interesting - something strange is still going on however.  See the following screen prints when I tried to use that (and I am running the latest and greatest).  I double checked that xsd and the ConfigDescriptionParameter - both seem to indicate that advanced is allowed but clearly it's getting flagged...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20641634/26976669-d70dd612-4cf2-11e7-97d2-c2810ef43ec2.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20641634/26976682-e6c26578-4cf2-11e7-8aeb-64a3986c1fff.png)

[2017-06-09T13:12:10Z | aounhaider1 | comment]
Should be added as a tag:
```xml
<parameter name="localIpAddress" type="text" required="false" groupName="advancedSettings">
	<label>Local IP Address</label>
	<description>Local IP Address (leave blank to auto discover)</description>
	<default>0</default>
	<advanced>true</advanced>
</parameter>
```

[2017-06-09T13:15:44Z | tmrobert8 | comment]
AHH - thanks I totally misread the xsd in my quick look.  You are correct and it does correctly show the "Show More" button in that case..

[2017-06-12T11:46:12Z | aounhaider1 | comment]
@kaikreuzer, @htreu what do you think the behaviour should be in this case?

[2017-06-12T13:42:45Z | htreu | comment]
@aounhaider1 My guess is that the `advanced`property on parameter groups should indeed supersede the property of the encapsulated params and display the `More` button for this group.
I will propose a fix for this.

[2017-06-12T13:44:21Z | aounhaider1 | comment]
Ok. Already did that. Will create a PR shortly.

[2017-06-13T06:20:24Z | htreu | comment]
Tnx a lot @aounhaider1! I´m also working on this but did a lot of refactoring left & right in the code. My suggestion is to merge your PR and I will rebase and propose my refactoring afterwards.

* #3195 is an issue and not a PR
* there is a reference between issue #3195 and PR #3196 
  There is a comment of @kaikreuzer "so I assume we should close this PR and maybe just do some hardening/safeguards in the registries?" So, could this one be closed?
* there is a reference between issue #3195 and PR #3670
  There are change request that doesn't seems to be fixed, yes.

[2017-07-26T14:08:34Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Right, #3670 waits for a few minor updates from @adimova.

> May be the decision is these handlers to register server trackers for the RuleRegistry service instead to relay on declarative services.

No, this won't solve the cyclic dependency.
Have you identified the cycle in detail? It is clear that the Rule***Handlers depend on the RuleRegistry, but which is the path from the RuleRegistry to the Handlers?

[2017-07-26T14:30:52Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Have you identified the cycle in detail?

I think I found the issue: The RuleEngine is within the RuleRegistry and thus draws in all its dependencies (like the ones to the Handlers). Imho, the proper architecture would be to have the RuleEngine as a separate service, which depends on the RuleRegistry (and listens to changes to its rules). That way, the cycle would be broken as the RuleRegistry would not have any dependency on the Handlers anymore.

[2017-07-26T15:24:49Z | danchom | comment]
@maggu2810 sorry, my mistake the PR is a #3670 and this PR #3196 is an old implementation and I think It can be closed. 
@adimova  is in vacation till to 07.08 and after that she will fix the Kai's comments 
@kaikreuzer the PR #3670 fixes circular dependencies between Registries and Providers because the registry listen for providers and the providers have to listen for registries to check if the provided elements have not existed in the registry yet.  The PR #3670 removes provider's dependency from registry.
RuleEngine is just an implementation and it does not have a public interface. Its public interface is a RuleRegistry. I think it should not be exposed as component. Also if we expose it as component we does not solve the circular dependency:
RuleRegistry -depends on-> RuleEngine -depends on-> HandlerFactory -depends on-> RuleRegistry

[2017-07-26T15:34:56Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> @adimova is in vacation till to 07.08 and after that she will fix the Kai's comments

As they are really minor, I would suggest that I simply add a commit that does the changes.

> RuleEngine is just an implementation and it does not have a public interface. I think it should not be exposed as component.

I didn't ask to expose it, I only said it should be registered as a service on its own. If it is registered with its implementation class, which is not in an exported package, it still will not be an "exposed component", right?

> Its public interface is a RuleRegistry.

No - if that were the case, it would be named RuleRegistryImpl. It is functionally something completely different than an implementation of the registry interface - that's why it should be factored out.

>  Also if we expose it as component we does not solve the circular dependency: ...

Of course we solve it, if the refactoring is done correctly:

RuleEngine -depends on-> RuleRegistry
RuleEngine -depends on-> HandlerFactory -depends on-> RuleRegistry

[2017-07-27T06:49:51Z | danchom | comment]
>As they are really minor, I would suggest that I simply add a commit that does the changes.

ok

>Of course we solve it, if the refactoring is done correctly:
RuleEngine -depends on-> RuleRegistry
RuleEngine -depends on-> HandlerFactory -depends on-> RuleRegistry

I've thought about such solution but in this case you can  have a register RuleRegistry without RuleEngine and what happen when a RuleRegistry's add, update, delete or setEnabled methods is called? You won't know if your command is executed by the RuleEngine. You have to relay on rule events which will make difficult to use rules. Also additional synchronization should be implemented between current rule registry rules and new one added during the rule engine initialization.

[2017-07-27T09:07:23Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> what happen when a RuleRegistry's add, update, delete or setEnabled methods is called?

The registry content is updated accordingly. This is all what is to be expected of it - it holds the rules and allows their modification.

Anybody who is interested in rules (like the rule engine) should register as a `RegistryChangeListener` on the RuleRegistry and will be notified of any changes and can react to it.

[2017-07-27T10:07:59Z | danchom | comment]
>Anybody who is interested in rules (like the rule engine) should register as a RegistryChangeListener on the RuleRegistry and will be notified of any changes and can react to it.

yes this will be done, but I mean the following problems:
1) RuleRegistry is used as public API for RuleEngine. (only through this api you can have influence to the rule engine). Unfortunately there are other public method which are not covered by the  RegistryChangeListener  i.e. isEnable(), setEnable(), runNow(). We have to introduce RuleEngineComandCallback interface to notify the RuleEngine about the actions. The other approach is the RuleEngine component to export its own public interface which will have to support these operation, but in this case we will have again the cycle dependency :
RuleEngine -> RuleRegistry  for add, update, remove 
RuleRegistry -> RuleEngine for setEnable, isEnable and runNow
2) When a user add a rule into RuleRegistry he won't know if the rule is running by the rule engine or not. He has to register rule status change event listener to be sure that his rule is processed by the RuleEngine, which I think is too complicated. At the moment if the rule is added into ruleRegistry it is a guarantee  that it is process by the RuleEngine.

[2017-07-27T11:25:13Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
1. We could create a RuleRegistryChangeListener interface, which extends RegistryChangeListener and allows to pass the calls to isEnable(), setEnable(), runNow(). This would not introduce any cycling dependency.

2. Well, the user can be sure that it is executed, if the solution ensures that the RuleEngine service is successfully started. This might be related to https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/1896. In general, I do not see the NEED to ensure that a rule engine is there. In theory, it is perfectly fine to have access to the RuleRegistry and simply add new rules to it. The question when, where and how they are executed should be out of scope. IF a client has specific needs to know exactly that this RuleEngine is active, we should think about exposing the RuleEngine service after all, so that your client can define a dependency on it.

Sounds good.

title: io.rest uses gson 2.5.0, although we so far only support gson 2.3.1
body:
I found this in my logs:

```
Exception in thread "Thread-65" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: tried to access method com.google.gson.Gson.newJsonWriter(Ljava/io/Writer;)Lcom/google/gson/stream/JsonWriter; from class org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.JSONResponse
        at org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.JSONResponse.lambda$0(JSONResponse.java:162)
        at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
```
A closer analysis shows that this method is only publicly available in gson 2.5, while my setup only has gson 2.3.1 available.

Interestingly, our smarthome.target resolves 2.2.4 AND 2.5.0, so the IDE picks up 2.5.0 and compiles against it.

As far as I remember, we wanted to be compatible with gson 2.3.1, but it all seems to be a bit messed up right now...

title: Remove separate altitude parameter from Astro binding
body:
When approving my auto-discovered Sun thing, I got this in my log:

```
15:52:30.491 [INFO ] [smarthome.event.ThingAddedEvent     ] - Thing 'astro:sun:local' has been added.
15:52:30.493 [INFO ] [me.event.ThingStatusInfoChangedEvent] - 'astro:sun:local' changed from UNINITIALIZED to INITIALIZING
15:52:30.500 [ERROR] [ding.astro.handler.AstroThingHandler] - Astro parameters geolocation could not be split into latitude and longitude, disabling thing 'astro:sun:local'
15:52:30.501 [INFO ] [me.event.ThingStatusInfoChangedEvent] - 'astro:sun:local' changed from INITIALIZING to OFFLINE
```
The issue is that the discovery now adds "<lat>,<long>,<alt>" in the geoLocation config parameter of the Thing, while it expects the altitude to be filled into the dedicated "altitude" parameter instead.

As we will soon have a [location context](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/3709), which also includes altitude information, I think it would make most sense to remove the "altitude" parameter of Astro things and rather mark the geoLocation parameter to be of context "location", which implicitly can hold an optional altitude value.

Here is my very simple test rule:

[2017-07-26T07:36:05Z | sjsf | comment]

[2017-07-26T07:46:04Z | sjsf | comment]
Aaaaah, haha, found it... 

In java (and xbase accordingly), a line break has no meaning. And `return` optionally _can_ have an argument. As you left out the semicolons, the interpreter reads it differently from what we humans intuitively would do. It uses the second log stamement as a return value, therefore executing it. When reformatting your code like following, the problem get more clear I think:

```
    logInfo("Info","Änderung SV Temperatur erkannt1")
    return logInfo("Info","Änderung SV Temperatur erkannt2")                                                                                                                                                              
``` 

Therefore in this case you need to help the interpreter, eliminating the ambiguity with a semicolon:

```
    logInfo("Info","Änderung SV Temperatur erkannt1")
    return;
    logInfo("Info","Änderung SV Temperatur erkannt2")                                                                                                                                                              
```

I will consider this caveat in my outstanding PR for the documentation.

[2017-07-26T11:51:27Z | ThomDietrich | comment]
@sjka haha nice catch. I'd also not have known that. Adding the semicolon is one solution but seems tricky and easy to get wrong. How would you feel about "return void" or any other argument as the standard solution for the documentation?

Btw. Thanks for the comprehensive docs PR ;)

[2017-07-26T15:35:45Z | sjsf | comment]
We would require something that is also a valid statement. `return void` is not, as `void` is not an existing identifier. That would be `return null` - but then again the syntax is incorrect leading to a  "Void functions cannot return a value."-error (which in fact the Designer would have complained about if @SebZim would have used it or would have inspected his log files... 😉 )

Unfortunately java was designed to have `;` - and leaving them out only works in most of the cases. This is one where it doesn't. 

So far I'm not aware of any better solution to this.

[2017-07-26T15:39:33Z | ThomDietrich | comment]
Ah I see. Okay then, please bear with me. :smiley:  What if you added another change to the validator to allow a return null? Sounds semantically okay to me **and** meaningful for the end user. Wouldn't that solve all problems?

(the Designer already has some flaws, we can add this minor one to it, IF someone would solve the others this one could be handled as well)

[2017-07-26T15:50:58Z | sjsf | comment]
Sure, no problem. However, this is not a question of only suppressing a warning - it's none of those warnings that _we_ invented ourselves (that would have been easy then...), but it actually comes from the base language. We of course _could_ change the DSL language definition so that it expects a return value. But then suddenly it's not optional anymore and you would _have_ to return something on _every_ rule. Which would be the much bigger pain.
In fact I don't think that so many users will run into this issue - most of the time you will do early returns based in a condition - and then the return statement is the last one in a block where it does not need the `;` because the parser can use the `}` for orientation.

I hoped there is a clean way to find a middle path.

title: PaperUI - DecimalType default value of thing parameter is parsed to Int
body:
I have following code describing a thing parameter:
``` 
<parameter name="targetResolution" type="decimal" required="true">
    <label>Resolution of the read Value</label>
    <description>
         Resolution of the value. Raw value will be multiplied with this.
    </description>
    <default>0.01</default>
</parameter>
```
If I try to add such thing in the UI the default value set is `0`. Integer values are shown correctly.
The backend handles the default value as String `"0.01"` and the API hands over the value `0.01`.
I assume there is something going wrong in the javascript.
comments:
[2017-08-08T11:59:00Z | Sydrimon | comment]
I found the source of this problem.

A decimal value gets parsed to Int [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/extensions/ui/org.eclipse.smarthome.ui.paper/web-src/js/services.js#L197) causing this problem. 
Introduced in #3656.

Also there is a decimal value parsed to Int [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/extensions/ui/org.eclipse.smarthome.ui.paper/web-src/js/services.js#L432), which causes the same problem.
Introduced in #1889.

Another occurrence, also related to the problem: [services.js#L484](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/extensions/ui/org.eclipse.smarthome.ui.paper/web-src/js/services.js#L484).

body:
On an Android tablet using Paper UI (in Chrome) and the Control page, as soon as I scroll with my finger, Paper UI is automatically switching to the next tab (location), even if I scroll only in the middle of a page.
On a PC using the mouse to scroll, this problem does not exist.
It makes the control page unusable on a tablet or phone.

title: Image Link: Authentication not working anymore in 1009/Karaf 4.1.2
body:

Not sure if this is related to snapshot build 1009 or with new Karaf Upgrade 4.1.2

But Sitemap-Images with authentication do not work anymore:

Image icon="camera" url="http://**user:password**@192.168.1.52/axis-cgi/jpg/image.cgi?camera=1&resolution=1280x720&compression=25" refresh=10000

comments:
[2017-08-13T20:15:59Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The ESH version has not changed between the builds 1008 and 1009.
The only thing that changed in this context is the version of Jetty (and thus also the Jetty Proxy, which is used for the image widgets) - it has been upgraded from 9.2.19 to 9.3.14. We would have to check whether our code requires some change here (and if so we need to think about more strictly defining the compatible version).

[2017-08-13T20:31:13Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The good news is: I can reproduce the issue.
The bad news is: We therefore indeed seem to have an issue 😞 .

I just briefly googled and came across https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/issues/806, which is fixed in 9.3.14 - afair, we did a workaround because of this bug, so it might make sense to use the new feature now. @svilenvul, as you were the bug reporter at that time, would you want to check that? It would mean though that we have to set the minimal version requirement of the Jetty client to 9.3.12 (which would be ok for me).

[2017-08-14T06:14:24Z | watou | comment]
It may be that later [AbstractProxyServlet.java](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commits/jetty-9.4.x/jetty-proxy/src/main/java/org/eclipse/jetty/proxy/AbstractProxyServlet.java) versions no longer call the deprecated [`copyHeaders`](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/2753/files#diff-58b13e7e76574d68a9bff9904cd8d817R56) (see my comment in the code) so the proxy servlet has to now instead override `copyRequestHeaders`. in order to maybe append the auth headers.

title: Astro binding :  Peculiarities of the Sun phase channel
body:
I am using the Astro binding in my openHAB system, using the Sun / Phase channel as a way to check the "state of daylight" in my rules. 

While testing this I was looking at the log files for a "full cycle" (i.e. a 24 hour period) and I noticed a couple of strange things. 

Here is a snip of my log file:

2017-08-14 03:55:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from UNDEF to NAUTIC_DAWN
2017-08-14 05:02:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NAUTIC_DAWN to CIVIL_DAWN
2017-08-14 05:50:00.004 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from CIVIL_DAWN to SUN_RISE
2017-08-14 05:54:00.002 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from SUN_RISE to DAYLIGHT
2017-08-14 13:34:00.002 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from DAYLIGHT to NOON
2017-08-14 21:14:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NOON to SUN_SET
2017-08-14 21:18:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from SUN_SET to CIVIL_DUSK
2017-08-14 22:06:00.007 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from CIVIL_DUSK to NAUTIC_DUSK
2017-08-14 23:13:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NAUTIC_DUSK to ASTRO_DUSK
2017-08-15 00:00:00.023 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from ASTRO_DUSK to UNDEF

The first thing I notice is that apparently the Sun / Phase channel will never report NIGHT as a state (contrary to what the documentation states) but instead goes back to UNDEF. 

The next thing is that the Sun / Phase channel can report a stated called NOON (and this is as stated in the documentation). As can been seen in the log this is reported as the phase from 13:34 until SUN_SET. 

As far as I know, however, NOON is a specific point in time (12:00 / midday) and not a period of time, thus (IMO) NOON should not really be reported on the Sun / Phase channel.
comments:
[2017-08-28T14:04:50Z | triller-telekom | comment]
> The first thing I notice is that apparently the Sun / Phase channel will never report NIGHT as a state (contrary to what the documentation states) but instead goes back to UNDEF.

This depends on your location. It might be the case that in this specific time of the year there is no astronomical night for you ;) You can use this [site](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/astronomy.html) to see if there is a night at your location.

[2017-08-28T14:18:12Z | sjsf | comment]
That would still leave the question: Why is it UNKNOWN then - even if there would be no "NIGHT" at a certain location, shouldn't it rather transition symmetrically from ASTRO_DUSK to ASTRO_DAWN then? In the definition, there is no room for an "UNKNOWN" phase.

[2017-08-28T14:34:31Z | kjasdal | comment]
> It might be the case that in this specific time of the year there is no astronomical night for you ;)

Although this holds true for the northern part of Norway - for parts of the year - I am afraid it does not for my part (I live at the south most tip). The site you linked to reports night as 23:26 until 03:27 for the current 24-hour period. 

The main point, however, is as @sjka pointed out; there should not be an UNKNOWN (or UNDEF as I experience) phase. If there is no night, then the transition should be nautical twilight -> astro twilight -> nautical twilight.

[2017-08-28T14:46:14Z | kjasdal | comment]
I just took a look at the logs for the previous 24-hour period, and I see that the situation is apparently a bit different than what I thought:

2017-08-27 23:37:00.010 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from ASTRO_DUSK to NIGHT
2017-08-28 00:00:00.028 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - AstroSunHome_sDaylight_Start changed from 2017-08-27T06:23:00.000+0200 to 2017-08-28T06:25:00.000+0200
2017-08-28 00:00:00.031 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - AstroSunHome_sDaylight_End changed from 2017-08-27T20:40:00.000+0200 to 2017-08-28T20:37:00.000+0200
2017-08-28 00:00:00.032 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NIGHT to UNDEF
2017-08-28 03:30:00.008 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from UNDEF to ASTRO_DAWN

As can be seen, NIGHT is indeed reported (as coming after ASTRO_DUSK), however, it seems that at midnight (when the scheduler runs the astro job to calculate values for the next 24-hour period, I presume) the state is set to UNDEF, and left like that until the next state transition (which is when ASTRO_DAWN starts).

[2017-08-29T11:57:48Z | kjasdal | comment]
Seeing that this has gotten a "bug"-label, I just wanted to summarize what I believe are issues that should be looked at (and hopefully corrected):

1) When the DailyJob is run at midnight, the Sun Phase state is set to UNDEF. 
- This should not happen (the state should continue to be NIGHT).
2) There is a Sun Phase called NOON that seems to have a duration of one minute (although some comment in the code states that NOON has the same start and end time). 
- NOON should not be a Sun Phase since this is a specific point in time, and not a duration.
- It makes sense to keep it as an Event, though. 
- If it is difficult implementation-wise to have one and not the other, I guess NOON could be kept with a duration of 0 minutes. 
- In this case, the DAYLIGHT period needs to be split into two periods; one before NOON and one after NOON, to be able to move back to DAYLIGHT after passing NOON. As it is now, NOON continues all the way until SUNSET, :-)

[2017-08-29T12:29:33Z | sjsf | comment]
Good summary, thanks!

1. Indeed, the first thing the DaiyJobSun does is republishing all channels with the claculations of a new sun object. This however appears to not have the correct phase calculated initially [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/0bae79367d47fcd8288670c7f79afcfbb15c5a9b/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.astro/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/binding/astro/internal/calc/SunCalc.java#L243). 

2. Sounds plausible to _me_. 
> If it is difficult implementation-wise to have one and not the other

Not necessarily... If you just drop [this one line](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/9480a0b3f32b835cfd7b86f4cccfaec23f44468c/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.astro/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/binding/astro/internal/job/DailyJobSun.java#L81), it's not a "phase" anymore but the events still get sent by the scheduled range (a few lines above). No need for any quirks with two DAYLIGHT jobs and the like. However, I think it's mainly a matter of how many people rely on the "NOON" phase in their rules which this would break. 

@gerrieg as the original author of the binding, do you have any particular opinion here?

[2017-08-29T17:02:08Z | gerrieg | comment]
1.) UNDEF should not happen
2.) Makes sense to remove NOON from the sun phase and keep it as event

@kjasdal can you please post (or send by mail) your coordinates so that i can try it myself. Then i can say more.

[2017-08-29T17:09:03Z | kjasdal | comment]

title: Inbox auto ignored results are never removed
body:
When adding e.g. a hue bridge manually, its result is automatically set to IGNORED in the inbox as expected. When removing the bridge, the IGNORED entry in the inbox must be automatically deleted so a new discovery can find it again. It turns out, that this is not happening most of the time.

The reason is, that we do not have such a thing as a Pre-Delete-Hook, where we could easily check and remove possible ignored entries.Listening to ThingStatusChangedEvents as currently implemented does not help, because a REMOVED event indicates that a thing is already removed and REMOVING is not always fired and sometimes directly followed by a REMOVED. In most cases we are accessing the ThingRegistry too late to get informations about the thing being removed (it just returns null).

title: Paper UI: new discovered things should be displayed as ignored when they are auto ignored
body:
When you ask for new discovery things for example for Sonos, new things are displayed at screen as "not ignored" while they are in fact ignored due to the automatic ignore mechanism (existing thing with the same representation property).
If you reload the inbox by clicking on the menu item "Inbox" then they are ignored as expected.
comments:
[2018-01-22T07:56:35Z | htreu | comment]
This is the result from my analysis:
* `PersistentInbox` will pass a newly discovered thing to the `thingAdded` method from the `AutomaticInboxProcessor` which does the `autoIgnore` check.
* the `AutomaticInboxProcessor` will call `setFlag(thingUID, IGNORED)` on the `PersistentInbox`. This marks the discovery result from the storage with the flag, not the instance which is currently processed by the `PersistentInbox`.
* `setFlag` will immediately post an `updated` event for the discovery result (note: this happens before an `added` event is emitted).
* Paper UI will happily ignore the `updated` event since no entry for the given thingUID is present in the Paper UI inbox repository.
* `PersistentInbox` will then post an `added` event with the instance the discovery service created. This instance does not have the `IGNORED` flag set.
* Paper UI will pick up the `added` event and display the discovery result as a new result, just because the flag is still set to `NEW`.

A refresh of the Paper UI inbox will retrieve all discovery results from the backend. Since the `IGNORED` flag was correctly set to the instance from the storage Paper UI will then correctly hide the auto-ignored result.

[2018-01-22T07:59:06Z | htreu | comment]
One solution would be to reload the discovered result from storage before emitting the first `add` event. This will then provide the correct flag.
The unused `updated` event is obsolete (in this scenario) but does not hurt as long as the client checks for existence of the given thingUID.

title: ConfigDispatcher: Config file processing order-dependent if exclusivePIDs are used
body:
### Context
The `org.eclipse.smarthome.config.dispatch.internal.ConfigDispatcher` processes configuration files in the `processConfigFile` method. How a config file is processed depends on whether it has a so-called _exclusive PID_ or not: A config file has an exclusive PID if its first line starts with a PID marker _pid:_ followed by a PID.

### The Issue
Consider the following two config files:

a.cfg:
```
pid:some_pid
A=some value
```

b.cfg:
```
some_pid:B=some other value
```

Then the processing of these two files in the ConfigDispatcher depends on the order in which the two files are processed:
* If `a.cfg` is processed first, then the resulting configuration contains both properties `A` and `B` for PID `some_pid`.
* If `b.cfg` is processed first, then the resulting configuration only contains property `A` for PID `some_pid`.

Frankly, I do not know which result is the correct one, but I think that it is not correct that it depends on the order in which the files are processed. 

One result of this 'order dependency' is that the test `ConfigDispatcherOSGiTest#theSameLocalAndGlobalPIDsInDifferentFilesAreConsideredOnePID` sometimes fails on my machine (it uses two config files with the same structure as in the example above) - depending on the order in which the two config files used by this test are processed (the config files are processed sorted by lastModified date, which is the same on my machine for both used config files). 

### Expected behavior?
As stated above, I do not know what the expected behavior is. However, from looking at the code of the method `ConfigDispatcher#processConfigFile` I see that there is some logic that tries to skip config properties for a PID if this PID is used as exclusive PID in another config file. Currently, this logic works only if the file with the exclusive PID is processed last. So I guess that the expected behavior could be that config properties for a PID are ignored if there is another config file which has this PID as exclusive PID. However, from looking at the unit test referenced above, skipping properties in files without exclusive PID is not expected. But of course this unit test might simply be buggy...

To conclude: Does anyone here know what is the intended behaviour here regarding parsing of config files with and without exclusive PIDs?
comments:
[2017-10-16T23:01:25Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
@htreu Could you have a look? I agree with @hsudbrock that there should be no dependency on the processing order.

[2017-11-07T11:32:48Z | htreu | comment]
Yes, agreed. The processing order should not change the result here.
Since we want .cfg files with an exclusive PID marker (like `pid:my.service.pid` in the first line) to be really exclusive and especially benefit from the file delete mechanism we should drop all other entries with this pid from other files. So when a file later defines a key/value pair for an already known exclusive PID (e.g. by defining the pid inline like `my.service.pid:key=value`) this line will be skipped.

The only order dependent processing is then given for .cfg files which define the same exclusive pid in the first line: here the file processed last will win and have its values passed to the configAdmin. A warning will be logged about the subsequent definition of an exclusive PID.

title: [Sonos] UPnP action invocation results in an empty result, which sets the Thing to OFFLINE
body:
UPnP is broken !
The following line is failing (returning an empty result):
https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/fee1c67521d3d2b84bdf8ec82552a50bfad6faf5/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.sonos/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/binding/sonos/internal/handler/ZonePlayerHandler.java#L837
The result with the Sonos binding is that the thing is set to OFFLINE.
I have 2 Sonos and strangely it happens only for one of my 2 Sonos.

It looks like a critical bug in the new library version we are relying on (jUPnP).

I switch back to snapshot 1065 immediately.
@kaikreuzer : I think you should announce in the forum to absolutely avoid the snapshot 1078 for all users using UPnP, until a fix is found.

[2017-11-11T18:17:33Z | lolodomo | comment]
As a temporay fix, could we revert to previous version of the library ?

[2017-11-11T18:33:00Z | lolodomo | comment]
After restoring snapshot 1065, I have no problem.
So the stuff relative with UPnP has been broken between 1065 and 1078.
There were 2 things changed:
* some packages moved
* version of the jUPnP library updated

[2017-11-11T18:40:14Z | lolodomo | comment]
I am suspecting this PR as natural source of the problem: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/4487

[2017-11-11T18:54:36Z | lolodomo | comment]
I am very confident that the problem is not inside the Sonos binding itself because I am running in my production environment the snapshot 1065 with a special version of the Sonos binding compiled recently from the PR 4500 and that works perfectly. This PR was the last change in the binding.

[2017-11-11T19:07:06Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> UPnP is broken !

Well, I have the impression you are generalizing a bit too much here.

- UPnP seems to work fine for discovery, there are no issues with Hue, Sonos, WeMo, etc.
- Sonos PLAY:1 works smoothly with UPnP actions and events, I do not see any issues with it.
- WeMo works smoothly with UPnP actions.

So what is left is that a specific action call that is done in the Sonos binding works differently than before. Let's spend the time and thoroughly analyse, why this happens and where the root issue actually is. In case it is in jUPnP, the issue should rather be reported at https://github.com/jupnp/jupnp.

> I have 2 Sonos and strangely it happens only for one of my 2 Sonos.

I couldn't exactly figure out what caused this behavior. The result of it was the the hydration of devices with didn't fully succeed as a few services were often missing due to the failed http processing.

[2017-11-16T14:19:25Z | htreu | comment]
I did an analysis, this is a bug in ESH.

### Technical explanation
Two ItemProviders will try to add new items to the ItemRegistry: 
* The ChannelItemProvider will create "virtual" items for every ItemChannelLink it starts to handle. In case the link points to an item which is not already loaded and added to the ItemRegistry it will create one which lacks of cause all the meta information like label, groupNames, etc.
* The ManagedItemProvider will add all the items loaded from the storage service (here MapDB) to the ItemRegistry. Here all the items have the full meta information available.

Since https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/3670 there is a mechanism in the AbstractRegistry which prevents duplicate elements. This introduced also the behaviour we can see here: When the ChannelItemProvider is the first to add its items to the ItemRegistry the ManagedItemProvider will later try to add its items too and create the log messages.

### Workaround
In case all items in a setup are either provided by .items files or created vie PaperUI/REST API and not automagically by the ChannelItemProvider (which is needed primarily when activating new channels in PaperUI in "Simple Mode"*), the ChannelItemProvider can be deactivated completely. To achieve this create a `channelitemprovider.cfg` file with content `enabled=false` in the `conf/services` folder of the installation.

\* in Simple Mode no real items are created but only "virtual" items are implicitly created by the ChannelItemProvider.

@mherwege, do you mind testing the described workaround with your setup?

title: Configuration normalisation not performed on channel configuration
body:
When saving channel configuration, normalisation is not performed on the channel configuration. Additionally, it looks like the defaults may not be of the correct type - defaults are specified as a ```String``` (ie in ConfigDescriptionParameterBuilder) and should be normalised before being passed to the binding.

For example, the following -:

```
            options = new ArrayList<ParameterOption>();
            options.add(new ParameterOption("65535", "Use On/Off transition time"));
            parameters.add(ConfigDescriptionParameterBuilder.create(CONFIG_ONTRANSITIONTIME, Type.INTEGER)
                    .withLabel("On Transition Time")
                    .withDescription("Time in 10ms intervals to transition from OFF to ON").withDefault("65535")
                    .withMinimum(new BigDecimal(0)).withMaximum(new BigDecimal(60000)).withOptions(options)
                    .withLimitToOptions(false).build());
```

will provide a String when the configuration is read from the channel.

title: No events received from ESH
body:
We are currently experiencing problems with receiving all kinds of events from ESH. It looks like for certain times we do not receive any events at all from ESH. If this happens, only events from ESH are affected, while at the same time we still receive events when the OSGI EventAdmin is used directly (we have some custom events in our own bundles, where the EventAdmin is used directly).

We have seen the issues from last December (#4591 and other issues referenced there) and think this could be related, but we do not see any log messages about the EventAdmin blacklisting certain services here. So we cannot say if there is a connection, but it seems likely.

We first observed this behaviour with the 0.9.0 release version.

title: Thing configuration descriptions not working
body:
ZWave configuration descriptions are no longer working - configuration from the internal ConfigProvider is ok, but configuration from the XML files is not provided. It seems that the conversion in the ThingConfigDescriptionProvider is not making the conversion from thing to thing-type.

Maybe it is related to https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/5021 as it's about the right timeframe for this having been introduced and it looks like the original provider was changed at this point to a new Alias interface (@sjka). From my quick look at this, it seems that the thing config provider is no longer being called (and possibly isn't registered from what I can see in the IDE).

title: Statechangelistener prevents GroupItem to be disposed
body:
When a GroupItem registers a StateChangeListener in form of another GroupItem, the deletion of the latter won't remove the StateChangeListener, because the toElement method in ManagedItemProvider creates a new instance of the GroupItem to perform the tidy up task on. Later the removeStateChangeListener of the newly created GroupItem will be called, but this will fail since there are none. The Java GarbageCollector will remove the GroupItem from the ItemRegistryImpl but stops at the old GroupItem, since it's still referenced from the GroupItem which holds the reference on it's listeners. When creating a new GroupItem with the same uid the GroupItem won't add the new GroupItem as a listener, since the overriden equals method of a GenericItem will state them the same, because the comparison isn't done by object id. Thus the listener of the old GroupItem will be used and the new GroupItem won't get updates.
If questions arise i'll be happy to provide additional informations.

Greetings,
maw

I did a little further analysis. There are two options:

a)
the thing handler _was_ successfully initialized before because it could handle the missing bridge situation gracefully and went ONLINE. Then the bridge handler is _not_ informed _correctly_ as the child handle won't be initialized again. It gets informed about the updated thing instead. All good, works a designed.

b)
the thing handle failed during the initialize and threw an exception, the thing went into `UNINITIALIZED/HANDLER_INITIALIZING_ERROR`. In this case, the framework attempts to initialize the handler. However, there is glitch in there - the handler was created before with the "old" thing, and therefore we  run into this situation:

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/ec3cc58a493da1293c166513928ce92b8c85eeff/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/ThingManager.java#L571-L574

title: Bridge nested syntax does not support different thingHandlerFactory for thing
body:
This issue is a follow up from #5301 and refers to a somewhat experimental technology at the moment.

Given are two bundles that share the same binding id. Reasons for this are described in #5301 A prototype for this is the [blukii support](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/tree/master/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.bluetooth.blukii) or the modbus based [sunspec support](https://github.com/mrbig/openhab2-addons/tree/3216-binding-sunspec-modbus/addons/binding/org.openhab.binding.modbus.sunspec)

The issue arises when the bridge and the connected thing are from different bundles, and the nested syntax is used:

```
Bridge modbus:tcp:se4000 [ ... ] {
    inverter-single-phase myinverter [ ... ]
}
```

Currently these items are silently ignored, because the GenericThingProvider checks the proposed thing with the bridge's ThingHandlerFactory only. [See here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/5528ad5e460e2d8b6412bc34610530c0f2f06a28/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.thing/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/thing/internal/GenericThingProvider.xtend#L232)

I propose, that we should rescan every thingHandlerFactory each time the code is recursing into nested bridges/things. To avoid incorrect connection between different bindings may the binding id could been checked and if they don't match then ignore the thingHandlerFactory.


Note: a workaround for this is to ignore the nested syntax in such cases and use flat list with references, so the above could be rewritten as:
```
Bridge modbus:tcp:se4000 [ ... ]
Thing modbus:inverter-single-phase:se4000:myinverter (modbus:tcp:se4000) [...]
```

[2018-04-29T12:50:36Z | hsudbrock | comment]
Thanks for pointing out this issue @PiscisSwimeatus.

@kaikreuzer I agree that the bundle should not become active at all on Windows. I think that, ideally, the bundle should not even be installed on a Windows system. I had hoped that this might be achievable using a requirement in a Karaf feature on the property `osgi.os`. However, I stumbled upon https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/1416, where it is stated that this property is not set within Karaf instances.

Hence, I see two points for improvement here:
1. Do net let the DS component `SysfsUsbSerialScanner` become active on Windows systems (or, more generally, on systems where the sysfs cannot be scanned). In consequence, the 5-second polling of the sysfs will not happen.
2. Move the bundle `org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.usbserial.linuxsysfs` to its own Karaf feature (currently, it is contained in the Karaf feature that also contains `org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.usbserial`).

I think that 1. should be implemented (and would also provide a PR for that). I am not yet sure whether, on top of the DS component not being active, the complete bundle should not be active.

When also implementing 2., I think that this would mean that one would have to explicitly install an additional feature for being able to use the USB-Serial discovery on Linux systems. This is why I am not sure whether this should be done (but could also provide a PR, if discussion result here is that we want this).

What do you think?

title: [astro] Time drift on positional job
body:
The sun elevation is supposed to be calculated at a regular frequency (default is every 300s). However, due to the use of `scheduleWithFixedDelay` for the positional job, which schedules the job starting from the termination of the previous job to the commencement of the next job, there is a small time drift introduced. This time drift can be anywhere from a few milliseconds to 35-40 milliseconds per execution, depending on the CPU speed.

Example of drift:
```
2018-04-30 17:36:52.955 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 262.15 to 263.18
2018-04-30 17:41:53.000 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 263.18 to 264.20
2018-04-30 17:46:53.042 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 264.20 to 265.21
2018-04-30 17:51:53.060 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 265.21 to 266.22
2018-04-30 17:56:53.093 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 266.22 to 267.21
2018-04-30 18:01:53.090 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 267.21 to 268.21
2018-04-30 18:06:53.113 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 268.21 to 269.19
2018-04-30 18:11:53.211 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 269.19 to 270.18
2018-04-30 18:16:53.241 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 270.18 to 271.15
2018-04-30 18:21:53.338 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 271.15 to 272.13
2018-04-30 18:26:53.378 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 272.13 to 273.10
2018-04-30 18:31:53.422 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 273.10 to 274.06
2018-04-30 18:36:53.458 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 274.06 to 275.03
```

This drift could be eliminated (or greatly reduced) by the use of `scheduleAtFixedRate` instead of `scheduleWithFixedDelay`.

The guidelines indicate `scheduleWithFixedDelay` is preferred. However, as the astro binding performs accurate calculations, it can be argued that the frequency with which those calculations are performed also should be accurate. Therefore a deviation from the guidelines is warranted.

Reference this forum discussion [here](https://community.openhab.org/t/astro-binding-event-drift/44328)

title: Sitemap updates the wrong widgets after reordering
body:
Let's assume we have a sitemap like this:

```xtend
sitemap test label="Test Sitemap" {
    Frame label="Test Items" {
        Text item=testNumber
        Text item=testDimmer
    }
}
```

It's going to look like this in Basic UI:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39534945-00250fec-4e33-11e8-8622-adb1cd3f3af6.png)

Now I have a rule that increments the testNumber item's state on a regular basis. 

When I now change the order of the two widgets in the sitemap file like this:

```xtend
sitemap test label="Test Sitemap" {
    Frame label="Test Items" {
        Text item=testDimmer
        Text item=testNumber
    }
}
```

then the Basic UI refreshes automatically and correctly looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39535106-5fff5b3e-4e33-11e8-914f-2ca106433536.png)

However, as soon as the numberItem state changes for the next time, it is going to look like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39535153-7f644f5c-4e33-11e8-81d6-36b87fe95990.png)

As you can see, the wrong widget gets updated.

After a quick analysis it looks like the `PageChangeListener` keeps operating with a stale collection of widgets and therefore calculates the widgetIDs wrong. 

This in fact is a regression introduced by #3846. I will push a fix which partially reverts #3846 in a few moments.

title: Bridge Thing offline, but child things stay online
body:
In my openhab binding (pentair), I have a serial bridge with several child things.  If there is a setup error for the bridge, I set the status of the bridge to offline (updateStatus(ThingStatus.OFFLINE, ThingStatusDetail.CONFIGURATION_ERROR, msg)).  This is reflected correctly in the paperUI.  However, all the child things still go ONLINE.  I had thought the framework took care of not allow child things to go online if their corresponding bridge is OFFLINE.  Can someone confirm or do I need to manually manage this part of the lifecycle in the binding?

Thanks,
Jeff
comments:
[2018-05-09T05:33:07Z | J-N-K | comment]
Your thing handler should take care of the thing‘s status in „bridgeStatusChanged“.

[2018-05-09T09:50:47Z | sjsf | comment]
The implementation in `BaseThingHandler.bridgeStatusChanged()` should by default do exactly what you want: 

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/936287de21b7a6baabcf969899b9b62d2faac0bf/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/binding/BaseThingHandler.java#L672-L680

If you didn't override this method in your thing handlers and it's not working as expected, then this needs to be looked into more closely for any potential bugs.

[2018-05-09T14:45:29Z | jsjames | comment]
I don't have bridgeStatusChanged overloaded.  But it appears that if the Bridge sets status to OFFLINE in its initialize function, bridgeStatusChanged is never called.  In my case, that is what is happening.

In looking at some other code in other another binding (dcsalarm), it looks like in the initialize function for the child things, they automatically set the child status to OFFLINE.  Then, they implement bridgeStatusChanged to determine when the bridge goes online and at that point initialize the child thing.

Assuming this is how it should work by design, I can implement the same in my binding?

[2018-05-09T15:15:23Z | sjsf | comment]
Ah, I see. I checked the `ThingManager` code and indeed you hit a weak spot there. The bridge obviously needs to be initialized first, before the thing handlers are created. So they cannot be possible to inform them because they simply don't exist at that point in time. 

However, when the `ThingManager` then turns to the thing handler, it only checks whether they are initialized:

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/5b746e3084ca2803400549bd5467a11c7116d92b/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/ThingManager.java#L520-L526

It doesn't care whether the bridge is online or not. The question now is whether it would help if the `ThingManager` would call the child thing handler's `initialize()` _only_ once the bridge becomes ONLINE. Under the assumption that the bridge is required in order to successfully communicate with the device, I think this would make sense. 

Nevertheless, the child handle must be able to cope with the situation that the communication breaks down at any time anyways.

So, TL;DR: No, I don't think this is good to implement this logic in the binding. It puts the same burden on all bindings. This is something which the framework should take care of. IMHO this is a bug.

[2018-05-11T09:07:56Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I do not agree that this is a bug in the framework - we require ThingHandlers to always set a ThingStatus within the `initialize()` method. If the pentair binding currently sets it to ONLINE no-matter-what, then this is clearly a bug in the binding.

As every binding must have some logic of how to determine a correct thing status (and by this obviously also reflecting the bridge status), this logic should best be called from `initialize` as well.

Not calling `initialize` at all by the framework is imho no valid approach as it must be absolutely valid to perform some handler logic upon startup even if there isn't any communication with the remote device possible. Note that the method is meant to initialize the handler, not the remote device.

[2018-07-09T14:15:16Z | triller-telekom | comment]
> Note that the method (`initialize`) is meant to initialize the handler, not the remote device.

I agree with this and maybe we want to consider, or at least think about, implementing a initialization method for the device as well, in the context of https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/3484. But this is out of scope for this issue...

So this makes me think whether we should move this issue to https://github.com/openhab/openhab2-addons where the pentair binding is located. There the binding can be fixed to properly handle the ThingStatus. WDYT?

[2018-09-11T14:13:07Z | htreu | comment]
> Assuming this is how it should work by design, I can implement the same in my binding?

@jsjames please continue with the fix of this issue in your binding. The discussion here shows that the handler initialization is responsible for setting the correct status. For child thing handlers this might be even `UNKNOWN` in case you are not able to decide the correct status right away.

title: Setpoint state contains whole label
body:
When using a setpoint with a label formatter the state of the setpoint seems to contain the whole formatter.

```
Number TestSetpoint_1
Number TestSetpoint_2
```

```
    Frame
    {
        Setpoint item=TestSetpoint_1 label="[%d]" minValue=1 maxValue=12 step=1
        Setpoint item=TestSetpoint_2 label="[%d s]" minValue=1 maxValue=12 step=1
    }
```

```
rule "Rollershutter"
when
    Item TestSetpoint_1 changed or 
    Item TestSetpoint_2 changed
then
    logInfo("TestSetpoint", triggeringItem.toString )
end
```

logg
```
[INFO ] [.smarthome.model.script.TestSetpoint] - TestSetpoint_1 (Type=NumberItem, State=6, Label=null, Category=null)
[ome.event.ItemCommandEvent] - Item 'TestSetpoint_2' received command 4 s
[vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - TestSetpoint_2 changed from 3 s to 4 s
[INFO ] [.smarthome.model.script.TestSetpoint] - TestSetpoint_2 (Type=NumberItem, State=4 s, Label=null, Category=null)
```

so the setpoint is not usable in rules as it does not only contain the number but the whole formatter as state.

title: Unit support broke lambdas in Rules/Scripts
body:
As mentioned [here](https://community.openhab.org/t/openhab-2-3-release-candidate-available/45318/29, closures don't work properly anymore. 

The reason is that the terminal rule which was introduced in #4818 had precedence over any other rule and thereby accidentally also "grabbed" the closures.  The `XClosure` also uses the same square-bracket syntax but not on terminal level.

Having looked into this, I don't see a way of fixing it unambiguously. The decision to use square brackets also in the context of quantities simply does not work.

title: [Tradfri] MemoryLeak on connection resume
body:
Whenever the Tradfri binding re-establishes a broken connection to the gateway, it leaks quite some memory to the heap. This is particularly painful when using an unstable link (e.g. via power-line communication). The fact that each instance of the `InMemoryConnectionStore` puts a towel onto 500000 seats (~2MB) by default adds a very painful trait to this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/40488351-e0d20894-5f66-11e8-91d0-8c98faad06d6.png)

In this case, ~200 MB were aggregated over the time of only 3 days. 

On a first quick glance it looks like the `CoapObserveRelation`s keep themselves entertained by re-trying to connect all the time and thereby re-scheduling themselves. They need to be cancelled explicitly. Not sure yet if there is anything else left to cleanup, especially the restart of the `DTLSConnection` might be dodgy too...

This seems to be a little bit more tricky than thought on a first place...

If I change the `JsonStorageService` to replace unwanted characters with for example "_", this service will always do that and look for files that have the "_" instead of ":" for example. This is no problem for new installations which do not yet have any jsondb storage files on the file-system.

On systems with existing jsondb files on the file-system, those files will not be found anymore.

Since the JSONDBStorgae is used throughout the framework I rather decided to fix this issue just in the biding, because using the ThingUID as a storage name is apparently not a good idea, at least on windows systems. title: UoM: 'toUnit' is not a member of 'org.eclipse.smarthome.core.library.types.QuantityType'
body:
In a rule under OH 2.3.0, I receive this log error:

```
'toUnit' is not a member of 'org.eclipse.smarthome.core.library.types.QuantityType'
```

in reaction to the expression `MyItemName.state.toUnit('mph')` for a `Number:Speed` item. Also, an attempt to `import tec.uom.se.AbstractUnit` at the top of the rule does not result in resolving `AbstractUnit` when the rule tries to use the `parse` static method.

@kaikreuzer:

> I have seen the same error and wondered why it happened. We might need some implicit imports in Xbase for it - @watou I would say that this is worth a separate issue (as I consider it a bug). 

See https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/5243#issuecomment-397846492

Example rule that produces the log message:

```
import java.net.URLEncoder
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Map
import java.util.TimeZone
import tec.uom.se.AbstractUnit

/* Uploads weather station data using this format:

   http://wiki.wunderground.com/index.php/PWS_-_Upload_Protocol
 */

rule PWS
when
	Item DavisVantageVueWindDirectionAverage received update
then
	val sdf = new SimpleDateFormat('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')
	sdf.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone('UTC'))
	val Map<String, Object> params = newLinkedHashMap(
		'action' ->           'updateraw',
		'ID' ->               'XXXX',
		'PASSWORD' ->         'xxxx',
		'dateutc' ->          sdf.format(new Date()),
		'winddir' ->          DavisVantageVueWindDirection.state,
		'windspeedmph' ->     DavisVantageVueWindSpeed.state.toUnit('mph'),
		'windgustmph' ->      DavisVantageVueWindSpeedMaximum.state.toUnit('mph'),
		'windgustdir' ->      DavisVantageVueWindDirectionAverage.state,
		'windspdmph_avg2m' -> DavisVantageVueWindSpeedAverage.state.toUnit('mph'),
		'winddir_avg2m' ->    DavisVantageVueWindDirectionAverage.state,
		'humidity' ->         DavisVantageVueHumidity.state,
		'tempf' ->            DavisVantageVueOutdoorTemperature.state.toUnit('°F'),
		'rainin' ->           DavisVantageVueRainCurrentHour.state.toUnit('in'),
		'baromin' ->          MeteoStickPressure.state.toUnit('inHg'),
		'softwaretype' ->     'openHAB 2.3')

	var url = 'https://weatherstation.wunderground.com/weatherstation/updateweatherstation.php?'
	var first = true
	for (key : params.keySet()) {
		if (!first) {
			url += '&'
		}
		url += key + '=' + URLEncoder::encode(params.get(key).toString, 'UTF-8')
		first = false
	}

	logDebug('PWS', 'url is {}', url)
	sendHttpGetRequest(url)
end
```
comments: [2018-06-18T13:45:19Z | kaikreuzer | comment] I did some analysis, it seems we have multiple problems: 1. Your rule is actually not correct. `DavisVantageVueWindDirection.state` provides you a `State` and `toUnit` is indeed not defined on `State`. If you instead do a `DavisVantageVueWindDirection.getStateAs(QuantityType).toUnit('mph')`, all should work as expected. 2. I would have expected a warning in the log at loading time of the rule, when such a problem exists. I have checked VS Code with LSP support enabled and this shows that the runtime is actually capable of finding this through static analysis: I do not know, why it fails to log this message upon loading of the file as well. 3. The message that is logged during runtime is confusing. What it probably tries to say is `'toUnit' is not a member of State`, but it prints the type of the actual instance, which is by chance a `QuantityType`, in which case (only) the statement is actually incorrect. [2016-06-16T11:25:25Z | afuechsel | comment]
I analyzed this a bit. `updateProperties()` actually updates the properties at least in the hue binding, but code is called more than once and the update is only beeing done because of the special implementation in the hue binding. Explanation: 

E.g. the hue binding sets 3 properties in its `HueLightHandler#initialize()` method: 

```
updateProperty(Thing.PROPERTY_MODEL_ID, modelId);
updateProperty(Thing.PROPERTY_FIRMWARE_VERSION, fullLight.getSoftwareVersion());
//...
updateProperty(Thing.PROPERTY_VENDOR, vendor);
```

What happens, is this: 
1. updateProperty calls `AbstractManagedProvider#update()` that logs a warning "Could not update element with key {} in {}, because it does not exists."
2. `ThingManager#thingUpdated()` is called. It throws an IllegalStateException. 
3. the initialize-Method of the HueLighthandler is left immediately due to this exception
4. This Exception is ccaught in the HueBridgehandler's polling loop
5. Now _only because this is a polling loop_ the initialize() method of the HueLightHandler is called _again_ trying to set the properties _again_ 
6. the first call updateProperty now woul _not_ again throw an exception, due to the check in BasicThingHandler, whether the value has already been set (which has been in the previous call) 
7. the second updateProperty will now be executed, logging again a warning, throwing again an exception and bailing out
8. pollingLoop continues...

Eventually, after several calls of the same code, all properties would be set, several exceptions would have been thrown, several log messages would have been shown... Not an ideal case. 

Bindings without such a loop would bail out at the first exception and no property would be set. 

### Suggestion
- Remove the IllegalStateException being thrown for read-only properties, replacing it with a debug logging
- change the warning logging to a debug as well

title: NPE in PersistentInbox
body:
We encountered a Nullpointer-Exception in `PersistentInbox` which prevents `org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.AutomaticInboxProcessor` component activation as it is thrown in a method called by the activate method.

    [SCR] Exception while activating instance org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.AutomaticInboxProcessor@fc49e9 of component org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.AutomaticInboxProcessor
    [...]
    Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
    --
    at org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.PersistentInbox.stream(PersistentInbox.java:303)
    at org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.PersistentInbox.getAll(PersistentInbox.java:297)
    at org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery.internal.AutomaticInboxProcessor.autoApproveInboxEntries(AutomaticInboxProcessor.java:230)

comments:
[2018-07-18T12:02:00Z | htreu | comment]
Summary of the findings in #5921:

The `StorageService` is `dynamic, mandatory` in `PersistentInbox` so an instance should be present when the `Inbox` is injected into `AutomaticInboxProcessor`. Depending on the `StorageService` implementation the `getValues()` method is the next candidate to return a `null` reference.

[2018-07-19T11:56:25Z | maggu2810 | comment]
@DaHoC It would be great if you can comment the commit ID your ESH bundles are based on to match the stacktrace to the correct sources.

The `PersistentInbox` has not been changed the last two month, but in general it would be helpful.

```Java
    @Override
    @NonNullByDefault({})
    public Stream<DiscoveryResult> stream() {
        return this.discoveryResultStorage.getValues().stream().filter(Objects::nonNull);
}
```

The `return ...;` line is the one the NPE is raised.

As @htreu already comment above, I don't this that `discoveryResultStorage` is null (if the lifecycle is not violated) so perhaps `getValues()` return null.

Which storage provider is used?

[2018-07-23T10:36:52Z | DaHoC | comment]
We encounter this issue already since around 15/Nov/17 all the time in a gateway which is permanently performing lifecycle-tests, so there is a chance that indeed a matching StorageService component is not available at that point in time when the `stream()` call is made, which in turn is called indirectly by the `AutomaticInboxProcessor` activator method.
But it might also be the case that the StorageService is present, but its `.getValues()` returns `null` - trying to gain access to that information, also to which storage provider is used.
The commit ID the ESH bundles are based upon should be 6d32c35f934b6b5a627cc4a32ff91564902bdc2a

[2018-07-24T07:57:20Z | DaHoC | comment]
Unable to provide more useful information, because during normal operation all services and dependencies are satisfied.
It is some effect only occurring during bundle / service life-cycle changes, maybe due to the way the `volatile` `discoveryResultStorage` is initialized aside during injection of the `StorageService`.
I came up with a possible explanation:

This injection is done in a different thread than the thread calling the `activate()` method, so that it causes a synchronization issue/race condition when in the "injection" thread the `discoveryResultStorage` is just about to being assigned while the "activate" thread accesses the not yet written (thus null) value.

To avoid this possible error cause, it is generally best to avoid misuse of (wired) setters and getters for other stuff than setting and getting the variable in question - It could be done rather easily in this case, and would complement the existing PR to make the code more clean & robust

[2018-07-24T09:54:24Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Thanks for your analysis.

> It could be done rather easily in this case, and would complement the existing PR to make the code more clean & robust

I assume you are talking about `PersistentInbox.setStorageService` here? How could that be easily changed considering that it is a dynamic reference?

[2018-07-24T10:37:11Z | DaHoC | comment]
Exactly, I meant providing an accessor for the `discoveryResultStorage` instead of initializing it in the wired setter of `setStorageService(final StorageService storageService)`, something like

    @NonNullByDefault({})
    private synchronized Storage<DiscoveryResult> getDiscoveryResultStorage() {
        if (storageService == null) {
            return null; // What to do in this case, should not happen
        }
        return storageService.getStorage(DiscoveryResult.class.getName(), this.getClass().getClassLoader());
    }

However, this requires the specific StorageService implementation to not create a new storage for each call of `storageService.getStorage(..)` (which is a getter, not a ctor, so by convention it should be fine)

[2018-07-24T12:37:12Z | maggu2810 | comment]
The activate method is not called before any mandatory references are set (regardless if it is dynamic or not).
The variable is volatile.

I don't get the race condition you try to explain above. Can you explain the potential race condition more detailed?

[2018-07-24T13:13:54Z | DaHoC | comment]
As said, it's just an assumption / attempt to explain a scenario where the NPE happens in lack of a better explanation:

E.g. the compiler/JVM/OSGi logic does not recognize that the `setStorageService` is not only a setter, but also initializes the `discoveryResultStorage`.
Therefore the OSGi lifecycle magic could mistakenly assume that the `activate()` method and this setter method are unrelated when in fact, the `activate()` method relies on this setter being called beforehand (wiring the storageService reference).
That could cause this storageService reference, especially as it is dynamic, to be injected at a later point in time, or/and by a different thread than the `activate()` method.

I'm open for alternative suggestions on how the NPE could otherwise happen.

Asking the other way round: What more can we do here than to make the code more robust in this place than done in the PR if we can't analyze the causes of this NPE properly?

[2018-07-24T13:35:35Z | maggu2810 | comment]

```

and check the result?

Adding the information if `timeToLiveChecker` reference is present and if it is cancelled should also state if there is a lifecycle violation by the caller.

title: ClassCastExceptions when updating SmartHome bundles
body:
migrated from Bugzilla [#478783](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=478783)
status NEW severity _normal_ in component _Core_ for _---_
Reported in version _0.8.0_ on platform _PC_
Assigned to: Project Inbox

On 2015-10-01 03:48:27 -0400, Jochen Hiller wrote:

> We are using Eclipse SmartHome running on an OSGi framework where we make on a regular base updates of bundles.
> It happened in rare cases (especially when a bundle does not stop correct) that during the update class loaders can not be cleaned up by the framework. This lead to the situation that after the update some bundles did use object instances from an old class loader.
> This happened for bundles where object instances are shared between bundles, the packages are exported by an Export-Package directive, but NOT imported in bundle via an Import-Package. We changed that in according bundles which did solve this issue.
> 
> There is blog post from Peter Kriens about concepts of Export/Import package since OSGi R4:
> http://blog.osgi.org/2007/04/importance-of-exporting-nd-importing.html
> 
> Peter recommends as a best practice that in standard case all Export-package should be reflected also as an Import-Package. 
> 
> We recommend to apply this best practice to all ESH bundles. We will provide a PullRequest where we change all MANIFEST that every Export-Package will have a corresponding Import-Package.
> 
> Any comments on that? Especially from people running ESH on other frameworks, like Equinox, Felix, Karaf.

On 2015-10-01 04:09:24 -0400, Markus Rathgeb wrote:

> I already stumbled over this topic after starting with OSGi.
> I don't know why this is not done. Perhaps because the Eclipse IDE does not generate that stuff in the Manifest.
> 
> For myself I am using the maven-bundle-plugin for OSGi bundles and delegate the Manifest generation (sometimes with some additional instructions in the pom) to that plugin.
> But the Eclipse IDE does support all that "non Eclipse stuff" (in a comfortable way).

On 2015-10-01 04:16:21 -0400, Kai Kreuzer wrote:

> So this means that the maven-bundle-plugin also automatically creates imports for all exports? So I take this as an approval of Jochen's request then.

On 2015-10-01 04:23:13 -0400, Markus Rathgeb wrote:

> maven-bundle-plugin:
> <Import-Package> is assumed to be "*", which imports everything referred to by the bundle content, but not contained in the bundle. Any exported packages are also imported by default, to ensure a consistent class space.
comments:
[2015-12-03T10:37:32Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
While we have added the imports on many bundles, it also lead to problems on the Xtext ones as they contain split packages.
After all, we came to the conclusion that while the CCE can be solved this way, you can have many other problems, if a bundle does not shut down correctly and thus keeps old classloaders blocked.
I therefore close this issue as won't fix.
