title: Allow bindings to deactivate auto-update for channels
body:
migrated from Bugzilla [#481178](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=481178)
status NEW severity _normal_ in component _Core_ for _---_
Reported in version _unspecified_ on platform _PC_
Assigned to: Project Inbox

On 2015-10-31 19:43:07 -0400, Kai Kreuzer wrote:

> By default, the auto-update binding sets the status for a channel after seeing a command for it. The binding must be allowed to deactivate this feature for certain channels, so that it can have the state updates under its own control.
comments:
[2017-02-27T09:42:10Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> By default, the auto-update binding sets the status for a channel after seeing a command for it. The binding must be allowed to deactivate this feature for certain channels, so that it can have the state updates under its own control.

I am currently looking into this...

Please correct me if I am wrong, but the auto-update post an update for the item after receiving a command for it.
This could currently be disabled by implementations of `AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider` by using the item name.

There could be different ways to implement that feature, so, without going into deeper details of the special implementations I assume the principle is equal.
The ItemChannelLinkRegistry needs to be used to get the channel UIDs of the linked channels.
Then we could take the binding ID and decide if an auto-update should be done (how it is done e.g. by provided services, a map that is filled by some code, ... does not matter now).

But what is the desired behaviour of:

* binding A provides thing A that contains channel `channel_A`
* binding B provides thing B that contains channel `channel_B`
* there is an item `multiLinkedItem`
* `channel_A` is linked to `multiLinkedItem`
* `channel_B` is linked to `multiLinkedItem`
* binding A wants to enable the auto update
* binding B wants to disable the auto update
* `multiLinkedItem` received a command (e.g. `SwitchType.ON`)

At the moment, if there exists multiple `AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider` for the same item the auto update is done if at least one enables the auto update.
Should we proceed the same way using binding IDs?

[2017-02-27T21:52:15Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Then we could take the binding ID and decide if an auto-update should be done

Hm, I think the binding ID is much too coarse grained. The idea of this issue was to achieve a similar feature as in OH1, where a binding can decide for each item (here now channel), whether it wants to disable the auto-update as it itself will take care of reliable status updates after commands. This feature very much depends on the specific channel, so having just all on/off isn't imho helpful.

Also note that the AutoUpdateBinding is a remainder of the otherwise already removed OH1 binding APIs - we will have to think about whether it makes sense to keep it in place (also with the AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider interface). While this still allows the user to add an `{ autoupdate="false"}` in an item file, there is no equivalent for any db defined items available. I therefore wonder if the ItemChannelLinks might not be a better place for such an information.

> At the moment, if there exists multiple AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider for the same item the auto update is done if at least one enables the auto update.
> Should we proceed the same way using binding IDs?

To me, this is a bit unlogical (I cannot remember the reason why it had been built like that). Imho it would be better to give every binding a veto, so that auto-update if off, if a single binding turns it off as it wants to take care of the updates itself.

[2017-02-27T22:06:37Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> so having just all on/off isn't imho helpful.

It is at least helpful for persons like me, that don't rely an the auto-update at all and so I want to disable it for every item that is linked to some channel of a thing of that bindings.

> The idea of this issue was to achieve a similar feature as in OH1, where a binding can decide for each item (here now channel), whether it wants to disable the auto-update as it itself will take care of reliable status updates after commands. This feature very much depends on the specific channel, so having just all on/off isn't imho helpful.

Hm, if the binding author wants to use the auto-update for some channels and don't want to use it for others channel, why not simply put the updateState line into the handleCommand method of the respective channels.
Why should I try add a bunch of configuration as binding author?
As he already implements the handleCommand method he could skip updating states for every implementation or handle it differently in the code.

> Also note that the AutoUpdateBinding is a remainder of the otherwise already removed OH1 binding APIs - we will have to think about whether it makes sense to keep it in place (also with the AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider interface). 

I don't think it is very useful for the normal use case.
Perhaps there should be one option to configure the behaviour for all the items that are not linked and so do not correspondent to any binding.

> To me, this is a bit unlogical (I cannot remember the reason why it had been built like that). Imho it would be better to give every binding a veto, so that auto-update if off, if a single binding turns it off as it wants to take care of the updates itself.

Okay for me, too, if we want to break the current behaviour.

[2017-02-28T07:00:36Z | maggu2810 | comment]
IIRC AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider is not inly a reminder but used by model.item

[2017-02-28T09:47:39Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> It is at least helpful for persons like me, that don't rely an the auto-update at all

Well, there is a much simpler solution for you: Simply remove the autoupdate bundle from your setup :-)

>  why not simply put the updateState line into the handleCommand method of the respective channels.

Because the default behavior, especially if there is NO binding is that the state update is done. Removing this feature would force every binding to do it manually.

> Why should I try add a bunch of configuration as binding author?

As we do not have a deactivation feature in place yet, but a large number of well-working bindings, I think this shows that deactivating the auto-update is rather the exception. And the required "bunch of configuration" could be a simple flag that we add to the channel xml, this can be pretty simply.

> AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider is not inly a reminder but used by model.item

Yes, it is used for parsing the `{}` parts of the item files. But this is part of "old" APIs - with ESH bindings, the only used value is the "channel" reference. I didn't say that we can easily remove the BindingConfigProvider interface right now, I just didn't want to raise its importance again.

[2017-02-28T12:15:43Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> Simply remove the autoupdate bundle from your setup

This does not work as long as I want to use an unmodified model.item.
Sure, I can add a custom bundle that provides the `AutoUpdateBindingConfigProvider` interface in the same package but this isn't a better work around at all.

And as you have written above, there are bindings that rely on the auto-update, so, removing the auto-update bundle completely will not work, too.

[2017-02-28T12:21:08Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I updated the PR #3082 
* The new interface offers two function to add and remove a configuration to enable / disable auto-update for a whole binding (by Binding ID)
* The new interface offers two function to add and remove a configuration to enable / disable auto-update for channels (by Channel UID)

[2017-02-28T12:22:34Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> This does not work as long as I want to use an unmodified model.item.

Ah, I wasn't even aware of the AutoUpdateGenericBindingConfigProvider. It does not seem to have any dependency to the model stuff, so possibly this could be moved to the autoupdate bundle (and thus allow you to not include it)?

[2017-02-28T12:32:17Z | maggu2810 | comment]
The class implements the BindingConfigReader interface that is part of model.item

[2017-02-28T15:13:56Z | sjsf | comment]
I just read though this discussion here. To be honest, I don't think this is going into the right direction. The problem I see is that the question whether the auto-update should be active or not not only depends on the binding developer's point of view, but also in many cases on the concrete setup and user preferences. 
As a matter of fact, this must be a property of each ItemChannelLink. Clearly, the binding may announce its preference (either per binding or per channel), but this can only be an indication for a default. In the end, the user must be able to override this.
I'm currently thinking about the profile idea (as mentioned in #583, #1043, #2226 - so far mainly in the context of triggers) and prototyping a little around this. My preference currently goes into the direction of decoupling ThingManager from ThingHandlers a little by adding a "routing" (or "profile") layer in between those two for triggers, updates and commands. 
So as an example, we would have a command-profile which simply delegated a command to the handler (i.e. "no-auto-update"), and another one which in addition also updates the item state (i.e. "auto-update"). Which one is taken depends on  

1. a configuration property of the ItemChannelLink
2. the binding's preference for a channel
3. the binding's preference generally
4. and "auto-update = true" as a default if none of the above gave any clue (in order to preserve compatibility). 

So, to be honest, I see that your approach fixing a flaw in the current auto-update binding. However, I would rather like to see it dropped completely and replaced by a core feature which is easier to handle configuration wise.

[2017-02-28T16:28:41Z | maggu2810 | comment]
@sjka Thank you for your comment.
What do you think about the scenario where two channels are linked to the same item?

To use your example:

* the first link uses the "no auto-update" profile
* the second link uses the "auto-update" profile

If the profiles are handled separately the "no auto-update" profile will delegate the command to the handler. The "auto-update" profile will delegate the command to the other handler and update the item.
So it fits to the old "logical OR" implementation.

This is okay for me (at least I think so at the moment) because if someone uses one item for two different channels the situation could be very indeterministic at all.
But this does not fit to Kai's expectations above.

> To me, this is a bit unlogical (I cannot remember the reason why it had been built like that). Imho it would be better to give every binding a veto, so that auto-update if off, if a single binding turns it off as it wants to take care of the updates itself.

[2017-03-01T11:15:14Z | sjsf | comment]
> if someone uses one item for two different channels the situation could be very indeterministic

That is indeed a very valid point. My intention was the opposite: that as a user, I want to stay in control of who (framework, binding - and if so: which one...) updates the state of an item, in order to make such situations as deterministic as possible. 

So to stay in the above example: What if both bindings "veto" the auto-update and handle it themselves? Which one wins? And what if they don't behave in the exact same way? As a user, I want to be able to fix this.

Nevertheless, I agree that my proposal for a default with the "logical OR" was not ideal. The "first veto disables the auto-update" might be the better default strategy. However, I still think that the user needs the ability to pick a "winner" binding. But maybe that's a different story about ignoring updates coming from a specific binding where the profile idea attached to ItemChannelLinks would be a better fit. And indeed, then it would be sufficient to have the auto-update configuration directly at the Item, and not at the ItemChannelLink. 

For the rest of my thoughts (i.e. influencing the communication between framework and binding wrt commands, updates, triggers in order to gain back some level control), I will of course create a separate issue once I have a valid proposal as a starting point. You convinced me that these two topics don't conflict with each other.

But back to the topic of this issue: I actually tend to agree that it would make sense to break with the existing behavior wrt auto-update:

* Auto-Update is the default
* Bindings may "opt-in" to take care of updating items (either binding-wide or for specific channels only) and by doing so they disable the auto-update for a linked item
* A user has the option to enable/disable the auto-update feature on item level, hence overriding the above logic completely.

When touching all this anyway, I would even consider moving it into the core.thing bundle, dropping the extra autoupdate one. Even if there are solutions which only use bindings that handle the updates themselves and therefore don't need the auto-update feature, then exactly these bindings will have a dependency to the autoupdate bundle because they want to declare their "opt-in". So I don't see any value in having it separated, or did I miss anything?

[2017-03-01T11:23:41Z | sjsf | comment]
PS: Just to make this clear

> And indeed, then it would be sufficient to have the auto-update configuration directly at the Item, and not at the ItemChannelLink.

I'm very well aware that as of today we don't have configurations on item level. And probably also don't want that. So we could use ItemChannelLink properties for this, but should be aware that conceptually this would be what it is: First "opt-in" of a binding wins for the whole item and an explicit enabling of auto-update at any ItemChannelLink would overrule any binding's opt-ins and still enable the auto-update.

[2017-06-07T16:00:48Z | digitaldan | comment]
ping!  
We also have a need for this in an upcoming omnilink 2.0 binding, I would vote to be able to configure this on the channel level.

[2017-08-24T10:10:43Z | triller-telekom | comment]
@digitaldan Currently there is a PR #4108 which introduces profiles on `ItemChannelLinks` and based on that there will soon be a follow-up PR introducing the ability to configure these auto-updates.

body:

On 2015-09-25 12:47:15 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> With the following simple rule, and with the Item TeslaScheduledDeparture holding a valid value (e.g. not NULL or UNDEF):
> 
> rule "Tesla - initiate variables rule"
> when 
>   System started
> then
>   TeslaScheduledDeparture.postUpdate(UnDefType.UNDEF)
>   logInfo("org.openhab","System Started : TeslaScheduledDeparture "+TeslaScheduledDeparture.state)
> end
> 
> the following is written to the logs:
> 
> 2015-09-25 18:40:12 [DEBUG] [.m.r.r.i.engine.RuleEngineImpl:267  ] - Executing startup rule 'Tesla - initiate variables rule'
> 2015-09-25 18:40:14 [INFO ] [o.e.s.model.script.org.openhab:48   ] - System Started : TeslaScheduledDeparture 2015-09-26T08:30:00
> 
> Does this async behaviour stem from the introduction of the safeCall()s? 
> 
> This is imho undesired behaviour, and leads to adverse effects in Rules. The workaround is to copy over Item.state(s) to locally defined variables at the beginning of each, to do the necessary processing, and at the exit of a rule, write back/postUpdate() any values to the Item.state(s)
> 
> Therefore, should lock()s be introduced on the ItemRegistry?

On 2015-09-26 03:40:32 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> > Does this async behaviour stem from the introduction of the safeCall()s? 
> 
> No, the safeCalls are executed synchronously. Only if a call takes longer than 10 seconds, the thread will continue to work.
> 
> ItÂ´s because a postUpdate is by definition asynchronously. The whole eventing system only allows asynchronous events.

On 2015-09-26 04:34:11 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> mhh... do you think this would not lead to problems then? like, you are never sure to have the latest value of an Item when you call .state 
> 
> Is there a recommended approach then for Rules?
> 
> Karel

On 2015-09-26 05:52:39 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> It depends. Do you really want to query the state of an item directly after you have updated it in a rule? If you sent a command you either donÂ´t know how long it will take before the binding changes the state. The behavior - independent from the eventing system - is just asynchronously.
> 
> What is your concrete use case?
> 
> If you want to get informed that a value was changed you can use the newly introduced ItemStateChangedEvent. This event is sent AFTER an item state was updated.

On 2015-09-26 05:59:06 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> I understand, but in this case the binding is not the limiting factor. it also happens with Items that are not bound to a binding.
> 
> ItemStateChangedEvent is not yet exposed to the ScriptEngine right?
> 
> K

On 2015-09-26 06:08:40 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> No itÂ´s not. But I think we donÂ´t need it there, as the Rule engine already has something like "Item MyItem changed" as a trigger. Even if the state of an Item might not be changed at this time, I think usually there is no problem, because you just work with the value from the update event inside the rule.

On 2015-09-26 07:19:08 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> Ah - that I am afraid does not hold true. At least in my case - you do not only need the value that has effectively changed, but also the latest value of all the there Items, either in or out "Item changed" clauses.
> 
> You either have to build very long complex Rules, with a trigger for every possible variable/Item you need in the rule, or you make a bunch of rules that are less complex, acting on a single Item. In such a constellation, if you update the value of an Item in Rule A, you do need that exact value maybe in Rule B. 
> 
> I can tell you from the use case I have here (automatic charging and pre-heating rules for my Tesla), that these "glitches" are very annoying and troublesome. And that is only relatively simple use case imho
> 
> Karel

> a check should be added to check whether a Job with the same identity exists in the scheduler, and if so, remove the existing job before trying to schedule the new job
>

Another use case I saw in the openhab2-addons repo is to get hold of the actual thing which is already accepted and start a discovery on the thing handler. This is also not intended and a misuse of the feature.

Instead of "resolving" the cyclic dependency like #6223 tried I suggest to completely get rid of the functionality introduced with the ExtendedDiscoveryService.
I will propose a PR which deprecates both interfaces `ExtendedDiscoveryService` and `DiscoveryServiceCallback` and introduces a default implementation for both methods `#getExistingThing` and `#getExistingDiscoveryResult` to always return `null`.

Ping @cdjackson: you are using the callback in the zwave binding. For [this feature](https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/blob/master/src/main/java/org/openhab/binding/zwave/discovery/ZWaveDiscoveryService.java#L216) (updating properties) you would have to introduce a binding locale map and cache results there.

[2018-09-18T10:41:36Z | cdjackson | comment]
So do I understand that you are removing the ability to check for, and get existing entries from the inbox?

[2018-09-18T11:49:03Z | cdjackson | comment]
> All occurrences merely check the existence of the discovery result or thing just to ignore the current result. This is actually a feature the persistent inbox already has, so it makes no sense to use the callback provided by the ExtendedDiscoveryService. 

This is not really correct that it makes no sense. The ZWave and ZigBee bindings use this to avoid having to perform lots of intensive discovery functions if they are already performed, and the thing is already in the inbox or approved. Instead of performing these functions, and then having the inbox ignore it, we check the inbox first to see if the thing already exists, and then don’t perform these intensive tasks.

I am not too keen to loose these functions, and if I understand correctly, you plan to remove them? Instead I think you propose that I need to replicate the inbox functions in the binding to know if the thing has already been added or not? It doesn’t seem very nice if this is the case, and has the potential to get out of sync. eg what if someone clears the inbox - how does the binding know this? 

Alternatively, we just have to perform the discovery every time, but that is likely to cause other problems on large networks.

It might also be worth reviewing https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1213 <https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1213> which was the original reason this was added. I suspect if we remove this, something will break.

[2018-09-18T12:37:40Z | htreu | comment]
yes, thats the plan. PersistentInbox is itself "clever" enough to deal with already existing entries. And as mentioned above, for the partial discovery you should then implement something which is binding local.

edit: sorry, I didn't mean to ignore your 2nd post. Autorefresh did only show me the first...

[2018-09-18T12:55:59Z | htreu | comment]
> perform lots of intensive discovery functions

Do you have a reference to this? I see from #1213 that this might be a problem. Although: when the binding/framework restarts and discovery starts fresh and new, how is "going back" to a raw discovery result a problem when the user didn't notice the old full fledged discovery result anyway?

[2018-09-18T13:33:54Z | cdjackson | comment]
No - I don’t have a reference to the intensive loading, but it came up again recently in ZigBee. Where people have large networks, it’s really useful for the binding to know if a thing is already known and included so we don’t have to blindly perform further discovery. On a Pi for example, just adding 20 or so things into the inbox, just to have them ignored was taking 20 or 30 seconds and maxing out the processor when it was otherwise meant to be doing discovery. Some people have networks with upwards of 100 devices - ok, maybe they have a better spec’d machine than a Pi, but if not, it is a big problem.

[2018-09-18T13:44:31Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I try to understand the discussion correctly, so please let me summarize:

* If a Z*** device is discovered the binding would like to know if the device is already known.
* "Is already known" could be:
  * a thing already exists
  * there exist already a discovery entry in the inbox

Right or wrong?

If it i a common use case, couldn't we provide a `KnownChecker` that provides a method `boolean isKnown(ThingUID thingUID)`. The `KnownChecker` could inpect the inbox entries and the thing registry.
If this is not a common use case, the binding could implement that service itself (and ignore the fact that it should not use that OSGi services like thing registry).

[2018-09-18T14:09:13Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
My expectation of discovery + inbox is that this is a passive scanning, which is just figuring out what is available in the network - causing 20-30s full CPU load sounds very wrong to me.
As long as a result is in the inbox, the user didn't express any interest in the device, so the system should not keep itself busy with it. Only once approved (and created as a Thing) should trigger expensive operations like active querying of all kinds of details.

[2018-09-18T14:12:19Z | cdjackson | comment]
> If a Z*** device is discovered the binding would like to know if the device is already known.
> "Is already known" could be:
> a thing already exists
> there exist already a discovery entry in the inbox
> Right or wrong?
> 
Yes, this is part of the issue.


The other issue is that once we add a thing, if we re-add it, then it will overwrite everything that is there, so any information already known is lost. This can happen occasionally, and causes confusion to users but is otherwise only a problem to the user. This was the original reason this was added as there was a lot of confusion!


> If this is not a common use case, the binding could implement that service itself (and ignore the fact that it should not use that OSGi services like thing registry).
> 
I have already had PRs rejected and been told that this is definitely not allowed...

[2018-09-18T14:15:17Z | cdjackson | comment]
> 
> My expectation of discovery + inbox is that this is a passive scanning,
> 
What does “Passive" mean? I thought that we need to have enough information to provide the thing type? That is NOT passive - in ZigBee and ZWave, this requires active scanning of devices. 

>  causing 20-30s full CPU load sounds very wrong to me.
> 
In the case of ZWave, it also requires the binding to look up a database of 800 devices and this takes time even if we already know all the information about the device!

> As long as a result is in the inbox, the user didn't express any interest in the device, so the system should not keep itself busy with it. Only once approved (and created as a Thing) should trigger expensive operations like active querying of all kinds of details.
> 
As above - in order to get enough information from the device to decide the thing type, active scanning is required.

[2018-09-19T08:40:27Z | htreu | comment]
> in ZigBee and ZWave, this requires active scanning of devices

With the ExtendedDiscoveryService gone (deactivated and deprecated) the only disadvantage would be to start scanning all over once the bundle/system restarts. During runtime you are able to cache results in-memory by yourself. 

> look up a database of 800 devices

This should neither be time nor space consuming. I do not consider this to be a problem where the existence of the ExtendedDiscoveryService helps a lot.

[2018-09-19T08:50:20Z | cdjackson | comment]
> During runtime you are able to cache results in-memory by yourself.

Agreed, this is possible.

> This should neither be time nor space consuming. I do not consider this to be a problem where the existence of the ExtendedDiscoveryService helps a lot
> 
How can it not be time consuming - it takes time/processing power to search a database right? On slow computers like a Pi, it takes a lot of time to search such a database - yes, it can be done in the background (and it is done in a separate thread in ZWave), but it still maxes out the processor for a (relatively) long time and I don’t immediately see a way around this? Yes, I could likely optimise the search algorithm to improve this, but so far it’s not been required, and even with an optimised search, it’s still going to take a significant amount of time, and systems with large networks will suffer.

I feel that there should be some sort of feedback available to help the discovery system in the binding and not simply assume that this is a one way path.

[2018-09-19T09:15:51Z | htreu | comment]
> it takes time/processing power to search a database right?

Of cause, I was exaggerating. What I mean is that any list of `800` is a relatively low number for databases. Even an in-memory map would probably do and would be blazing fast. But as you already mentioned this would be optimising an nothing in the light of this discussion.

> Agreed, this is possible.

Thanks for your agreement. I will close #6223 and author a 2nd commit which implements the suggested solution.

[2018-09-19T09:24:51Z | cdjackson | comment]
> 
> Thanks for your agreement. I will close #6223 <https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/6223> and author a 2nd commit which implements the suggested solution.
> 
I was agreeing that I can implement a local cache - but this will still be a major pain by deprecating this and as I said, I think there should be some feedback from the inbox, or even things list, into the discovery element of the binding to help the binding. It might work on the smaller systems that most people are used to, but on large complex systems such as ZWave where many people have large networks, it is not so nice.

As I already said, it takes quite a long time on a Pi to search the ZWave database - on a small network, I was recently seeing 20 seconds. Even if I optimise this, and can reduce it by 75%, we still have 5 seconds on a small network - for people with large networks (and 100+ devices is not uncommon) it will not work well on low powered systems.

Anyway, I guess I won’t convince you and we will have to live with this.

[2018-09-19T13:59:40Z | htreu | comment]
> it takes quite a long time on a Pi to search the ZWave database

Again, w/o deeper knowledge of the ZWave protocol, just from a computing pov this sounds like too much for a query in a 800 record database. It seems to be a good candidate for optimisation.

> I was agreeing that I can implement a local cache

We have to sync on this prior to merging #6237. I will leave a note on the PR.

[2018-09-19T14:19:47Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> What does “Passive" mean? I thought that we need to have enough information to provide the thing type? That is NOT passive - in ZigBee and ZWave, this requires active scanning of devices.

Yes, agreed. So let's reformulate it to "minimal effort" :-)

> I feel that there should be some sort of feedback available to help the discovery system in the binding and not simply assume that this is a one way path.

The problem at hand is that this two-way solution introduced a cycling dependency, which must be avoided in the architecture. Looking at it in detail, we also noticed that 95% of the places where `ExtendedDiscoveryService` is used, it is not done for a reason it was introduced for - so this is a clear signal that it's purpose is unclear to most people and we should clean this up.
Z-Wave is really the only remaining user of it. But I agree with you that we must come up with a decent alternative that is acceptable for you and implementable without much effort. Unnecessarily querying the Z-Wave network is to be avoided, I fully agree with you.

So I actually see two parts that you need:
1. Figure out if you have already discovered it, i.e. it is in the Inbox and update it with additional information, in case you found any.
2. Figure out if you have to care at all about it or if it already exists as a Thing and thus is irrelevant for the discovery.

For (1), the suggestion from above would be to keep a local map of previous results in the discovery service, which should make everything possible just as it is today with the sole restriction that it would be lost after a restart - but imho this is something we all could live with.

For (2), you actually do not access to all Things, but only to the Things that your `ZWaveControllerHandler` knows about - and luckily, the `ZWaveDiscoveryService` already has access to the `ZWaveControllerHandler`. Could a simple method be added to the handler that would answer whether a Z-Wave Thing of a given UID already exists or not? It seems to me as if there is no need to route this through the framework at all.

Wdyt?

[2018-09-19T18:41:04Z | cdjackson | comment]
> Again, w/o deeper knowledge of the ZWave protocol, just from a computing pov this sounds like too much for a query in a 800 record database. It seems to be a good candidate for optimisation
> 
I will see if I can optimise this. However note that while it’s 800 devices, the database is probably about 5 to 10 times larger as each device has multiple sets of IDs.  All I can say is that on slow computers (I say RPi,but I’m not sure it was a Pi - it was a commercial system) it was taking a long time for a small network. I will have to spend time to optimise this and see where it ends up, but it won’t be for a while unfortunately.

[2018-09-19T18:53:21Z | cdjackson | comment]
> So I actually see two parts that you need:
> 
There was also the original reason for adding the method - and that is to update the inbox properties so we don’t have things in the inbox seemingly disappearing. I can probably do something in the binding to reduce this issue, but it can’t be completely resolved without some knowledge of the inbox.

> 
> Could a simple method be added to the handler that would answer whether a Z-Wave Thing of a given UID already exists or not? It seems to me as if there is no need to route this through the framework at all.

Thanks Kai. So you mean add a “getChildThings” method (or whatever name) that provides a list of all things currently known by the bridge? This might solve the majority of the issues.  I will take a look at the ZigBee and ZWave bindings to see if this resolves this issue.

I’m away on holiday at the moment so probably won’t get to look at this until next week anyway.

Thanks.

[2018-09-27T07:28:00Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> so we don’t have things in the inbox seemingly disappearing

This should be covered by using a cache in the discovery service. And having things disappear and rediscovered after a reboot should be acceptable.

> So you mean add a “getChildThings” method (or whatever name) that provides a list of all things currently known by the bridge? 

Yes, exactly.

FTR: I'd like to merge #6237 soon, but I think its impact is ok for the snapshot builds and I just did an OH milestone. We would therefore have about a month time until the next milestone to do the adaptions in the concerned bindings, hope that's ok.

[2018-12-21T11:41:40Z | wborn | comment]
Do I correctly see that with the deprecation of the `ExtendedDiscoveryService`, its methods now always return `null`? So any `DiscoveryService` still using these deprecated methods may now have severe performance issues? 

It would sure explain why my Plugwise Zigbee mesh (40+ nodes) is very unstable nowadays because the discovery service is constantly requesting data from each and every (offline) node in the mesh. :disappointed: 

Looks like the `ZWaveDiscoveryService` also didn't got updated yet. So I think you may run into the same issues with large networks @cdjackson?

title: GroupFunction name EQUAL or EQUALITY?
body:
Found this in my log:
```
12:46:50.961 [INFO ] [smarthome.event.ItemStateChangedEvent] - Sun_Elevation changed from 32.911390868338536 to 32.82965662193761
12:46:51.096 [INFO ] [smarthome.event.ItemStateChangedEvent] - Moon_Azimuth changed from 54.55240850571265 to 54.80388014618922
12:46:51.099 [INFO ] [smarthome.event.ItemStateChangedEvent] - Moon_Elevation changed from -36.231753744300484 to -36.1101579166758
12:46:52.752 [ERROR] [re.internal.items.GroupFunctionHelper] - Unknown group function 'EQUALITY'. Using Equality instead.
12:46:54.390 [ERROR] [re.internal.items.GroupFunctionHelper] - Unknown group function 'EQUALITY'. Using Equality instead.
12:46:56.025 [ERROR] [re.internal.items.GroupFunctionHelper] - Unknown group function 'EQUALITY'. Using Equality instead.
```

Unfortunately, there is no stacktrace provided, so I cannot see where this might come from.

In `GroupFunctionHelper` I can see that only the name `EQUAL` is expected there, while [our documentation](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/docs/documentation/concepts/items.md#derive-group-state-from-member-items) talks about `EQUALITY`. Something does not seem to be consistent here...
comments:
[2018-09-24T11:29:05Z | maggu2810 | comment]
Hm, I don't know which one should be preferred `EQUAL` or `EQUALITY`.
But it must be consistent.

Any objections?

[2018-09-26T08:47:30Z | htreu | comment]
My suggestion is to just update the docs to EQUAL as the code and all "working" installations are using it. Installations using EQUALITY will see the warning nonetheless.

[2018-09-26T08:52:04Z | htreu | comment]
Also the xtext definition says `EQUAL`.

[2018-09-26T09:13:27Z | htreu | comment]
Unfortunately we accept `EQUAL` as a valid group function string, but when GroupItem is serialized with the default group function `Equality` we are not able to deserialize it back w/o the warning.
I added a commit to the proposed fix which accepts both `EQUAL` and `EQUALITY` in the GroupFunctionHelper.

title: PaperUI: Context "thing" with limitToOptions=true does not work
body:
If a ConfigDescription has a parameter that has the `context` "thing", PaperUI renders a nice drop down of all available things.

However it should be possible to offer options and limit the list of things to these given options.

At the moment, PaperUI simply ignores the given options and the `limitToOptions=true` setting and lists all available things.
comments:
[2018-09-25T14:39:42Z | htreu | comment]
It seems that pre-given options with contexts `item` or `thing` will be ignored. You can however supply a list of `FilterCriteria` to the `ConfigDescriptionParameter`. This list will be matched against the list of things in Paper UI.

[2018-09-25T14:45:14Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I'd agree with @triller-telekom that this should be considered a bug. If there is a provided option list, this should be taken into account.

[2018-09-25T15:00:40Z | htreu | comment]
I would consider this a new feature...
Why not using the existing functionality and provide a list of FilterCriteria? Its specifically designed for this case and with no extra effort.

[2018-09-25T15:09:37Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
FilterCriteria filters for certain types. Why should that be helpful here?
And why is it a missing feature and not a bug, if limitToOptions=true does not limit the values to the provided options?

[2018-09-26T05:52:54Z | htreu | comment]
> And why is it a missing feature

because the use of `context` as of now was not meant be be used with existing options. At least in the  code there is no sign of this behaviour.

> FilterCriteria filters for certain types

And if I'm not mistaken it filters for explicit values, like `UID=myThingId`. And given you provide a list of thingIds it should just work fine.

I will provide a PR which tests this behaviour for Paper UI.

Thanks @resetnow for spending your thoughts on that - I meant to implement it already all the time, but also noticed that it isn't as straight forward as initially thought and hence I never found the time yet to do it properly.

Your approach is in-line with my initial thoughts, yes. The problem that I am seeing here is that this would result in a terrible huge number of widget events (both on the OSGi event bus + through SSE). I therefore think that we need some logic to only create&send those events, if they are really needed.
My thoughts were that the UI should subscribe to a sitemap and only then such events are created&sent (until an unsubscribe or timeout). This is not necessarily nice, but I think necessary. My assumptions are:
- When navigating to a new page, you always do a request like /basicui/app?w=FF_Bath&sitemap=demo.
- It is enough to receive updates for widgets of the page that is currently shown.
- You only need the SSE connection for receiving updates of page/widget infos.

If this is correct, my suggestion would be to:
- Create a new url where you can subscribe for sitemap events through SSE. The first information that this SSE connection will give you is a subscriptionId. This is valid as long as the SSE connection is established - it is more or less a session id.
- You pass this subscriptionId as an additional parameter to the HTTP requests when you change a page.
- This will have the effect that the SSE events that are sent are now only events for the page that you have requested last.

I should be able to implement the server side for such a behavior. If this meets your requirements, that would be perfect. I hope I do not miss anything relevant...

title: [mqtt-things] Homie device doesn't update its read-only channel
body:
Hi @davidgraeff!

Sorry for bothering you again, but I think that I have found a bug in the mqtt-things binding. As you know, I'm using this script to test my "virtual" Homie 3.0 devices:

```python
import random
import time
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

mqtt_broker_host = "localhost"
mqtt_broker_port = 1883
mqtt_client_id = "homie_3.0_temperature_sensor"
mqtt_client_keepalive = 60

homie_prefix = "homie"
homie_version = "3.0.0"
homie_device_id = "homie-3-temperature-sensor"
homie_device_name = "Homie 3.0 Temperature sensor"
homie_device_ip = "192.168.1.150"
homie_device_mac = "DE:AD:BE:EF:FE:ED"
homie_device_nodes = ["temperature"]
homie_device_state = None

def publish_homie_version(client):
    topic = "{}/{}/{}".format(homie_prefix, homie_device_id, "$homie")
    client.publish(topic, homie_version, 1, True)

def advertize_device():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "init", 1, True)
    publish_device_info()
    publish_node_info()
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "ready", 1, True)

def publish_device_info():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$homie", homie_version, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$name", homie_device_name, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$localip", homie_device_ip, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$mac", homie_device_mac, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$fw/name", "sensor-firmware", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$fw/version", "1.0.0", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$nodes", "temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$implementation", "homie-python", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$stats/interval", "60", 1, True)

def publish_node_info():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$name", "Indoor temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$type", "Temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$properties", "temperature", 1, True)

    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature", 23, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$name", "Indoor temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$settable", "false", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$unit", "ºC", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$datatype", "float", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$format", "-20:120", 1, True)

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, rc):
    print("Connected with result code {}".format(rc))
    advertize_device()


def on_message(client, userdata, msg):
    print("{} -> {}".format(msg.topic, msg.payload))


def loop():
    last_temperature_time = 0
    while True:
        if (time.time() - last_temperature_time) > 5:
            temperature_value = random.uniform(20,25)
            print("Sending tempertaure value: {0:.2f}ºC".format(temperature_value))
            client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature", "{0:.2f}".format(temperature_value), 1, True)
            last_temperature_time = time.time()
        time.sleep(1)


client = mqtt.Client(mqtt_client_id)
client.on_connect = on_connect
client.on_message = on_message

client.will_set("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "lost", 1, True)

client.connect(mqtt_broker_host, mqtt_broker_port, mqtt_client_keepalive)

client.loop_start()

try:
    loop()
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("Stopping client")
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "disconnected", 1, True)
    client.disconnect()
    client.loop_stop()
```
The device is discovery perfectly and the thing is imported flawlessly, with its "Indoor temperature" channel. The problem is that, although the script is configured to send a new temperature value each 5 seconds (a random value between 20 and 25), the item is never updated and I can see the following message in the karaf console:

```
13:48:38.718 [WARN ] [ng.mqtt.generic.internal.ChannelState] - Received MQTT data on homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature. This channel is read only!
```
If the Homie property is read-only (not settable), the binding should not subscribe to the "/set" topic, but in this case the binding is blocking the "common" state topic. Are you aware of this problem? Otherwise, I haven't encountered any problem, awesome work!

Best regards and keep up with the good job,

Aitor

title: [MQTT] brokerId must be a configuration parameter of a broker
body:
In ESH, EVERY thing/bridge must have at least one configuration parameter. The instance must NOT be determined by the ThingUID.

The MQTT Broker type is incorrectly modelled. `AbstractBrokerHandler` does a
```
this.brokerID = thing.getUID().getId();
```
Instead, this id must be taken from the Thing configuration (and thus must be declared in the config descriptions).

I just checked:

3. The `SystemBrokerHandler` class is not using configurations.

title: BaseThingHandler.editThing() does not preserver State
body:
When calling this method somewhere in the Handler, then a new Thing is created, and assigned to handler.thing, but in the process the State of the original Thing is not preserved or copied over (but is set to the default UNINITIALIZED). Moreover, the Thing assigned to handler.thing is not the same object instance as the one that is tracked by the ThingManager. That means that for example in the osgi console, the Thing can be "ONLINE", but the Thing referenced by the handler will be UNINITIALIZED
(See also https://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/t/1072808/)

body:
Using PaperUI (openHAB2 beta 1), I installed the NTP binding. A ntp:ntp:local thing was created. Then I edited its parameters to switch from default server 0.pool.ntp.org to 0.fr.pool.ntp.org. If I open again the parameters, the value is 0.fr.pool.ntp.org as expected.
Now if I stop OH2 (logout command in the console) and start again OH2, when I edit my NTP thing parameters, my hostname is now 0.pool.ntp.org rather than 0.fr.pool.ntp.org
comments:
[2016-01-19T16:12:21Z | marcelrv | comment]
@lolodomo thanks for your finding.
This seems some sort of issue in the persistence of config parameters.
I'm not sure if this is directly related to the binding itself.

I'll try to replicate this here on my instance.

[2016-01-19T16:37:25Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I can reproduce it and @marcelrv is right - this has nothing to do with the binding, but seems to be a bug in the core framework. I will analyze it further...

[2016-01-19T17:09:37Z | marcelrv | comment]
I can replicate this issue, in fact it it applies to any config parameter, not only hostname.
**I can confirm this not only applies to NTP binding but applies to other bindings as well**, e.g. I have replicated this issue in the yahoo binding. 
NB, it is not always, so I guess there is some timing issue
- during the session parameters are correctlyu updated, binding is using updated values.
- after shutdown and restart the values are lost. binding fall back to the default values from xml in ESH-INF

[2016-01-20T12:13:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I found the problem, it is after all in the NTP binding:
If an existing thing is re-discovered, updated configuration from the discovery result is automatically sync'ed to the thing. As the NTP discovery set the default values, this overwrote any changes upon a rediscovery (which was automatically triggered at system startup).
I have removed this now in the NtpDiscovery in #894

[2016-01-20T17:40:33Z | marcelrv | comment]
@kaikreuzer maybe we need to move it to the forum, but I would think that is conceptional not the right approach. This way somehow the discovery should be made aware of all the changes.
I would assume that discovery does what it says: discovery. From that point onwards it is up to the user to update the configuration in either the binding or via the UI. It would be very hairy if we mix these.

e.g. take here the locale, there is no default set in the esh xml file, nor should there hence with the change made it will be left blank, 
I intentionally made it in the way it is as to have the clear example of how this field should be populated (formatted).

I think there will be many other examples as well where values set during discovery will be updated by the user later onwards. (same thing for e.g. the yahoo binding, I updated the location ID, to the one better reflecting my location, but it got changed back by discovery...not what I want)

It has to be done only when the rule is created > Should it also automatically discard invalid connections? No because the user decision always has priority. > Do we have to differentiate between connections that were auto-added and ones that were declared by the user/UI? Yes because the user decision always has priority. [2016-02-24T15:50:25Z | danchom | comment] On the other hand, applying of the auto mapping will not be a problem, if we have a parameter or configuration property or entire new add method. The user will specify if he expect auto mapping or not. [2016-02-24T16:20:06Z | kaikreuzer | comment] > It has to be done only when the rule is created I don't agree - there is no difference between an "initially created rule" and a "completely edited rule that only has the id in common with the previous version" - so for me, it should be applied on any update as well. > No because the user decision always has priority. Which means that the REST request would result in an error, because we would not accept invalid mappings, right? This can be awkward, because the user might not have created the connection himself (it was the auto-mapping upon creation), but only edited a detail that made the connection become invalid. So we shift the responsibility to the UI to make sure that invalid connections are automatically removed before submission. > Yes because the user decision always has priority. Well, the user automatically has priority, as no auto-mapping will take place if he already created connections himself. The question is rather if there is a use case where the user wants to specify that a certain (obvious and thus auto-mapped) connection MUST NOT be created. I don't really see a convincing use case for that. [2016-02-24T17:17:28Z | adimova | comment] I see the things like this: If the user has left some inputs not connected to outputs, then the auto-mapping should be applied on them, if it is possible, no matter if the rule is newly created or updated. A validation has to be performed in both cases and the rule should be left NOT_INITIALIZED if it fails. Then it will be the user's responsibility to make the rule "valid". I do not see a reason to differentiate between connections that were auto-added and ones that were declared by the user/UI. [2016-02-24T18:57:30Z | maggu2810 | comment] Hm, what about my commets above? The REST API could provide a function to do that auto-mapping that receive all informations (the mapping with not be done in the REST implementation, but forwared to). It could return an error if no auto-mapping could be done. If no auto-mapping is necessary or it could be done correctly a valid JSON structure could be returned. The very simple UI could then on save / update call the auto-mapping function (if it needs to be done or not). If that auto-mapping succeeded (again regardless if something has been changed or not) the JSON rule could be saved using the current REST API. If that auto-mapping failed an error page / dialog could be shown. [2016-02-25T07:41:58Z | danchom | comment] My point of view is the auto mapping should be some kind of initial initialization of the rule, in case when the user can't, don't know or is lazy to do it itself. If the auto mapping overwrite user decisions we can have following problems: 1) the user will never remove connection which is done by auto-mapping 2) the user can receive unexpected results base on created rule. I think it is not unusual to have a module type with defined inputs which are not connected anywhere. For example we can have a module type of add action with defined 8 inputs (because we want this action to be universal and adds up to 8 (for example) digits). Usually only part of these inputs will be used, the other should be empty. If the auto mapping decides to links these not connected inputs to available outpus, the result of add operation will be unexpected. And the worst is that the user can't fix the unwanted links because they will be applied again after the update. @maggu2810 we are discussing the case when we have only one add(rule) method in the ruleengine and it should do auto mapping by default. [2016-02-25T09:14:59Z | adimova | comment] > the auto-mapping should be applied on them, if it is possible I mean that if the inputs are defined as required, has no default value and user has left them unconnected, then the auto-mapping should be applied on them [2016-02-25T12:07:38Z | kaikreuzer | comment] > The REST API could provide a function to do that auto-mapping that receive all informations This means that the UI has always to do at least two calls and that it must not forget the first one. This is imho an option, if we say that auto-mapping is an optional feature that a UI is free to decide to use it or not. If it is mandatory, I would actually not expose it through REST. > we can have a module type of add action with defined 8 inputs (because we want this action to be universal and adds up to 8 (for example) digits) The proper design would probably to have a single input with multiple=true. In general, when talking about "the user" here, we should have in mind to bother him as little as possible with any of this. Ideally, the current Rule UI should be sufficient for him, so the goal is rather to provide module types with clean interfaces, which allow auto-mapping of modules. Manual mapping is rather a feature for developers, who create complex templates that might be using more generic and versatile module types internally. [2016-02-25T12:34:35Z | danchom | comment] > Manual mapping is rather a feature for developers, who create complex templates that might be using more generic and versatile module types internally. I'm concerning this won't be possible, because the auto mapping will overwrite complex logic of template. [2016-02-25T12:36:57Z | kaikreuzer | comment] Who ever claimed that auto-mapping should overwrite anything? [2016-02-25T12:40:11Z | danchom | comment] In case when auto mapping is applied on every update it can overwrite such rules. Also the template rule is converted into regular rule and auto mapping can add additional connections. [2016-02-25T12:48:12Z | kaikreuzer | comment] As stated in https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/886#issuecomment-188330967: "the user automatically has priority, as no auto-mapping will take place if he already created connections himself" [2016-02-25T13:15:44Z | danchom | comment] Sorry may be my misunderstanding. Let summarize if I understand right? 1) Auto-mapping always will be applied on add (update) methods when a rule does not have any connections. When a connection was set, the auto mapping must be skipped. 2) Auto mapping will do connection only when the input tags are subset of the output tags. 3) when connections can't be done by auto-mapping the rule engine will return rule without connections silently 4) in case of conflict, an input can be connected to more then one output, the auto mapping must skip this input and leave it unconnected. [2016-02-25T13:39:21Z | kaikreuzer | comment] 1) ~~rule does not have any connections~~ -> input does not have a connection. 3) What do you mean by "return"? Yes, upon creation or update, the rule will simply be exactly the one that was passed as a parameter. So there is no "silence" here, it is just the normal behavior. [2016-02-25T14:17:11Z | danchom | comment] > 1) rule does not have any connections -> input does not have a connection. rule does not have any connections I mean there are not any connections between inputs and outputs of modules of the rule. If there is at least one connection IMHO the auto mapping should be skipped because the 'user' was set his decision. Otherwise if we try to reconnect empty inputs on each update we go back to the overwrite complex rule logic scenario (for example set by template) . This means the behavior of the rule won't be determinated [2016-02-25T15:05:26Z | kaikreuzer | comment] No, this doesn't make sense, see my first comment in https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/886#issuecomment-188330967. You might be simply adding another module to the end of a rule and while the existing ones are already connected, the newly added one definitely needs to be auto-mapped then. [2016-02-25T16:06:28Z | danchom | comment] Ok 1) Auto-mapping always will be applied on add (update) methods when a input does not have a connection. When a connection was set, the auto mapping must be skipped. If someone want to leave an input unconnected a new tag can be put to the input and the auto mapping will not connect it. [2016-03-10T06:14:33Z | danchom | comment] Implemented by #1125

title: [yahooweather] YahooWeatherDiscoveryService.getWoeidData() URL discontinued
body:
One can no longer query Yahoo! YQL with a lat,long to return a WOEID.  

References:
- [Yahoo! Developer forum post](https://developer.yahoo.com/forums/#/discussion/7838/tahoo-geo-placefinder-does-not-work%3D%3D%3D)
- [openHAB forum post regarding 1.x weather binding](https://community.openhab.org/t/yahoo-weather-service-issue-weather-binding-1-7-1/6528)
- https://github.com/openhab/openhab/pull/3888
comments:
[2016-01-28T10:41:45Z | watou | comment]
Possible changes to address the discontinued Yahoo! geo.placefinder service:
1. Write a trivial service that runs at a well known address and uses the [Flickr API to retrieve woeid from lat,long](https://www.flickr.com/services/api/flickr.places.findByLatLon.html), and caches the results to minimize queries.  This may conflict with Flickr terms of service, so that would need to be verified first.
2. Remove discovery from yahooweather binding.
3. Write a new binding using an alternative weather provider that does not require API keys and provides weather by public IP or lat,long (such as [met.no](http://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/1.9/documentation), whose data and API are excellent, from my experience).

I could implement 3 above if anyone is interested.

[2016-01-28T11:47:51Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The main purpose for the YahooWeather binding was so far to serve as an example for [the tutorial](https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/development/bindings/how-to.html). Luckily, this tutorial never covered the discovery part of the binding :-)
So in order to keep at least parts of the binding that are relevant for the tutorial, I would opt for option 2 above.
For option 3, I think we will sooner or later see the [openHAB Weather binding](https://github.com/openhab/openhab/wiki/Weather-Binding) being ported to the new APIs. But there is imho no rush to do this right now.

Could you prepare a PR for option 2?

[2016-01-28T11:54:46Z | watou | comment]
> Could you prepare a PR for option 2?

Yes; I will add it to my queue.  Feel free to assign this issue to me.

[2016-01-28T12:00:17Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I would like to but I cannot, since only official committers are in the team list on Github and I do not have the rights to change that...

[2016-01-28T12:08:53Z | watou | comment]
No worries.

title: Introduce a mechanism to easily register action method signatures
body:
The Designer of openHAB 1 had most bundles containing actions included and thus way able to resolve these actions in the rule&script editors (for auto-completion, syntax checks etc.).

It also included the possibility to add further bundles in an `addons` folder by the user, although this mechanism never worked well.

The ESH Designer only contains a few "core ESH" actions. As it is not feasible to automatically bundle action-addons with it, there should be a way to easily add such method signatures (the code itself is not required for the editors).
comments:
[2016-02-22T21:59:29Z | SuperOok | comment]
What exactly is the problem that you cannot provide actions later by some bundle? Is it that the Xtext grammar needs to know everything in advance? Isn't this the use case of Xbase integration in the grammar? Or is it an issue with class loading? Maybe fragments or buddy policy help?
Maybe I do not get the problem right.

[2016-02-23T07:33:47Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The code that provides the action definitions for the scripts/rules can be found [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.script/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/script/scoping/ScriptImplicitlyImportedTypes.java#L89).
As I said, in theory, putting the action bundles in the `addons` folder should make them being resolved and their services being available.
Feel free to figure out, why this isn't working as expected. A difficult thing to get right is probably that you need all dependencies of the action bundles being available as well - and as the Designer does not have all the bundles of the runtime, this can be hard. That's why I think we would need a new/better mechanism than relying on registered OSGi services here.

[2016-02-25T19:42:07Z | SuperOok | comment]
Hmm... the Designer is an Eclipse RCP Application, so why don't we use Eclipse mechanisms? The Bundles could be explicit Eclipse Plugins and register themselves either via Eclipse extension point or OSGi Service.
For the dependencies a p2 Update Site could be provided such that you can install the addons with the standard Eclipse installation mechanism:
http://www.vogella.com/tutorials/EclipseP2Update/article.html#tutorial_p2ui

Eclipse would then resolve all the necessary dependencies if they are provided by any known update site.

[2016-02-26T09:49:56Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
>  The Bundles could be explicit Eclipse Plugins

Well, they are explizit OSGi bundles and thus can be installed on RCP, yes. 
Using a p2 site merely means that you have the additional overhead of creating p2 feature, a repo and an update site (which you then have to manually add to your Designer first. Also note that the Designer would need all the update site management integrated, so you rather end up with a full Eclipse IDE than just a small RCP application.
And doing all this would not bring you any closer to the solution: You would still have the problem that the action bundles have many dependencies on the runtime, bindings, etc. and you simply won't be able to resolve them all cleanly.

[2017-01-23T10:55:04Z | sjsf | comment]
> You would still have the problem that the action bundles have many dependencies on the runtime, bindings, etc. and you simply won't be able to resolve them all cleanly.

This definitely is a pain. The root-cause for all this is the fact that we actually are running more or less a complete runtime framework inside the designer. To my understanding we are doing this mainly to allow the scripts and rules (i.e. Xbase) to use the classpath for looking up what kind of commands should be there. IMHO this completely sucks.

For sure, Xbase _by default_ uses the classpath to resolve its stuff. However, this does not have to stay like that. We could have our own type provider implementation which feeds Xbase with whatever we think should be available (or not...). We don't need access to the _real_ java classes for this, as long as we know how they _look_ like.

Now, assuming we could do the above magic, don't have a full ESH framework running underneath and simply operate on the DSLs: Where do you _then_ know what actions should be available?

One way of solving this would be to introduce a direct connection to the _real_ runtime. I.e. extend it with a REST API to read the available actions (together with all their methods and arguments).

This would "break" the concept that the designer is a real standalone one, because without the connection to the runtime it cannot tell which extensions are there. But let's face it: It is broken today too.

WDYT?

[2017-01-23T11:10:33Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Yes, having a REST connection was also the intention of https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/619 and being able to directly read the available actions would be nice.

I only fear that this will mean quite some implementation work, which might not be long-lasting. My hope would be to offer a "designer runtime extension" in the future (see https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/1402), which would then naturally have access to all details of the runtime (as this is where it is running itself then).

So as a mid-term solution, I think we could do e.g. with an "action.xml" file that the Designer could reference (or e.g. expect to find it in the configuration folder), which could contain information about the solution specific actions (for openHAB, we could maintain such a file that simply has all actions available).

Also note, that with the new rule engine, the "old" actions will be obsolete some day and we might rather allow Xbase to access module types (and we wrap old actions into a module type for backward compatibility).

[2017-08-29T15:50:55Z | htreu | comment]
The designer is not actively maintained anymore, please see https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/4139#issuecomment-325333205.

@sjka please close.

In all other places (other handlers) there is not a colon (Please see handlers map of BaseModuleHandlerFactory. I don't know why, may be to have less string concatenations). In all these places  ruleId + moduleId is unique  identifier of the handler. 
The RuleEngine has a mapping between module type and list of rules where the module type is  used. (In that way it changes rule state not_initialized <-> initialized) 
A rule which have composite module type depends on its all child module types. There for the composite module type has to update Rule Engine's module type to rule mapping. 
The colon is used to separate rule id from the rest of prefix, because if you have a nested composite module types (i.e. ItemStateChangeTrigger) the method is called in recursion and rule id will be loosed. For that reason the composite module type uses colon in definition of unique id of handler.

title: DiscoveryResults not updated on DiscoveryService change
body:
When particular DiscoveryService is changed (eg. there are new properties added to the discovery results) the already discovered things are not been updated.

This is due to the cache used in DiscoveryServiceRegistryImpl:

`private HashMultimap<DiscoveryService, DiscoveryResult> cachedResults = HashMultimap.create();`

Javadoc of `HashMultimap` says: 
`Adding a new key-value pair equal to an existing key-value pair has no effect.`

Possible solution is - each time an entry is put to the map - already existing entry to be first removed from the map
comments:

I'm missing at least a test case in `DiscoveryServiceRegistryOSGITest` for this as part of your PR...

[2017-01-04T10:15:56Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Adding a new key-value pair equal to an existing key-value pair has no effect.

Can you explain why the new key-value pair is equal to the old one in that case?

[2017-01-04T10:46:30Z | ivivanov-bg | comment]
@kaikreuzer - the new value is the same as the old one because the `equals` method of the `DiscoveryResultImpl` only checks the `thingUID` - and in my current scenario - the `thingUID` is the same but there is change in the properties map of the discovery result.

However - changing the `equals` method is not desired because we will end up having two discovery results for the same `thingUID` with different properties 

@sjka - you are correct - this only happens for `DiscoveryListener`s which are added after the 'DiscoveryResult' is been created. And the test is on it's way.

Thanks a lot for adding the test-case. I left a few comments where I think you can make it more readable. 

What Kind if IDE are you using? I think there is something wrong with your formatter - at least I get whitespace changes in the lines you wrote when I save that file again.

However, there is something that I'm wondering about your test-case: Have you ever tried running it without the change you did in `DiscoveryServiceRegistryImpl`? 😉

[2017-01-04T18:29:55Z | ivivanov-bg | comment]
@sjka I think I addressed your comments.

About the IDE - I use Eclipse - the formatting looks fine on my end but just in case  - I applied the ESH formatter once again.

About the other question - Yes - I tried the tests without the change to `DiscoveryServiceRegistryImpl` and I noticed very strange behavior of groovy as the tests were passing even without the fix.

Basically - when I print the content of the `cachedResults` map in the `DiscoveryServiceRegistryImpl` - it behaves as expected - the same element is NOT added to the map on the second call.

However - if I print the content of the very same map inside the groovy test - the content of the map is replaced on the second discovery.

This is IMHO totally strange and questions the correctness of all groovy tests. Can you please explain me why is this happening and is this expected behavior?

Regards,
Ivo

[2017-01-06T08:54:09Z | sjsf | comment]
> This is IMHO totally strange and questions the correctness of all groovy tests. Can you please explain me why is this happening and is this expected behavior?

No, the "problem" is not groovy - what you are seeing here in your test-case is a feature from the PersistentInbox: It [synchronizes](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/master/bundles/config/org.eclipse.smarthome.config.discovery/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/config/discovery/internal/PersistentInbox.java#L186) newly discovered information with previous results.

The `PersistentInbox` is also a discovery listener. So it depends on the order: if yours is called after the inbox all *seems* to be good. 

The fact that the inbox manipulates the original object can be considered as yet another bug which needs to be fixed.

title: Synchronous Execution of Astro Startup Jobs and minor fixes
body:
The scheduling operations schedules few jobs and executes 2 specific jobs immediately. These two jobs are executed in a different thread to prevent blocking the thread that spawns it. 

In addition, during handler initialize, channel linking and unlinking, we reschedule the jobs. And every time, before we reschedule the jobs, we remove the jobs from the ESH Core scheduler that are associated with the current thing.

As the jobs that execute immediately are handled by different threads, it is sometime noticed that while rescheduling, removal of jobs did occur after the jobs got rescheduled. This created unexpected issues in ESH Core scheduler. In this PR, we have rendered the asynchronous operations of executing immediate jobs in different threads to synchronous execution so that we can make sure the removal always happens before rescheduling.

Another note is that previously we required `equals` and `hashcode` to be overriden by `AbstractJob` but currently it is not used anymore. These `equals` and `hashcode` affected normal executions of scheduled jobs as well. Hence, the methods have been removed.

title: Added Composite Jobs for range events if scheduled at same instant
body:
The scheduler works on the unit of seconds. For range events, it can also schedule two events to be executed at the same instant. Due to parallel execution, there are inconsistency about the executions of the range events that are scheduled for same instants.

Therefore one second to the end event has been added to assure the synchronous execution of the range start and end events.

title: [LIFX] Update ThingStatus at most once a second
body:
With this PR the `LifxLightHandler` will only update the ThingStatus when there is a change.

Each received message currently always results in a `ThingStatus.ONLINE` update. This causes a lot of unnecessary `ThingStatusInfoEvent` s, logging etc. which generate unnecessary CPU load.
comments:
[2017-07-08T06:13:47Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
It isn't recommended for bindings to do this check. The framework already checks whether there is a change or not and actually issues different events (updated vs changed). The logging can be configured to only log change events (that's the default in openHAB), so additional updates should do no harm.
By filtering it, you now suppress the information on when the light has been seen online last (we do not show this anywhere yet, but I would like to have such a feature in future).

So I vote against this PR, sorry 😎

[2017-07-08T07:13:20Z | wborn | comment]
When my 38 lights just remain online the light state is continuously polled. Each received message results in an online update. This PR saves with my 38 lights about ~1535 updates per minute.

When you start sending commands to your lights for some animation this number will rapidly increase because more messages are received.

The online/offline status works very well for LIFX lights. So if you want to know when the light was last online you can still use the transition from online to offline for this.

[2017-07-08T07:21:03Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> ~1535 updates per minute.

Ok, that's a lot indeed :-)

>  you can still use the transition from online to offline for this

Not, if it hasn't gone offline at all. But ok, if you say that an ONLINE status cannot be older than a second in any case (as otherwise it would have gone OFFLINE already), my argument probably does not matter to much here.
Nonetheless: With your change, we would see a "last ONLINE message" which has a date from when it went online instead of "now-1s". So could you find a way to at least regularly do a setStatus, even if it hasn't changed? Doing it once a second would still reduce the number of messages from 1535 to only 38 :-)

title: fix resource leak
body: Fixes: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/3919
comments:
[2017-08-01T04:32:53Z | htreu | review:COMMENTED]
Is there a reason not to use `org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.toString(InputStream)`? I have the feeling we are not consistent in using external utils vs. implementing this stuff on our own.

[2017-08-01T05:37:04Z | maggu2810 | comment]
Hm, I don't see any reason to use an third party (`IOUtils`) function for something that could be solved our self without adding lot's of code. As we could use `try-with-resources` that solves the resource leak with standard language features, I prefer using Java features only.

[2017-08-01T07:42:31Z | htreu | comment]
To be clear on my first post: I was not talking about your refactoring, which makes perfect sense here. My suggestion is to drop the private method `convertStreamToString ` entirely and replace it by the IOUtils call.

We touched this topic quite a few times now. And I guess its matter of taste somehow: How far do you want to take protection from the 'not invented here'  syndrome vs. implementing small features and not depend on too many external libraries.
From my pov I would rather depend on wide spread external libraries then doing stuff on my own. And when it comes to dependencies which are already there its even more of an argument for me.

[2017-08-01T08:05:26Z | maggu2810 | comment]
@htreu To be clear, too: It is okay for me to use wide spread external libraries that are present in the most runtimes at all (so IMHO the most common ones).

I am not familiar with the Hue code, but IMHO introducing a separate function or using `IOUtils` directly depends how often the method `convertStreamToString` is used and how the implementation using `IOUtils` looks like.
I assume `IOUtils.toString(is)` does not do the job. We need to split on "\\A" and take the first entry. Correct?
Isn't a separate function with a represent name better if we need to use such a split and selection multiple times?

As you know the code base better, can you give me an example how the change would look like?

[2017-08-01T08:37:17Z | htreu | comment]
I guess the main thing here is the line `scanner.useDelimiter("\\A").next()` which was technically not clear to me either but I must admit I did take the exact same line from stackoverflow in the past to convert InputStreams to Strings. I did a little research and found this article: https://community.oracle.com/blogs/pat/2004/10/23/stupid-scanner-tricks

The line effectively takes the whole content of the InputStream and reads it into the String. The \A refers to the beginning of the Stream. So the Scanner will tokenize the whole Stream until it reaches the next beginning (which is not present here) resulting in the whole string being taken as the first token.

With this in mind I guess its fine to replace the method. Its only called once in the HttpClient in the hue binding.

On another note: We should replace the internal HttpClient from the hue binding by the jetty client (or even better by the `org.eclipse.smarthome.io.net.http.HttpUtil`) but thats another PR with some more analysis :-)

[2017-08-01T11:06:47Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
The PR as it is is imho fine, so I merge it.

Nonetheless, I agree with @htreu that it makes sense to refactor the code and remove this method as its implementation is not easily understandable and we allow extensions the use of Commons IO, which offers a stable feature for getting a String out of an InputStream.

[2017-08-01T11:59:30Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> I agree with @htreu that it makes sense to refactor the code and remove this method

It's fine for me, too.
Perhaps @htreu would like a PR that address it. :wink:

[2017-08-01T15:04:31Z | htreu | comment]
here you go :-)

title: Astro: Schedule Jobs 30sec after midnight to ensure to be on the next…
body:
… day

Fixes #4018

Signed-off-by: Stefan Triller <stefan.triller@telekom.de>
comments:
[2017-08-28T09:12:38Z | maggu2810 | comment]
Can you please give me some more details why 0h 0m 30s? is on the next day and 0h 0m 0s isn't?

[2017-08-28T09:23:34Z | triller-telekom | comment]
The problem is that our scheduler calculates the milliseconds until the next execution and in the cases of the bug that I am fixing the scheduler and the system time are a few (milli)seconds off and thus the expression scheduled to be executed at 0h 0m 0s is executed before midnight which is the day before. And in case of the Astro binding we are only interested in the day and not not the actual time of the cron execution.

If a cron expression that is using "00:00:00" as execution trigger is executed on the old day, I would say this is an unexpected behavior.

Changing the trigger cron expression will mask the error but not really solve the bug.

Indeed you are right. But there a quite a few bug reports regarding the random skipping of Astro events [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/4018) and in the openHAB [forum](https://community.openhab.org/t/astro-binding-problem-events-do-not-trigger-multiple-triggers-solved/30320/12) so the idea was to have a quick fix for the next ESH stable and then fix the scheduler.
