title: [Core] Added support for quoted strings in rule triggers
body:
According to #2826, the following works

```xtext
rule "Test Rule 1"
when
    Item test changed to world
then
    // This is IS working
end
```

while the following is NOT working:

```xtext
rule "Test Rule 2"
when
    Item test changed to "world"
then
    // This is NOT working
end
```

With this PR, I so far have only added a test-case for this. And indeed it fails and results as expected in 

```
testChangedEventTrigger_withoutQuotes(org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest)  Time elapsed: 0.639 sec
testChangedEventTrigger_withQuotes(org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest)  Time elapsed: 0.034 sec  <<< FAILURE!
org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[world]> but was:<["world"]>
	at org.junit.Assert.assertEquals(Assert.java:115)
	at org.junit.Assert.assertEquals(Assert.java:144)
	at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest.assertUpdateTriggerWithNewState(RuleTest.java:82)
	at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest.testChangedEventTrigger_withQuotes(RuleTest.java:66)
```

So the quotes somehow end up inside the string! 

It looks like this behavior gets better when defining the trigger in [Rules.xtext](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/09d8095efe9933216874e488b379cd9a10aa85e2/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/rule/Rules.xtext) instead as

```xtext
ChangedEventTrigger:
	'Item' item=ItemName 'changed' ('from' oldState=ValidState)? ('to' newState=ValidState)?
;		
ValidState:
	ID | Number | STRING
;
```

directly like this:

```xtext
ChangedEventTrigger:
	'Item' item=ItemName 'changed' ('from' oldState=(ID|Number|STRING)? ('to' newState=(ID|Number|STRING))?
;		
```

However, we then would lose the nice way of integrating the content proposal in [RulesProposalProvider.java](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/3ae5d7b1b284f2bde6199bfe8dad950fd38cae39/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.ui/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/rule/ui/contentassist/RulesProposalProvider.xtend). So there must be a better way to "trick" xtext into behaving well. Any suggestions? @chriskn or @cdietrich maybe?

relates to #2826
Signed-off-by: Simon Kaufmann <simon.kfm@googlemail.com>

I discussed this with @sjka and in the light of https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/4009 we came actually to the conclusion that the main issue is that the registries return entities that have setter methods, while they should only refer to an interface with getters instead.
Thinking back, we once created the `Rule` class with the intention to make it a POJO that is directly serialisable to JSON - we have learned over time that this isn't easily feasible and thus we ended up with an additional `RuleDTO` by now. Effectively, there isn't any good reason against a `Rule` interface anymore and in turn the `RuntimeRule` could become a `RuleImpl`, which would be the instances that the `RuleRegistry` and the `RuleManager` internally work with - this would be fully in sync with the Thing infrastructure.

I am just trying such a refactoring and in general it seems that a lot of complexity can be reduced, so I think it is a decent way to move forward.

title: [Core] Fixed daylight saving time (DST) bug in scheduled jobs
body:
While searching for possible future execution candidates there is a
problem if a change from standard time to daylight saving time occurs.

This time jump forward leads to a duplicate of a date. For example in
Europe, Germany SUN 2018 Mar 25 3:00:00 exists TWICE because the time was
shifted from 2am to 3am.

While pruning the execution candidates we only kept the next 2 whereas the
first usually is the current time, which leaves the 2nd candidate to be
the final one. If the time change occurs we only have 2 same dates which
both are the current time and thus both are discarded.

With this PR I have changed the implementation to keep 3 candidates, so
there will be a future execution date left.

Fixes #5294
Fixes #3185

[2018-05-02T17:12:21Z | sjsf | comment]
While doing some manual testing, I realized that there is another potential source for wrong widget ID calculations: The `SitemapSubscriptionService` and the `SitemapProvider` both registered themselves as `ModelRepositoryChangeListener`s at the `ModelRepository`. The former uses the latter to get a cached instance of the model. 
There is no guarantee though about the order in which they get their `modelChanged()` methods called. So in case the `SitemapSubscriptionService` got called first, it used the stale widget copy given by the `SitemapProvider`, which can't know anything about the new model at this time. 
I have added a second commit which fixes this aspect by letting the `SitemapSubscriptionService` subscribe at the `SitemapProvider` for changes instead of the `ModelRepository` directly, thereby making sure it only gets notified when its trusted provider also knows about the change.

title: Do not use invalid filenames on Windows for JSON storage
body:
Windows has a rather long list of forbidden characters in filenames, see

https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa365247(VS.85).aspx

Linux-like systems only disallow / and the null-byte.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filename#Reserved_characters_and_words

By URLencoding the string, all of these characters are safely transformed
into %<HexValue> and % is an allowed character. This encoding is even
reversible.

Given that we will not run on RT-11 systems we should be safe.

I use a maximum length of 127 to be safe even on android systems:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13204807/max-file-name-length-in-android

The down-side is that even spaces are now converted into %20, but I chose
to use URLencoder.encode instead of implementing the conversion by myself.

For existing storages I check whether a file exists and keep using it.

Fixes #5687

Signed-off-by: Stefan Triller <stefan.triller@telekom.de>

body:
This fixes and issue introduced by #6005, leading to the following CCE:

```
Exception in thread "pool-38-thread-1" java.lang.ClassCastException: org.eclipse.smarthome.io.transport.mdns.ServiceDescription cannot be cast to java.lang.Comparable
        at java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentSkipListMap.cpr(ConcurrentSkipListMap.java:655)
        at java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentSkipListMap.doPut(ConcurrentSkipListMap.java:835)
        at java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentSkipListMap.putIfAbsent(ConcurrentSkipListMap.java:1962)

        at org.eclipse.smarthome.io.transport.mdns.internal.MDNSClientImpl.registerService(MDNSClientImpl.java:175)

This was because `ConcurrentSkipListSet` expects `Comparable` content, but `ServiceDescription` isn't. I don't see why that would have been required, so I changed it to a more relaxed concurrent set implementation.

title: [Homematic] Leave the binrpc connection open for a configurable time
body: Signed-off-by: Gerhard Riegler <gerhard.riegler@gmail.com>
comments:
[2018-08-27T07:31:16Z | mdicke2s | review_comment]
As long as `closeSocket()` is called inside the finally block, it is not required to call it within the catch block. So as it is implemented here, it will be called twice in case of (EOF)Exception.

[2018-08-27T07:37:29Z | mdicke2s | review_comment]
I know that this line was untouched, but once we are at this code section I would like to take a closer look:

- Due to https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/development/guidelines.html#e-logging the log level `ERROR` should be used if there is something tremendously wrong and the system cannot recover normal operation by itself. @gerrieg Does this apply here?
- `EOFException` is not logged at all, whereas any other type of Exception is treated as an error. @gerrieg is that intended?

[2018-08-27T08:10:07Z | mdicke2s | review:CHANGES_REQUESTED]
Hi @gerrieg 

As I understood the code, the `SocketHandler` is responsible for opening&closing sockets. This happens on every call of `BinRpcClient#sendMessage(int, RpcRequest<byte[]>)`. It gets recreated every time when `config.getSocketMaxAlive()` seconds have passed. Moreover it gets closed immediately as soon as a `BinRpcMessage` was processed by `BinRpcResponseHandler`. 

Having this contribution merged, the `BinRpcResponseHandler` does not close the socket after receiving a callback, but stays listening. Is that related to one of the existing bugs?

`BinRpcResponseHandler` as well as `SocketHandler` will both close the socket after SocketMaxAlive is reached. Assuming that this doesn't necessarily happen at the same time, it is possible that `BinRpcResponseHandler` closes a socket that just has been opened by `SocketHandler` a moment ago. Therefore I wonder if it is malicious to have this close twice in the codebase. What do you think?

[2018-08-28T14:07:42Z | htreu | review_comment]
Indeed, ERROR logging is reserved for the framework. Please use WARNING in case the user is able to correct the situation and/or should be informed. Use DEBUG in all other cases.

[2018-08-29T07:00:40Z | gerrieg | comment]
> Having this contribution merged, the BinRpcResponseHandler does not close the socket after receiving a callback, but stays listening. Is that related to one of the existing bugs?

Yes, when java closes a socket, the underlying OS sets the socket to a WAIT state and removes it after some time. If there are many events in a short time, some users report that they are running out of sockets and the communication stops (e.g in Docker). It is also not necessary to always close the socket.

> BinRpcResponseHandler as well as SocketHandler will both close the socket after SocketMaxAlive is reached. Assuming that this doesn't necessarily happen at the same time, it is possible that BinRpcResponseHandler closes a socket that just has been opened by SocketHandler a moment ago

This can't happen. The SocketHandler is only for requests TO the gateway. It is not used for responses FROM the gateway.

And yes of course, i don't need the closeSocket calls if it is also in the finally block. I also changed the logging level.

[2018-08-29T07:32:58Z | mdicke2s | comment]
Thanks for addressing my feedback. I guess growing number sockets is a common source of failure in smarthome systems, so I appreciate to keep the socket open :+1: 

> This can't happen. The SocketHandler is only for requests TO the gateway. It is not used for responses FROM the gateway.

That is correct.... Sorry, I must have mixed two things there. Looking again at the code I see that those sockets are entirely independent:

- `SocketHandler` (which is used in `BinRpcClient#sendMessage(int, RpcRequest<byte[]>)` comes with socket on "gatewayAddress"-IP and "rfPort"
- `BinRpcResponseHandler` comes with socket on "callbackHost"-IP and "binCallbackPort".

Maybe I was mislead by the description of `socketMaxAlive`. According to `HomematicConfig.java` as well as `README.MD`:

> The maximum lifetime of a pooled socket connection **to** the Homematic gateway in seconds

Well, it seems actually like a minor issue, but to avoid confusion, I would suggest to either:

- have two separate `socketMaxAlive` parameters (in/out)
- adjust the description to make clear that it is used for both

[2018-08-29T08:03:00Z | gerrieg | comment]
I prefered to adjust the description. I think a second parameter is not necessary.

[2018-08-29T08:10:12Z | mdicke2s | comment]
thx @gerrieg 
IMHO it is ready to merge @htreu

[2018-08-29T08:43:22Z | htreu | comment]
Thanks for the info @mdicke2s, please approve the changes.
Unfortunately we have to wait a while, travis is taking a nap...

title: LoL actuator library failure
body:
PROBLEM

When running github:///upm/master/examples/lol-example.cxx the Olimex LoL lights up but in a rather uncontrolled way. Even doing something simple like:

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    sensor = new upm::LoL();
    sensor->setPixel(1, 1, 1);
    sensor->setPixel(1, 2, 1);
    sensor->setPixel(1, 3, 1);
    sensor->setPixel(1, 4, 1);
    usleep(100000000);
}

CONFIGURATION

So did you comment out that line from _hal_aci_tl.cpp_ then? By default MRAA sets up SPI as msb first with

body:
in  [configAN3944](https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/blob/master/src/mpr121/mpr121.cxx#L150) the CDT register is set to 0x04 which is an invalid value. Consequences are:
- lock-in of the sensor to "touched" state when touched for long periods of time ( > 10 seconds)
- lock-in sensor  to "touched" state when left alone for more than an hour
  
  The CDT part of register 0x5D (Highest 3 bits) should at least be set to 001 as indicated in the Application Note AN3889 , as you can see from the below screenshot of the application note:

![screen shot 2016-05-19 at 1 12 48 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3643758/15403179/bcae4340-1dc5-11e6-9662-0a5e1c138e76.png)

in the current [configAN3944](https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/blob/master/src/mpr121/mpr121.cxx#L150) the highest 3 bits of 0x5D are set to 000 which is invalid.

![screen shot 2016-05-19 at 1 12 55 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3643758/15403213/f103d54c-1dc5-11e6-9eb4-10b94cd2154a.png)

title: Undefined symbols in JS modules installed from npm with UPM 1.0.0-src
body:
Looks like there is a problem in some of the jsupm_* modules when using from JS for UPM version `1.0.0-src` when installed using npm.

When trying to call the jsupm_biss0001 module, even with just the normal example, I receive the following error:

```
ERROR: /usr/bin/node: symbol lookup error: /home/root/.node_app_slot/node_modules/jsupm_biss0001/build/Release/jsupm_biss0001.node: undefined symbol: _ZN3upm8BISS0001C1Ej
```

https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/issues/489 looks to be the same problem.
comments:
[2016-11-29T19:17:59Z | Propanu | comment]
Yes, they are the same problem, and it looks like this happens in cases where we have a C++ source wrapping a C implementation. Need to investigate further to figure out what's causing it.

[2016-12-06T06:08:44Z | benjaminmathews | comment]
Found the cause (and a solution) for the referenced issue : https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/issues/489
See this discussion: https://communities.intel.com/thread/108426
It wasn't a problem with the library (I think!). Code is working fine now, when we don't force Intel XDK to download and install the individual jsupm_* module.
Hope this info is of use.

[2016-12-09T03:01:46Z | Propanu | comment]
On the Edison you'll have the libraries that provide these undefined symbols on the system's path, or the XDK will install them for you. I'm fairly certain that's why it works for #489, but that really hides the true issue, which has to do with how node-gyp compiles the sources from NPM on your system.

[2016-12-15T18:45:21Z | Propanu | comment]
New version is up on NPM, 1.0.2-src. I've tracked the issue and found out it was caused by the makefile template node-gyp uses to build the sources. The target rules only use the base filename, thus if you have both a *module.c* and *module.cxx* in the same package, one of them will not be included in the build.

Since I doubt this can be fixed quickly by the node-gyp guys, I decided to rename our C sources while packing them in order to fix this. Everything seems to work as intended now.

title: problem in button_context - gpio_pin defined as uint8_t in button.h
body:
I am using Grove PI board connected to UP-Squared board. To test Grove button, I used button APIs from button.h available on UPM (v1.6.0).  The Grove button doesn't work.
I see that in 'button_context', gpio_pin is declared as '**_uint8_t_**', which results in a problem when an offset of 512 is added along with the digital pin number to initialize gpio in button_init().

ie. For a Grove button connected to digital pin 7, mraa_gpio_init() call is made with the value set to 7 instead of 519 due to overflow.

Shouldn't this be declared as **_'int_**'?

Having lwip debug enabled my log looks like this when i try to publish a 17kB buffer: ``` tcp_write(pcb=0x3ffdf778, data=0x3ffe436c, len=5744, apiflags=3) tcp_write: queueing 6536:7972 tcp_write: queueing 7972:9408 tcp_write: queueing 9408:10844 tcp_write: queueing 10844:12280 tcp_output_segment: 6536:7972 tcp_output_segment: 7972:9408 tcp_output_segment: 9408:10844 tcp_output_segment: 10844:12280 +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+- tcp_input: flags -+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+ tcp_process: Connection RESET E (4691) MQTT_CLIENT: Error write data or timeout, written len = -1 E (4691) MQTT_CLIENT: Read error or end of stream E (4701) MQTT_CLIENT: Error to public data to topic=/topic/qos0, qos=0 ``` For some reason, looking at Wireshark, the first TCP-package gets followed by a response from my computer with a ACK and RST flag. Sending a message with 16kB data and a topic length of 11B causes the header to be ``` 0x30, // Publish, no DUP, QoS 0, no Retain 0x8D, 0x7D, // remaining length of 16013B 0x00, 0x0B, // topic length 11B topic... ``` which works fine and is right according to MQTT 3.1. Sending a message with 17kB data and a topic length of 11B causes the header to be ``` 0x30, // Publish, no DUP, QoS 0, no Retain 0xF5, 0x84, // ... this is wrong. Beginning with the LSB (0x84) there is a continuation bit which would indicate a 3B long remaining length field. So the following 0x00 gets included into the remaining length field too. As a result the topic length field ix 0x0B and the first byte of the topic. That causes a wrong topic length and unreadable MQTT package. The right remaining length would be 3B (0xF5, 0x84, 0x01). 0x00, 0x0B, // topic length 11B topic... ``` [2019-03-28T21:15:00Z | david-cermak | comment] Hi all, Can we close this older issue? title: turn off log2ram
body:
log2ram maps 50M of ram.  Logs are rotated weekly and stay uncompressed in the /var/log directory.  When this happens, the /var/log directory will eventually explode, and no log can be written. (ever).   And we lost 50megs of memory

To fix this problem, 
solution 1:
Tune /var/log  such that log2ram maps to a directory that max can ever be is less than few megabytes.  And logrotate to somewhere else.

solution 2:
stop using log2ram and use what ever it is there.

"
   In principle, UPnP IGD should allow clients to specify a lifetime on
   port mappings.  However, a Google search for "UPnP NewLeaseDuration"
   shows that in practice pretty much every client uses
   "<NewLeaseDuration>0</NewLeaseDuration>" to request an infinite
   lease, and the protocol has no way for the NAT gateway to decline

title: Bug in interrupt handling without storing DSP/FPU registers
body:
# Issue Summary
- **Type**: *Bug* 
- **Category**: *BSP* 
- **Release Version**: Specified version such as 2016.05 or All

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bug

## Development Environment
- **HOST OS**: Windows 10, 64bit

- **TOOLCHAIN**: MWDT L-2017.06

- **BOARD**: EMSK 2.3

- **ARC CORE**: Any

## Bug Description
   FPU and DSP registers are not saved during handling of interrupts and exceptions, This may lead to undefined behavior.
For my case: I have a thread that has a division operation, and there is a **vKernelTick** which is the ISR of tick timer of freertos port. This interrupt has also a division operation in calling of **board_timer_update**. **MW** is optimizing the local variables in case of division and use the **accl** and **acch** registers, so if the tick interrupt happens  after performing the division operation and before using **accl** or **acch** register, there will be a corrupted values in those registers when returning from the ISR where an exception happened and the arc_reset is called.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enhancement
   Adding the following code to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE and EXCEPTION_PROLOGUE at **arc_asm_common.h**
```
#if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT
	SAVE_R58_R59
	SAVE_FPU_REGS
	SAVE_DSP_REGS
#endif
```
and the following to INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE and EXCEPTION_EPILOGUE
```
#if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT
	RESTORE_DSP_REGS
	RESTORE_FPU_REGS
	RESTORE_R58_R59
#endif
```
same as SAVE_CALLEE_REGS and RESTORE_CALLEE_REGS.
comments:
[2019-03-14T08:02:10Z | vonhust | comment]
If interrupt handlers will use DSP/FPU (which is not recommended as these operations are time consuming), these registers should be pushed and popped

at the entry and exit of interrupts, i.e, move  the pop/push from SAVE_CALLEE_REGS/RESTORE_CALLEE_REGS to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE/ INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE.

The hardware will not push&pop these regs automatically (same for ARM).

So this is not a bug, but a choice.

[2019-04-02T15:07:34Z | mfarag13 | comment]
Hi @vonhust ,
DSP Operation (Division) is already used in an interrupt **vKernelTick**  at freertos port for ARC in function **board_timer_update**.
In this case freertos port should be updated. or we can add push/pop to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE/ INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE.

  <build>
<pluginManagement>
<plugins>

</plugins> 
 </pluginManagement>
  </build>
```

So in conclusion: Somehow there was a problem in the pairing process resulting the GU10 bulbs to be recognised as remotes. This resulted in the original error. The solution was to reset the Gateway and re-pair the network. This problem can be identified by looking at the `5750` key, this has a value of `2` when identified as a lamp and `0` when identified as a remote.

While figuring this out @ggravlingen and @lwis made a fix. That fix is now only worth something as a fallback for when this issue appears again.

The IKEA app identifies devices differently than Pytradfri does. IKEA doesn't seem to rely on the value of `5750` at all or on `3311` being present. Instead, the app probably looks at the presence of any lamp values (ex: Lamp state, dimmer value etc.). A curious choice when `5750` exists.

We can automate the detection of this issue, that might be a good addition to the examples or wiki.

title: Setting color values individually
body:
### Where are you using pytradfri (eg stand-alone, Home Assistant etc)
Stand-alone

### Version of pytradfri
5.2.1

### Expected behaviour
```
lamp.light_control.set_hsb(1000, 1000, None)
```
Above code should update hue and saturation, but leave brightness unchanged. This is the behaviour of 5.2.0

### Actual behaviour
Program crashes with the following (partial) traceback:

```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pytradfri/device.py", line 224, in set_hsb
    self._value_validate(brightness, RANGE_BRIGHTNESS, "Brightness")
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pytradfri/device.py", line 266, in _value_validate
    if value < rnge[0] or value > rnge[1]:
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
```

In other words. The value validation I wrote blocks this type of use.

### Solution
The easiest solution is changing the value validation to allow `None` as a value. 

See PR #139

title: vscpl1_usb2candrv.dll not able to open more than one interface
body:
System: Windows 7-64, latest release of vscpd/works, USB2CAN interface with firmware 1.5 (latest)

Neither the usb2can.dll provided by 8devices nor the vscpl1_usb2candrv.dll provided in:
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/tree/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can

is able to open more than one CAN interface at any one time. This seems to be known problem, as in file
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/common/dlldrvobj.h
line 41 the maximum number of opened drivers is limited to 1. Changing this constant from 1 to 256 does not change the behaviour - still only one channel can be opened, further calls to CanalOpen() will not do anything but return an error.

Furthermore the handle returned by CanalOpen() is always 1681 for any number of usb2can-interfaces on the same machine.

That said, it seems that in file
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/common/dlldrvobj.cpp
in line 178 we get always 1681 as handle. This may be the case because the break in line 179 always breaks the for-loop counting through all interfaces.

Sadly even with removing the break (which seems to be obvious) the dll is still not able to open multiple interfaces - but the returned handle now changes, at least sometimes, to values of 1681, 1682, 1683 and 1684 (and probably more) - but still only one usb2can is delivering data.

Reproduction:
1. have two usb2can-interfaces with different serial numbers,
    having at least one node running on each interface makes sense,
    but is not required to produce the error
1. configure vscpd to have those two interfaces enabled and supported
2. start vscpd and watch the debug output

Hope its ok for both of you that I am writing something to the problem,  because some days ago I took a look at that area.
1. CANAL_USB2CAN_DRIVER_MAX_OPEN has to be set greater than 1, because the dll driver limits with that the max. number of usb2can objects.
2. In my eyes the "break" in https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/common/dlldrvobj.cpp you mentioned Stefan, is necessary. Because the CDllDrvObj::addDriver method searchs for a empty slot and if a empty slot is found, it will assign the usb2can object to this slot and break out of the loop.

If you really change only the CANAL_USB2CAN_DRIVER_MAX_OPEN to e. g. 10, then clean everything and compile it again, it should run.

Your log shows "Failed to open driver. Will not use it!", which is thrown only in case that the handle is lower or equal than 0, not 1681! So it is strange that you see always 1681?! But it would match in case the CANAL_USB2CAN_DRIVER_MAX_OPEN is set to 1.

Please add a printf after line 97, after line 104 and after line 106. in CanalOpen (https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/win32/usb2candrv.cpp) and we should see how it behave.

title: "Failed to update data" when writing register
body:
Context:
- VSCP 1.0.1.12 on Ubuntu 14.04 LTS
- VSCP daemon running locally, VSCPworks running locally
- USB2CAN converter to a bus with 21 Mespelare v9 modules

History:
- ip link set can0 up
- /etc/init.d/vscpd start
- /usr/local/bin/vscpworks & 
- Start VSCP client window, connect to daemon
- Start VSCP device configuration window, connect to daemon

Known good baseline:
- read registers for device 0x0D, read successful
- change value for register 0x27, click Update, write successful, functionality as expected (shows register write worked)

Bug:
- wait half an hour or so
- change value for register 0x27, click Update. Lots of debug messages in the terminal window where VSCPworks was started, "Failed to update data" message window. 
- kill -9 [vscpd and vscpworks], daemon restart, vscpworks restart, register now reads and writes correctly.
- When testing functionality or re-reading the node's registers, it is clear that the data was written to the node correctly, but VSCPworks still threw an error.
- Changing the node ID input box on the top of the screen and updating (re-reading) all the node's registers also makes the error go away.

title: VSCP Works regsiter save/load does not work
body:
Dear,

I have found what I believe to be a bug in the export registers to file funtion in VSCP Works. Running version 0.4.0.15.

Reproducing:

Open the device configuration window.
Load a node's registers.
Select "File" - "Save registers to file" and save into a .reg or .xml file
Select "File" - "Load registers from file" and re-load the file we just saved.
An error pops up saying "XML parsing error: 'not well-formed (invalid token)' at line 256.
When opening this file in a text editor (Notepad++) I find a value "0×" on line 256. There are a total of 4 occurrences of this value. When doing a search for this value and replacing any occurrences with "0x", VSCP Works is then able to import the file correctly. Note the subtle difference in the way the "x" is represented.

I believe there is a bug (typo?) in the export file code in the device configuration window.

Cheers,
David.

title: Action  Send event to remote server (seg fault)
body:
On a Raspberry Pi (four cores) with a DM that use action 0x43 (Send event to remote server) there will be seg fault's occasionally. Unable to repeat on a x86 machine (two cores) but can verify on the Raspberry Pi.  

Error probably has to do with race condition in thread that handles tcp/ip communication. Will not be fixed in current source but instead fixed by on-going rewrite of tcp/ip communication code.

David.

title: VSCPworks 1.0.0.70 attempts to write reserved registers
body:
Scenario:
- read a node's registers (all registers)
- save registers to file
- change node Id in device config window
- load registers from file
- click Update

VSCP will write all registers, even the VSCP reserved registers 0x80-0xFF. The node handles this correctly by refusing to write the reserved registers, and instead returning the value.
comments:
[2015-02-18T13:07:57Z | grodansparadis | comment]
This is a good find which also had page related errors. The functionality has changed slightly as a valid register set now must be have been read in before new registers can be loaded. If not an update will be done before registers are loaded.

title: `AppDaemon.sun_down` has timezone issues
body:
I've been having some problems with automations relying on `AppDaemon.sun_down`. After some debugging, both `self.AD.sun['next_rising']` and `self.AD.sun['next_setting']` appear to be off by a day:


    In [21]: now = datetime.now(pytz.UTC)

    In [22]: str(self.AD.sun['next_rising'] - now)
    Out[22]: '14:10:31.195186'

    In [23]: str(self.AD.sun['next_setting'] - now)
    Out[23]: '1 day, 1:23:54.195186'

Home Assistant correctly reports the next sunset to be in about three hours, yet AppDaemon is off by a day, which flips the `sun_up` and `sun_down` automations. Looking at the code, it seems like the issue stems from these two lines in `appdaemon.AppDaemon`:

    def update_sun(self):
        # now = datetime.datetime.now(self.tz)
        now = self.tz.localize(self.get_now())

The commented out line correctly reports my time, while the second one just attaches my timezone to the current UTC time, which is wrong.

Is this a configuration issue on my end?
comments:
[2018-03-04T14:48:15Z | acockburn | comment]
The commented out line was replaced by the current one so that time travel would work properly - I'm not sure why it's broken. What timezone are you using?

[2018-03-16T19:22:27Z | puddly | comment]
I'm using `America/New_York` in my Home Assistant configuration file but changing it to another timezone doesn't make a difference.

Am I misreading the intent of the code? `self.get_now()` returns a timezone-unaware `datetime` object that implicitly uses UTC and then it's just given my local timezone, which results in `now` containing the wrong time.

For calculating the time the sun will rise at a particular point, I don't think the local timezone needs to be involved anywhere beyond the `astral.Location` initializer in `AppDaemon.init_sun`. Will the following change work?

    now = pytz.utc.localize(self.get_now())

I think it'd be better to have `AppDaemon.get_now` return a timezone-aware datetime object.

[2018-03-16T19:54:21Z | acockburn | comment]
What API calls are you using? My code shows all things working as expected, when using the published interfaces. and if there were an issue here the scheduler would be out of whack for sunrise and sunset, and I'm not having any issues with that.

```python
  def get_sun_info(self):
    self.log("Current sun state: Up = {}, Down = {}".format(self.sun_up(), self.sun_down()))
    self.log("Next sunrise: {}".format(self.sunrise()))
    self.log("Next sunset: {}".format(self.sunset()))
```

```

2018-03-16 15:48:55.368289 INFO dep1: Current sun state: Up = True, Down = False

2018-03-16 15:48:55.374357 INFO dep1: Next sunset: 2018-03-16 19:00:20
```

Which is correct.

What update_sun() is actually doing is coming up with timezone aware datetime objects that are in the UTC timezone.

[2018-03-16T20:14:07Z | puddly | comment]
I was using `self.sun_up()` and `self.sun_down()` in my automations.

If I use the following code:

I get the following output:

title: PyYAML-5.1 breaks !secret tag parsing
body:
After an update with `pip3 install --upgrade appdaemon`, AD would not start anymore. The systemd journal shows the following:
```
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]: /opt/appdaemon/lib/python3.5/site-packages/appdaemon/admain.py:184: YAMLLoadWarning: calling yaml.load() without Loader=... is deprecated, as the default Loader is unsaf

Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]: ERROR Error loading configuration
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]: ERROR parser says
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]: ERROR   in "<unicode string>", line 8, column 14:
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]:           token: !secret ha_token
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]:                  ^
Mar 23 19:50:45 shodan appdaemon[18236]: ERROR could not determine a constructor for the tag '!secret'

Downgrading PyYAML to 3.13 solves the issue.
This could be an upstream issue, since it looks like there are some problems with 5.1 which may be related and possibly fixed in 5.2: yaml/pyyaml#265

title: Priority issue - Apps not respecting priority
body:
I am having an issue where my app priority doesn't seem to be respected. 

I have two apps, one that installs prerequisite python packages (install_dependencies), and one that imports one of those packages (cox_usage).

The apps are configured as follows:

```yaml
install_dependencies:
  module: install_deps
  class: InstallDeps
  priority: 0
  packages:
    - lxml
    - responses
    - mechanicalsoup

cox_usage:
  module: cox_usage
  class: CoxUsage
  priority: 99
```

Every time I recreate my docker container I have to comment out the cox_usage module, allow install_dependencies to complete, and then uncomment cox_usage. If i don't do this, AppDaemon gets stuck in a constant boot loop because cox_usage fails to load due to a ModuleNotFoundError. I have the exact same problem if I add install_dependencies as a dependency to the cox_usage app, so that's not a solution either. 

My understanding is that install_dependencies should run first, but it does not. 

I was able to remedy this in my testing by renaming install_dependencies to aaa_install_dependencies so that it runs first.

title: No network on hassos 3.5 with dtoverlay=pi3-disable-bt
body:
I tried the update to hassos 3.5 from 2.12 on my Raspberry Pi 3B and the update ended with the network not being available anymore.

I have narrowed this down to having
```
dtoverlay=pi3-disable-bt
```
in my /boot/config.txt file to use the my Razberry Z-Wave board. This parameter was necessary to have the Z-Wave controller module available and is documented here:
https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/z-wave/device-specific/#razberry-board

Without the dtoverlay=pi3-disable-bt in config.txt my Pi is booting properly (but I suppose won't have zwave anymore.

you need only `enable_uart=1`. I will look if I can find an issue on raspberry github org because we use the origin raspbian firmware/kernel

Have you try to change` /dev/ttyAMA0` in `/dev/ttyS0` ?

[2019-09-17T15:58:59Z | Try2Fly | comment]
No I did not try that. So you suggest to only change to `/dev/ttyS0` and not change the config.txt file?

both  `/dev/ttyAMA0` and `/dev/ttyS0` do not give me a working raspbee.

title: Setting single node property re-uses range from previous set
body:
This defect is against 2.0 (master)

If you set a node property using a range, like this:

```
Homie
  .setNodeProperty(valvesNode, PROPERTY_TIME)
  .setRange(valve)
  .send(String(time));
```

and then later set a single (non-range) property, like this:

```
Homie
  .setNodeProperty(batteryNode, PROPERTY_VOLTAGE)
  .send(String(voltageCoefficientSetting.get() * ESP.getVcc()));
```

The second set re-uses the left-over range value from the previous set.  In my case, the first set, above uses topic `devices/sprinklers/valves/time_6` and then the second set incorrectly sends `devices/sprinklers/powerUSB/voltage_6` when it should be just `devices/sprinklers/powerUSB/voltage`.  This is because HomieClass::setNodeProperty() doesn't clear the range when generating and returning the SendingPromise.

setNodeProperty() should clear the range in the sendingPromise before returning it.

I have a pull request for your consideration, coming shortly.

body:
Hi,

I've been testing the new changes with OTA and base64 and I haven't been able to successfully get it to work yet. 

To report the current situation, when sending a ota (using @mrpace2 script) the device is issuing a 400 BAD_CHECKSUM, but rebooting and then not responding until hard reset.

I can provide the logs from serial and mqtt if needed.

Is there anyone working on this? Otherwise I can take a look at it and try to solve it.
comments:
[2016-11-14T20:56:04Z | marvinroger | comment]
Can you test without base64? I think the base64 implementation is somehow broken.

[2016-11-14T21:33:59Z | unknown_author | comment]
A pair of MQTT and serial logs would be great. Also, can you share your base64-encoded firmware and the matching firmware binary? Note that this is just for trying to help with the `400 BAD_CHECKSUM`. 

You must have sent an MD5 which is why Homie rebooted after the failed OTA attempt. Something went wrong during that reboot. This is probably unrelated to the triggering `400 BAD_CHECKSUM` issue. See #204.

[2016-11-14T22:10:18Z | marvinroger | comment]
@camilorodegheri Closing this, as the base64 OTA issue will be tracked here: #204

> but rebooting and then not responding until hard reset

As @mrpace2 said, there's a known esp8266/Arduino issue. When you flash a firmware over Serial, calling ESP.restart() right after (which is done internally in Homie) hangs the ESP8266 the way you're experiencing it. However, if you power cycle the device after the flash, it will work restart without any issues.

So, as a rule of thumb: after you flash any sketch on the ESP8266, power cycle it once. There won't be any `ESP.restart()` issues after that. 😉

title: MQTT Traffic Load
body:
I have four NodeMCU boards running Homie v2.0.0 connected to a Raspberry Pi 3 running Mosquito.  Each Homie device is sending data back every 30 seconds.

CPU idle time as reported by top is around 98%:  Receive data as reported by bmon peaks at about 2k bytes/second and transmitted data peaks at about 800 bytes/second.  Life is good.

If I stop Mosquito, then the receive traffic jumps to 64 K bytes/second and the transmit traffic jumps to 115K bytes/second.

My guess is that the Homie devices are flooding the Pi's AP with attempts to reconnect??

I don't plan on stopping Mosquito during normal operation, but I don't want to bring the Pi to its knees if I need to stop the broker for some reason.  I'm using ssh over WiFi to do development and the connection becomes almost unusable if I stop Mosquito.

If my guess is correct about the Homie devices, then is there a way to throttle back on the retries?

Thanks,
Bob

[2016-11-22T17:52:49Z | flaviostutz | comment]
Marvin,

For that kind of retry, a common practice is to retry in doubles of time from the last time to avoid flooding when an error won't be fixed in a long time. 
For example:
- first try: 1s
- second try: 2s
- 4s, 8s, 16s... 1h, 2h... 6h, 12h...

Many implementations also limits max delay time to avoid getting month delayed retries...

Just a tip...

title: MQTT communication issues when base_topic and device_id is large (v2.0.0 develop)
body:
Sorry posting this "develop" branch issue here, but I couldn't lose this bug's track. I just managed to workaround a messy problem here (two days debugging it!).

When I configure my device (POST http://192.168.123.1/config) without the "device_id" field in the JSON, it restarts, connects to Wifi, connects to MQTT, but then it can't manage to publish/subscribe and I get on timeout cycles of reconnections and trials of publishing of "$online" state with no success. 

I tried with two different MQTT servers on the cloud. One of them works flawslessly (test.mosquitto.org) and another on my VPS (a default configured mosquitto 1.4.10 - latest). I have problems with the later and with test.mosquitto I have no problems. I do connect/pub/sub flawslessly with my MQTT client to both servers, which drove me crazy!

The workaround solution was to define "device_id" on config.json, but I wanted to let Homie use the default device_id on its own. I don't know if there is something with the full mac address being on the default "device_id"... 

See attached tcpdump captures on the server.

title: Bug when using getMqttClient() feature.
body:
Hi,
When using the `Homie.getMqttClient();` feature the OnMessage callback is called but topic argument is not complete.

This is due to the BootNormal.cpp OnMessage callback that suppress '/' and remplace those by '\0' vithin the topic buffer variable(which will be then given to our custom OnMessage callback).
Topic is shorten until node, property and  set field are behind the end_of_string.

I agree that this bug appears depending on in which order OnMessage callback are registered, but this seems a bit dirty when processing message to not check device-id while subscription are possible for any MQTT topic.

I made a fix to BootNormal.cpp, the fix consist in verifying that arriving message are destinated to current device-id (after processing for Broadcast messages)

[2016-12-02T17:09:54Z | elbowz | comment]
I have found the same bug...this [commit](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/commit/14994b3225e51fa8a4c8430153fca76716f14729) is the problem!

This because ```device_topic``` and ```deviceId``` is not the same :)

```
const char* messageDeviceId = Interface::get().getConfig().get().deviceId;
for (uint16_t i = 0; i < strlen(device_topic); i++) {
    if ((device_topic[i] != messageDeviceId[i]) || (device_topic[i] == '/' && messageDeviceId[i] != '\0')) {
    return;
    }
}
```

- devices/**device-ID**/node-ID/property
- ```device_topic```: *node-ID/property*

body:
Don't use big strings in (eg;relay012345544444)

**HomieNode lightNode1("relay012345544444", "switch");** 

it will keep crashing your ESP8266.

_If you ESP is crashing without any message (at boot time) then this is the cause._

NOTE : I am on develop branch and this is the same issue on Master branch too.

-Venkat


Before submitting your issue, make sure:

- [ ] You're using a [stable release](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/releases), not the Git development version which is, by definition, unstable
- [ ] You've read the documentation for *your* release, which is in the `docs/` folder of the `.zip` of the release you're using, especially the **Getting started** and **Troubleshooting** pages, which contain respectively the minimum required version of the dependencies, and some answsers to the most common problems
- [ ] You're using the examples bundled in *your* release, which are in the `examples/` folder of the `.zip` of the release you're using. Examples in the latest git revision might not be backward-compatible with your release

Thanks!

title: after just 50 days uptime jumps to 40 years
body: after approximately 50 days the number of milliseconds returned from the millis() function overflows. this is not properly handled in Uptime::update (src/Homie/Uptime.cpp). this leads to "uptimes" of over 40 years, and that after just 50 days.

title: MQTT $localip gets truncated
body:
Having an issue with Homie v2.0.0 MQTT $localip
it gets truncated in the last symbol when published in MQTT:
e.g. instead of "192.168.1.128" it gets "192.168.1.12", tested this on two nodes but with the same results.
comments:
[2017-02-28T11:13:59Z | bertmelis | comment]
try changing the file BootNormal.cpp on line 193:

```C++
snprintf(localIpStr, MAX_IP_STRING_LENGTH - 1, "%d.%d.%d.%d", localIp[0], localIp[1], localIp[2], localIp[3]);
```
to
```C++
snprintf(localIpStr, MAX_IP_STRING_LENGTH + 1, "%d.%d.%d.%d", localIp[0], localIp[1], localIp[2], localIp[3]);
```
If it works, you should also changed it BootConfig.cpp. But if this fix works, I would think the bug is that the IP gets truncated by 2 characters.

title: MQTT not reconnecting after days of uptime vs. minutes / hours
body:
Hi!

My mosquitto server goes offline from time to time (separate issue to resolve), but when this happens, homie does not always reconnect after the server is rebooted and mosquitto is again running. I can only reproduce the issue after letting it run for several days, not minutes or hours.

Here I left it running for a few days, and this morning I have this message (after the server crash):
> MQTT packet acknowledged, packetId: 7459
> ...
> Looping through the various sensor, but there has was no change in their state, until:
> ...
> Heap size: 30968
> Temperature: 24.20 °C
> Humidity: 43.20 %
> Lux: 21 lx
> Motion: CLOSED
> MQ:23.74    LPG:0.00 ppm    CO:0.00 ppm    SMOKE:0.00 ppm
> ✖ MQTT disconnected
> Triggering MQTT_DISCONNECTED event...
> MQTT disconnected, reason: 0
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...

After 8h in this state, its not moved on and it never tries to reconnect, but other sensors have. I've not managed to figure out what, or why, it does not reconnect. As I can see other sensors are reporting in, the problem is not with the mosquitto server. Log file on the mosquitto server shows no traffic from this node when it is in this state.

After resetting the device, and then manually stopping the mosquitto service:
> MQ:23.74    LPG:0.00 ppm    CO:0.00 ppm    SMOKE:0.00 ppm
> ✖ MQTT disconnected
> Triggering MQTT_DISCONNECTED event...
> MQTT disconnected, reason: 0
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...
> Retrying (500ms)...
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...
> Retrying (1000ms)...
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...
> Retrying (2000ms)...
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...
> Retrying (4000ms)...
> ↕ Attempting to connect to MQTT...

It all looks normal and when the mosquitto service is started, homie reconnects and all is good.

Versions: Using your mqtt client and homie (2) as of March 10th.

Any idea as to why it fails to reconnect after days of uptime vs minutes or hours?
Is there additional debug information I can provide?

JJ

As I stated in my Update: If you define more than one HomieSetting with a default value via `setDefaultValue` the error occurs. To reproduce: Define more than one HomieSetting, make more than one defined with a default value using `setDefaultValue.` Set values in the App/Web different from the defaults and those manual, non-default values are not used during runtime and are not settable via MQTT $configuration/set. 

Don't use `setDefaultValue` or only once and they become settable via APP/Web and MQTT. So my uneducated guess is, that there is a parsing error in /Utils/Validation.cpp

[2017-04-19T19:49:19Z | kartom | comment]
@marvinroger: Thanks a lot for spending time testing this, and for the nice work with the whole framework! 

However I can reproduce the problem in two different ways (using ArduinoJson v2.8.4):

Way 1:
1.  Leave the default values in the app.
2. Try to change the settings via MQTT.

Way 2:
1. Created a sketch without the HomieSettings. 
2. Configure the device
3. Add the HomieSettings to the sketch and update the ISP
4. Try to change the settings via MQTT

I believe this because as soon as you have one setting in the "settings" section of the config.json then all others settings can be set from MQTT, regardless if the setting exists or not.

`if(!parsedJson.containsKey("settings")) {
    parsedJson.createNestedObject("settings");
}`

title: Make sure every announcements packet are sent
body:
AsyncMqttClient v0.7.0 `publish` returns `0` if there's not enough space for a packet to be sent.

We need to implement a state machine to retry sending if there's not enough space.

The only impact currently is that some announcements packets will get lost if you have a lot of nodes (> 28 in my case, might be lower/higher for you).

title: Homie 2.0 remains forever waiting for Wi-Fi connection
body:
I have a Homie node in operation (boot normal mode) working ok. If I press the RESET button in the ESP8266 the firmware restarts. After the initial debug messages Homie attempts to connect to WiFi but it remains there forever. This is the last debug message:

↕ Attempting to connect to Wi-Fi...

After several hours of investigation I've discovered that if I remove power supply from ESP8266, wait for a couple of minutes and power it up again, now the node works ok. It looks as if Homie get stacked in a wait loop for the wifi connection event, but this event never takes place because the wifi connection still exists (probably, the time required to reset the system is so small than the WiFi station didn't notice that the ESP8266 was disconnected and so the wifi connection was not dropped. And when the ESP8266 asks to connect to wifi it never receives a new connection as it still exists. Not sure if this is the cause but it is the only explanation I have. But I don't know how to fix this behaviour. 

I also have noticed this problem when the node is in operation and I upload a new firmware (direct upload, not using OTA). After the upload is finished, ESP8266 automatically restarts and the new firmware is executed (boot normal mode). Homie attempts to connect to WiFi but it remains there forever. And the only solution is to remove power supply for a couple of minutes.

I'm using Homie 2.0 from development repo.

title: READY_TO_SLEEP fires prematurely
body:
I'm following the docs to go into the deep sleep. However, when HomieEventType::READY_TO_SLEEP event is being generated, it seems to me that the MQTT client is not cleanly disconnected yet. I'm looking a the network trace, and the TCP connection is being left open when the device goes to sleep (when I call ESP.deepSleep(secs) as a response to HomieEventType::READY_TO_SLEEP). 

If I just set a flag when handling the event, and call ESP.deepSleep from the main loop, 100ms later, I can see TCP connection being closed properly.

Perfect timing, I've just updated the [temperature example](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/blob/master/examples/TemperatureSensor/TemperatureSensor.ino) with what you want! What you need is `setSetupFunction()`.

::verify(): calculated uint8_t: 16 10 AF 7D 9C 0B 21 0B F9 D7 5E 3C 94 AC 0A A9 2A A0 3B 93
SAN[0] == localhost
common_name = [tiggr.ww.mens.de]
> certificate matches
```

(Obviously the HTTP request proper fails)

Also, changing one octet of the fingerprint causes the fingerprint verification to fail.

[2016-03-21T14:19:35Z | marvinroger | comment]

[2016-03-21T18:37:26Z | marvinroger | comment]
Okay, I got it. The `verify()` method has to be called right after a `connect()`. The problem is PubSubClient handles the connection and write things right after. So there is no window to call the `verify()` method.

[2016-03-21T18:47:36Z | jpmens | comment]
That would mean having to pass a callback for verification to [::connect](https://github.com/knolleary/pubsubclient/blob/master/src/PubSubClient.cpp#L116), wouldn't it? Ouch.

[2016-03-21T18:59:23Z | marvinroger | comment]
Yes, or a new parameter to check in PubSubClient for a fingerprint... Which is not cross platform. So, we're facing an impasse. I'll open an issue in the PubSubClient repo, to discuss about it.

[2016-03-21T19:04:06Z | marvinroger | comment]
But [someone managed to make it work](https://github.com/knolleary/pubsubclient/issues/84#issuecomment-173677183), so I am probably saying stupid things.

[2016-03-21T19:19:27Z | jpmens | comment]

The problem was what I said: 

> Okay, I got it. The verify() method has to be called right after a connect(). The problem is PubSubClient handles the connection and write things right after. So there is no window to call the verify() method.

As a workaround, I now connect to the server and check the fingerprint, then disconnect and let PubSubClient connect to the broker. So yes, an attack is possible during this tiny timeframe, but I can't do anything, this has to be fixed in PubSubClient.

1458722417: Socket error on client Homie-cf3a07e0, disconnecting.

``` ino
#include <Homie.h>

const int PIN_RELAY = 16;

HomieNode lightNode("light", "switch");
HomieNode pingNode("ping", "pong");

bool lightOnHandler(String message) {
  if (message == "true") {
    digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, HIGH);
    Homie.setNodeProperty(lightNode, "on", "true"); // Update the state of the light
    Serial.println("Light is on");
  } else if (message == "false") {
    digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, LOW);
    Homie.setNodeProperty(lightNode, "on", "false");
    Serial.println("Light is off");
  } else {
    return false;
  }

  return true;
}

bool pingHandler(String message) {
  Serial.println("ping here");
  Homie.setNodeProperty(pingNode, "pong", "Bonjour!");
  return true;
}

void setup() {
  pinMode(PIN_RELAY, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, LOW);

  Homie.setFirmware("sub2-relay", "1.0.0");
  lightNode.subscribe("on", lightOnHandler);
  pingNode.subscribe("on", pingHandler);
  Homie.registerNode(lightNode);
  Homie.registerNode(pingNode);
  Homie.setup();
}

void loop() {
  Homie.loop();
}
```

The good news is, it is much better, the bad news is, it is not good. I have the following observations:
1. My small test sketch (`sub2.ino` as shown above) actually works, and I was able to "ping" it.
2. Fingerprint checking doesn't work: it's actually completely ignored, i.e. wether I use correct or incorrect fingerprint in configuration makes no difference. (I haven't been able to look at your code though)

1459003383: Received SUBSCRIBE from Homie-cf3a07e0
1459003383:     sensors/homie/cf3a07e0/# (QoS 1)
```

I think Homie is literally _killing itself_! My previous experience with PubSubClient on Arduino shows that if I send out a few messages "en block" it just dies. In this particular case, Homie is sending out several publishes, eg. during setupHandler, and they're being bounced back to the device; I think it then just dies.

I will try, time permitting, to observe this a little closer, but I believe that ought to be the reason...

Be that as it may, congrats so far!

[2016-03-26T21:25:46Z | jpmens | comment]

```

```

This would prevent most publishes from a Homie device being sent back to the same Homie device. I'm 3/4 or 7/8 convinced the device is hanging itself up due, not to your code, but to PubSubClient.

1459150544: Socket error on client Homie-cf3a07e0, disconnecting.
```

[2016-03-28T16:31:58Z | marvinroger | comment]
I can't optimize things more than this, if it's still an issue, it has to be solved in PubSubClient or in the Arduino for ESP8266 SSL implementation. :confused:

I have an idea. By default, the ESP runs at 80MHz. I have seen projects running at 160MHz when using SSL. With twice the power of calculation, maybe the `handshake failure` will disappear, and the `touch and go` you're describing might disappear... What do you think?

[2016-03-28T18:55:47Z | jpmens | comment]
As long as the chip then doesn't burn a hole through my desk, I'd say "let's try it"! ;-)

[2016-03-28T20:38:01Z | marvinroger | comment]

[2016-03-29T09:42:51Z | jpmens | comment]
One word: **SHIP IT**! (Ok, those were two words, but you get the drift.)
1. Homie hasn't been able to kill itself with pubs/subs yet; it survived many resets, which it didn't do previously.
2. My _heavy_ sketch has been running sans disconnects since 08:16 this morning. (I'll continue to monitor for 24h)
3. Fingerprint checking works! (I've tested positive and negative.)

You've done a tremendous job, thank you.

I would like to recommend adding something like this to the Wiki:

### Fingerprint

Adding a TLS fingerprint effectively pins the device to a particular certificate. Furthermore, as currently implemented by _WifiSecureClient()_, both `mqtt.host` and `ota.host` are verified against the server certificate's common name (`CN`) in the certificate subject or in the SANs (subjectAlternateName) contained in it, but not in their IP addresses. So, if the certificate used by your server looks like

```
Subject: CN=tiggr.example.org, OU=generate-CA/emailAddress=nobody@example.net
...
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
  IP Address:192.168.1.10, DNS:broker.example.org
```

enabling fingerprint in Homie will work only if `host` is set to `tiggr.example.org` or `broker.example.org` _and_ the correct fingerprint is used; setting `host` to the IP address will cause fingerprint verification to fail.

title: $stats/interval always 0
body:
The topic $stats/interval is always 0.
Maybe because in L359 there is a division by 1000 where the value is already in seconds - for me there is no need to do this division.

https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/blob/99161ce03c7ff1c8d3dc1fcc52abbf081212b68f/src/Homie/Boot/BootNormal.cpp#L359

why is there no need for 'you' ? are you changing the $interval value from the default?

[2018-05-06T08:54:10Z | mwildbolz | comment]
No need, because regarding to Homie specification this value is in seconds and the STATS_SEND_INTERVAL_SEC is also a value in seconds. So you don't need to divide it by 1000 - would only be necessary if the value is in ms.

And yes, I'm also changing the device_stats_interval through configuration.
I would also expect, that the changed value is written to this Homie topic.

[2018-06-10T13:03:46Z | CapnBry | comment]
This report is correct, STATS_SEND_INTERVAL_SEC is in seconds and the code divides it by 1000 expecting it to be in milliseconds before outputting it. In the code:
```
  const uint32_t STATS_SEND_INTERVAL_SEC = 1 * 60;
```
Where it uses the interval it also expects seconds:
```
  _statsTimer.setInterval(Interface::get().getConfig().get().deviceStatsInterval * 1000);
```
So one of the two is wrong and I believe @mwildbolz is correct considering the constant name is SEC and not MSEC. (it should be `itoa(STATS_SEND_INTERVAL_SEC, statsIntervalStr, 10);`)

[2016-04-16T14:57:11Z | DavidStacer | comment]
I had this problem too on a Wemos D1-mini. Updating the driver did not solve it.

To diagnose this and see all the message, I connected up another USB serial port adapter. Then connected the RX from the second serial board to the D1-mini TX pin and tied GND to the serial board. I then used Termite terminal program to monitor the serial traffic.

I changed the default Homie baud rate to 74880 - that is ESP8266 default boot baud rate. This allowed me to see the ESP8266 boot up messages too.

Now I could see all of the messages.  When I pulled the main D1-mini USB cable and plugged back in, the majority of the time I would see:
â€¢ SSL: no
  â€¢ OTA
    â€¢ Enabled: no
Flagged for reset by pin
Device is in a resettable state
Configuration erased
â†» Rebooting in config mode

My theory:
When pinMode(this->_interface->reset.triggerPin, INPUT_PULLUP); is executed, the onboard D1-mini USB Serial adapter **may** not let the GPIO0 pin go high right a way. If you look on the D1-mini schematic, the RTS is connected to the GPIO0 pin via resister and NPN transistor. I'm speculating that the PC driver needs to give it a command to change (high or low don't know which).

Placing a delay(50); after the Homie.setup() and before the Homie.loop(); seemed to solve the problem too but I didn't like that as a solution.

Looking much deeper into the bounce code for the switch I found the default state is set to 0 meaning the switch is closed - requesting configuration mode.  In Bounce::attach I changed it to be state=1; as the default.

I have cycled the D1-mini with the USB cable many times and it seems to have fixed the problem of going into configuration mode without pressing and holding the switch.

[2016-04-16T15:53:16Z | marvinroger | comment]
@DavidStacer so what can I do at Homie's level? There is no way to programmatically set the default value of the state in Bounce2. So changing [this line](https://github.com/thomasfredericks/Bounce2/blob/master/Bounce2.cpp#L25) to `state = 1;` fixes the issue for you?

Maybe I can add this in the in troubleshooting in the docs?

[2016-04-16T17:40:18Z | DavidStacer | comment]
Changing that line did fix it for me because [Bounce attach()](https://github.com/thomasfredericks/Bounce2/blob/master/Bounce2.cpp#L25) sets the default to 0 but 1 would be a better default for this application.

When _handleReset call is made to [_resetDebuncer.read()](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/blob/master/src/Homie/Boot/BootNormal.cpp#L292l) it just returns the current  [Bounce::read()](https://github.com/thomasfredericks/Bounce2/blob/master/Bounce2.cpp#L87) value. The current state is still low because [update()](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/blob/master/src/Homie/Boot/BootNormal.cpp#L290) has only been called one time, so we really are not getting a debounced reading but just the initial reading.

I think its hard to fix in Homie but maybe don't call the _resetDebuncer.read() until the [DEFAULT_RESET_TIME](https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/blob/master/src/Homie/Constants.hpp#L18) has passed since boot up but that is just another way of delaying. I guess we are delaying the time before getting the switch value vs. holding up the rest of the program.

I will test out that idea and see if it works.

You can disable the reset trigger completely with Homie.disableResetTrigger() and it will stop deleting the config.  If you want the reset trigger behavior, you may be able to move it to another pin.  I have not attempted this.

title: Some WiFi passwords characters are not valid
body:
I have a very complex WiFi password and some of the characters in it caused Homie trouble.

Testing shows that:
% &  " ' + _      Cause issues. Some failed in the config loading, some never connected to wifi.
~!@#$^*()-={}[]:;<>?,./`Aa1234567890    All work.

This [Stackoverflow link ](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4919889/is-there-a-standard-that-defines-what-is-a-valid-ssid-and-password) says any character should work for WiFi, so possibly its  a Web UI or json issue.

I tried in a native Arduino IDE 
const char\* password = "~!@#$^*()-={}[]:;<>?,./`Aa1234567890%&+_'\"";  and that password worked. I had to escape the " with \"  .

I'm going to setup a separate IOT WiFi network so its not an issue for me but I wanted to document the characters that you can't use in your WiFi password and maybe save someone else some debug time.

List that won't work spelled out with hex
  percent  0x25
  ampersand 0x26
  double quote 0x22
  single quote 0x2C
  plus sign 0x2B
  underscore 0x5F

Actually there's a way to initialize a struct with the `setRange()`.

``` c++

```

Seems like PlatformIO was updated on the CI or something. @ivankravets sorry for the ping once again, what needs to be updated on our side?

[2016-09-10T21:37:05Z | ivankravets | comment]
@marvinroger Thanks! Interesting moment. Looks like need to document it. PlatformIO 3.0 is really and has been significantly improved and simplified. No need to install library manually :) See my PR https://github.com/marvinroger/homie-esp8266/pull/151

---

Story...

PlatformIO handles dependencies when you install a library. It can be manual installation or specifying dependency in project file `platformio.ini`.  

Here we have 3-rd situation. Your library depends on a few other libs. It's OK and COOL. But... You use CI that doesn't handle dependency. title: Bugfix base64-encoded firmware when (size mod 3) equals 1
body:
I noticed an issue with base64-encoded OTA updates: for some firmware base-encoded OTA update worked and for some it didn't.

It turned out that, if the real firmware size modulo 3 equaled 1, firmware was incorrectly rejected with `400 BAD_FIRMWARE`. The reason was that the code I added only expected the real firmware size to be off by **one** from the "guestimated" size (3/4 ratio of the total length of the `=` padded base64 payload). However, the real firmware size may as well be off by **two** from the 3/4 ratio.

Examples with some realistic firmware sizes:

| Real firmware size | Real size modulo 3 | Base64 length | Base64 Padding | Estimated firmware size | Size off-by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 346992 | 0 | 462656 | (none) | 346992 | 0 |
| 346993 | 1 | 462660 | "==" | 346995 | 2 |
| 346994 | 2 | 462660 | "=" | 346995 | 1 |
| 346995 | 0 | 462660 | (none) | 346995 | 0 |
| 346996 | 1 | 462664 | "==" | 346998 | 2 |
| 346997 | 2 | 462664 | "=" | 346998 | 1 |
| 346998 | 0 | 462664 | (none) | 346998 | 0 |

Or, more general (N = any natural number):

| Real firmware size | Real size modulo 3 | Base64 length | Base64 Padding | Estimated firmware size | Size off-by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N*3 | 0 | N*4 | (none) | N*3 | 0 |
| N*3+1 | 1 | (N+1)*4 | "==" | N*3+1 | 2 |
| N*3+2 | 2 | (N+1)*4 | "=" | N*3+1 | 1 |

This PR fixes the base64 length issue. In addition, the PR adds a check for payload size evenly dividable by 4 with base64-encoded payloads.

Checking the "$state" topic for not "false" was wrong, because since v3

I expanded our validation logic that automatically corrects this case `{"platforms": [{ ... }]}`. It will also correct users doing this `[{ ... }]`. This also catches this in the accessories; `{"accessories": [{ ... }]}`.

If a user, royally jacks this up and adds multiple platforms or accessories in one json field, IE. `{platforms": [{ ... }, { ... }]}` or `[{ ... }, { ... }]`, an error is thrown and the user is unable to save until the error is cleared.

@Doublenik8
I am assuming you can access the interface from **http://hoobs.local**. If you can't let me know.

## Environment
1. Download and install [https://www.getpostman.com/](https://www.getpostman.com/).
2. Open Postman and then click on the workspace dropdown. (Next to Invite) and then click on **Create New**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 12 55 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352170-c704e780-1827-11ea-869f-18d756c53147.png)
3. Set the name to **HOOBS** and click **Create Workspace**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 12 57 01 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352249-eef44b00-1827-11ea-9f42-525b73ea004d.png)
4. Make sure HOOBS is selected (You just created it, sometimes Postman doesn't automatically select it)
5. Download this from HOOBS [https://github.com/hoobs-org/HOOBS/raw/master/postman.zip](https://github.com/hoobs-org/HOOBS/raw/master/postman.zip) and un-zip it.
6. Click the Manage Environment button (it's the gear in the upper right).
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 00 14 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352488-793caf00-1828-11ea-934a-225679810bfe.png)
7. Click **Import**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 01 22 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352527-8fe30600-1828-11ea-9f57-f2a8aabe4b13.png)
8. Browse to the un-zipped file from HOOBS and select **enviornment.json**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 02 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352605-b7d26980-1828-11ea-9604-740e805ebe1e.png)
9. Clock on **hoobs.local**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 18 52 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353607-f9fcaa80-182a-11ea-8759-31d08d72de33.png)
10. Set the **username** and **password** fields. This will be the same username and password you use to log into HOOBS.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 17 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353642-1567b580-182b-11ea-9f80-63ffa257f2fc.png)
11. Click **Update**
12. Now close the dialog (Not Add, use the X)
13. Now in the Environment drop-down, select **hoobs.local**.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 04 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352711-fcf69b80-1828-11ea-9e0d-c42fe598ee84.png)

## Commands
Now that you have the environment setup, you need to add the commands.
1. Click File -> Import
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 10 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353084-cbca9b00-1829-11ea-96a1-29773722c402.png)
2. Go to the **Import Folder** tab and then Click **Choose Folders** and select the **collections** folder. (this is from the zip file you downloaded from HOOBS)
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 29 10 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354324-79d74480-182c-11ea-88d1-4ba55b3eb2c0.png)
3. You should see all of the commands now
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 13 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353257-3f6ca800-182a-11ea-9ce4-8e5260f5d89f.png)

## What I Actually Need
Now you can run commands against the HOOBS API.
1. Open **Authentication** and click on **Login**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 14 48 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353353-6aef9280-182a-11ea-8974-6dbe952e1425.png)
2. Click **Send**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 15 31 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353405-7fcc2600-182a-11ea-8532-0f8a0fea5405.png)
3. You will see this, but you don't need to do anything with it. It's just logging in.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 23 43 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353948-b6567080-182b-11ea-8b69-4503be28f1de.png)
4. Now open **Accessories** and click on **List Accessories**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 24 34 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353986-cff7b800-182b-11ea-8196-7fc8b3802401.png)
5. Now click **Send**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 25 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354033-e6057880-182b-11ea-9fa4-d837c16517a0.png)
6. You will see something like this.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 25 54 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354065-f584c180-182b-11ea-9610-306f1b7ef38f.png)

`hoobs@hoobs:~/.hoobs/etc $ hoobs -D

[Homebridge] [12/26/2019, 12:18:01 AM] Service is running on port 51826.`

**Version**
HOOBS 3.1.10
Node v10.17.0
NPM 6.11.3

**Did you upgrade**
Please let us know if you upgraded from a previous version.

comments:
[2019-12-26T05:36:43Z | askovi | comment]
Nevermind. Not a permission issue. It seems like when installed without root, it didn't add this part to the config.json file:

`"bridge": {
        "name": "HOOBS",
        "port": 51826,
        "pin": "031-45-154",
        "username": "A3:CC:53:A0:A3:3D"
    },
   "system": "hoobs"`

Adding that part to the config got it working

[2019-12-26T18:11:55Z | mkellsy | comment]
This is happening because there is config clean logic that is removing the bridge section. I restricted this to only accessories and platforms.

[2019-12-27T06:18:51Z | askovi | comment]
So the same JSON syntax error was happening to another customer. Here's how I fixed it:

1. Added the bridge section and the system:hoobs to config.json
2. deleted layout.json
3. Added an empty array [ ] in access.json (file was empty) 

Errors went away and it booted fine after that. Please check what could cause any of the above to fail.

I added file try catches for the access and layout files.

Zero length file issues. Run the testing reset script before shipping.

```

This is done in HOOBS Server 3.2 and HOOBS Desktop

title: start events not propagated to all devices
comments:
[2014-06-08T17:19:36Z | deadprogram | comment]
@blalor thanks for helping isolate this. I know @zankich has mentioned this problem before, but this is a good example case. We'll work on it.

[2014-06-09T23:20:12Z | stewart | comment]
Looking into this more, it's actually _technically_ not a bug. What's happening is due to Node's event loop, by the time the event listeners are attached for the devices, the events have already been emitted, so we can't hook into them. The exception is for the last device, which emits the 'start' event on the same tick that the work block begins processing and sets up the handlers.

The devices are all going to be started by the time the work block begins running, so the device 'start' events are more or less worthless, and will be removed from both docs and code shortly.

title: Intel Edison read specific i2c register
body:
I am writing a driver for the MPU9150 IMU.  I am attempting to read a byte from a specific register and am always getting back the value from the first register on the device.

The sysfs i2c implementation sets the command byte to 0 for all reads:
https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot/blob/dev/sysfs/i2c_device.go#L103

Per the documentation here (https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/i2c/smbus-protocol), an I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA operation uses the command byte to set the starting register for the read but that is always set to 0.

An I2C_SMBUS_READ_BYTE operation will use the register from a previous write but not I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA.

Are all drivers that currently implemented just happening to be reading from the first register or am I missing something obvious?
comments:
[2016-03-18T04:00:30Z | deadprogram | comment]
Looks like this is an oversight that does not impact you if you are using an i2c adaptor that does not support the block data reads.

The solution is probably use the first byte of `b` as the register for that call. What do you think?

Hi @allanglen looked at this with fresh eyes, and I see that the `Write()` command is doing the right thing: https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot/blob/dev/sysfs/i2c_device.go#L128

I am going to make a similar change to `Read()`, would you be able to test this out on your hardware config?

title: ServoDriver / ServoWriter inconsistencies
body:
While adding a ServoWriter implementation to c.h.i.p, I noticed that the ServoDriver accepts movement in angles (0-180) and calls the underlying ServoWriter with a span (0-255).

However, the ServoWriter implementations for raspi and beaglebone both expect movement argument to be in angles, which breaks when someone uses a ServoDriver to talk to the device.

Not sure how to proceed, and not cause more problems / break compatibility.
comments:
[2017-01-24T17:59:18Z | deadprogram | comment]
Hi @erkkah that was an error that was introduced thru some incomplete refactoring. Thanks for the catch.

What we want to be happening, is that the `gpio.ServoDriver` should be passing along the angle value to `adaptor.ServoWrite()`. Then the specific adaptor can handle it however it needs to. In the Beaglebone case, by accepting an angle and scaling to a pwm duty cycle and calling PWMWrite. In the Firmata case, by just passing along the angle value.

So the conversion logic should be in the adaptor, not the `ServoDriver`.

[2017-01-24T21:40:32Z | erkkah | comment]
