title: I2C WriteBlockData not working as expected
body:
Hi,

As discussed in [this](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/golang-nuts/0_cZNZ3vykM) thread on the golang-nuts list.

I am using GoBot v1.2 that has the rewritten i2c subsystem, to try to drive a [PiGlow](https://shop.pimoroni.com/products/piglow) (based on a SN3218 IC) connected to a Raspberry Pi 1.
The code is written using the "metal bot" style as I would like to reuse this as part of another project.

My sample code is available on the Go playground as:
[https://play.golang.org/p/Xma_6zBtT2](https://play.golang.org/p/Xma_6zBtT2)

When I run this code it shows no output. None of the error values are non-nil and led zero does not light on the PiGlow.

As far as I can tell I am communicating with the PiGlow over i2c correctly. My code is based on that of Toon Schoenmakers [code](https://github.com/schoentoon/piglow). This code is not based on the GoBot 12c subsystem. However. Toon's test code works correctly and drives the PiGlow as expected.

Can someone with more experience of GoBots i2c subsystem make a suggestion as to what I might be doing wrong, or if this is a new bug in the i2c subsystem on a RaspPi.

Thanks

Owen
comments:
[2017-02-20T17:03:04Z | erkkah | comment]
Hi there.

A difference from Toon's code is that you do a "reset" and then return. I don't know how the PiGlow works, but it seems as you init everything, turn on a light, and then reset everything again before exiting. Don't know what "reset" does, but it's not used in Toon's example.

Possibly the default raspi bus in GoBot is not the same as bus 1 used in the other code. But you should have gotten errors then, I guess.

[2017-02-20T17:43:26Z | owenwaller | comment]
Hi Erkkah,

Firstly, if I take out the reset behaviour (aka the call to PiGlow.Halt()) I see the same behaviour - i.e. nothing. So it's not the reset call that is the problem. Although you are correct that pointing it in does seem a bit pointless if I want the led to stay on.

Secondly there is only one i2c device on the Rasp Pi 1 and its at /dev/i2c-1.
If I print the result of Adaptor.GetDefaultBus() call as used in the Adaptor.GetConnection call it will return 1.
Toon's code also uses 1 as the i2c bus number.

In fairness, I do believe that on a Rasp Pi 2 and 3 the default i2c bus is in fact 0.

Owen

[2017-02-20T17:51:13Z | deadprogram | comment]
Hi, everyone

I notice that the implementation being used by PiGlow calls to `WriteByte()` and `WriteByteBlock()` are basically does the equivalent of what Gobot is doing as `WriteByteData()` and `WriteBlockData()`.

At least one immediate difference I see, is that the implementation of `WriteByte()` is simply using the sysfs and not actually calling the SMBUS implementation:
https://bitbucket.org/gmcbay/i2c/src/1235f1776ee749f0eaeb6de69d8804a6dd70d9d5/i2c_bus.go?at=master&fileviewer=file-view-default#i2c_bus.go-80

Not sure if that is actually the issue here, but seems worth pointing out.

[2017-02-20T21:41:04Z | erkkah | comment]
Interesting.
So I guess one test would be to use the Write method instead of WriteByteData to see if it works any better.

[2017-02-20T21:52:35Z | owenwaller | comment]
Erkkahj,

I'm not 100% sure what you mean here but...

All the WriteXXX, ReadXXX, Write and Read calls in i2c.go are just wrappers around calls to

sysfs.I2cDevice.Write(byte) or sysfs.I2cDevice.Read() 

The source is [here](https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot/blob/master/drivers/i2c/i2c.go#L49)

Where as Toon's code bypasses sysfs entirely, and writes directly on the SMBUS. Which I think is Ron's point above.

[2017-02-20T22:04:41Z | erkkah | comment]
Hi Owen,

I think it's the other way around, or something like it :)

The WriteXXX and ReadXXX calls in i2c call the corresponding methods in sysfs, which in turn are implemented using the SMBUS ioctl calls.

The Write and Read calls on the other hand use direct file IO (direct I2C).

The library used by Toon's code mixes, and uses SMBUS for the block call and file IO for the WriteByte call.

To test with as little differences as possible, you could try to replace your WriteByteData calls with Write calls.
That was all I meant.

[2017-02-20T23:43:00Z | owenwaller | comment]
Erkkah,

Err exactly which type do you want me to call Write on? The Connection type?

Owen

[2017-02-20T23:48:04Z | owenwaller | comment]
Ah ha!

Okay if I take Erkkah's suggestion and swap all of the WriteXXX calls to i2cDevice.Write calls then it works. I get exactly what I expect - no errors and lights in the PiGlow.

My updated code is here:
[https://play.golang.org/p/-zcc2ODfLZ](https://play.golang.org/p/-zcc2ODfLZ)
Which enables LED zero for 5 seconds before turning it off again.

So, if this is a direct write to the i2c bus then it works. But if the WriteXXX calls are via syscalls to the ioctl on the smbus then it doesn't.

So it looks like you syscalls aren't working as you expect. Which at least narrows down the problem.

Owen

[2017-02-21T11:31:38Z | deadprogram | comment]
This is great work, thanks for looking into it!

One question: if you replace only the `WriteByteData()` with `Write()`, but left in the `WriteBlockData()` did that work? Trying to determine of all the syscalls were not working as expected, or only that one, since this is similar to what the gmcbay/i2c package does.

[2017-02-21T13:03:41Z | erkkah | comment]
Yes, great find!

Really interesting if the device supports SMBUS block operations but not the `WriteByteData()` call.

[2017-02-21T14:15:49Z | owenwaller | comment]
OK so I have just tried this.

In the Start() method if I swap out the 2nd call to Write()
```
// Start initiates the Driver
func (p *PiGlowDriver) Start() error {
	b := []byte{enableOutput, 0xFF}

```
for a call to WriteBlockData() like this:
```
// Start initiates the Driver
func (p *PiGlowDriver) Start() error {

	w, err := p.conn.Write(b)

It breaks the code. Nothing happens on the PiGlow after the change to WriteBlockData - no lights and no errors when the code runs.

So whatever is going on WriteBlockData() is broken.

Owen

[2017-02-21T14:23:17Z | owenwaller | comment]
And just to confirm this. 

If I swap a call to Write() for a call to WriteByteData() for the `enableOutut` byte at the start of the Start() method. And then replace the WriteDataBlock() with a Write() again for the `enableLeds` write in the above code everything still works.

So the combinations of:

WriteByteData() and Write works ok
WriteByteData() and WriteBlockData() fails

So the issue is defiantly under the call-stack of WriteBlockData.

Owen

[2017-02-22T07:54:29Z | deadprogram | comment]
Thanks @owenwaller for helping track this down. I renamed the issue to better reflect what the problem seems to be here.

Also, please feel free to create a PR with your PIGlow driver, if you get a chance. We would probably however want it to accept a `Connector` instead of an already existing `Connection` as the param, which would break your own current code.

[2017-02-22T16:00:49Z | owenwaller | comment]
NP. Once things are fixed I'd be happy to put together a PR for the PiGlow. 

I'll open a new issue for it as I need some advice as how best to achieve that.

[2017-02-22T21:56:16Z | erkkah | comment]
I found a difference between the i2c module used in Toon's code and the Gobot implementation in that that the prior always uses the PEC block transaction while Gobot always uses the non-PEC.
Added a possible fix in PR #378.

[2017-02-23T07:21:46Z | deadprogram | comment]
@owenwaller if you get a chance to test this, it would be greatly appreciated.

[2017-02-23T12:25:23Z | owenwaller | comment]
So pulling the request with:
```
git fetch origin pull/378/head:i2c-pec-fix
git checkout i2c-pec-fix
```
Then trying a quick a dirty test, by swapping the previous and working call to Write() to WriteBlockByte in the Start() method. So from this:
```
func (p *PiGlowDriver) Start() error {
	err := p.conn.WriteByteData(enableOutput, 0x01)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	b2 := []byte{enableLeds, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}

```
to this
```

The code fails. There are no lights. The first version works, the later doesn't.

[2017-02-23T19:57:49Z | erkkah | comment]
Hi Owen, that's curious, thanks for trying it out.

Can you go directly to  `WriteBlockData` in `sysfs/i2c_device.go` and hard code it to use `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA_PEC`?

With that, it should be the exact same code as in the other library, it would be interesting to figure out if it's the functionality check that fails or what it is.

[2017-02-23T21:40:11Z | owenwaller | comment]
Hi Erkkah,

Err, I can do but I'm not entirely sure what I'm supposed to change in `WriteBlockData` to enable this.
Can you paste in a diff of some sort and I'll make the change?

Owen

[2017-02-23T21:45:43Z | owenwaller | comment]
Err but while I look in `sysfs/i2c.go` at the `WriteBlockData code, it looks like you are throwing away data, if the function is passed more than 32 bytes. We have this circa line 167...
```
	if len(data) > 32 {
		data = data[:32]
	}
```
Which is silently throwing away data. Why? And surely that should fail with an error - the input data byte slice was to large or something similar?
In my case I'm only ever passing in 19 bytes, so I'm not falling foul of this. But others might be.

[2017-02-23T22:31:41Z | erkkah | comment]
Sure, change the WriteBlockData method to this: https://gist.github.com/erkkah/503607981df5c3ed2b74bbde61221a3a

[2017-02-24T07:26:01Z | erkkah | comment]
Looks like I made a mistake when importing constants from the c headers. Really confusing. 
I have updated the PR,  but I need to get a device that behaves consistently with block transfers to test and really fix this. 
Thanks again Owen for reporting and testing on your end. 
/Erik

[2017-02-24T16:16:23Z | owenwaller | comment]
Hi Erkkah,

Yeah, it works! And err, I need to eat some humble pie....

So what I have just tried is this:
```
git fetch origin pull/378/head:i2c-pec-fix
git checkout i2c-pec-fix
```
I am assuming this includes the updates to the PR.

If I then replace just the `Start()` method with the version [above](https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot/issues/372#issuecomment-281978596) then I get what I expect. No errors and a light on the PiGlow.

At the minute this is the only `Write()` that I have replaced with a call to `WriteDataBlock()`.

Let me add calls to `WriteDataBlock` everywhere else to confirm things, but at the minute it looks like the PR is good and works. Adding the extra error when the data is truncated would be nice, as I didn't actually know there was a 32 byte limit on the data block size.

And now for my humble pie...

Erkkah, I feel I own you an apology. I suspect your PR, may have worked first if I'd have tested it correctly.
At some point I have done either `go get github.com/hybridgroup/gobot` or a `git clone https://github.com/hybridgroup/gobot ~/go/src/github.com/hybridgroup/`. So I'd shadowed the gobot tree under `~/go/src/github.com/hybridgroup/gobot`.

Then of course when I tested your PR I pulled your PR into the source tree rooted under `~/go/src/github.com/hybridgroup/gobot` which is the wrong source tree and err, not even being built. I only realised this when I added some trace lines into you PR and they didn't appear.

Apologies if I mislead you or Ron.

Owen

[2017-02-24T17:29:19Z | owenwaller | comment]
Hi Erkkah,

Nope we are __still__ broken. Sorry. I can't write more than a single byte using `WriteDataBlock`.
As soon as I change the code that writes the 18 byte data block needed to turn on the leds I get no output (and no errors). If I replace that call with a `Write()` that writes the 18 bytes I need for the leds + one more for the command, everything works again. 

As far as I can tell there are two separate issues going on. One I can fix the second I think is down to you.

In the code the call to `copy` is wrong. You had:
```
copy(buf[:1], data)
```
But that needs to be:
```
copy(buf[1:], data)
```
Copy copies min(len(dest), len(src)) bytes. In your code `buf[:1]` is a slice is one byte. So you only copy one byte, not the whole array.

My current version - with some tracing and error detection - looks like [this gist](https://gist.github.com/owenwaller/593cfb0193e41acecbce153845edf588)

As an example of what I am trying this output using the above gist should explain things:
```
Number of bytes copied: 18
len(data)=18
data:[]byte{0xff, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0}
len(buf)=19
buf:[]byte{0x12, 0xff, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0}
```
It looks like the call to `d.smbusAccess(...)` just isn't writing (all?) of the bytes.
Your gist, includes an undefined constant `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA_PEC` which might fix things but I need the value to try it. :)

Owen

[2017-02-24T19:49:16Z | erkkah | comment]
Hi Owen.

Great find that silly copy thing! Looks like we can share that humble pie :)
And - that shadowing thing can be really confusing. I mainly use vendoring, and have fooled myself a number of times. Thank you so much for continuing to investigate.

My confusion, and what I would like to understand better, is the different "size" argument options. I have seen a bit of contradictory information, but now trust the "latest" linux header files (/usr/include/linux/i2c.h).

I believe the constants I have in https://github.com/erkkah/gobot/blob/i2c-pec-fix/sysfs/i2c_device.go, should work, and that the `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA` (value 5) you use in your gist is correct.

However, the I2C lib that Toon's code is using uses `I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA` (value 8).

If it turns out that the latter is more widely supported, we should probably move to that, and change the functionality check accordingly.

Your latest gist, does it work?

/Erik

[2017-02-24T20:01:41Z | erkkah | comment]
BTW, that copy fix made both my devices "behave", accepting `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA` writing just fine. Changing to `I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA` made one of the devices (TSL2561) fail.

/Erik

[2017-02-24T20:05:50Z | owenwaller | comment]
Ah ha! I have success.

So my change is:
```
I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA       = 8 //5
```
i.e. from 5 to 8. If I rebuild everying (with my copy fix) it works. I get a light on the PiGlow and no errors.

On my Pi a `uname -r` returns `4.4.38+`

So yes, redefining I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA and using my gist means I have a working solution.
But what you seem to be saying is that the value of I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA is kernel version dependant. Is that correct?

Owen

[2017-02-24T20:27:47Z | erkkah | comment]
Great news!

To answer your question - no, but I'll try to explain.

When entering this, I did what I use to do, and read the documentation. In this case, I went to https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/i2c/dev-interface and https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/i2c/smbus-protocol.

From there, I got the picture that `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA` is to be preferred over `I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA`:
```
The following I2C block transactions are supported by the
SMBus layer and are described here for completeness.
They are *NOT* defined by the SMBus specification.
```

However, when I started to look into other I2C libraries, I found that they used the `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA_PEC` constant (value 8) for block operations, which made me read up on PEC.

Now - the meaning of that constant seems to have changed with Linux versions, and PEC control is now a separate ioctl.

Don't know exactly when that changed, but it looks like a 2.X vs 4.X change. We should be safe with the values now in `/usr/include/linux/i2c.h`.

In addition to this confusion, different devices, as we now have shown, support different block operations. The PiGlow likes 8 but not 5, while the TSL2561 is the exact opposite. The DRV2605L supports both.

I'm starting to think that we should expose both, and document thoroughly.

@deadprogram, what do you think?

/Erik

[2017-02-24T21:09:18Z | owenwaller | comment]
You mean have a

`WriteBlockData(...)`
and new
`WriteBlockI2CData(...)`

We could make `WriteBlockData(...)` take a `[32]byte` not a `[]byte`. That would both remove the if check, and fix the block length at a maximum. Which is what the protocol docs seem to suggest. That would be a breaking change though. `WriteBlockI2CData(...)` would still take a `[]byte`. But then the protocol docs aren't clear. As I read this:
```
I2C block transactions do not limit the number of bytes transferred
but the SMBus layer places a limit of 32 bytes.
```
You can send more than 32 bytes to the IC, but things will be chunked into 32 byte blocks. So should the implementation do this chunking for the programmer?
In this case the COMM "byte" can be multi-byte so presumably more than 32 bytes + whatever length of data it needs.
 
All of this would be fine with me. As a driver writer you'd then have to read the IC docs and take your best guess. If as I've found out, if one write call fails then you'd just have to try the other one.

Owen

[2017-02-25T09:42:14Z | deadprogram | comment]
This is a great conversation here.

Regarding block operations, that might also be platform/kernal version based, not device based. @owenwaller you are on Raspi but @erkkah you are using CHIP, correct? Some platforms still work on older kernels right now, I'd rather not lose that.

I'd also rather continue to let Driver authors avoid knowing quite this much about the low level i2c implementations if they do not have to. The original naive sysfs implementation has the advantage of not having to know as much about what you are doing to get it to work as you expect. 

On a side not, we should probably failover to the sysfs equivalent operation if the desired block operation is not available, so Drivers can "just work", but can use the new helper functions.

The current `WriteBlockData()` should probably continue to accept `[]byte` and then either return an error if over the limit, or automatically chunk the write. We should not make Driver authors have to deal with that themselves.

If for a particular Driver we need a specific block operation, and it is supported on the platform, we could use an optional config to set that, or something?

Anyhow those are a few of my thoughts. This is awesome.

[2017-02-25T12:38:33Z | erkkah | comment]
In my case the support is device dependent, but might very well be platform dependent as well.
So, three dimensions of compatibility.. I'm starting to think that block operations are too complex to be worth supporting at this level. It seems as direct sysfs writes "always works" for block type writes.

Failover would be great, but in my case, would not work either. I never get any errors, the functionality checks seem to pass, yet it did not work.

If we keep `WriteBlockData()` I agree we should keep the `[]byte` interface. Passing a `[32]byte` would need a separate length argument for all cases where the intention is to write less than 32 bytes.

Why I started to work on this area in the first place was that I could not get word size reads to work on the TSL2561 using the original implementation. Then I tried to make the interface as close to the underlying system calls as possible, reusing the same operation names, et.c.

I think it's easier now to write correct driver code using the exposed Byte and Word methods, but the Block stuff so far has proven the opposite.

So, right now, I would suggest removing block operations, or adding separate methods for the two kinds.

[2017-02-25T12:49:38Z | deadprogram | comment]
That probably makes sense, @erkkah 

How about we leave in the `WriteBlockData()` interface, but just use it as a wrapper for a sysfs implementation for now. We can revisit the details on the "pure" SMBUS impl in the near future.

[2017-02-25T19:45:42Z | owenwaller | comment]
@deadprogram. Yes, I am on using a Raspi 1 running a `4.4.38+` kernel on jessie.

`WriteBlockData` should not chunk. It can only ever write 32 bytes max.. The SMBus spec seems to forbid chunking in this case. From the [spec ](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/i2c/smbus-protocol)
```
The opposite of the Block Read command, this writes _up to_ 32 bytes to 
a device, to a designated register that is specified through the
Comm byte. The amount of data is specified in the Count byte.
```
If the data parameter remains as a `[]byte` then it should error if its passed more than 32 bytes.
The new `WriteBlockI2CData` that I'm suggesting has no max limit, but would instead write all the data out in 32 byte chunks automatically.

I would agree that the signature or `WriteBlockData` should not change. But nor should we delete/depreciate it in favour of just a `Read`/`Write` pair.

@erkkah one difference I have with the PiGlow is that its a write only device. You can't read the values of registers from the IC itself. 

In terms of knowing which function to use. I've just checked the [PiGlow's datasheet](https://github.com/pimoroni/piglow/blob/master/datasheets/sn3218-datasheet.pdf) and it doesn't say anything about writing to the SMBus in  `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA` vs. `I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA` mode. To paraphrase the data-sheet it just says "write bytes to this address to get things to happen". So from the data-sheet alone I'd have no way to know which one of `WriteBlockData` or `WriteBlockI2CData` to call. I'd just have to try both and find which one works.

Having thought about this again is not ideal. It makes me question my suggestion of a new `WriteBlockI2CData` method in the first place.

But I don't see a way to avoid it. The functions act differently in relation to chunking - as per the spec.

The only other option that I see, would be to replace the implementation of `WriteBlockData` (and maybe all the `WriteXXXX` methods) with simple call the the underlying `Write`. @deadprogram is this in effect way you are saying? But then do you error if you are passed more than 32 bytes? I'm not sure you can...

Is the flip-side of this decision that we'd be using userland access to the i2c device. Rather than off loading the work to the kernel side driver as the native SMBus ioctl's would do?

I am not sure there are any easy or clear cut decisions on this, other than that we can't break existing code that is out in the wild.

Owen

[2017-02-25T19:58:58Z | owenwaller | comment]
@erkkah Thinking about this for 2 seconds more :).

Why don't you try the reverse of what I did. In your TSL2561 code, swap all of your `ReadXXX` calls for `Read` and similarly swap all of the `WriteXXX` calls for `Write`.

Does your device still work? Do you need to care if you write (or Read?) form the SMBus in `I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA` or `I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA`?

Owen

@owenwaller, the layer in `drivers/i2c` does two things, first it adds support for i2c on platforms that do not have sysfs, currently the firmata has it's own implementation. Second, it makes it possible to support several different i2c buses at the same time in a consistent manner.

In the sysfs case, it acts as a proxy on top of `sysfs/i2c_device.go`, so you are right that the interfaces are duplicated.

The general idea of the chosen set of methods is to make it easy to follow datasheets and preexisting example code. WriteBlockData happens to be part of the SMBus lingo, and is always limited to 32 bytes. For a pure SMBus device, it is not possible to use `Write()` with bigger blocks.

The challenge with implementing `ReadBlockData()` using `Read()` is to write the register/command byte to the device before reading. Some devices will accept setting the register/command by a single byte write before reading. If that is not accepted, `Read()` will always start from register 0, so even if you want to read from regs 5 to 15 you would have to read the first 5 and throw away the result.

Because of this, I think it is safe to leave `ReadBlockData()` out.

title: Humidity is disabled in the BME280 I2C driver because of a missing write operation
body:
Calling the `Humidity()` function on the `BME280Driver` I2C driver results in the error: "Humidity disabled".

This is because the `initHumidity()` function is incomplete; it writes out the humidity data acquisition options, but doesn't then write to the "ctrl_meas" register, as per Section 5.4.3 of the BME280 data sheet:

> The “ctrl_hum” register sets the humidity data acquisition options of the device. Changes to
> this register only become effective after a write operation to “ctrl_meas”.

I have a patch so can generate a pull request if someone else can confirm that this is the case! I have tested this on a Raspberry Pi Model B using the Sparkfun BME280 Atmospheric Sensor Breakout with gobot 1.5.0 and golang 1.7.5.

title: Bulk device operations throw an error even if all individual devices are processed successfully
body:
Device bulk operations, such as apiClient.deleteMultipleDevices() will throw an "com.ibm.iotf.client.IoTFCReSTException: Some devices deleted successfully" exception when the status code is 202 even if all of the devices were processed succesfully.
See: https://docs.internetofthings.ibmcloud.com/apis/swagger/v0002/org-admin.html#!/Device_Bulk_Configuration

`
[
  {
    "typeId": "string",
    "deviceId": "string",
    "success": true
  }
]
`

To work around this, I've had to catch the exception, check for status code of 202, parse the result and check each "success" property.
I think the client API should take care of this instead of leaving it to the user.

title: Client needs to be able to set connection and read timeouts
body: While investigating a load test hang, I noticed we stopped getting data from the JMeter test when we did a restart on the load balancer.   We debugged the problem and found that the JAVA API Client hangs and never returns if it sent a request and it looses the connection while waiting for the reply.   I looked at the Java API Client code but we could not find any way to set a timeout.   We believe this hang can be resolved if we were able to set a connection timeout and a read timeout in this client.
comments:
[2018-10-31T15:02:53Z | miketran78727 | comment]
In many asynchronous calls (connect, disconnect, publish, subscribe), the client library is currently using `waitForCompletion()` without specifying a timeout value.   Therefore, the calling thread will block and may not return to the caller.

The fix is to add a new global property named `"ActionTimeout"`, in milliseconds which can be set by the application when instantiating the IoT client objects.  If the `"ActionTimeout"` property is not specified, the default timeout is 30 seconds.

Also new methods with a `timeout` parameter will be added for publishing/subscribing events and command.

title: Connect timeout problems
body:
https://github.com/ibm-watson-iot/iot-java/blob/e1a2f9184fe28829ba69f67230b2cdc13ba2a693/src/main/java/com/ibm/wiotp/sdk/AbstractClient.java#L117

We need to fix the timeout handling on connect:

```
MqttConnectOptions options = config.getMqttConnectOptions();
mqttAsyncClient.connect(options).waitForCompletion(DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT);
```

`DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT` is 5 seconds (and is fine for publishes/subscribes etc) ... but is also being used for the connect, which can take more than 5s in some network conditions.

In https://github.com/ibm-watson-iot/iot-java/blob/e1a2f9184fe28829ba69f67230b2cdc13ba2a693/src/main/java/com/ibm/wiotp/sdk/device/config/DeviceConfig.java#L91 (and similar config classes) we set the connection timeout in paho to 60 seconds.

Let's set the timeout we use on this wait to slightly longer than the paho timeout -- 80 seconds, so that the wait does not timeout while paho is still trying to connect, and will only fire if something has gone wrong and paho hasn't itself timed out and returned by the time it should have done so.

While we're at it, let's also increase public static final long `DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT` to 10 seconds, if network is going heroicly slow it's better to cater to this, there's no real benefit to giving up 5 seconds earlier.

I looked into that, here is what I found:

You can set the name characteristic, but this has to happen before you pair with iOS:
```python
# This must happen before pairing:
acc = Accessory.create("MyAcc", pincode=b"203-23-999")
s = loader.get_serv_loader().get("TemperatureSensor")
s.add_opt_characteristic(loader.get_char_loader().get("Name"))

# OK, the service will show as Foo when paired
```

However, changing the name after that doesn't work and this is a bug in HAP-python. This is because iOS doesn't know it has new values to read. The way to notify about this, is to change the [config version](pyhap/accessory.py#L121) of the accessory - something I have not implemented yet.

Fortunately, this is not hard to fix and will do so in a few days. Until then, you can workaround this by doing:
```python
# acc is your Accessory.
# driver is the AccessoryDriver that manages acc (as in main.py)
# Change name
acc.get_service("TemperatureSensor").get_characteristic("Name").set_value("new name", False)
# Bump config version
acc.config_version += 1
# Update mDNS information so that iOS clients know they have to re-fetch acc info.
driver.update_advertisment()
# Persist the new config_version (see issue #11)
driver.persist()
```

Thanks for uncovering this, I will try to make it easier to change such optional chars (i.e. without the workaround). Note that for some optional characteristics, like StatusLowBatter, iOS listens for updates, so the workaround is not needed.

title: Enforce value constraints in Characteristic. Distinguish raw and HAP value.
body:
Currently, Characteristic only respects min/max value constraints when sending its state through the `to_HAP` method. However, when a value change is published to iOS clients (`notify`), the sent value could be outside of min/max range. There should be a distinction between actual char value and it's "hap" representation, .e.g:
```python
char = Characteristic(...)
char.value  # raw value
char.get_value()  # hapified value
char.set_value(value, ...)
# ^ should be equivalent to
if value not in self.allowed_values: raise ....
self.value = value
```

import time

class Timer(object):
    def __init__(self, timeout, target_function, target_f_kwargs):

        self.time_count_precision = timeout/10

                self.semaphore.release()

                continue

            self.time_lapsed += self.time_count_precision
            self.mutex.release()

    CLOSED = 1

        kwargs = {'value': LOCK_STATE.CLOSED}

        self.target = self.get_service("LockMechanism").get_characteristic("LockTargetState")
        self.target.set_value(LOCK_STATE.CLOSED)

    def set_state(self, value):
        self.current.set_value(value)
        #self.target.set_value(value, should_callback=False)  <<< now I need this because the timer

    def lock_target_callback(self, value):
        if value == LOCK_STATE.OPEN:
            print("OPEN")
            self.timer.start()
        else:
            print("CLOSED")
            self.timer.cancel()

when the timer ends the `lock_target_callback` is executed with close value, but the target remains unmodified because it wasn't triggered by the phone app, so that was the reason I wanted to update the `LockTargetState` value. 

Although it's quite straight forward solving my problem: calling a different function when the timer ends and updating the values there (`current` and `target`), I'm still confused why I can't force the `target` update. I know that the `target` value was already set by the phone trigger, but if I want to set it again (probably with the same value), why it's not possible?
I don't know if I'm expressing myself correctly. Thanks in advance.

[2018-02-20T21:55:36Z | ikalchev | comment]
What follows is a guess, but I am very confident this is exactly what happens:

## Background
When iOS connects to an Accessory, it doesn't close the connection (socket) - it keeps it alive and doesn't say when it leaves (makes sense, because phones move, go to sleep, etc.). It is the accessory's responsibility to "expect" a dead connection.

So using this keep-alive connection, the accessory can send an event, which is what happens when you call `set_value(value, should_notify=True)`. But because the connection could be stale, HAP-python sets a timeout of 3 seconds for the send and if it doesn't happen, it shuts down the connection. After the send the timeout is removed.

On the same connection, iOS can decide to make a HTTP request, such as "set this value to this accessory" and waits for a reply to that request.
## The problem
When I set the timeout to None (i.e. no timeout) instead of 3 seconds, the problem vanishes completely. So I think there is some race condition in which the timeout is not removed properly, which causes a timeout in the thread that makes the request reply. What is more, I think that even if you use the "working" solution of ElectronicLock I posted earlier, there is a chance that it will also timeout.

Thanks for focusing my attention on this - I will try to address this ASAP.

title: WiFi Reconnect Issues
body:
I've had to power of/ on my thermostat a couple of times in the last 3 months as it has dropped off the network and never reconnects (MQTT messages stop working/ there is no assigned DHCP lease etc). I suspect my automated AP firmware update causes the wireless to disconnect, but the thermostat simply never reconnects and is the only IOT device (of about 30) that doesn't. No SoftAP etc, it's just offline.

The thermostat itself works, in that the relay is triggered at target temperature and the target temperature can be adjusted.

Not sure if it matters but I tend to run with webServer set to false.

Is there any way to increase logging/ send serial logs to MQTT or another source? 

Has anyone else experience issues such as this?
comments:
[2019-11-14T21:08:34Z | cclein | comment]
This just happened to me two days ago.

[2019-11-15T06:34:04Z | klausahrenberg | comment]
Yes it's correct. Reconnection doesnt work well until yo restart the device - which is quite difficult by a wall-mounted device :-) I will fix it in a future version.

[2019-12-11T08:23:18Z | klausahrenberg | comment]
Could you please install version 0.97 and test again? Reconnection should be possible now.

[2019-12-12T02:53:37Z | klausahrenberg | comment]
New version 0.98 with several bug fixes. Please take attention to following: 
- After update all settings must be reconfigured
- MQTT topics has changed completely between v0.95 and later, see Readme.md for new json structure

I have two BHT-002-GCLW. One of them has the 99a the other one is the 99b FW on it. Both of them are loosing the wifi connection within 15 minutes after I restarted them, and never reconnect. The older one had the 95 on it before, there was never problem with it. Will I need to downgrade to have a stable wifi connection, or is there any solution for this? Cheers

Try 0.99c. Connection was lost and did not reconnect. Hope, it's solved, I'm on testing now and it looks good so far. This issue is tracked here: https://github.com/klausahrenberg/WThermostatBeca/issues/57

title: Sync service, endpoint, pods behind service to all nodes  is very inefficient and unnecessary
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Thanks!-->


**What happened**:
We need sync service and pods behind it to node for service discovery and loadbalance in edgemesh, we don't know which node needs which services, so we sync service and pods behind it to all nodes. This is very inefficient and unnecessary

**What you expected to happen**:
Sync service and pods behind it to nodes that really needs the service

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Design defect

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- KubeEdge version: v1.0.0
- Hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Others:
comments:
[2019-08-10T16:49:46Z | anyushun | comment]
How to resolve it?
### Precondition
1. EdgeController create CRD NodeService(means **Node** that needs access to the **Service**)
```
type NodeServiceSpec struct {
    Node   string
    Service string
}
```

### Query service and pods behind it
1. EdgeMesh query service and pods behind it from edgecontroller when client pod access a domain name like ```{name}.{namespace}.svc.{cluster}```
2. EdgeController create NodeService when receive query service or pods behind service
3. Response to EdgeMesh
    1. Service and pods behind it when found, meatamanager save it
    2. NotFound type message when not found, metamanager do not save it

**_note: In order to prevent malicious attacks, traffic control needs to be considered in the product version._**

### Sync service and pods behind it
1. EdgeController watch NodeService and cache as 
```
sync.Map{
    "service.namespace/service.name": []string{"node.name"},
}
```
2. Controller watch service and endpoint. Get all nodes from cache and then sync service and pods behind it to these nodes

[2019-08-10T16:50:45Z | anyushun | comment]
@qizha Please take a look if this can be done.

[2019-08-10T17:30:34Z | sids-b | comment]
There maybe some problems with this approach, I had discussed with @qizha earlier,

1) If a node is offline, it will not be able to resolve the request.
2) Multiple query to cloud for resolving a single service(Since metaManager does not save the metadata). There will always be a need for edge node to query the cloud as the node doesn't know the latest endpoints/pod behind the service. This may increase a lot of traffic.

[2019-08-11T13:49:03Z | anyushun | comment]
Hi Sid, I updated the comment and didn't describe it clearly last time.

> 3. Response to EdgeMesh
    1. Service and pods behind it when found, meatamanager save it
    2. NotFound type message when not found, metamanager do not save it

Your questions:
1. MetaManager send query message to cloud when not found in local storage. If node is offline, There are two situations, no matter what kind of situation, it is the same as the current performance:
    1. Service and pods behind it not found in local storage, query message can not be sent to cloud, DNS resolve with failure
    2. Service and pods behind it can found in local storage(maybe the old version), use the old service and pods behind it
2. EdgeController create NodeService when first query come. EdgeController watch NodeService and cache node <-> service map in memory. On the other hand, EdgeController watch service and endpoint, sync service and pods behind it when service and endpoint changed, this will stay up to date

[2019-09-11T06:38:11Z | sids-b | comment]
@anyushun as per our offline discussion, If the node becomes offline before querying any service. The calls will always fail. Closing this issue for now. Please reopen for further discussion.

Successful installation of KubeEdge

keadm init --kubeedge-version=1.1.0

This is mainly failing because when kubeedge-v1.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz is extracted with "tar -C /etc/kubeedge  -xvzf kubeedge-v1.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz" it creates a folder name "kubeedge-v1.1.0-linux-amd64" rather than "kubeedge" (which was previously in version 0.3)

**CloudSide Environment**:
Ubuntu 18.04 LTS

To Fix: (I might be wrong)

Either the zip file should be created that it creates a folder Kubeedge (as previously done in Kubeedge version 0.3) (Better and faster fix) or Keadm source file needs to be modified.

title: Treat master as a edge node

**What happened**:
There is an error in the log:
`ERROR channelq/channelq.go:101 rChannel for edge node family-nc02u is removed`
As @sids-b mentioned in slack:

Give a edge role to edgenode and do not treat a node with master role as a edge node. In this way, we can do some management to edge node particular especially when there is one K8S master managing node located on both cloud and edge.

title: If edge core didn't handle pod delete event from cloud, pod remains with status Terminating
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Thanks!-->


**What happened**:

Pod (running at edge) remain with status Terminating.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3324663/54588464-0a32e680-4a5e-11e9-899f-6da4c0f02e2e.png)

For temporary go over this problem, I have to delete meta entry of the pod in edge.db and delete the pod object in etcd manully.

**What you expected to happen**:

Pod should be deleted.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Deploy pod to edge, after pod up and running, kill edge core, delete the pod, again start the edge core.

Then the pod we intend to delete get never deleted, ramains with status Terminating.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

The downstream controller (response for trigger event to edge side) just try to notice edge once, and if failed did nothing but log an error.

https://github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/blob/6878d86b9ec33ca716933575b93ef70663504ba5/cloud/edgecontroller/pkg/controller/controller/downstream.go#L51-L67

**Environment**:
- KubeEdge version: v0.2
- Hardware configuration: irrelevant
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): irrelevant
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): irrelevant
- Others: irrelevant
comments:
[2019-03-19T08:16:20Z | sids-b | comment]
cc @Baoqiang-Zhang

[2019-03-19T09:05:44Z | Baoqiang-Zhang | comment]
There are no message cache in edgecontroller&cloudhub right now, maybe we can add cache to send message reliable.

[2019-03-19T09:13:52Z | tedli | comment]
I don't think cache at controller side is a good idea. If controller be killed or downed for some reasons, the cache also gone. (and cache makes it hard to further deploying controller with multi replicas)

I think we may group pods by nodes, and sync this pods to each node, and edge side could determine which pod should exist which should be deleted.

[2019-03-19T10:59:28Z | tedli | comment]
I found that metamanager periodically sync pod status from cloud. But only unmarshaling message content to `interface{}`, didn't check fields of the pod status object (the interface{}).

So I think we can add some conditions here to work out this case:

https://github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/blob/6878d86b9ec33ca716933575b93ef70663504ba5/edge/pkg/metamanager/msg_processor.go#L328-L339

If no disagreements, I'm glad to fix this issue.

[2019-03-19T11:05:50Z | m1093782566 | comment]
@tedli 

I am happy to see the PR.

[2019-03-19T12:39:37Z | sids-b | comment]
@tedli Please go ahead and fix this issue :) We are very open to contributions from community.

[2019-03-20T12:25:58Z | tedli | comment]
I'm working on this issue, I plan to handle this by adding some condition in cloud controller, at where controller handles pod statuses syncing from meta manager, then cloud side could list pods using k8s client, and filter out which pod should be delete and still exist at edge side, by filtering out these pods, cloud can trigger delete event again, to let edge delete the pod.

But, it depends on #268, the #268 should be fixed first.

[2019-03-20T16:08:06Z | CindyXing | comment]
I echo what Tedli called out about the issue by adding a cache. 
@tedli, please go ahead and share the PR. I commented #268. 

Yes, we had thought about "I think we may group pods by nodes, and sync this pods to each node, and edge side could determine which pod should exist which should be deleted.". Would love to hear more of your thoughts.

[2019-03-26T03:55:09Z | tedli | comment]
Whether to implement a cache or other mechanisms to solve this issue, a way of event ACK is needed. Also because of all the actions were taken in an async way, a situation that edge side is handling the event just didn't response to cloud in time, the cloud may think that edge side didn't get the event handled at all, so cloud side may resend the event. If so, should edge just ignore the duplicated event or response something to cloud to indicate event is duplicated (the previous event the not duplicated one should response in the normal way)

[2019-03-26T04:11:06Z | CindyXing | comment]
Considering edge can connect/disconnect, I think we can't (can't easily) prevent duplicate event sent from cloud. Rather we should make sure customers' intention/events are sent reliably from cloud to edge. 

We probably need to evaluate what kinds of events sent from cloud to edge; whether there is any side effect for edgecore to process the event twice. 

So far we are sending deployment actions from cloud to edge. It seems benign for edgecore to process the event twice. Let me know if you think differently.

[2019-06-24T10:05:51Z | rohitsardesai83 | comment]
@tedli , what can we do about this issue ?

[2019-06-24T10:21:34Z | tedli | comment]
@rohitsardesai83 
My solution of syncing all pods every time edge connect to cloud indeed lacks of consideration, and according to the discussion above, I agree with introducing cache mechanism. However by doing so things turns complicated. I think it should be considered at  architecture level of edge-cloud communication. It's a big topic at code level. (AFAIK edgecontroller cannot run with replicas to achieve HA for now on)
CC @shouhong @nkwangleiGIT

[2019-07-21T14:01:30Z | sids-b | comment]
@tedli , I think this issue can be fixed with #725 ?

[2019-07-22T01:03:50Z | tedli | comment]
Glad to know the progress about this. I will close this issue, and #725 take this over.

Moving the docs to the website repository will open up two possibilities.  
1. Documentation can be displayed on the website itself.  
2. Documentation can be displayed as it is currently being done, using readthedocs.  

If we go with option 1 then developers will have to follow the markdown and shortcodes that are required for the website.   
If we go with option 2 they can continue doing what they are doing but need to make sure they follow the contribution guides and style guides for readthedocs.  
Either way, if we continue using the Readme files to have all the information we need to make sure we update the relevant sections in the documentation pages.   
There are some parts which are duplicated. We have to decide which parts can be removed from the Readme files.  
There will be some overhead on developers to make sure documentation is done properly.  
With the current process we will end up having to make a lot of fixes after merging new PR'S.  
I recommend having two reviewers for documentation PR's. One technical writer/developer who can verify the contents and one person who can verify the document style guides and contribution guides are being followed.

[2019-04-22T03:57:11Z | anvithks | comment]
@kevin-wangzefeng This is not a bug. This is how readthedocs works. It generates html pages from our md files. The link to the md files is available in the "Edit this document is Github" link at the top right corner.

If we want to edit the files, readthedocs provides a link on every page at the top which says "Edit on Github". This opens the doc in the Github markdown editor.

title: edgecontroller panics when there is no configuration for cloudhub.ca, cloudhub.cert, cloudhub.key.
body:
**What happened**:
edgecontroller crashes with missing configuration for cloudhub.ca, cloudhub.cert, cloudhub.key.

**What you expected to happen**:
Exit gracefully with missing configuration information.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Remove configuration for
  ca: /tmp/rootCA.crt
  cert: /tmp/edge.crt

title: Supports automatic deletion of edge containers if their pods do not exist in the cloud.
body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

Supports automatic deletion of edge containers if their pods do not exist in the cloud.

**Why is this needed**:

When we delete pods in the cloud, if the network is disconnected, the containers on the edge will not be deleted.This will lead to inconsistencies between the cloud and the edge, even if the network is connected.That will create a series of problems, such as the inability to  update the services in the cloud before logging in  edge nodes to remove the old containers.

So I think it's necessary to support the ability to automatically delete edge containers when pod not found in the cloud.

the code in github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/cloud/edgecontroller/pkg/controller/controller

```GO
func (uc *UpstreamController) updatePodStatus(stop chan struct{}) {

			switch msg.GetOperation() {

					}
					if err != nil {
						log.LOGGER.Warnf("message: %s, pod is nil, namespace: %s, name: %s, error: %s", msg.GetID(), namespace, podStatus.Name, err)
						continue
					}
          
          //……
}

title: race condition @ DTContext.Lock / DTContext.Unlock
body:
**What happened**:
We have a potential race @ locking / unlocking the device mutex. (https://github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/blob/0ddc4b3f7752fb527c73bec4d5d2adbe5f3635f2/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontext/dtcontext.go#L107-L128)

EXAMPLE CASE:
- 2 messages from the same device
- start handling first message
  - run dtc.Lock('xyz')
      - success on dtc.Mutex.Lock()
      - success on deviceMutex.Lock()
      - success on dtc.Mutex.Unlock()
- start handling second message
   - run dtc.Lock('xyz')
      - success on dtc.Mutex.Lock()
      - bounded waiting on deviceMutex.Lock() # beause the first message has this mutex
- continue handling first message
  - run dtc.Unlock('xyz')
     - bounded waiting on dtc.Mutex.Unlock() # because the second message has the mutex

**What you expected to happen**:
no race condition

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
not relevant
comments:
[2019-06-03T10:06:32Z | m1093782566 | comment]
Oh, nice catch! @subpathdev

[2019-06-03T11:24:28Z | subpathdev | comment]
Do we really need dtc.Mutex.Lock() / dtc.Mutex.Unlock() in this context?

[2019-06-03T19:01:44Z | sids-b | comment]
Thats a nice catch @subpathdev . The lock function is called once at the beginning of the deviceTwin module in a synchronous for loop.
https://github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/blob/be4d5e34012d41246919296ee378c1834b9ec097/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontroller.go#L185-L204

The SyncDeviceFromSqlite then calls the lock function. 

The main reason for dtc.Mutex.Lock is to guard against race condition in case of dealMembershipDetail from cloud. Cloud sends an array of added, removed devices. So dealMembershipDetail function calls these function to get a lock on full context so that twin or device functions don't read/modify the device state at that time.
https://github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/blob/be4d5e34012d41246919296ee378c1834b9ec097/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontext/dtcontext.go#L131-L138

So we need dtc.Mutex.Lock()

[2019-06-03T19:16:16Z | sids-b | comment]
But yess, the lock function can cause a deadlock as it can be called for same devices for 2 different messages as explained by you. But I think removing dtc.Mutex.Lock won't be a correct solution.

[2019-06-03T19:32:15Z | sids-b | comment]
I was thinking a solution could be removing dtc.Mutex.Lock() only from the Unlock function. Would it be a correct solution though ?
cc @m1093782566 @rohitsardesai83 @subpathdev

[2019-06-03T21:13:34Z | subpathdev | comment]
The actual state doesn't provide the described functionality in all states. Here is an example of what can go wrong:

we receive a message of a device:
-> lock dtc.Mutex
-> lock device mutex
-> unlock dtc.Mutex

now running dealMembershipDetail
-> lock dtc.Mutex

at this point we can modify the device twin without locking the dtc.Mutex.
( I hate race conditions )

I think we should lock the device in the functions and not the list of all devices. (critical sections should be as small as possible)

[2019-06-03T21:23:07Z | sids-b | comment]
@subpathdev , I think there is one more step here

now running dealMembershipDetail
-> lock dtc.Mutex
-> lock deviceMutex

We may get stuck in a deadlock here as device message has not yet unlocked dtc.Mutex is in lock state.

How about make dtc.Mutex a RWMutex. We can use readlock in Lock and Unlock functions and then not have deadlock. Thoughts ?

[2019-06-04T05:56:57Z | subpathdev | comment]
Yes I think that is the right way. Thank you @sids-b .

[2019-06-04T09:46:19Z | subpathdev | comment]
I would use the lock dtc.Mutex in the dtc.Lock function and unlock it in the dtc.Unlock() function. (like the commit above) Thoughts?

The cloud and edge should connect normally and edge node should come to ready state

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Build cloudcore and edgecore images using the docker file provided
2. Register the node with API server using node.json
3. Attach the certificates and config files as volumes and deploy the cloud core
4. Create a node port service to connect to cloud core.
5. Attach the certificates and config files as volumes and deploy edge core

Cloud core and edge core pods come to running state but node does not come to ready state

I see that the previous code was marshalling the incoming message and sending and i see that in the current implementation we are sending the message without marshalling, maybe this is causing a problem in unmarshalling in device twin membership ?

[2019-07-11T15:45:29Z | shouhong | comment]
@sujithsimon22 Previously the WebSocket and Quic prototols have different WriteData() function implementions. The WebSocket implementation directly uses WebSocket interface and Quic implementation uses unified Viaduct interface. So we selected Quic implementation as the unified one for both protocols. 

I have two doubts for the above guess:
1. If the problem lies here, it means this feature does not work for Quic protocol from the beginning. Is this true?
2. In WriteData(), it marshalled the whole Message struct. But UnmarshalDeviceTwinUpdate() only unmarshalled Message.Content part. This does not match.

[2019-07-12T02:39:44Z | jwzl | comment]
@sujithsimon22  Indeed, WriteData() finally call websocket send(), and  this method will translator.NewTran().Encode(rawData, msg)  to encode the msg, and reciver sides will call translator.NewTran().Decode(rawData, msg) to Decode the messge.  that is , message in websocket  layer should be okay.

In cloud sides, msg.content dosen't decode the msg.content,  but in edge side, devicetwin call    UnmarshalDeviceTwinUpdate() to encode the msg.content,  then device twin print the err msg:
"Unmarshal update request body failed, Please check the request"

[2019-07-12T04:27:16Z | sujithsimon22 | comment]

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35599628/61102545-e9b6ee00-a48b-11e9-9ca5-b74ec9c7fbf5.png)

[2019-07-12T08:53:17Z | jwzl | comment]
@sujithsimon22   Finally, I found this problem is that : we call the json.Marshal(message.Msg.Content)  in github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontroller.go: 
func classifyMsg(message *dttype.DTMessage) bool {
![classifyMsg](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10529845/61117803-5d91d000-a465-11e9-9417-336a2c1676cc.png)      

**But ,  this call will cause the error** since the msg.content  has been Marshaled in github.com/kubeedge/viaduct/pkg/translator/message.go when the msg send:
![encode](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10529845/61117620-e2c8b500-a464-11e9-8e8a-5e6c1d47e9d3.png)
![topro](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10529845/61117626-e65c3c00-a464-11e9-84f5-9ea33d6d3b3b.png)

the msg.content will be Marshalled when send from cloud.
**But, msg.content will not be unMarshalled when recieved from edge sides**, let's show you:
![decode](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10529845/61117720-228f9c80-a465-11e9-8510-bfe23b4b7281.png)
![proto](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10529845/61117725-26232380-a465-11e9-9134-8cd5b23c3049.png)

This is not be unmarshaled since protoMessage.content is a type of []byte.
So, the viaduct will not  unmarshal  the msg.content,  So recall the  json.Marshal(message.Msg.Content)  in github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontroller.go will cause this problem.

We should mask all  json.Marshal() in  github.com/kubeedge/kubeedge/edge/pkg/devicetwin/dtcontroller.go: classifyMsg().

title: Bugfix: modify the default kube qps value for edgecontroller
body:
Signed-off-by: Su Xiaolin <linxxnil@126.com>

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Set the default burst to 200, which is twice the value of default kube QPS(100)
‘’‘The rate limiter allows bursts of up to 'burst' to exceed the QPS, while still maintaining a smoothed qps rate of 'qps'.‘’‘
When the request suddenly becomes larger than the QPS，set the burst largger than QPS，the rate limiter will allow request exceed the QPS which can reduced request latency
comments:
[2019-12-30T06:18:50Z | kadisi | review_comment]
could you please explain why it was changed to 5 ?

[2019-12-30T06:26:05Z | kuramal | review_comment]
The qps should less than the burst. The rate limiter allows bursts of up to 'burst' to exceed the QPS, while still maintaining a smoothed qps rate of 'qps'.
In keeping with [client-go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1e7c07ac4ea28587551c1e766b16d1eeb834185f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/config.go#L44).

[2019-12-30T08:12:33Z | kevin-wangzefeng | comment]
For a bugfix, you would need to:
1. describe the bug, how to repro, and what kind of effect it causes
2. how the fix is implemented and why

[2019-12-30T08:16:30Z | kevin-wangzefeng | review_comment]
EdgeController is an aggregation of shadow management for pods, nodes, configmaps etc. at edge. The default value 5 in k8s client-go is for a single client e.g. kubectl, which is quite different with EdgeController load here.

[2019-12-30T08:17:48Z | kevin-wangzefeng | review_comment]
Would recommand increase burst instea.
And it would be even better if you can provide test result comparison between before and after.

title: fix cloudpart cannot run in container
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Currently the kubeedge cloud part image can not be running in container.
Firstly it is because the cloud part is refering to some device types definition in the edge codes.
when we build the cloud part image, the edge part codes will be invovled into the cloud part image.
The sqlite is required for edge but not for cloud.
currently becase of some edge device types are referred by cloud part
so that the cloud part image will require sqlite.
we need to let the common device type definition into the common folder.

Another reason is about the deployment yamls like the modified files in this pr.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: #396

comments:
[2019-04-30T10:17:51Z | rohitsardesai83 | comment]
@trilokgm , can you please resolve the conflicts ?

[2019-04-30T17:00:15Z | rohitsardesai83 | comment]
@trilokgm , the beehive core has a graceful shutdown method which does modules cleanup. When we call os.Exit(1), this would trigger the graceful shutdown right ? is this happening now ?

[2019-04-30T17:00:37Z | rohitsardesai83 | review:APPROVED]
lgtm

[2019-04-30T20:17:11Z | trilokgm | comment]
> @trilokgm , the beehive core has a graceful shutdown method which does modules cleanup. When we call os.Exit(1), this would trigger the graceful shutdown right ? is this happening now ?

Beehive captures os signals and makes call which end up in context cleanup. The goroutines are not stopped in graceful shutdown call.

os.Exit(1) does not send any signal to invoke graceful shutdown execution flow. The program exits with an error code, here it is 1. There is no panic or stack trace generated.

I had given a thought about using uniform error codes, had to drop the idea due to significant usage of go routines without error notification.Due to this, there is not much significance seen for using error codes for now.

[2019-04-30T20:48:10Z | CindyXing | review:APPROVED]
This is great change! Thanks Trilok. 

Can you create a readme for this code patter to ensure we follow it in any future development? 
We should also scrutinize existing code and see whether we are doing it.

[2019-04-30T20:51:29Z | CindyXing | review_comment]
The benefit of panic is the exception callstack. Here we log error in the module start where the error is clear. So log the error and exit is fine.

title: fix bug #866
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
1. When edge node disconnecting from edgecontroller, the edgecontroller does not aware this until the next keepalive message is not received from the edge node. 
2. The edge node connection information is not cleaned up until the edgecontroller aware the edge node is not alive.
3. If the edge node connect to edgecontroller again before the previous obsolete connection information was cleaned up, it will get an error.
4. To fix this problem, add retry mechanism to wait for the previous obsolete connection information to be cleanup.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #866

Can we not have something similar in viaduct as well ? I remember that in previous implementation it didn't need to wait for keepalive interval to remove the connection. Any thoughts ? @sids-b 1. In previous implementation, there is a "EventReadLoop" function in which there is loop to **actively** read data from edge node (the timeout value is keepalive interval). In this example, the server side register a callback function named "handleServer" to **passively** read data from client side. body:
Right now the URI validator we have created works both for one URI (String) and a list of URIs (Array). To make the validator complete you must be able to set an optional parameter to set the fact that the field can accept URIs or an URI.

Something like this should work.
`validates list: uri: {array: true}   # accept list of uris`

This is needed because if later on we want to make a check on the URI to extract something we could have some errors and it would be better to find it before. If we do not have this validation option we could send an array of URIs where only one can be accepted and have unexpected errors.

title: Values of zero are being omitted
body: **(Semi) BUG REPORT** Noticed this when the value field wasn't being written out onto a kafka topic. This may be more of an issue with what protoc generates but I believe Mainflux should account for this. So I wanted to just make sure you all were aware it. 1. What were you trying to achieve? Sending a message where the value is zero. 2. What are the expected results? That the `value` field does not get omitted and contains a value of zero when the message that is sent contains 0. 3. What are the received results? The value field gets omitted and is non-existent rather than zero 4. What are the steps to reproduce the issue? The way I found easiest to visualize this, was through subscribing to the NATS channel where the normalized messages are written to (out.senml for example) and then decoding the messages. - Sub to out.senml and capture the output. - Send a message containing a zero for the value for example: ``` [ { "bn":"MVP-mikes-fridge-sensor:", "bt":1537822790, "bu":"degC", "bver":5, "n":"Temperature", "u":"degC", "v":0 } ] ``` - Decode that output using protoc and although a value was sent, it does not appear What I am seeing when I do this: 5. In what environment did you encounter the issue? Kubernetes 6. Additional information you deem important: I believe that a Zero value should be valid and not get omitted anywhere in Mainflux. Since things like refrigerators/freezers can send temperatures that are 0. The issue probably truly lies in protoc/go since protoc generates message.pg.go: ``` type Message struct { ... Value float64 `protobuf:"fixed64,6,opt,name=Value,proto3" json:"Value,omitempty"` ... } ``` Due to a combination of omitempty getting added and zero being considered empty in go, the `Value` field does not get populated. Let me know thoughts about this!

Current `device` model (https://github.com/Mainflux/mainflux-lite/blob/master/models/device.go, https://github.com/Mainflux/mainflux-lite/blob/master/models/deviceTemplate.json) has no reference to `channel`s created for this device - only `channel` holds the referenced device `Device` ID: https://github.com/Mainflux/mainflux-lite/blob/master/models/channel.go, https://github.com/Mainflux/mainflux-lite/blob/master/models/channelTemplate.json

`channel` is accessed as `localhost:7070/devices/<device_id>/channels/<channel_id>`. When DELETE is issued on this URI, channel will be deleted. However - when DELETE is issued on `localhost:7070/devices/<device_id>` only device will be deleted, but not the channels that belog to this device - and we will not be able to access them anymore (since we will not have ID of the device anymore).

Do we have to keep list of `channels` in `device` struct? Xively holds the array `channels` inside `device`: http://developer.xively.com/assets/Xively_QS_TimeSeries.pdf. Not sure how M2X does it, but it is worh looking: https://m2x.att.com/developer/documentation/v2/device

title: Correct usage of docker persistent volumes
body:
As I was working on #636 I've noticed that some volumes are generated when executing `docker-compose`.

I've dug a bit deeper and I've found out that we're already using volumes for the users-db, things-db, mainflux-redis, mainflux-things-redis, bootstrap, influxdb-writer, cassandra-writer, mongodb-writer containers, but we delete them with `make cleandocker` and `make cleanghost`.

Here is the test procedure:

1. start from clear state

```
$ make cleandocker

$ docker volume ls
DRIVER              VOLUME NAME
```

2. start Mainflux
```
$	docker-compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d (equivalent to make run)
```
3. the state with the volumes afterwards:
```
$ docker volume ls
DRIVER              VOLUME NAME
local               18f49a276e35cc4ad115ecefd638a1b594538b7abe117d4abb2ee9ce60700231
local               264a2c95f31d7d51291ef9cca2294d017d51c5961e421a2e35797ee070505172
local               c2442c40d8dca66ae9f96ff5c438417d6a12f19f56b3f03501d3b3a129b41c3d
local               d5886127963d2728dd2d3e7b31c4f4ad66ffa135550c2fce633ab0f342177832
```

4. find the containers to which these volumes belong to: `docker ps --filter=volume=<VOLUME_NAME>`
```
$ docker ps --filter=volume=18f49a276e35cc4ad115ecefd638a1b594538b7abe117d4abb2ee9ce60700231 --filter=volume=264a2c95f31d7d51291ef9cca2294d017d51c5961e421a2e35797ee070505172 --filter=volume=c2442c40d8dca66ae9f96ff5c438417d6a12f19f56b3f03501d3b3a129b41c3d --filter=volume=d5886127963d2728dd2d3e7b31c4f4ad66ffa135550c2fce633ab0f342177832
CONTAINER ID        IMAGE                  COMMAND                  CREATED             STATUS              PORTS               NAMES
0e0dd71e5174        postgres:10.2-alpine   "docker-entrypoint.s…"   19 minutes ago      Up 19 minutes       5432/tcp            mainflux-things-db
039b13ffd155        redis:4.0.9-alpine     "docker-entrypoint.s…"   19 minutes ago      Up 19 minutes       6379/tcp            mainflux-redis
2e4188a46327        postgres:10.2-alpine   "docker-entrypoint.s…"   19 minutes ago      Up 19 minutes       5432/tcp            mainflux-users-db
bdde4c8e5f25        redis:5.0-alpine       "docker-entrypoint.s…"   19 minutes ago      Up 19 minutes       6379/tcp            mainflux-things-redis
```

5. The existence of the volumes can be easily confirmed by checking the Dockerfiles from which the docker hub images are build:

* Postgres 10.2-alpine  [Dockerfile](https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/blob/master/10/alpine/Dockerfile#L145)
* Redis 5.0-alpine [Dockerfile](https://github.com/docker-library/redis/blob/60db7082c81f5d457046f199244c5d651f04b3fa/5.0/alpine/Dockerfile#L60)
* Redis 4.0.9-alpine  [Dockerfile](https://github.com/docker-library/redis/blob/8e1acc18156603cc3643bf22ced6069cf8be1622/4.0/alpine/Dockerfile#L60)
* Cassandra [Dockerfile](https://github.com/docker-library/cassandra/blob/064fb4e2682bf9c1909e4cb27225fa74862c9086/3.11/Dockerfile#L156)
* InfluxDB [Dockerfile](https://github.com/influxdata/influxdata-docker/blob/d76a6a184dec6a82978964882641a743adb76989/influxdb/1.6/alpine/Dockerfile#L31)
* MongoDB [Dockerfile](https://github.com/docker-library/mongo/blob/7276b14c1e9b5f83b37f5f452e6a9f293aea2d8b/3.6/Dockerfile#L90)
* Grafana [recommended setup](http://docs.grafana.org/installation/docker/#grafana-container-with-persistent-storage-recommended)




6. cleaning up the docker containers
```
make cleandocker
```
this make task calls the `cleanghost` task which contains a `docker volume ls -f dangling=true -q | xargs -r docker volume rm` commands which deletes all the dangling volumes. __The problem is that it deletes all__ dangling volumes, volumes not connected to any container. IMHO this is totally wrong. We should only delete the containers which we have created and not all of the dangling containers which means we might delete some oder important data from other containers. The __second problem__ is that the deletion of the dangling containers happens before the Mainflux containers are stopped and removed so we leave some "garbage" behind. If a new composition is executed there will be 8 volumes which are created by us. The volumes from ther previous composition are deleted on the second run of `cleandocker` or `cleanghost`
In fact, the whole `cleanghost` target does not check if the containers, images or volumes are created by us or not, but it simply deletes them all.

__The solution__ for this problem would be to use names for the volumes so that we can filter them easier, clearly show which volumes were created by us and delete only these volumes and add filters to all of the `cleanghost` commands. We should also add a switch which will tell if the volumes should be deleted or not. The default behavior should be the same as now, when the switch is not present the `cleandocker` and `cleanghost` make task should delete the volumes.

Also, having proper names for the volumes makes it straightforward to backup and restore them without too much hassle and playing around with to many docker commands ;)

Although this is more an enhancement, I've marked it as as bug as well, as we delete all exited contaniers and unused images instead of deleting only the things that we have created

title: Runtime error in normalizer - CBOR SenML
body:
Publishing SenML/CBOR topic looking like `[{0: "TST", 4: true}]`  in CBOR diagnostic notation (`81 a2 00 63 54 53 54 04 f5`) causes runtime error in normalizer.
Fix me, but I am sure that the message conforms [RFC 8428](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8428).  
```bash
mainflux-mqtt   | {"level":30,"time":1573140521695,"msg":"published","pid":1,"hostname":"34e546c4ae1a","client":{"id":"GlobalClient"},"message":{"topic":"channels/1531a2f3-5a2a-4404-a168-cad5ea289d4c/messages/ct/application_senml-cbor","qos":0,"retain":false},"v":1}
mainflux-normalizer | {"level":"warn","message":"Method normalize took 46.934µs to complete with error: cbor decode error [pos 3]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0.","ts":"2019-11-07T15:28:41.695720118Z"}
```

On the other hand  the message encoded as
```bash
[{"n": "TST", "vb": true}]
81         # array(1)
A2         # map(2)
61         # text(1)
6E         # "n"
63         # text(3)
545354     #"TST"
62         # text(2)
7662       # "vb"
F5         # primitive(21)
```
is processed fine.
Seems there is RFC 8428 violation bug in https://github.com/cisco/senml + https://github.com/ugorji/go . See  "RFC 8428 (August 2018) Jennings, et al. Standards Track [Page 19]"

1. Run 'python -m ensurepip' before checking pip. (still will fail if the ensurepip module is also disabled). 
2. Just run the [get-pip.py](https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py) directly.

title: Update IoT Hub installer such that it works for users who only have resource group-level access
body:
The IoT development kit includes tasks that are added to Visual Studio Code that will deploy an IoT Hub into Azure. If the user you use to connect into Azure while following these tasks only has resource group-level access (i.e. no subscription access), the deployment will fail unnecessarily because it will attempt to register the Microsoft.Devices resource provider even if it is already registered in the subscription, in the context of a user who only has resource group-level access.

The root issue lies on line 21 of task-iothub.js. Instead of lazily assuming you are a subscription admin and forcing the registration of the Microsoft.Devices resource provider, the logic should check to see if the Microsoft.Devices resource provider is already registered or not before attempting to register the resource provider. This approach allows a subscription admin to register the Microsoft.Devices resource provider so that other users who do not have that level of access can successfully deploy IoT Hubs into the resource groups where they have access.

To fix this, replace this line (line 21):

```javascript
_context.next = 7;return azurecli.exec('provider register -n "Microsoft.Devices"');case 7:
```

With the following lines:

```javascript
_context.next = 5;return (azurecli.execResultJson('provider show -n "Microsoft.Devices"')); case 5:
devicesProvider = _context.sent;_context.next = 7;if (devicesProvider.registrationState === 'NotRegistered') {
    console.log('Registering resource provider "Microsoft.Devices" in subscription ' + context.subscription);
    return azurecli.exec('provider register -n "Microsoft.Devices"')};break;case 7:
```

I would have made these changes in a PR myself, but @ArthurMa1978 informed me on Gitter that the task part of the device SDK is not open source at the moment and requested I log the issue here so that it can be addressed in the new VS Code extension that is coming soon. I already made these changes locally and it seems to work just fine using a user who only has contributor access to a single resource group in Azure, with no subscription-level permissions at all.

title: Graceful handling of titles for complex action/event declarations
body:
Declaration of non-simple actions/events is a particularly onerous task that could be alleviated if some simple safe defaults can be presumed.

Currently, this (legitimate) declaration...

``` python
local_event_MyEvent = LocalEvent({'schema': {'type': 'object', 'properties': {
        'myProperty1': {'type': 'string'},
        'myProperty2': {'type': 'string'}}}})

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5266533/19210062/e6efe8e4-8d63-11e6-9556-3e044655cec3.png)

The "undefined" bug aside, normally, without any explicit title-overrides, the UI generates graceful versions using event/action names e.g. **MyEvent** is used as a title despite it not explicity being declared via `... = LocalEvent({'title': 'My Special Event', 'schema': {'type': ...```

In the same way,  it should treat the above example like this:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5266533/19210077/3e3c1ac8-8d64-11e6-8758-08f250343ead.png)

or for a cleaner look, this:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5266533/19210082/588e452c-8d64-11e6-88f5-44ee0aa2fc80.png)

or this space-conscious version which is especially great when several array elements are involved:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5266533/19210220/d6f48892-8d67-11e6-88a1-435b15220a40.png)

The equivalent (onerous) code being:

``` python
local_event_MyEvent2 = LocalEvent({'schema': {'type': 'object', 'title': 'Properties', 'properties': {
        'myProperty1': {'title': 'myProperty1', 'type': 'string'},
        'myProperty2': {'title': 'myProperty2', 'type': 'string'}}}})
```

this:

``` python
local_event_MyEvent3 = LocalEvent({'schema': {'type': 'object', 'title': '...', 'properties': {
        'myProperty1': {'title': 'myProperty1', 'type': 'string'},
        'myProperty2': {'title': 'myProperty2', 'type': 'string'}}}})
```

and this:

``` python
local_event_MyEvent3 = LocalEvent({'schema': {'type': 'object', 'title': '', 'properties': {
        'myProperty1': {'title': 'myProperty1', 'type': 'string'},
        'myProperty2': {'title': 'myProperty2', 'type': 'string'}}}})
```

title: Toolkit-timer: 'delay' parameter is not respected after first use and in stopped state
body:
The toolkit Timer uses *firstDelay* and *interval* parameters to control the timer behaviour. If the timer is stopped and the delay is ever re-set using **setDelay** or **setDelayAndInterval** methods, only the *interval* part is respected when the timer is restarted.

Note, that when the timer is in a running state, the methods correctly behave as expected (both are respected).

Correct behaviour would be for both parameters to be respected whether in a running or stopped state, with *firstDelay* reset every time a **setDelay___** function is used.

==> notification.operationName  [in template "unknown" at line 5, column 18]

----
Tip: It's the step after the last dot that caused this error, not those before it.
----
Tip: If the failing expression is known to be legally refer to something that's sometimes null or missing, either specify a default value like myOptionalVar!myDefault, or use <#if myOptionalVar??>when-present<#else>when-missing. (These only cover the last step of the expression; to cover the whole expression, use parenthesis: (myOptionalVar.foo)!myDefault, (myOptionalVar.foo)??
----

----
FTL stack trace ("~" means nesting-related):
	- Failed at: ${notification.operationName}  [in template "unknown" at line 5, column 16]
----

title: Activate command for nRF24L01 toggles plus features
body:
According to the nRF24L01 datasheet (non-plus!) the ACTIVATE command toggles advanced features each time it is called:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7716005/43391165-3c7073b2-93f0-11e8-888b-27b83612b5c6.png)

We must make sure the radio is in a default state, with ACTIVATE features switched off before executing the ACTIVATE command.
Currently, the RF24_enableFeatures() call (which executes the ACTIVATE command) is called from setup with the radio in Standby-I mode:
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/development/drivers/RF24/RF24.cpp#L506

It is likely that the radio has to be brought to PowerDown mode, or even power cycled to get to a defined ACTIVATE state.

I don't have non-plus radios available. Can someone verify if current implementation toggles the  advanced feature availibility?
