title: Hardware ACKs cannot be enabled per packet
body:
EN_DYN_ACK shall be set in the FEATURE regsiter to enable the W_TX_PAYLOAD_NOACK command.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7716005/43395256-b8029fca-93fd-11e8-902b-c521cac699d0.png)

This command is used to disable hardware ACKs on a per packet basis:
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/development/drivers/RF24/RF24.cpp#L314
comments:
[2018-08-22T16:35:42Z | Yveaux | comment]
After discussion with @tekka007 we decided to keep the DYN_ACKs disabled, as some clones have the ACK bit reverted wrt genuine nRF24s. In a network which contains all nRF24s with identical ACK bit behavior the function could be enabled, but for a normal user it is impossible to determine the ACK behavior of its radios.
Closing issue.

The MySensors code referred to is misleading as it contains an option to disable hardware ACKs on a per packet basis, which doesn't work.
Submitted as a separate issue #1187.

title: Echo and EchoRequest bits are swapped in MyMessage
body:
In master bit 3 of byte 4 represents "Ack request" and bit 4 (is) "Ack":
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/f4fd69eb131cd5df5572bc9018d3aa2245020123/core/MyMessage.h#L253
In development the Ack function has been renamed to Echo (#1103).
Apparently the bit assignment has also changed, to bit 4 of byte 4 represents "EchoReq" and bit 3 (is) "Echo":
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/ad6c483bef122571b5f3d98448f10fdcac9291e6/core/MyMessage.h#L52

Now I don't receive an echo anymore. In the previous version I used this was what was shown on the log:

title: [Security] Nodes should always indicate signing preference
body: If a node that used to require signing is reconfigured to not support signing at all, it does not send a I_REQUEST_SIGNING to let the GW update the requirement table. Only by letting the node support signing but not require it and present it will the GW table be properly updated.
comments: no_comments_in_source

title: [Security] signing bypass flaw
body: Messages with ACK-bit enabled bypass signing verification.
comments:
[2015-12-12T13:26:02Z | fallberg | comment]
Intended behaviour in the context that acks are not supposed to be signed but it was erroneously assumed that acks were simply sent to the caller without further processing. 
The fix for this will be to require acks to be signed (if the receiver of the ACK require this).

[2015-12-12T16:26:00Z | tekka007 | comment]
Signing ACK is not a bad idea, however, it won't necessarily solve the issue here. The fixes are (1) to not process ACK messages in the library and (2) verify ACK-bit in the callback function before further processing (see SecureActuator sketch). 
We should eventually consider a different way of ACKing a message, i.e. via a designated I_type + full hash of the original message. Let's have a chat about that.

title: pinIntTrigger should be made volatile
body:
in MyHwATMega328.c, pinIntTrigger is not declared volatile : this makes the internalSleep function sleep more than expected.

Expected result : when an interrupt happens, the sleep() function should return true immediately
Actual result : the sleep function returns true (correct value), but only once the full time has elapsed

By setting internalSleep volatile, the behaviour is as expected.

Current behaviour might depends on compiler options.

(sorry for not providing a patch, I think it is quite straightforward!)

title: presentNode is not called on gateway with only local sensors
body:
On gateway with only local sensors, without `MY_RADIO_FEATURE`, `presentNode` is not called. This breaks the API specification and controllers will have a hard time registering the local sensors if the parent node is missing.

Bug reported from user of home assistant controller in pymysensors repo:
https://github.com/theolind/pymysensors/issues/51

and in the forum:
https://forum.mysensors.org/topic/4276/converting-a-sketch-from-1-5-x-to-2-0-x/2

The relevant parts of the code:
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/986389b12591917ecbc44021c63a2cdf6f8c8222/MySensors.h#L56-L58

https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/986389b12591917ecbc44021c63a2cdf6f8c8222/core/MySensorsCore.cpp#L152-L154

https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/934ccf30b205afad2086c908a367c4205ce580cd/core/MySensorsCore.cpp#L181-L190

https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/934ccf30b205afad2086c908a367c4205ce580cd/core/MySensorsCore.cpp#L325-L329

A temporary workaround is to call `present` with child id 255 directly in the sketch in `setup`:

```
void setup() {
  // Present node as repeater node.
  present(255, 18);
}
```

My suggestion is to move the check for `MY_RADIO_FEATURE` to somewhere here:
https://github.com/mysensors/MySensors/blob/934ccf30b205afad2086c908a367c4205ce580cd/core/MySensorsCore.cpp#L192-L213

I don't know exactly what calls in that section needs a radio, so if someone can advise or hint where to look, I can push a PR more quickly.

title: AVR: Pin interrupt may not get detached after calling hwSleep
body:
When calling the hwSleep() variant taking 1 or 2 pin interrupts, the pin interrupt(s) are not detached on return in the following cases:
1. Wake by timeout: no interrupt(s) detached
2. Wake by pin interrupt: in case hwSleep is called with 2 pin interrupts, the interrupt that didn't occur does not get detached.

A pin interrupt that did not get detached will be detached the next time it occurs.

title: AVR might sleep with interrupts disabled
body:
See potential issue here: http://playground.arduino.cc/Learning/ArduinoSleepCode

MySensors interrupt handlers for sleep (wakeUp1() & wakeUp2()) should disable sleep, by adding a call to sleep_disable()

title: AVR might wake from pending external interrupt
body:
Pending external interrupts are not cleared when attaching an interrupt handler.
This might cause an AVR to immediately wake up again when going to sleep, without an interrupt actually triggering the wake.
Ref: https://forum.arduino.cc/index.php?topic=59217.0
comments: no_comments_in_source

title: AVR Sleep times deviate from watchdog timer
body:
For sleep times <= 125ms the breakdown into individual watchdog timeout intervals is wrong.
This might cause deviation of actual sleep time from requested sleep time.

title: Fixing the code for use of: MY_USE_UDP & MY_CONTROLLER_IP_ADDRESS
body:
Things was working in version 2.0.0 then someone re-wrote line 178 of MyGatewayTransportEthernet.cpp removing
`#if defined(MY_CONTROLLER_IP_ADDRESS) ` // version 2.0.0
and adding
`#if defined(MY_GATEWAY_CLIENT_MODE)` // version 2.1.1

Now the Gateway won't send the UDP data to the Controller.
To fix it you have to replace line 178 from MY_GATEWAY_CLIENT_MODE to MY_CONTROLLER_IP_ADDRESS like in version 2.0.0

Regarding to MY_USE_UDP please also see fix: #817 
I think I'm the only one using ESP8266 and UDP.

title: Receive corrupted ID when using multiple repeaters.
body:
Hello,

I recently installed a mysensors network in a large building on two floors. Since I have placed several repeaters, I find random problems during the associations of sensors.


## Description of the problem :

During the association, **randomly**, the sensor receives an ID longer than the 3 characters of range 0-255 normally expected.

These are often numbers 255 or 100 placed after the ID, other numbers appear or changes the ID itself, but this is more rare.

I suspect that repeaters "overwrite" the value by repeating at the same time the payload. (not sure).

The fewer repeaters in the bridge area, the less problems are manifested. (no problem without repeaters).

In the example below, the good ID sent by the gateway is 197, the sensor receives 197255 and takes ID 135 after conversion:
197255 = b110000001010000111, converted to uint8, only the last 8 bits on the right (b010000111) are retrieved, giving 135.

### For information, here is the topology of the network setup:

![img_0931](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4836635/30483613-c7ca5586-9a27-11e7-846d-1b4640149b0c.jpg)


## Proposed amendment to the code:

I have not yet figured out the exact origin of the problem, however it seems to me it would be a good idea that the protocol is resistant to this ID corruption:

In the transportAssignNodeID function of MyTransport.cpp, the test:
```
// verify if ID valid
if (newNodeId! = GATEWAY_ADDRESS && newNodeId <= AUTO) {
```
Replacing "! =" With "<=" is not enough because the conversion to uint8 returns a pseudo-random number when the ID is greater than 255;

Change to uint32 type rather than uint8 works but is not optimized and could result many side-effects.

I propose this modification based on the length of the message which has the advantage of not touching the statement of the function:

### Before:
```
bool transportAssignNodeID(const uint8_t newNodeId)
{
	// verify if ID valid
	if (newNodeId != GATEWAY_ADDRESS && newNodeId != AUTO) {
		_transportConfig.nodeId = newNodeId;
		transportSetAddress(newNodeId);
		// Write ID to EEPROM
		hwWriteConfig(EEPROM_NODE_ID_ADDRESS, newNodeId);
		TRANSPORT_DEBUG(PSTR("TSF:SID:OK,ID=%d\n"),newNodeId);	// Node ID assigned
		return true;
	} else {
		TRANSPORT_DEBUG(PSTR("!TSF:SID:FAIL,ID=%d\n"),newNodeId);	// ID is invalid, cannot assign ID
		setIndication(INDICATION_ERR_NET_FULL);
		_transportConfig.nodeId = AUTO;
		return false;
	}
}
```

### After:
```
bool transportAssignNodeID(const uint8_t newNodeId)
{
	// verify if ID corrupted
	if(mGetLength(_msg) <= 3) {
		// verify if ID valid
		if (newNodeId != GATEWAY_ADDRESS && newNodeId <= AUTO) {
			_transportConfig.nodeId = newNodeId;
			transportSetAddress(newNodeId);
			// Write ID to EEPROM
			hwWriteConfig(EEPROM_NODE_ID_ADDRESS, newNodeId);
			TRANSPORT_DEBUG(PSTR("TSF:SID:OK,ID=%d\n"),newNodeId);	// Node ID assigned
			return true;
		}
		TRANSPORT_DEBUG(PSTR("!TSF:SID:FAIL,ID=%d\n"),newNodeId);	// ID is invalid, cannot assign ID
	} else {
		TRANSPORT_DEBUG(PSTR("!TSF:SID:FAIL,CORRUPT\n"),newNodeId);	// ID is corrupted, cannot assign ID
	}
	setIndication(INDICATION_ERR_NET_FULL);
	_transportConfig.nodeId = AUTO;
	return false;
}
```

[2017-09-18T13:32:11Z | graham-hanson | comment]
Hi @user2684,

You can enable compiler warnings in the Arduino IDE in File, Preferences - set Compiler Warnings to All.

You should fix the two "return-statement with no value" warnings - in these cases, the functions will return an undefined value (what the C++ standard calls "undefined behaviour" - meaning that you may sometimes get the expected effect but you may get a different effect each time you call the function and that includes sometime crashing the program completely!)

The problem with the line

    if (_sensors[sensor_index] != 0) _sensors[sensor_index] == 0;

which was originally just 

    _sensors[sensor_index] == 0;

is that it should simply be 

    _sensors[sensor_index] = nullptr; // Reset the pointer

i.e., an assignment rather than an equality test - very common mistake but it indicates the importance of using the highest level of warnings from the compiler!
(Note C++11 prefers use of the nullptr literal to zero as it can only be assigned to a pointer variable and is self documenting.)

Regards
Graham (also graham86 on MySensors forum)

Just a question. Those "deprecated" warnings, where referring to "(int)myvar" style casts? Because if true, those are C-style casts, being osed on cpp files, and they're old, but completely supported (and btw used by everyone). I also get those warnings in my IDE, but can be safely ignored.

[2017-10-02T08:06:31Z | graham-hanson | comment]
Hi Sergio,
The deprecated conversion warnings are because the code is assigning a string constant - `""` to a `char *` variable.
The problem is that a string constant has type `const char[]` so assigning to `char *` looses the `const`. (And also because the code could then attempt to write to the constant string, which, probably doesn't have enough space, may be shared with other pieces of code and may be in Read Only memory)
 
In this case, as all the member variables (3 of them from memory) causing this warning are assigned pointers to strings that are never updated, the variables should be declared as e.g.,

    const char * _value_string = "";

(To clarify, the strings assigned to the variables are never updated through the variable, but pointers to different strings are assigned to the variables.)

I have never come across as case where the compiler generates a warning for simply using a C-style cast in a C++ program instead of the C++ equivalent cast.  GCC will warning about certain conversions such as using `(char*)` to remove the constness from a `const char*`,  because it is dangerous.
The use of C-Style casts in a C++ program are not recommended as they, as in the example above, override some of the C++ language protections and result in "dangerous" code.

Finally, it is considered bad practice to ignore compiler warnings, even if .  Best practice is considered to be to compile with the highest warning level available and to "fix" all warnings.  In fact, the preferred method is to enable the compiler "Warnings are Errors" option (-Werror for the gcc compiler used for Arduino).  In practice, it can be difficult or impossible to remove all warnings, in particular because some my be generated by library code. However, the aim should be to reduce the number of warnings as far as possible, and for warnings in your "own" code to be reduced to zero.

title: For sensors creating multiple child IDs allow invoking their functions just once
body: Issue described here: #176
comments:
[2017-08-08T20:06:56Z | SergioRius | comment]
If you see this as an issue, I would understand the problem as an architectural issue. The structure clearly started as something simple, node-sensor. But now we must do more complex things.
Well I think the classes should be modified to allow better hierarchical organisation and iteration.
NodeManager is the root container. Should include a collection of "Sensors" what already does. But it mixes sensors and child. Collection nodes should be accessed like this:

`nodeManager.get(sensor).get(child)`

At some point, you would also want to access and modify base class elements, like settings. Then you will need a differentiation like this:

`nodeManager.Settings.LoopDelay = value`

And then:

`nodeManager.Sensors.Add(SENSOR_EXAMPLE, myOption)`
`nodeManager.Sensors(x).setType(V_ONETYPE)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child(y).setSamples(5)`

And you also can have defaults and/or apply properties to all child or first child. This makes it coherent and expandable.

`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child.First.setSamples(5)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child.All.setSamples(5)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).setSamples(5) //All could be default`
`ForEach s in nodeManager.Sensors {...`

[2017-08-09T07:50:26Z | user2684 | comment]
You are 100% right, all of this is due to a mix of sensors and children which is causing all of this confusion. I think the approach you have proposed is the best possible, with an additional contained in between. I'll try to draft something as v1.7 development will start so we can check together if the direction is the right one.
Thanks again for sharing this thought!

[2017-08-20T17:06:28Z | betonmoewe | comment]
Maybe it would be a good idea, to have one instance of one specific sensor class with all the variables and parameters wich are global for all the different measurements (childs) of this sensor. And there is an array of pointers/IDs of all the child instances (for each measurement) of this sensor. The setter methods are either  looping through this array or are called for only some of the childs.
I think, this could be a way without changing too much code ...
Best regards
Betonmoewe

[2017-09-16T16:56:09Z | user2684 | comment]
Hi guys, thanks for the feedback so far. This issue is number 1 priority for v1.7 and I think must be addressed before adding other sensors or fixing other issues before would have an overall impact. The thing is we need to 1) define a new hierarchy 2) redefine the terminology.

Up to v1.6 we have an array of pointers to instances of Sensor and subclasses. When registering a sensor providing more than one measure (e.g. temperature and humidity), registerSensor() creates two instances of the same class and registers two child IDs by adding two pointers to the array.
Requirements are:
- registerSensor() must be called once to avoid the user to take care of registering multiple measures
- each measure must be associated to a different child id since must be presented independently 
- user must be able to invoke methods for each child id of a sensor
- user must be able to invoke methods which apply to all child ids of a sensor

Let's start from Sergio's idea which I think should cover all those requirements. I struggle a bit to understand the relationship between Child and Sensor. Also, that .first. and .All., is it from a specific C++ object or it is just pseudo-code? Thanks!

[2017-09-16T19:16:00Z | SergioRius | comment]
That was some pseudo-C# code, but it could work on cpp. First, I would try if we can use vectors for storage (there's a small library for arduino). They allow add and remove elements, but I dunno if they are feasible on low perf boards.

We must also think on allow a function callback for "sensor" action. Then we could make virtual "physical sensors" or electronics that are **not directly related to a pin for actuating**, like a shift register.

[2017-09-30T14:48:55Z | user2684 | comment]
Hi guys, I spent some time thinking about this architectural thing and get lost pretty quickly :(
Let's assume we have a Sensor class containing one or more Child. 
registerSensor() will create an instance of something derived from Sensor which will create in its constructor the required Child. The good thing is registerSensor() will be cleaner since objects that need to be shared among the Child will be created in Sensor and not in registerSensor(). Child will be created by passing a reference to Sensor I guess. 
Then comes the time to understand if the existing functions of Sensors need to stay there or moved into Child. Theoretically almost all must go into Child but the following:
```
    void setPin(int value);
      void setPowerPins(int ground_pin, int vcc_pin, int wait_time = 50);
      void setAutoPowerPins(bool value);
      void powerOn();
      void powerOff();
```
However if we want to apply the same setting to all the Child belonging to the sensor we need to replicate ALL the other functions which will cycle through the Child and invoke the methods. This scares me since we are already almost out of storage and this will make the code much longer, complex and resources intensive but providing little value. 
An alternative could be a set of static function which I don't like much. 
Any good alternative?
Thanks

[2017-10-01T09:56:54Z | SergioRius | comment]
You must think in what elements are properties from the sensor and what are tools from the framework.
Usually, only properties should be part of the objects. As you don't want to replicate them for every object. As a start, you should pass objects to methods of NodeManager class for doing actions.

[2017-10-01T09:59:31Z | SergioRius | comment]
If you want, we can talk through chat on this and perhaps do some work together. Just drop me a line when you will get on to this.

[2017-10-01T13:54:22Z | user2684 | comment]
Ok, let me try to follow your line of thinking. Despite almost all the properties can be child-specific, this is going against the need to 1) make it simple 2) do not use additional storage. So let's assume to keep to the very minimum the child-specific properties. What properties MUST be child-specific? This is the list:
* child_id
* presentation
* type
* description
* value_type

This can be the minimum set of information a Child class can have.  So let's assume a Sensor will have a data structure with those properties for each Child. This may somehow solve the problem (and creating a few others which I cannot see right now) because 1) would avoid invoking the same methods on all the child (because those parameters will be attached to Sensor and not to child) 2) would save additional space since for sensors with multiple child a single instance of the Sensor class would be created and not many.
How does it look like?

[2017-10-01T17:27:40Z | user2684 | comment]
I spent some time thinking about the idea above and doing some initial tests and I think it could work. Each Sensor will have a data structure to store a list of Child with the information reported above. No more the need then to create multiple instances of the class for each child id. There will be one single instance for the sensor containing its child id. In the Sensor's loop(), for each Child onLoop() will be executed. The challenge will be with received() when loop() of a child only needs to be executed but I think we could find the way to make it working. 

This approach could also solve a bunch of other problems: since the logic in registerSensor() is no longer needed (Sensor will create any additional objects in its constructor since all the child belonging to it will be within the instance) we could even simplify the main sketch.
Something like the following would allow the user to set any parameter to the object without the need to get and cast and do all the complex stuff required right now:
```
// declaring the instance directly in the main sketch
SensorAnalogInput analog(A1);
analog.setReportIntervalSeconds(60);
// register with NodeManager
nodeManager.registerSensor(analog);
```
Of course there will be no compatibility with previous version but I can live with it.
Hope to have some sample code to share in a couple of weeks.
Thanks

[2017-10-14T16:54:25Z | user2684 | comment]
Hi, I've done some steps ahead (PR #229) and looking for your feedback.
First of all this is not intended to work yet, just trying to understand if it might be the right way to go based on my thoughts shared in the previous message. 
Have a look at SensorSHT21 which is the only one I started changing. 
The Sensor class has now a list of children in it so registerSensor will register a single instance of SensorSHT21. 
Sensor::loop() has also been changed to iterate across all the children. 
Performance-wise, many things can still be optimized. 
But how does this approach look like to you?

[2017-10-15T17:40:20Z | user2684 | comment]
Another few improvements in PR #229. Both _sensors and _children have been now migrated into a vector-like structure as @SergioRius recommended. 
Sensors' registration has been over simplified. No more the need to register a sensor, something like the following will be enough:
```
// create a NodeManager instance
NodeManager nodeManager;
SensorSHT21 sht(nodeManager);
/ before
void before() {
  // setup the serial port baud rate
  Serial.begin(MY_BAUD_RATE);  
  sht.setReportIntervalSeconds(60);
}
```
The sensor will register itself against NodeManager. No more the need to get and cast either as you can see above. Much more intuitive I hope.
After creation sensors and children can be easily access:
```
nodeManager.sensors.get(0).something()
nodeManager.sensors.get(0).children.get(0).something()
```
The values have been moved into the Child class, however I don't like at all the mess I'm doing declaring a variable for each type (int, float,double,string) and then using only one in Sensor::loop() (same with the previous versions). I'm sure this would help us saving a good amount of storage but fixing this would go way beyond my c++ knowledge.

title: SensorSwitch::onInterrupt() doesn't reliably detect rising/falling edge
body:
The issue is that there is a delay between the interrupt being triggered, and when this line of code executes:

https://github.com/mysensors/NodeManager/blob/4525b56f642d5996035f732a5a383ded59cdb9ed/NodeManagerLibrary.ino#L1549

The delay is typically 2ms if SERVICE_MESSAGES is not enabled, and 200-1500ms if SERVICE_MESSAGES is enabled. 

Say `_mode==FALLING`, and the pin receives a very brief pulse (e.g. a very brief push of a button); by the time this line of code runs the input may have gone high again, so `(_mode == FALLING && value == LOW)` will return false, and the method will interpret this as an invalid value.

My use case is a push button where I want to measure the length of time the button was pressed for. I've created a custom sensor that subclasses SensorSwitch; in the onInterrupt() method I need to be able to reliably tell whether the interrupt was triggered by a FALLING edge (button pushed) or a RISING edge (button released), even if the button was pushed so briefly that the pulse is only a few ms long. 

I believe the only reliable way to detect whether a CHANGE interrupt was triggered by a RISING or FALLING edge is to read the pin as the very first instruction in the ISR (and store it somewhere for later use). 

Apologies if that doesn't make sense (struggling with words today), happy to clarify if needed.

Very good point indeed. I should probably read store the value in the NodeManager's class like we do for _last_interrupt_pin just after the interrupt is triggered. I'll work on it, thanks.
PS. SERVICE_MESSAGES should be gone in the development branch

title: ESP8266 gateway crashes when configuration reply received from child node
body:
I am testing sending a configuration message to a subordinate node of my ESP8266 gateway device to setIsMetric to one and back to zero.  The gateway device handles the message sent to it fine and relays it to the subordinate HyTiny which successfully changes its mode to metric and back as expected.  However when the gateway receives the reply message from the HyTiny board it crashes.  The message the HyTiny sends is:
```
SEND D=0 I=200 C=0 T=48 S= I=0 F=0.00
1240480 TSF:MSG:SEND,102-102-0-0,s=200,c=1,t=48,pt=5,l=4,sg=0,ft=0,st=OK:22
```
When the gateway receives this message it crashes in the call to strtok_r at line or near line 191 at the statement below because at that point the value of the pointer string is zero.

`_child_id = atoi(strtok_r(const_cast<char*>(string), ",", &ptr));`

This is in the function:
```
// contructor, tokenize a request in the format "child_id,function,value"
Request::Request(int recipient_child_id, const char* string) {
```

I'm afraid I don't have much to add at this point, I only just realized the crash was happening on the reply from the HyTiny rather than on the message to the gateway from the controller.

I will look further into the code to try and understand how the reply is getting constructed.

I believe the gateway is improperly treating the reply from the subordinate node as a configuration command to the gateway itself -- I don't know if this is because the reply is incorrectly constructed by the subordinate node or because it is being incorrectly interpreted by the gateway node as a configuration command.

This is for a configuration command of "0,42,0" -- it appears the gateway is properly relaying back out via the MQTT bus.  I'm really not certain about what is happening a this point.

void SensorConfiguration::onReceive(MyMessage* message) {
  // expect a REQ, V_CUSTOM message

title: NodeManager and MySensors openHAB binding: constant reset
body:
Environment:
 * NodeManager installed on Arduino Uno
 * NodeManager configured to be a Serial Gateway
 * NodeManager has enabled **FEATURE_DEBUG** flag
 * Arduino Uno connected to openHAB
 * openHAB has installed MySensors Binding

Result:
 MySensors openHAB Binding constantly reconnects to serial port causing the Arduino Uno to be restarted as well. This looks a bit poor.

This behavior is a side effect of printing to serial port some "bogus" (debug) characters by NodeManager. When NodeManager is configured to be a Serial Gateway, those debug messages doesn't follow the [MySensors Serial API](https://www.mysensors.org/download/serial_api_20).

I think that MySensors openHAB Binding should be resistant to such a bogus messages. I have already reported this issue as tobof/openhab2-addons/issues/116.

Here are the log messages that are printed to serial port by Arduino Uno with NodeManager:
```
NodeManager v1.7
LIB V=2.3.0-alpha R=- E=- T=G A=A S=- B=-
RADIO...0;255;3;0;14;Gateway startup complete.
0;255;0;0;17;2.3.0-alpha
OK
0;255;3;0;11;NodeManager
0;255;3;0;12;1.0
READY 

MY I=0 M=255 
INT P=3 M=255
INT P=2 M=255
```

While I'm good with NodeManager sendings debug messages to serial port, there is only one thing that could be improved in NodeManager. This message looks faulty but it could be easily improved:
```
RADIO...0;255;3;0;14;Gateway startup complete.
```
I believe that a **new line character** is missing after `RADIO...`
comments:
[2018-06-19T11:59:28Z | user2684 | comment]
Thanks for reporting this issue. I believe would be a bit harder to make NodeManager following the MySensors Serial API since the structure of the message is completely different and sometimes it is needed to print out something different than just numbers. Workaround would be to turn FEATURE_DEBUG  OFF, as you have probably already done. 
The newline missing is because NodeManager prints "RADIO..." than after the radio communication has been established, prints out an "OK" so to make radio troubleshooting when the MySensors debug is off easier because the OK never comes if there is any communication issue. Makes sense?

[2018-06-22T20:26:51Z | wmarkow | comment]
Thanks, I didn't take a closer look in the source code and I didn't know about that **FEATURE_DEBUG** flag. I have switched it OFF and everything works fine.

Related that radio debug messages: maybe it would be good idea to use `Serial.println` anyway and display debug messages always with newline at the end. In that case it could look like on the example below

```
Checking RADIO...
0;255;3;0;14;Gateway startup complete.
RADIO OK
```

[2018-07-19T19:26:27Z | user2684 | comment]
Fixed by #387 by forcing FEATURE_DEBUG to OFF if MY_GATEWAY_SERIAL is defined.
I've noticed NodeManager's debug for a gateway bring also an additional problem: slow down the communication with the controller, especially at low baud rates, preventing a controller supporting smart sleep to respond timely. Hence disabling debug output for a serial gateway looks like the best option for now

[2018-07-20T08:16:11Z | wmarkow | comment]
Sounds good for now. I can imagine that a lot of debug messages can slow down the communication (and data processing by Arduino), especially at lower baud rates.

title: Issue with FEATURE_CONDITIONAL_REPORT with interrupt
body:
I have a battery powered node with a BH1750 sensor for which I have set conditional reporting as follows:

`light.children.get(1)->setValueDelta(2);
  light.children.get(1)->setForceUpdateMinutes(25);`

Attached to the same node I have a SensorDoor using interrupts. I had a problem when only rising changes were being sent back to the controller. The interrupt would fire and pre-post sleep messages would be sent but the actual payload:0 message would never be sent. If FEATURE_CONDITIONAL_REPORT was disabled it would work properly.

I tracked it down to _min_threshold var being set to FLT_MIN which comes up as 0. This meant the 0 value was being filtered out in the ChildInt::sendValue(bool force) method.
I set this in my node code:
`door.children.get(1)->setMinThreshold(-FLT_MIN);`
This resolves the issue. 
But probably that was not how this function was intended. Aware you are mid-way through a rewrite so maybe this doesn't apply any more but thought I'd point it out anyway as took some tracking down!

title: Display update of SSD1306 broken in latest version
body:
In the latest development version, a SSD1306 display will NOT update its texts. The reason is that in Sensor::loop the check 
    	if (_evaluateTimer(_measure_timer) || message != nullptr) {
will never return true, because the timer is explicitly set not to trigger at all in the OLED display's constructor. So by default, the display will update once (when _first_run == false) and then never again.

Since Sensor::loop is not virtual, I also don't see any chance in a Display object to override the loop behaviour, either.

In previous versions, I could add a Child to cause the check in the loop to evaluate to true. However, this has changed in the latest development version and an existing child no longer forces the onLoop function to be called at all. This makes sense, but it breaks the workaround I had to use to make the OLED update so far.

Any idea how to make the OLED displays update, while not sending data to the gateway for them?
comments:

I believe the "obscure" and not documented way this was supposed to work in my mind when restructuring the code was to have the report timer to off  with `setReportTimerMode(DO_NOT_REPORT) ` (a display should never report back to the gateway otherwise would generate unnecessary traffic) but having the user customizing the refresh interval with the measure timer (by calling `setMeasureTimerMode()` and `setMeasureTimerValue()`) through which the display's `onLoop()` is called. 
Makes sense? (if it does I definitely need to document this better...)

[2018-10-21T14:13:17Z | kainhofer | comment]
Ah, I see. That certainly makes sense. Unfortunately, the logic in Sensor::setup messes up the measure timer for the Display class:
  * Display::Display calls setReportTimerMode(DO_NOT_REPORT)
  * Sensor::setup copies DO_NOT_REPORT to the measure timer, too

Unfortunately, the Sensor::setup function is not virtual, so I don't see any easy way in the Display class to check whether a report interval was explicitly set by the user or implicitly by Sensor::setup...

In my view, the Display class should set the nodeManager's report interval as default for its _measure_timer. Then this issue would be solved.

title: NRF51 implementation has millis() wrap around after ~38 hours, timer no longer triggers
body:
The NRF51 core implementation has a millis() counter that wraps around after ~38 hours. 

Unfortunately, after the wrap-around the main loop is still called, but each sensor's timer will never expire, because in Timer::isOver()
    		if (millis() > _target) return true;
will never match. The _target will be set to a value larger than the wrap-around.

The Timer::isOver function needs to add a detection for millis() wrap around for implementations that do not use the full value range of unsigned long...

title: Dynamic state description broken in snapshot 1693
body:
Dynamic state description is no more working, empty list are rendered by UI.
Default widget which should be a selection is no more working too, text widget is used.
This is probably a consequence of this recently merged PR:
https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/pull/1010

The problem was introduced aftter snapshot 1678.
Coming back to snapshot 1678 until it is fixed.
comments:
[2019-09-21T09:55:42Z | cweitkamp | comment]
Why did you think it is related to #1010?

[2019-09-21T10:03:28Z | lolodomo | comment]
Because the choice of default widget depends on whether the state description is editable or not. It looks like now the state description seems to answer "not editable" while it should return "editable".
https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/master/bundles/org.openhab.core.ui/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/ui/internal/items/ItemUIRegistryImpl.java#L244
https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/master/bundles/org.openhab.core.ui/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/ui/internal/items/ItemUIRegistryImpl.java#L781
And it looks like the only very recent PR that was in relation to "editable".

[2019-09-21T10:07:55Z | lolodomo | comment]
Additionally, I don't know if the editable property is important for the build of dynamic state options but apparently they are no more built correctly.

[2019-09-22T11:39:43Z | cweitkamp | comment]
No, not really. The fix in #1010 addresses a `editable` property of the `EnrichedItemDTO` for the REST endpoint. It states when an item is managed by a `ManagedItemProvider` - meaning can it be removed via REST interface / is it managed via storage or is it configured by the user in a text file. This value is not related to the `readOnly` property of the `StateDescription`.

title: Unable to add Things via text config after they previously removed
body:
I noticed a problem in OpenHAB2.5.0M1 & OpenHAB2.5.0M2.

When commenting out a 'Thing' via a text file and later re-adding that same 'Thing' by removing the comments - the text file gets parsed correctly but the 'Thing' is never created (again).

Just to clarify: This is not an issue with a specific binding (in this case the Astro binding). I just used this for testing purposes because it's a small, stable binding than be installed and configured quickly. This issue also applies to other bindings and their config. 

To reproduce I installed the 'Astro' binding and created a `astro.things ` text file containing the following configuration:

```
Thing astro:sun:home        "VT_Astro_Sun"          @   "Virtual"       [ geolocation="6.524379,3.379206", interval=60 ] 
{
    Channels:
        Type rangeEvent : rise#event [
            offset=0
        ]
        Type rangeEvent : set#event [
            offset=0
        ]        
}
Thing astro:moon:home       "VT_Astro_Moon"         @   "Virtual"       [ geolocation="6.524379,3.379206", interval=60 ]
```

This works as expected and creates two Things in OpenHAB.

Next I comment out the 'VT_Astro_Moon' in the 'Thing' config and it's handler gets disposed and the Thing disappears from OpenHAB as expected.

When I remove the previously added comments to have OpenHAB (re)create the 'VT_Astro_Moon' thing nothing gets created.

I'm not sure if the problem lies with the original Thing not properly getting disposed or with the instantiation of the Thing/ThingHandler when I try to add it again.

I tested this on an OpenHAB build running on Windows 10 as well as within a Docker container on RancherOS. All builds were freshly installed and contained no other bindings or configurations other than what is there by default.

~~I will try to see if I can reproduce this on 2.4.0 and the 2.5.0-SNAPSHOT as well~~

EDIT: I was able to reproduce this behavior in 2.4.0 as well as the latest SNAPSHOT. The only ways around this issue are: 
- To rename the 'thing_id' part of the configuration. (`Thing <binding_id>:<type_id>:<thing_id>`)
  - OR-
- To restart the entire OpenHAB instance

title: [serial] dropdown of choices collapses to first selected port
body:
Currently running S1585, but this may go back to 2.4. I have only observed this using the zigbee and zwave bindings, but there have been reports in the forum where this occurs for other bindings. [Here's one for jeelink and zwave](https://community.openhab.org/t/snapshot-version-of-zwave-cannot-find-serial-port-after-oh-restart/73638/25?u=5iver). 

**To reproduce**
1) install the zwave and zigbee bindings with controllers for each, but don't configure yet
2) observe that the serial port dropdown for both bindings contain all ports
3) configure a port for zwave
4) observe that the serial prort dropdown for the zwave and zigbee bindings now only contain the port that had been selected for the zwave binding
5) after an OH restart, observe all ports are in the dropdown again for both bindings
6) configure a port for zigbee
7) observe the serial port dropdown for both bindings now only contain the port selected for zigbee

Possibly related, I also observe the zigbee binding losing it's serial port connection about once a day. The zigbee binding uses [gnu.io.SerialPort](https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zigbee/blob/master/org.openhab.binding.zigbee/src/main/java/org/openhab/binding/zigbee/handler/ZigBeeSerialPort.java#L28) and zwave uses [org.eclipse.smarthome.io.transport.serial.SerialPort](https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/blob/master/src/main/java/org/openhab/binding/zwave/handler/ZWaveSerialHandler.java#L22). So, possibly a conflict in using the different transports?

More details can be found here (see issue 2)... https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/issues/1165. 

Note: After manually installing the bindings, the dropdowns have disappeared completely and allow free-text entries for the port. When doing the manual install, I only installed the openhab-core-io-transport-serial and openhab-core-config-discovery-usbserial features to resolve serial dependencies. However, zigbee still looses connection to its port at least once a day.
comments:
[2019-05-08T07:12:24Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> After manually installing the bindings, the dropdowns have disappeared completely and allow free-text entries for the port. When doing the manual install, I only installed the openhab-core-io-transport-serial and openhab-core-config-discovery-usbserial features to resolve serial dependencies.

You need to install `org.openhab.core.config.serial` if you want serial configuration support.
If you want to install the whole serial support you just need to install: [openhab-transport-serial](https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/0168145/features/karaf/openhab-core/src/main/feature/feature.xml#L495)

If you install some `openhab-core-...` features you only install a specific function only.

There are other features that aggregate specific functions to provide a better user experience: https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/0168145/features/karaf/openhab-core/src/main/feature/feature.xml#L403-L503

[2019-05-08T08:10:50Z | 5iver | comment]
Thank you, Markus... that helps a lot! I incorrectly thought that with the zwave binding move to the newer transport that I needed to install those other features, rather than openhab-transport serial. Serial in OH is still an unknown for me.

I just updated to S1587 and I'm back to managed bindings and dropdowns. Shouldn't this be marked as a bug?

[2019-05-08T08:13:30Z | maggu2810 | comment]
> unmanaged bindings and dropdowns

You have written a good explanation of the buggy dropdown behaviour. Yes, I assume it is a bug (at least "somewhere").

What do you mean by unmanaged bindings?
It is related to this topic or is it another issue?

[2019-05-08T08:24:13Z | 5iver | comment]
Typo... managed bindings... as in not manually installed. That may not be the correct way to describe this, but similar to managed/unmanaged Items and Things.

[2019-05-11T13:30:24Z | 5iver | comment]
After reading through some code, especially [SerialPortUtil](https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/master/bundles/org.openhab.core.io.transport.serial.rxtx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/transport/serial/internal/SerialPortUtil.java), on a whim I added my ports into EXTRA_JAVA_OPTS. After a restart, the dropdown shows all ports. So, in reproducing this, be sure not to have any ports in there.

[2019-06-10T21:03:41Z | wborn | comment]
The issue is that `SerialPortUtil` sets the environment variable `gnu.io.rxtx.SerialPorts` to a value when it's not set:

https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/7f5ceefa26ffdf6ea290c9717868814b6318ff13/bundles/org.openhab.core.io.transport.serial.rxtx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/transport/serial/internal/SerialPortUtil.java#L44

After that, whenever nrjavaserial is used to get the serial port identifiers (`CommPortIdentifier.getPortIdentifiers()`), it will only return the ports set in that environment variable (see [nrjavaserial code](https://github.com/NeuronRobotics/nrjavaserial/blob/e06ed10e23284c36d19225b907e0b7a3b2736833/src/main/java/gnu/io/RXTXCommDriver.java#L418-L422)). So maybe it can be fixed by making sure the environment variable is restored to its original value after using it for creating the `SerialPortIdentifierImpl`?

https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/blob/7f5ceefa26ffdf6ea290c9717868814b6318ff13/bundles/org.openhab.core.io.transport.serial.rxtx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/transport/serial/internal/RxTxPortProvider.java#L49-L58

Using `openhab-runtime-base` in every feature has the "advantage" that all the feature repositories (openhab2-addons, webui, ...) are rather useless for non official openHAB distributions.

But I assume you will argue, that the addons are not suspected to be used by others.

The distribution knows every feature repository, so it can consum features from all of them. It is the best place to combine features of different repos.

Right, but it is the "base" feature for the add-ons. I think this was already discussed in the past. title: Be sure to start the serial providers before the bindings using them
body:
It was discovered at least with the Z-Wave binding that at startup, the serial port is unknown by the openHAB serial abstraction. Just restarting the binding later solves the problem (the serial port is correctly identified).

https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/issues/1203

The Z-Wave binding handler factory bundle has a "immediate = true" property but it is not yet sure that it is the cause of the issue.

The current assumption is that the openHAB serial abstraction should be started with a higher priority, meaning with a start level < 80.

WDYT ?
comments:
[2019-07-22T13:36:28Z | maggu2810 | comment]
If the consumer (e.g. a binding binding) depends on a provider (e.g. serial abstraction) the DS implementation (e.g. SCR) already ensures that the dependent service is already been started.

Perhaps a required dependency is missing?

[2019-07-22T13:58:22Z | maggu2810 | comment]
Is it related to #805 / #866?

[2019-07-22T14:53:46Z | lolodomo | comment]
It is relative to openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave#1203 , that is the Z-Wave binding not starting anymore at openHAB startup.
@cdjackson idea is that the startup of the USB driver is not yet completed when the binding is started.

[2019-07-22T15:34:00Z | wborn | comment]
Regardless of whether is this is some OHC regression... it's still a valid use case that a user starts the runtime while the USB Stick used by the Z-Wave Binding is not inserted. The binding itself should be able to recover from this once the serial port is again available. Users might also decide to unplug it while the binding is running and reinsert it at a later time. I specifically tested this use case with the Plugwise Binding. That  binding periodically tries to reconnect to the Stick.

[2019-07-22T15:39:05Z | lolodomo | comment]
Yes, I fully agree and this is something I do with my bindings too (like Powermax for example).

[2019-07-22T15:42:22Z | lolodomo | comment]
But in my use case, the Z-Wave stick is connected to my RPI since a long time when I start openHAB. And the tty is present. So this error should not occur when the binding asks for the port identifier.

[2019-07-22T15:50:37Z | lolodomo | comment]
Just to be sure, when "immediate = true" is set, this does not bypass the first startup of all dependencies before the bundle is started ?

[2019-07-22T16:36:43Z | cdjackson | comment]
> it's still a valid use case that a user starts the runtime while the USB Stick used by the Z-Wave Binding is not inserted.

I guess that's a matter of debate ;)

In any case, this is not something that has ever been supported in the binding, and while I do agree it would be a useful feature, it is not super easy to implement so has not yet been implemented. The expectation has always been that the serial driver is available when the binding starts - and it always has been as it was a direct dependency. Unfortunately that is no longer the case, and we now have this issue I guess.

[2019-07-22T18:41:51Z | maggu2810 | comment]
If the dynamic behavior of OSGi and the presence or absence of serial devices cannot be handled by the Z-Wave binding easily, why not depend on a specific serial implementation and ensure that it is present, up and running?
You just need to add the specific requirements to the manifest...

[2019-07-22T18:59:39Z | cdjackson | comment]
> why not depend on a specific serial implementation

Yep - that's what the binding has always done, but some time back it was requested to move the serial implementation to use the ESH abstraction, so now we have the problem.

It might be possible to simply continue to retry the initial connection. The point I was responding to above was the request to handle removing and re-adding the dongle which is more problematic.

[2019-07-22T20:28:35Z | wborn | comment]

> This continues until a result resource bundle is instantiated or the list of candidate bundle names is exhausted. > If still no result bundle is found, the base name alone is looked up. If this still fails, a MissingResourceException is thrown.

title: Corrected rounding behaviour of decimal values in 1.x compatibility layer

[2014-06-20T08:59:41Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
This is not what I suggested. I said "the setting "ignore ssl certificates" should actually only be taken into account for the remote url".

[2014-06-20T09:02:54Z | belovictor | comment]
Ah. Did you mean that for local URL certificate should always be ignored at all?

[2014-06-20T09:08:14Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Yes!

[2014-06-20T12:12:04Z | belovictor | comment]
Why do you need local SSL at all then?

[2014-06-20T12:22:29Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
See our Skype discussion:

[15/06/14 22:51:47] Kai Kreuzer: Because it is unsecure and my credentials could be read in clear text!
[15/06/14 22:52:19] Kai Kreuzer: (but http is my current workaround of course)
[15/06/14 22:53:14] Victor Belov: insecure in the home network?
[15/06/14 22:55:23] Kai Kreuzer: Yes, you should not treat your intranet to be secure. Any trojan on your PC could potentially take over your openHAB if you use it without any credentials.
[15/06/14 22:56:28] Kai Kreuzer: Any guest that you give access to your wifi just has to install openHAB and gets instantly full access through auto-discovery… (and not everybody has a separate guest-wifi, such as you)

[2014-06-20T12:24:28Z | belovictor | comment]
There is another solution. We can create our own CA, issue certificate for openHAB's local connections and trust it in the client app. I think this would be better, wouldn't it?

[2014-06-20T12:37:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Hm, but this would not be bound to any domain name and the openHAB server certificate would be publicly available on GitHub. So any attacker could use it as well to do man-in-the-middle attacks without the client apps having a chance to notice it. And that's exactly what a certificate check is supposed to prevent, isn't it?

[2014-06-20T13:11:51Z | belovictor | comment]
But would it be worser then self-signed certificate? In your scenario with ignoring certificate validity on the local connection MiM will work fine anyway?

[2014-06-20T13:12:38Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> But would it be worser then self-signed certificate?

No, it will be exactly the same. So why considering it at all?

[2014-06-20T13:13:20Z | belovictor | comment]
Because it doesn't give user an option to ignore any certificates at all.

[2014-06-20T13:15:03Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
!? Of course, if you deactivate the option, all certificates will be ignored (the remote ones through the setting, the local ones always). I don't get your point...

[2014-07-17T17:27:30Z | belovictor | comment]
This is fixed in the upcoming app update - user will now be warned about invalid certificate and will have a choice of either aborting connection, accepting it once or accepting it always. Later, if the app receives a certificate which is different from the one remembered, user will be warned about certificate mismatch and will have a choice to abort, accept it once or accept it always again.

[2019-06-26T13:53:28Z | weakfl | comment]
@timbms I was actually looking into #269, but since charts are more or less images, I had similar problems as described here.

A couple of observations:

There's a race condition in `NewImageUITableViewCell.loadImage()`:

```
DispatchQueue.main.async {
    self?.widget?.image = image
}
self?.layoutIfNeeded()
self?.layoutSubviews()
if self?.delegate != nil {
    self?.delegate?.didLoadImageOf(self)
}
```

The delegate function `self?.delegate?.didLoadImageOf(self)` is called before `self?.widget?.image = image` is set. This triggers a second call of `loadImage()` when `reloadRows(at:with:)` gets called.
What's the reason to set the widget image asynchronously anyway?

Using `beginUpdates()`/`endUpdates()` instead of `reloadRows(at:with:)` fixes some layout issues for me. And since the cell data doesn't change, reloading the row isn't necessary.

There are still issues with rotation though. After rotating from portrait to landscape **and back** to portrait the cell height is wrong. I have no idea why though :/
Of course you could just call `reloadData()` after rotation to work around the issue, but I'd be interested to know what is causing it in the first place.

I'll submit a (WIP) PR for #269 shortly, maybe you have an idea what's causing the rotation issue.

Regarding the slowness, with the switch to Alamofire, a connection pool is used to load content from the openHAB server.  By default this pool is set at 4 connections.  I believe that the AFNetworking version used a connection per request so was able to parallelize the requests more and may have resulted in faster loading in some situations.  

Round-trip latency to the server could play a big part here and a higher connection pool count would likely speed things up.  Since this is just a theory, I'll maybe create a PR which allows the pool size to be configured and then people could experiment with different pool sizes to see what impact it has on load times.

There’s a simple typo in the implementation of `USARTSerial::availableForWrite()`:

``` cpp
int USARTSerial::availableForWrite(void)
{
return HAL_USART_Available_Data(_serial);

int USARTSerial::available(void)
{
return HAL_USART_Available_Data(_serial);
}
```

https://github.com/spark/firmware/blob/develop/wiring/src/spark_wiring_usartserial.cpp#L69

It should probably be `HAL_USART_Available_Data_For_Write`. However, if I fix that and use it with code like:

``` cpp
        Serial.printlnf("%d", Serial1.availableForWrite());
        Serial1.println("01234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789");
        Serial.printlnf("%d", Serial1.availableForWrite());
```

The output is:

```
0
50
```

I’m unclear of how the function is supposed to work. Should it:
1. Return the number of bytes waiting to be written out from the buffer (0=empty send buffer), which is what it does.
2. Return the number of bytes you can write to the buffer without blocking, which would be SERIAL_BUFFER_SIZE - the value currently returned.

Rick

body:
Flashing the electron with the same app over and over again, I observe different application checksums, but they remain consistent between DFU attempts.

    TRACE: application state checksum: 8458b248, expected: 2a92a22f

If I change the app slightly (log message) I see:

If I change the app slightly (add another function key for one of the same functions) I see:

    TRACE: application state checksum: 8458b248, expected: 62fde692

- `DEBUG("application state checksum: %x, expected: %x", actual, app_state_crc);` Note: actual on left, and app_state_crcc on right of logs message.  This seems to contradict the results above when the actual app flashed to the device is changing (notice the left crc value is constant).  Perhaps the logs need to be flipped?  Expected should be what is stored in backup SRAM, and if it is... then the results above are odd.

- This only seems to be the case when `DEBUG_BUILD=y` during compile time.  If `DEBUG_BUILD` is not defined, application checksums appear to match after first reset (via button, DFU same app, etc..)

- This is important because the electron system firmware is compiled by default with `DEBUG_BUILD=y`, and when the application checksum is the same (as is the case when sleeping and waking up), the handshake process can be VERY short which means little data used.  When the application checksum is different, unnecessary data usage is occuring for each re-connection to the cloud.

title: [Electron] Application/System thread not blocking on calls to modem with SYSTEM_THREAD(ENABLED)
body:
SYSTEM_THREAD(ENABLED) is not blocking on calls to the modem, so the application thread doesn't wait for the modem to finish before going to the next instruction in user code.  Thus Cellular.on() and SLEEP_MODE_SOFTPOWEROFF will not work properly with threading enabled currently.

## Example of non working code

SYSTEM_THREAD(ENABLED);

void setup() {
}

void loop() {
  // we need to turn on the modem in SEMI_AUTOMATIC mode first, 
  // so that AT commands can be sent to turn it off
  Cellular.on();
  // system will not wait for power on AT command sequence

  System.sleep(SLEEP_MODE_DEEP, 15); 
  // system will not wait for power off AT command sequence

As a work around you can break out the commands separately and add delays after the commands.   Cellular.on();
  delay(10000); // this can really be up to 20 seconds worst case

  Cellular.command("AT+CPWROFF\r\n");
  delay(2000);

  FuelGauge().sleep();

body:
The device should close it's end of the TCP connection after sending the response data. This doesn't happen for the first connection, but does happen on subsequent connections. 

Expected outcome
```
Given I have photon in listening mode
And the computer's Wi-Fi is connected to the Photon's AP
When I run `echo -e -n "device-id\n0\n\n" | nc 192.168.0.1 5609`
Then the device should output some JSON
And the stream is closed
And When I run `echo -e -n "device-id\n0\n\n" | nc 192.168.0.1 5609` again
Then the device should output some JSON 
And the stream is closed
```

Actual outcome

```
Given I have photon in listening mode
And the computer's Wi-Fi is connected to the Photon's AP
When I run `echo -e -n "device-id\n0\n\n" | nc 192.168.0.1 5609`
Then the device should output some JSON
And the stream remains open
When I press Ctrl-C the command exits
And When I run `echo -e -n "device-id\n0\n\n" | nc 192.168.0.1 5609` again
Then the device should output some JSON
And the stream is closed
```

What happens in practice is the stream from the first command is not closed. Instead, you have to use Ctrl-C to close the stream.  Subsequent invocations of the same command then sees the device correctly close the stream automatically. 

Tested on a Photon, firmware 0.4.9 and 0.6.0

title: Photon/P1 does not always recover from a WiFi channel switch / WiFi.ready() can return true with IP 0.0.0.0
body:
## Bug Report
According to the docs, WiFi.ready() returns true only if the device is connected to WiFi and has a valid IP address. My P1 based board connects to WiFi without problems initially. Then it loses network, and the code I have to restore WiFi is not triggered, because WiFi.ready() stil returns true.

I have narrowed down the cause to WiFi channel switching. Auto channel seems to be the default on many routers, so this affects many setups.

Initially, this bug report was about WiFi.ready() returning 'true' while the IP address was `0.0.0.0`, but this seems to be one of the symptoms of WiFi channel switching not being handled correctly.

### Expected Behavior

#### WiFi.ready()
WiFi.ready() returns true only if the P1 has a valid IP address, as described here:
https://docs.particle.io/reference/firmware/photon/#ready-

What should it do?
Return `false` if the IP address is `0.0.0.0`.

#### Channel switching
The photon should be able to switch seamlessly to a new WiFi channel if the router changes the channel.

### Observed Behavior

When I switch the WiFi channel on my router, the behavior of the photon is not consistent.
I see one of the following behaviors:

* Photon starts blinking green. Display shows WiFi.ready() returning false and IP address becoming 0.0.0.0. A short blue blink is followed by a white blink and then green blinking again and a successful reconnect.
* Photon starts flashing green, then switches to breathing green. WiFi.ready() stays true, but IP address becomes 0.0.0.0. Doesn't recover from this state. It's in limbo until a reboot.
* Hard fault SOS (1 blink).


### Analysis of the problem

In my application, I display WiFi status on a TFT display. It displays the IP address in light grey when connected and in dark grey when not connected (code below).

![2017-08-20 12 51 47](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1708921/29494587-dfb846a0-85ad-11e7-830b-b1f1f5ec7425.jpg)


```
void ControllerWiFiView::update(bool wifiConnected, char * const ipAddress)
{
    if(obj != nullptr){
        obj->clrScheme->fore = wifiConnected ? D4D_COLOR_LIGHT_GREY : D4D_COLOR_GREY;
        D4D_SetText(obj, ipAddress);
    }
}

void ControllerWiFiPresenter::update(){
#if BREWPI_USE_WIFI
    char ipAddressString[16];
    bool wifiConnected = WiFi.ready();
    piLink.ipAddressAsString(ipAddressString);
    view_.update(wifiConnected, ipAddressString);
#endif
}
```

I observe light grey with IP address 0.0.0.0. This means that it is possible for the P1 to get in a state where WiFi.ready() returns `true`, while the IP address is `0.0.0.0`.

I have connected a debugger and step debugged the code with Eclipse. This confirms that WiFi.ready() returns `false`.

I cannot fully step debug to the actual code that determines the ready status, because it seems to be a dynalib system call. But here is my analysis:

WiFi.ready() calls network_ready(..)
```
    bool ready(void) {
        return network_ready(*this, 0, NULL);
    }
```
Which is defined here:
```
DYNALIB_FN(4, system_net, network_ready, bool(network_handle_t, uint32_t, void*))
```
And results in:
```
bool network_ready(network_handle_t network, uint32_t param, void* reserved)
{
    return nif(network).ready();
}
```
Which seems to call `wifi.ready()`.

I think all the virtual functions eventually end up here (ManagedNetworkInterface class):
```
    bool ready() override
    {
        return (SPARK_WLAN_STARTED && WLAN_CONNECTED);
    }
```
So the volatile status byte WLAN_CONNECTED is used.
It is set to `1` on a successful DHCP connect. 
It is set to '0' on 
`ManagedNetworkInterface::notify_disconnected()`
`ManagedNetworkInterface::disconnect()`
`ManagedNetworkInterface::off()`
In `system_network_internal.cpp`

My guess is that the notify_disconnect never happens in this case. I have set a breakpoint on all 3 write occurrences that set WLAN_CONNECTED to zero. We'll have to wait until it happens again.

Log in to your router, change the WiFi channel.

I am running the latest 0.7.0-rc.3 system firmware, compiled with arm-non-eabi-gcc 0.5.3.
I also use:
```
SYSTEM_MODE(MANUAL);
SYSTEM_THREAD(ENABLED);
```

However, this behavior has been present with older versions of the system firmware too (0.5.3). It seems to occur less often on 0.7.0 though.

### References

Full firmware I am running:
https://github.com/BrewPi/firmware

Code to maintain WiFi connection (it can switch between WiFi and Serial):
https://github.com/BrewPi/firmware/blob/master/app/controller/PiLink.cpp#L80

Code to display WiFi status on display:
https://github.com/BrewPi/firmware/blob/master/platform/spark/modules/eGUI_screens/ConnectivityDisplay.cpp#L42

### Possible workaround
Instead of `WiFi.ready()` use `WiFi.ready() && WiFi.localIP()[0]==0)`.

Related forum topic (from 2014): https://community.particle.io/t/wifi-ready-not-working/6627

body:
In an attempt to investigate the terrible WiFi reliability and TCP reliability that has gone unfixed for at least 6 months now, I wrote some test code and stumbled upon very bad behavior when handling WiFi. Please stop ignoring this Particle. Read the full bug report below, because it is complex. It is affecting my customers. I bought a lot of units from you, cores, photons, P1's. As a long time customer, I'm very disappointed that a WiFi IOT product does not take bug reports about bad WiFi reliability more seriously.

title: Electron power-on connectivity issues with 0.8.0-rc
body:
## Bug Report

### Expected Behavior

Stay connected without an external battery.

### Observed Behavior

Upgrading to 0.8.0-rc7 has made it so our units no longer stay connected when booted off the power supply. We are using a regulated lab 5V supply rated well in excess of 5A.

This was reproduced across multiple Electrons.

Another user reported similar issues with 0.8.0-rc3.

### Steps to Reproduce

The Electrons boot and stay connected when a battery is present; but without the battery, on the first boot they do not stay connected. What’s weird is that they do complete the handshake and deliver an initial diagnostics message (we can see it in the console), but then they go silent and become unreachable. The cyan LED starts blinking rapidly.

It’s also weird that the battery can be removed and then the Electron rebooted without reproducing this problem. It really is only on initial power-on.

Using particle device doctor to downgrade to 0.7.0 solves the problem.

This occurs whether the firmware was compiled for 0.7.0 or 0.8.0-rc4 (-rc7 is not available right now as an option in Particle Dev).

This is using a 3rd party AT&T SIM, with KeepAlive set at 60 seconds.

## Bug Report

### Expected Behavior

attachInterrupt(D7, myFunc, RISING) == true;

### Observed Behavior

attachInterrupt(D7, myFunc, RISING) == false;

Using firmware 1.4.0, attempt to attach an interrupt to D7 on a Boron device and it will return false.

#if Wiring_Cellular == 1

   * which is shared with BATT_INT_PC13 for power management */
  if (pin == D7) return false;

I'm fairly certain Wiring_Cellular still gets set on the Boron though.

title: Feature request: Put modem in standby without sleeping MCU
body:
### Request:
On some of the sleep modes available for the electron it is possible to set the SLEEP_NETWORK_STANDBY flag. This will put the modem in standby mode before putting the MCU to sleep.

It would be really handy to put the modem in standby mode but keep the MCU active. This would drastically reduce power consumption and when data is ready to be sent a connection to the operator can quickly be made.

### Some background information:
I built a solar powered weather station also measuring wind speed. Anemometer rotations are counted using a counter IC. Every 5 seconds the Electron is woken from sleep, reads and clears the counter and goes back to sleep. After 5 minutes of collecting data, the average, maximum and minimum wind speed are calculated. The modem is turned on and the results are published to a web server. Then the modem is turned off and the Electron goes back to sleep. The cycle repeats.

The problem with this approach it that it takes at least 20 seconds to connect to the cellular network and a lot of data is used in the process.

The alternative is not to sleep at all, but this is really power hungry which is a problem for a solar powered system.

### My  proposed solution:
Put the modem in standby mode. When the Electron is woken up every 5 seconds to read the counter the modem should remain in standby mode. When 5 minutes passed, the modem should come out of standby mode, publish data and then go back to standby.

Currently the modem only remains in standby while the Electron is sleeping.

Any advice on how to achieve this would be appreciated.

title: Send endlessly returning zero
body:
_This bug is top priority because it blocks deep update. Must resolve ASAP._

Often, but inconsistently, OTA updates will fail, usually right at the beginning.  When they fail, the LED turns magenta and simply freezes, then after 20 seconds, the Core gives up on the TCP socket and reconnects to the Cloud.

Here is more detail on the conversation between Core and Cloud during this type of failure and the code path through the communication library, firmware, and common library.
- The Spark Cloud sends an `UPDATE_BEGIN` message, which the Core handles [here](https://github.com/spark/core-communication-lib/blob/master/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L1005).
- The Cloud successfully receives the [empty acknowledgement](https://github.com/spark/core-communication-lib/blob/master/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L1009).
- The LED turns magenta inside the [`prepare_for_firmware_update` callback](https://github.com/spark/core-communication-lib/blob/master/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L1016) (implemented [here](https://github.com/spark/core-firmware/blob/master/src/spark_utilities.cpp#L431) in core-firmware, mostly delegated [here](https://github.com/spark/core-common-lib/blob/master/SPARK_Firmware_Driver/src/hw_config.c#L1478) in core-common-lib)
- The `UPDATE_BEGIN` handler [attempts to send](https://github.com/spark/core-communication-lib/blob/master/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L1023) the `UPDATE_READY` message
- Our blocking send implementation [times out after 20 seconds](https://github.com/spark/core-communication-lib/blob/master/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L221)
- That's because the [CC3000 `send` call](https://github.com/spark/core-firmware/blob/master/src/spark_utilities.cpp#L382) is endlessly returning zero, meaning it is neither sending anything nor alerting us to an error condition.

This may (not necessarily, but worth testing) be a result of our [removal of `select` back in February](https://github.com/spark/core-firmware/commit/2988e1112bf21efa531de89c2229b27543b702fa) to speed up OTA updates.

@satishgn Please stop all other work and fix this as soon as possible. If we have a fix by tomorrow (Monday) morning (in Minneapolis) then we may be able to deploy deep update this week. Otherwise it will probably have to wait until I (@towynlin) arrive in San Francisco in a week.

If anyone from the Spark community wants to help with debugging this one, please do! **All hands on deck!** We want to deploy the TI patch for CFOD, which we're calling "deep update", but that must wait on a fix for this issue.

CC: @zs- @dmiddlecamp @joegoggins @mohitbhoite @andyw-lala

title: Photon long handshake => malformed description message
body:
On prototype photon boards, the cloud handshake often takes many seconds longer than expected. After some digging into this, we found that the device service is receiving a malformed CoAP description message. Here are two examples in xxd format:

```
0000000: d5ff 267d 9521 7b22 6622 3a5b 5d2c 2276  ..&}.!{"f":[],"v
0000010: 223a 7b7d 7d                             ":{}}
```

```
0000000: 2159 bc92 3fe9 7b22 6622 3a5b 5d2c 2276  !Y..?.{"f":[],"v
0000010: 223a 7b7d 7d                             ":{}}
```

In both cases the first 6 bytes are malformed, whereas everything after that is fine. In particular, the device service is crying foul when the most significant 2 bits of the first byte of the message (the CoAP version) are anything other than `01`, the only value allowed by the CoAP spec.

As can be seen obviously in [the code](https://github.com/spark/firmware/blob/feature/hal/communication/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L612-L617), the first 2 bytes should always be `0x61 0x45` and the sixth byte should always be `0xff`. The 3rd, 4th, and 5th bytes may be anything.

I suspect one of two things is happening. Either:
- the RTOS on the Photon is interleaving access to `queue` so that those bytes are being overwritten (e.g., by a `blocking_receive`) before we finish the `blocking_send` of the description message, or
- whatever resides immediately before `queue` in memory is writing beyond the end with pointer math and the buffer overrun is not being caught by the compiler

Low priority for the moment (since handshake always eventually succeeds), but @m-mcgowan take a look when you're in the mood for some low level debugging.

title: spark protocol: events with composite names only work for the handler in slot 0.
body:
A composite event name is one containing a slash, such as "test/event1". When a composite event name is received, the receive buffer is modified in place from the CoAP data to produce the full name. However, this only works correctly for the first iteration of the loop and so only for the event handler at slot 0 - subsequent iterations of the loop over the remaining handlers (https://github.com/spark/firmware/blob/feature/hal/communication/src/spark_protocol.cpp#L1063) don't compare the handler filter with the full event name, but just the name component up to the first slash,  e.g."test". Since the handler filter ("test/event1") is more specific than the apparent name of the event ("test"), the handler isn't invoked.

The fix is to decode the event name and data once outside of the loop, and then use that info in a loop to check for a match against each handler.

title: Wi-Fi automatically connects to AP after WiFi.on()
body:
Hi there,

In general, `WiFi.on()` would not connect photon to an AP until `WiFi.connect()` is called. If I make the photon out of the AP range, it will always try to connect to the AP. Then I turn off the WiFi using `WiFi.off()` and then turn on it again by `WiFi.on()`, photon launched to connect to the AP immediately , instead of staying at fading blue. I.e.:

case 1.WiFi.on() -> stay at fading blue
case 2.WiFi.on() -> WiFi.connect() -> connect failed and WiFi.off() -> WiFi.on() -> connect to AP immediately.

Is the case 2 normal or a bug?

I looked into the code, I think it is probably caused by not clearing the wlan watch dog(`CLR_WLAN_WD()`) when calling WiFi.off(), so that upon the WiFi.on() is called the watch dog fired in function `manage_network_connection()`. Am I right?

If this is not a potential bug, I will close this issue. Waiting for your respond.

They are the same thing, but I agree most people see a null terminator and know what's going on without thinking about it.  Sometimes the way to go though is to match the style used in the existing file instead of applying your own style here and there. If we can pre-size the internal buffer to be larger than the input string (say 10 chars) and then provide a string that is 7 chars long, with a length of 5, then we verify that only 5 chars were copied to the buffer, and not 7. title: Correctly process APPLICATION/SYSTEM DESCRIBE requests
body:
Fixes #1181

**NOTE:** Device currently receives incorrect DESCRIBE request with `flags=0x09` (see https://github.com/spark/firmware/blob/dfc5e68866cdd794d17ab51640ca565ae3a757ab/communication/src/protocol_defs.h#L91). The length of the request also seems to be wrong (judging by #1181), and instead of 9 bytes, the device receives 16 bytes, all extra bytes are 0x09:
```
Photon:                        41016b7d02b16409 09 09090909090909
Electron DESCRIBE_SYSTEM:      4101305d01b16441 01
Electron DESCRIBE_APPLICATION: 4101305e02b16441 02
```

The PR accounts for this by assuming that the server actually requests `DESCRIBE_ALL (0x03)`, if describe flags byte `>= DESCRIBE_ALL (0x03)`

title: Feature/arduino compatibility regression
body:
Attempts to restore 0.6.0-style arduino compatibility as outlined by issue #1278 

In a nutshell:

- the default is 0.6.0 Arduino compatibility - let's call this partial compatibility. 
- applications and libraries include "Arduino.h" to define `ARDUINO` and bring in many more additional defines to complete the Arduino API.  We'll call this full compatibility. 


## Mixing libraries that require partial and full Arduino compatibility

Libraries that require full Arduino compatibility may include Arduino.h in their library header file, while libraries that depend on partial compatibility (because they themselves define missing symbols) don't include Arduino.h.  If a library requiring partial compatibility is included after one requiring full compatibility then the partial compatibility library may break, since Arduino symbols that it's not expecting will be defined. 

The workaround for this is to include all libraries requiring partial compatibility before libraries requiring full compatibility in the application file.

[2017-03-28T01:02:59Z | m-mcgowan | comment]
## Internal Design

- The partial Arduino API as it was in 0.6.0 is defined in `spark_wiring_arduino.h`. This file has been restored to it's former 0.6.0 state without the new Arduino APIs. This file is always included with Particle.h/application.h. 

- The full Arduino API is declared in "Arduino.h". By keeping it separate we make a clear distinction between which symbols are included in the partial API and the full API. 

- There is some overlap of the partial API and the full API - `constrain` and `range` are examples. In the partial API, these are declared as templates. In the full API, they are macros. Hence, the usual trick of using `#ifndef constrain` won't work in the full API since it's defined as a template and not a macro. The workaround is to use `PARTICLE_WIRING_ARDUINO_TEMPLATE` as a define when these few common symbols have already been defined in the partial API, so they are not re-defined in the full API.  If we are splitting hairs, this may mean that some arduino libraries fail to compile in cases where the template does not behave the same as the macro (or that they are relying upon double-evaluation side-effects of the macro!!).  In this rare (hopefully non-existent) case, it is possible to get the arduino version of these defines, by disabling the preprocessor, and including `Arduino.h` at the top of the sketch.

title: [USB] Fixes an issue with Serial when receiving consecutive multiple 64-byte transmissions from Host
body:
### Problem

With RX queue full, the device NAKs OUT (Host->Device) transfers. With `bInterval` set to `0` (1 ms) this causes the device to spend too much time in USB interrupt, not giving any processing time to the application/system thread to consume RX queue. For some reason CDC driver on OSX doesn't attempt to send any data after about 300 NAKed transfers. Closing/re-opening the port doesn't help either.

### Solution

Set `bInterval` to a maximum value (16 ms) on OUT endpoint to give enough time for the device to consume RX queue and not send too many NAKs to Host.

We should probably add some workaround as well: e.g. count the number of NAKs sent and silently drop incoming data after a certain threshold instead of NAKing it. Even though this is OSX driver's fault. :face_with_head_bandage:

### Steps to Test

The bug is easily reproducible on OSX when setting WPA Enterprise credentials over Serial. A simple copy-paste of a certificate (e.g. CA) will not complete and get stuck somewhere half-way through.

title: Fix endless IWDG reset loop
body:
### Problem

In order to minimize usage of the DCT in the bootloader, the firmware now uses backup registers to store system flags (see https://github.com/spark/firmware/pull/1325). This poses a problem when firmware is downgraded from 0.7.0-rc.1: bootloader enables IWDG and sets a flag in the backup registers, but an older firmware is unable to detect that IWDG is running since it expects IWDG flag to be set in the DCT. This causes the device to reset every 5 seconds.

### Solution

Do not enable IWDG if currently flashed firmware has a version number lower than 0.7.0-rc.1. This gives user a possibility to downgrade the bootloader properly.

### Steps to Test

1. Set all module versions to 200 (0.7.0-rc.1) in [system_module_version.mk](https://github.com/spark/firmware/blob/fix/disable_iwdg/modules/shared/system_module_version.mk).
2. Compile and flash all system parts **and bootloader** to the device.
3. Flash 0.6.2 firmware via DFU. The device should work normally without resetting unexpectedly.

title: [Photon/P1] Fixes thread priority issues
